# Defence Determination 2016/19, Conditions of service

made under section 58B of the Defence Act 1903

**Compilation No. 159**

**Compilation date:** 10 September 2026

**Includes amendments:** Defence Determination 2026/15

This compilation is in 4 volumes

**Volume 1 Chapter 1 – Chapter 5**

Volume 2 Chapter 6 – Chapter 11

Volume 3 Chapter 12 – Chapter 17

Volume 4 Endnotes

Each volume has its own contents

**About this compilation**

**This compilation**

This is a compilation of *Defence Determination 2016/19, Conditions of service*, that shows the text of the law as amended and in force on 10/09/2026 (the ***compilation date***).

The notes at the end of this compilation (the endnotes) include information about amending laws and the amendment history of provisions of the compiled law.

**Uncommenced amendments**

The effect of uncommenced amendments is not shown in the text of the compiled law. The details of amendments made up to, but not commenced at, the compilation date are underlined in the endnotes. Any uncommenced amendments affecting the law are accessible on the Register (www.legislation.gov.au).

**Application, saving and transitional provisions**

If the operation of a provision or amendment of the compiled law is affected by an application, saving or transitional provision that is not included in this compilation, details are included in the endnotes.

**Modifications**

If the compiled law is modified by another law, the compiled law operates as modified but the modification does not amend the text of the law. Accordingly, this compilation does not show the text of the compiled law as modified. Any modifications affecting the law are accessible on the Register.

**Self repealing provisions**

If a provision of the compiled law has been repealed in accordance with a provision of the law, details are included in the endnotes.

### Chapter 1: Introduction

#### Part 1: About this Manual

###### 1.1.1 Simplified outline of this Determination

This Determination is the main authority for providing members and their families with benefits as a part of their conditions of service. It provides the legal basis for implementing conditions of service policies that support members and their families. Chapter 2 also provides some benefits to people applying to join the ADF in limited circumstances.

The Determination is broken up into chapters that deal with specific subject matters, as outlined below.

Chapter 1 provides information that applies across the determination, including advice on how the determination is to be read, definitions, technical rules, application and savings provisions, and obligations and responsibilities on people who receive benefits under the determination, such as providing notice of a change in circumstances that may affect eligibility for a benefit.

Chapters 2 to 11 generally provides benefits for members who are in Australia. Some benefits may also continue to apply to a member when they are providing service overseas, such as leave. In addition to specific benefits provided to members, Part 2 of Chapter 3 provides rules for the administration of salaries and salary-related allowances made by the DFRT. Many benefits are provided to members based on the composition of their families.

Chapters 12 to 16 provide benefits for members who are working overseas on short-term duty, as a consequence of a posting overseas, or on a peacetime deployment overseas. Members overseas may still be eligible to receive some benefits under chapters 1 to 11, depending on their individual circumstances.

Chapter 17 is specific to warlike and non-warlike deployments overseas. Members on a deployment overseas may still be eligible to receive some benefits under chapters 1 to 11, or chapters 12 to 16 depending on their individual circumstances.

Unless specified, benefits provided in this Determination only apply to members on continuous full-time service, which includes members in the Permanent Forces and members of the Reserves on service option (SERVOP) C.

<td></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">If Christmas day is on a Wednesday — 24 December to 1 January.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

<td colspan="2">If Christmas day is on a Thursday — 25 December to 2 January.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

</tr>

</tr>

</tr>

<tr>
<td></td>

</tr>

<td></td>

<td></td>

<td colspan="2">Destruction of, or damage to, any property.</td>

<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">Disruption to essential services.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> This is not limited to naturally occurring events (such as earthquakes, floods or storms), but would, for example, include fires, explosions, accidents, epidemics, pandemics, emissions of poisons, radiation or other hazardous agents, hijacks, sieges, riots, acts of terrorism and hostilities by an enemy.</td>
</tr>

Under section 58A of the Act, member also includes a person who has ceased to be a member, whether by reason of death or otherwise.<br><b>Note 2:</b> Section 1.2.1 restricts the application of the Determination to members on continuous full‑time service, unless otherwise specified.</td>

###### 1.3.4 Posting period – within Australia

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">For service within Australia, a member's posting period starts on the day they begin duty at a primary service location and ends on the day they finish duty there, subject to subsections 2 to 6.<br><b>Note:</b> Posting period for a member on a long-term posting overseas is defined in section 12.3.16.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s duty begins on any of the following days that they arrive at the location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The Saturday, Sunday or public holiday immediately before the day they begin duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The last day of their paid leave before the day they begin duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The day they are granted a removal to the location, or any later day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member’s resident family are granted a removal to the member’s housing benefit location and arrive there before the member, the posting period starts on the day their resident family arrive.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s duty ends on any of the following days that they leave the location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The Saturday, Sunday or public holiday immediately before the day they finish duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The last day of their paid leave immediately before the day they finish duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The day they are granted a removal from the location, or any later day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member’s resident family are granted a removal from the housing benefit location and depart after the member, the posting period ends on the day their resident family depart.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6.</td>
<td colspan="2">In deciding whether it is reasonable for a member's posting period to start on an earlier day or end on a later day, the CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The circumstances of the member’s removal to or from the location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The number, age, gender and circumstances of the member’s resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The availability of rental accommodation at the location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Any other factor relevant to the posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> The specific provisions in other Chapters regarding the start and stop of particular benefits override this definition.</td>
</tr>
</table>

<tr>
<td></td>

| Item | Column A<br>Member situation | Column B<br>Type of accommodation |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | They are one of the following.<br>a. A member with accompanied resident family.<br>b. A member who has no resident family but who has an adult child. | Any of the following.<br>a. The member’s suitable own home.<br>b. A suitable Service residence.<br>c. A home for which rent allowance is payable. |
| 2. | The member has unaccompanied resident family. | 1. For the member, any of the following.<br>a. Suitable living‑in accommodation.<br>b. A rented home for which rent allowance is payable.<br>c. A surplus Service residence.<br>d. Accommodation provided under Chapter 7 Part 7.<br>e. An appointment, tied or assigned Service residence under Chapter 7 Part 6 Division 6.<br>2. For the unaccompanied resident family the accommodation that was approved as suitable for them to live in at the family benefit location. |
| 3. | The member meets all the following.<br>a. They are a member with unaccompanied resident family.<br>b. They have unaccompanied resident family at a location that is not a family benefit location. | Any of the following.<br>a. Suitable living‑in accommodation.<br>b. A rented home for which rent allowance is payable.<br>c. A surplus Service residence.<br>d. Accommodation provided under Chapter 7 Part 7. |
| 4. | A member who has no resident family. | Any of the following.<br>a. The member’s suitable own home.<br>b. Suitable living‑in accommodation.<br>c. A rented home for which rent allowance is payable.<br>d. A surplus Service residence.<br>e. Accommodation provided under Chapter 7 Part 7.<br>f. An appointment, tied or assigned Service residence under Chapter 7 Part 6 Division 6. |

|  | **Note:** Section 7.5.2 provides a different definition of Suitable accommodation for the purpose of Chapter 7 Part 5. |
|---|---|

##### Division 2: Key definitions relating to location

###### 1.3.8 Service location

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">Service location means any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is on continuous full-time service, the location where the member is normally expected to provide capability under any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>A posting order.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>An alternate located work agreement.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>A transition location (general) agreement.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iv.</td>
<td>A transition location (medical) agreement.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is posted to any of the following, the ship’s or submarine’s home port.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>A seagoing ship.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>A seagoing submarine.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>A flight liable to embark on a seagoing ship.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is on Reserve service, the location where they are expected to provide capability on the day they provide reserve service.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.3.9 Primary service location

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">Primary service location means one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member only has one service location, the service location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member has more than one service location, the location specified in any of the following agreements as the member’s primary service location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member’s alternate located work agreement.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member’s transition location – general agreement.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The member’s transition location – medical agreement.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is a member on reserve service, one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>If the member is required to perform duty from multiple service locations from the same posted position — the location where they are expected to provide the majority of their capability in the financial year.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>For any other member — the location of the position they are posted to.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.3.10 Housing benefit location

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">Housing benefit location, in relation to a member, means one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is serving within Australia — any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Any area that is within 30 km from the member’s primary service location that can be travelled by vehicle on a public road.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Any area in which a member can travel by public transport in 150 minutes from the member’s primary service location and return for the purpose of commencing duty and returning home after ceasing duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>An extended housing benefit location under section 1.3.11.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iv.</td>
<td>If a Service residence has been provisioned for the member’s primary service location in an area that does not meet subparagraph i, ii or iii, the location of the Service residence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>v.</td>
<td>An area approved for a member participating in the flexible housing trial under section 7.1.15.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member is on a long-term posting overseas — the location that the member is provided housing for the purposes of their long-term posting overseas.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.3.11 Extended housing benefit location

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Extended housing benefit location for a member means an area extending the housing benefit location described in paragraphs 1.3.10.a. and b. that meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The extension of the housing benefit location has been requested by the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The CDF is satisfied that the member’s attendance at their primary service location will not be adversely affected by any additional travelling time to their primary service location as a consequence of extending the member’s housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.3.12 Family benefit location

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">Family benefit location means any of the following that is not in the member’s housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member is one of the following — the location to which their resident family received a removal under this Determination, other than under section 6.5.46A or Chapter 6 Part 5 Division 10.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member has unaccompanied resident family and no accompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member is posted to a seagoing ship or submarine.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The member has accompanied resident family and no unaccompanied resident family and is deployed for 6 months or longer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iv.</td>
<td>The member has unaccompanied resident family and no accompanied resident family and is on a long-term posting overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member was recruited from overseas and has unaccompanied resident family and no accompanied resident family — the location of the member's resident family’s first Australian home.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">If all of the following apply — the location the member’s resident family lives.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member has unaccompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Before the member had an unaccompanied resident family the member had an accompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The unaccompanied resident family remain in the location where they were the member’s accompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">Despite subsection 1.c, family benefit location does not include the location the member’s resident family live if all the following are met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Before the member had an unaccompanied resident family the member had an accompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">During the period the member had accompanied resident family they lived in a location (the alternate location) which was approved under an Alternate located work agreement.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">Before the member’s alternate located work agreement was approved, the member’s resident family did not live in the alternate location.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 3: Key definitions relating to resident family

###### Subdivision 1: Accompanied resident family

###### 1.3.14 Accompanied resident family

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">A person is accompanied resident family of a member if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The person meets the definition of recognised family under section 1.3.1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member has applied for recognition of the person as accompanied resident family on the approved form.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">One of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The person meets the criteria for a type of accompanied resident family in Subdivision 2: Types of accompanied resident family</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The person is accompanied resident family of a dual serving couple under Subdivision 5: Dual serving members.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.3.15 Effect of temporary separation

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">A person does not cease to be accompanied resident family of a member if they are temporarily separated from the member due to one of the following reasons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Service reasons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member or their partner has an illness or infirmity which prevents them from living together.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">A circumstance in which the CDF is satisfied of all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The reason for the temporary separation is unforeseen.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The separation is genuinely temporary.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The person intends to permanently re-join the member within a reasonable timeframe.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### Subdivision 2: Types of accompanied resident family

###### 1.3.16 Accompanied resident family — Partner

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A partner of a member is accompanied resident family of a member if any of the following apply to the partner.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They live in a home with the member on a permanent basis.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are reasonably expected to live in a home with the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">If they are not an Australian citizen or the holder of a permanent visa, they live in a home with the member and the CDF is satisfied that they meet one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They hold a temporary visa that is expected to lead directly to the grant of a permanent visa.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They have applied for a temporary visa that is expected to lead directly to the grant of a permanent visa.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">In this section, the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Permanent visa</b> has the same meaning as given in the <i>Migration Act 1958</i>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Temporary visa</b> has the same meaning as given in the <i>Migration Act 1958</i>.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.3.17 Accompanied resident family — child

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A child is accompanied resident family of the member if any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They live with the member on a permanent basis in the member’s housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are reasonably expected to live with the member in the member’s housing benefit location for at least 90 nights in a year.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> If a member is on a flexible service determination, the member’s nonworking period does not affect the 90 night period when the child stays with the member in the housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.3.18 Accompanied resident family — Child less than 90 nights

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A child is accompanied resident family of a member if they are expected to live with the member at their housing benefit location for less than 90 nights a year and the CDF is satisfied that they are not able to meet section 1.3.17 having regard to any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The arrangements for the child's contact or residence with the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member's access to the child.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The distance and transport between the child's location and the member's location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The nature and extent of the member's Service commitments.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>Other factors that may be relevant to the relationship of the child and the member.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.3.19 Accompanied resident family — Child absent due to education

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">A child is accompanied resident family of a member if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member has accompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member does not have a partner who is recognised as resident family and has no accompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The child is absent from the member’s home only because they are undertaking full-time primary, secondary or undergraduate tertiary education.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### Subdivision 3: Unaccompanied resident family

###### 1.3.19A Member this Subdivision does not apply to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This subdivision does not apply to a member who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member’s partner is also a member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member and their partner occupy living-in accommodation at their housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.3.20 Unaccompanied resident family

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A person is unaccompanied resident family of a member if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The person meets the definition of recognised family under section 1.3.1</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member has applied for recognition of the person as unaccompanied resident family on the approved form.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subject to subsection 1A, the person meets the criteria for a type of unaccompanied resident family in Subdivision 4: Types of unaccompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> If all of the member’s resident family are children, this subsection is displaced by subsection 2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1A.</td>
<td colspan="3">If a person meets all of the following, Subdivision 5: Dual serving members applies and provides who is accompanied resident family and who is unaccompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are part of a dual serving couple.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They live in a different housing benefit location to their partner.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is eligible for the recognition of the resident family as unaccompanied resident family if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s resident family are children.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF is satisfied of all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>That there is an appropriate recognised other person to care for the children.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Subject to subsection 3, the children are being cared for in a home maintained by the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member has applied for recognition of the child as unaccompanied resident family on the approved form.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">The child meets the criteria for a type of unaccompanied resident family in Subdivision 4: Types of unaccompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">For the purpose of subparagraph 2.b.ii, a <b>home maintained by the member</b> must be the home the children lived in with the member in the member’s previous housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> To avoid doubt, a member who occupied living-in accommodation in the previous housing benefit location was not maintaining the home.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.3.21 When resident family cease to be unaccompanied

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Resident family cease to be unaccompanied resident family of a member if any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The resident family no longer meets the criteria for a type of unaccompanied resident family in subdivision 4 of this Division.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The member commences a new posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The CDF is satisfied that the member’s resident family no longer meet the purpose of being recognised as unaccompanied.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td><b>Note:</b> The CDF must inform the member of the decision.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> Nothing prevents the member from reapplying for recognition of a person as unaccompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### Subdivision 4: Types of unaccompanied resident family

###### 1.3.22 Unaccompanied resident family — In connection with a posting

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">Resident family is unaccompanied resident family if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member commences a new posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Immediately before commencing a new posting, one of the following applies.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The resident family was accompanied resident family of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The resident family was unaccompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member resides in their housing benefit location without any accompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.3.23 Unaccompanied resident family — In connection with a posting to a seagoing ship or seagoing submarine

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">Resident family is unaccompanied resident family if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Immediately before becoming unaccompanied resident family, the resident family was accompanied resident family of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They are posted to a seagoing ship or seagoing submarine.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They are granted a removal for their resident family to a family benefit location under section 6.5.21.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>They reside in their housing benefit location without any accompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.3.24 Unaccompanied resident family — Resident family moving away from the member

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">Resident family is unaccompanied resident family if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The resident family meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Immediately before becoming unaccompanied resident family, they were accompanied resident family of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They move away from the member’s housing benefit location</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member resides in their housing benefit location without any accompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.3.25 Unaccompanied resident family — On return from a deployment

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">Resident family is unaccompanied resident family if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The resident family meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Immediately before becoming unaccompanied resident family, they were accompanied resident family of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>During the member’s deployment, they moved to a family benefit location or another location for family support.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>On return from deployment, they do not commence a new posting in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They reside in their housing benefit location without any accompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.3.26 Unaccompanied resident family — Partners who do not live together

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">A partner is unaccompanied resident family if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF is satisfied that the member and their partner are not able to live together due to one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Service requirements.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Court orders relating to a child of the member or of the person.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>Court orders relating to the safety and welfare of a person.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member resides in their housing benefit location without any accompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.3.27 Unaccompanied resident family — Recognised family in connection with recruitment from overseas

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">Recognised family is unaccompanied resident family if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They were recruited from overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They were moved to Australia at Commonwealth expense.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>They reside in their housing benefit location without any accompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The recognised family’s first home in Australia is not in the member’s housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.3.28 Unaccompanied resident family — Compassionate reasons

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Resident family is unaccompanied resident family if the CDF is satisfied that there are compassionate reasons to recognise them as unaccompanied resident family, having regard to the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The health and welfare of the member and their resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Any other relevant matter.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">In making a decision under subsection 1, the CDF must also specify the duration in which the decision is to apply.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.3.29 Unaccompanied resident family — Child absent due to education

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A child is unaccompanied resident family of a member if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member has unaccompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The child is absent from the member’s home only because they are undertaking full-time primary, secondary or undergraduate tertiary education.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The member resides in their housing benefit location without any accompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### Subdivision 5: Dual serving members

###### 1.3.30 Who this subdivision applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This subdivision applies to a member (the first member) who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member’s partner is also a member (the second member).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The first member has a different housing benefit location than the second member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Despite subsection 1, this subdivision does not apply if both members occupy living-in accommodation.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.3.31 Dual serving member – Partner only

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">If the member’s (the first member) only resident family is their partner (the second member) and the first member is nominated as having unaccompanied resident family, the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The first member is accompanied resident family of the second member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The second member is unaccompanied resident family of the first member.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.3.32 Dual serving member – One member lives without resident family

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">If one of the members does not live with any resident family (the first member) and the member’s partner lives with the resident family (the second member), the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>In relation to the first member, their resident family are unaccompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>In relation to the second member, their resident family are accompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.3.33 Dual serving member – Both members live with resident family

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">If both members live with resident family and a member (the first member) is nominated as having unaccompanied resident family, the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>In relation to the first member, their resident family are unaccompanied resident family and they have no accompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>In relation to the member (the second member) not nominated as having unaccompanied resident family, their resident family are accompanied resident family and they have no unaccompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> Rules for nomination are set out in section 1.3.34.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.3.33A Dual serving member – One member occupies living-in accommodation

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">If the member (the first member) occupies living-in accommodation and the other member (the second member) lives out, the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The first member is unaccompanied resident family of the second member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The second member is accompanied resident family of the first member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> The second member remains accompanied resident family of the first member under section 1.3.31 if the second member is required to live in temporarily for service reasons.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.3.34 Dual serving member – Rules relating to nomination

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">For the purpose of section 1.3.31 and 1.3.33, the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A nomination may be made by a member or their partner.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If a nomination is not made, the senior member is taken to be nominated as having unaccompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The classification of the resident family applies regardless of who they live with.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 4: Key definitions relating to people

###### Subdivision 1: General

###### 1.3.35 Child

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A child of a member or their partner is a person under 21 years of age who meets any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are, or were before they turned 18 years of age, a child of the member or the member’s partner for the purposes of Part 7 Division 1 Subdivision D of the <i>Family Law Act 1975.</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are, or were before they turned 18 years of age, the subject of a permanent care order issued by a court or statutory authority and placed in the member’s or the member’s partner’s care.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF or decision maker is satisfied that they have joined the member’s household in anticipation of being placed in the member or the member’s partner’s care under a permanent care order issued by a court or statutory authority.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">Despite subsection 1, the age limit of 21 does not apply to a person if the CDF or decision maker is satisfied of all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The person is an invalid or has a disability.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The person is unable to live independently.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The person is dependent on the member, their resident family or a recognised other person for in-home care.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">A person ceases to be a child under subsection 2 if the CDF or decision maker is satisfied any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The person is living separately from the member, their resident family or a recognised other person on a permanent or indefinite basis.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The person is able to live independently from the member, their resident family or a recognised other person.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">In this section <b>decision maker</b> means any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">For paragraph 1.c — a Commanding Officer, Officer Commanding or Unit Executive (Air Force only) not below Major in the member's direct chain of command.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">For subsection 2 and 3 — any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Director General Defence Member and Family Support.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>A person not below Captain working in the Directorate Helpline, Incidents and Welfare Policy.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>A person not below or APS 5 working in the Directorate Helpline, Incidents and Welfare Policy.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.3.36 Partner

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">Partner, in relation to a member, means a person who meets any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are in a registered relationship prescribed by the law of a State or Territory with the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are in a de facto relationship with the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">One of the following applies.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They are married to the member under the <i>Marriage Act 1961</i>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They are in a marriage with the member that is recognised under the <i>Marriage Act 1961</i>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">A CDF recognised partner under section 1.3.38.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">Subject to section 1.3.38, a person ceases to be a partner if the CDF is satisfied that the person lives separately and apart from the member on a permanent or indefinite basis.<br><b>Note 1:</b> Living separately and apart from the member on a permanent basis is an indication of a breakdown in the relationship.<br><b>Note 2:</b> A member and their partner may cease to be partners even if they continue to reside in the same residence or that either party provides some household services to the other.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.3.37 Recognised other person

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">Recognised other person, in relation to a member, means a person who lives with the member or their resident family and who is any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">An adult child.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">A live-in carer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">A guardian or housekeeper.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subject to subsection 2, a person has an interdependent relationship with the member if the CDF is satisfied the member and the person have a close personal relationship having regard to the following factors.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The permanency of the relationship.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The degree of emotional support the interdependent relationship provides to the person or the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The financial support provided to the person by the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iv.</td>
<td>The degree of support and personal care the interdependent relationship provides to the person or the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A person must not be recognised as being in an interdependent relationship under paragraph 1.d if the CDF is satisfied that any of the following circumstances apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The person's relationship with the member is one of mere convenience.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">There is alternative support, care or accommodation available to the person.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The person is a resident child carer living with the member's family but is not otherwise recognised family of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">Despite subsection 1, an adult child is not required to live with the member or their resident family if sections 1.3.19 or 1.3.29 applied prior to the person turning 21 years old.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### Subdivision 2: Partners

###### 1.3.38 CDF recognised partner

| 1. | CDF recognised partner means a person who the CDF is satisfied would be recognised as being in a de facto relationship with the member if they were living together. |
|---|---|
|  | **Note:** De facto relationship is defined in section 1.3.39. |
| 2. | A member must use the approved form to apply for recognition of a CDF recognised partner relationship. |
| 3. | An application may be approved in relation to a period immediately preceding the application date. |

###### 1.3.39 De facto relationship

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">De facto relationship means a relationship between two persons who are both at least 18 years of age, and the CDF considers the relationship meets section 2F of the <i>Acts Interpretation Act 1901</i>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member must use the approved form to apply for recognition of a de facto relationship.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">A de facto relationship may be recognised under subsection 1 if the partners are temporarily separated due to one of the following reasons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member or their partner has an illness or infirmity which prevents them from living together.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>A circumstance where the CDF is satisfied that the member and their partner usually live together but are separated temporarily.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> This subsection cannot apply to a relationship where the couple have never lived together.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">To avoid doubt, an application may be approved in relation to a period immediately preceding the application date.<br><b>Note:</b> Approval of a past period may require adjustment of allowances and benefits and this may result in recovery action, with the member or their partner having to repay benefits to Defence or other Commonwealth agencies.</td>
</tr>
</table>

|---|---|

|  | For the purpose of the *Fringe Benefits Tax Assessment Regulations 2018,* a dependant of a member means a person who is resident family of the member. |

#### Part 5: Member's obligations

###### 1.5.1 Simplified Outline of this Part

Members have obligations when they receive benefits under this Determination.

These obligations are to ensure that members receive the correct benefits throughout their ADF careers.

Providing accurate information (section 1.5.2) and timely advice of changes in circumstances (section 1.5.3) minimise the chance of an overpayment and the subsequent recovery of money from the member (section 1.5.5).

If a benefit is payable by reimbursement, members are required to provide evidence of the expense (section 1.5.7).

###### 1.5.2 Obligation to provide accurate information

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member must provide accurate information in their application.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Defence may take into account information that a member's recognised family or recognised other person provides to ensure that correct benefits are provided in relation to the member's service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member has claimed, or otherwise receives, a benefit, the CDF may from time to time ask the member to provide information about their relationships and living arrangements to do any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>To verify the relationships or living arrangements that affect eligibility.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>To categorise their family members and to provide benefits they and any recognised family or recognised other person are eligible for.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">Giving false or misleading information is a serious offence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note 1:</b> Sections 137.1 and 137.2 of the Criminal Code create offences for providing false or misleading information or documents. The Criminal Code is a Schedule to the <i>Criminal Code Act 1995</i>.<br><b>Note 2:</b> Section 56 of the <i>Defence Force Discipline Act 1982</i> creates a military disciplinary offence for a false statement made in an application for a benefit.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.5.3 Change in member's circumstances

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies if a member, recognised family or a recognised other person meet all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They have qualified for a benefit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The circumstances on which they qualified for the benefit change.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A person who applies for a benefit under this Determination is responsible for informing themselves about the benefit they are claiming.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member must notify their Commanding Officer in writing about the change by the later of the following days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The day that is 14 days after the member’s circumstances change.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">A day that the CDF is satisfied is reasonable in the circumstance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member must notify one of the following, in writing, of a change in circumstances that relates to, or may affect, their eligibility for housing assistance under Chapter 7 within 14 days of the change occurring.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is occupying living-in accommodation — Commanding Officer, Officer Commanding or Executive Officer not below the rank of MAJ at the base where the member is required to occupy living-in accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is receiving any other type of housing assistance — Defence Housing Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member must fill in and provide the approved form to their Commanding Officer as soon as practicable after any of the following events.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The number of people in the member’s recognised family changes or recognised other person.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is notified of a change of service location and it is reasonable to expect that any of the following may change in the new service location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member has accompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member has unaccompanied resident family and no accompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The member has no recognised family or other recognised persons.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.5.4A Contributions and payments payable by a member not receiving salary

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member not receiving salary for any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member meets a condition under section A.1.4 of DFRT Determination No. 2 of 2017, <i>Salaries</i>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member is on a nonworking period under the member's flexible service determination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Any unpaid contributions or payments are a debt to the Commonwealth. The Commonwealth may recover any unpaid contributions or payments.<br>Note: The Accountable Authority Instructions issued under Section 20A of the <i>Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013</i> (PGPA Act) provide guidance and relevant procedures relating to debt management to ensure officials can meet their obligations under the PGPA Act.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.5.5 Recovery by the Commonwealth

| 1. | This section applies if a member must repay an overpayment of salary or allowances to the Commonwealth. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The Commonwealth may recover the overpaid amount from the salary and allowances that the member has been – or may be – paid. The Commonwealth still has the right to recover the overpaid amount by other means.<br>**Note:** The Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013 recovery processes are usually used to do this. |

###### 1.5.6 Decision makers to avoid conflict of interest

| 1. | This section applies if a member would get a personal benefit from a decision they are authorised to make. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The member must refer the decision to another decision maker at or above their rank or classification. |

###### 1.5.7 Member to provide evidence of payment

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member who is eligible for the reimbursement of a payment they made.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member must provide any of the following as evidence that they made the payment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Written evidence, including any original receipts.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A statutory declaration if written evidence is not available.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member must provide the items when they lodge their claim for reimbursement or as soon as practical after that time.<br><b>Note:</b> A person who knowingly makes a false statement in a statutory declaration under the <i>Statutory Declarations Act 1959,</i> as amended, is guilty of an offence under section 11 of that Act. They could go to prison for 4 years.</td>
</tr>
</table>

#### Part 6: Payment of benefits in special circumstances

###### 1.6.1 Dual entitlement – member's partner is also a member

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies if all the following are met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member's partner is also a member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Both members are eligible for any of the following benefits at the same time or for the same event.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Disturbance allowance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Reimbursement for childcare on removal.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>Assistance or reimbursement for home sale or purchase.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iv.</td>
<td>Reimbursement for loss on sale of furniture and effects.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>v.</td>
<td>Reimbursement for loss on sale of a vehicle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>vi.</td>
<td>Reimbursement for cost of insurance on removal of urgently needed household items.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>vii.</td>
<td>Reimbursement for education costs for a child under Chapter 8 Part 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>viii.</td>
<td>Reimbursement in place of a child’s scholarship.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">If subsection 1 applies, benefits are provided to one of the members, as determined by the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If both members jointly nominate one of them to receive the benefit — the nominated member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the members do not jointly nominate a member, one of the following applies.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>If the members hold different ranks — the member who has the higher rank.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>If the members hold the same rank — the member with greater seniority.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">If a member is eligible to receive a benefit listed in subsection 1 and the member’s partner is also eligible for a similar benefit not provided in Chapter 1 to 11 of this determination, the benefit payable to the member is reduced by the amount of the similar benefit.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.6.1A Payment of contributions by another person

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member not receiving salary for any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member meets a condition under section A.1.4 of DFRT Determination No. 2 of 2017, <i>Salaries</i>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member is on a flexible service determination — during their nonworking period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member may nominate, in writing, their partner to pay contributions owed by the member if all of the following conditions are met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Their partner is also a member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Their partner has consented in writing to make the contributions on the member’s behalf.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note 1:</b> Their partner may revoke consent at any time.<br><b>Note 2:</b> Contributions are to be paid through the Department of Defence pay system.<br><b>Note 3:</b> If the contribution is not paid by their partner, the contribution may be recovered from the member as a debt owed to the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.6.2 Payment of benefit to another person

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">If a member requests to have a benefit paid to another person, all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member must nominate in writing the person to receive the payment on their behalf.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The other person must consent to the disclosure of their personal or financial information, and to receiving the payment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The member must provide the alternative payment details.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.6.3 Payment of amount to a person under legal disability

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies if an amount is payable to a person who has a legal disability.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The amount may be paid to a trustee appointed by the CDF to act on behalf of the person.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2A.</td>
<td colspan="2">When appointing a trustee to act on behalf of the person, the CDF must consider any directions given by the person before they suffered the disability.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">All of the following apply to an amount paid to a trustee under subsection 2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The trustee will hold it on trust for the benefit of the person in accordance with any directions of the CDF.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>It is taken to have been paid to the person.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.6.4 Payment of amounts on death of a member

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">An amount payable to a member on their death may be paid to one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s recognised family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s legal personal representative, if all of the following are met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member has no recognised family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The CDF considers it appropriate.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The amount may be payable to more than one of the member’s recognised family if the CDF is satisfied of the losses each person suffers through the loss of the member’s earnings.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">If a payment under subsection 1 is not made within 12 months of the member’s death, the amount must be paid to the member’s legal personal representative.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">If no-one is eligible for a payable amount, no payment will be authorised.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.6.5 Effect of death on eligibility for salary and allowances

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">For the purpose of payment of salary or allowances, a member ceases continuous full-time service when any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member has died.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member is missing and presumed dead.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1A.</td>
<td colspan="2">If paragraph 1.b applies and the member is later found alive, the period the member was missing does not count as a break in their service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a certificate of death has not been provided to state a date of death or presumed death for a member under a relevant Commonwealth, State or Territory law, then for the purpose of the benefits provided under this Determination, the CDF, a Service Chief or the Director General Defence Member and Family Support may determine that a member died on a particular date.</td>
</tr>
</table>

#### Part 7: Imprisonment, detention and custody within Australia

###### 1.7.1 Purpose

|  | This Part sets out what happens to a member’s salary and benefits during a period of imprisonment, detention or custody. |
|---|---|

###### 1.7.2 Member this Part applies to

|  | This Part applies to a member, including a member of the Reserves on Reserve service, who is imprisoned, in detention or in custody within Australia. |
|---|---|

###### 1.7.3 Member this Part does not apply to

| 1. | The CDF or the Chief of Defence Intelligence may specify a member to whom this Part does not apply for a particular period or activity. |
|---|---|
| 2. | When making a decision under subsection 1, the CDF or the Chief of Defence Intelligence must have regard to the nature of the member’s duty. |

###### 1.7.4 General rule – benefits and contributions

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section does not apply to a member in the following circumstances.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If individual periodic imprisonment periods of imprisonment are less than 7 consecutive days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the full length of imprisonment is less than 7 days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">A decision under subsection 3 does not apply to any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member's salary or DFRT allowances.<br><b>Note:</b> Sections 1.7.5 and 1.7.6 specify the effect of imprisonment, detention or custody on salary and DFRT allowances.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member's leave credits.<br><b>Note:</b> Division 1 specifies the effect of imprisonment, detention or custody on leave credits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The member's contributions towards a Service residence, rent allowance or living-in accommodation.<br><b>Note 1:</b> Division 2 specifies the effect of imprisonment, detention or custody on housing assistance.<br><b>Note 2:</b> This subsection does not prevent the CDF from ceasing a member’s eligibility for housing assistance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member has been imprisoned, detained or held in custody for a period of 7 or more continuous days the CDF may decide to do the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Reduce or cease a benefit that the member was receiving before the member's imprisonment, detention or custody.<br><b>Note:</b> The CDF may set a future date when the benefit will be reduced or ceased.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Increase a contribution payable by the member, but not above the actual cost of the benefit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> To avoid doubt, a member will continue to receive benefits for the first 7 consecutive days of imprisonment, detention or custody. The 7 days starts on the day the member is imprisoned, detained or taken into custody.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member's benefit or contribution is changed by the CDF under subsection 3, the CDF may review the decision after 7 days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">When reviewing a decision under subsection 4, the CDF may decide to do any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Reinstate a benefit that had been ceased or reduced.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Reduce, including a further reduction of benefits previously reduced, or cease other benefits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Reduce a contribution that had been increased.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Increase a contribution, including a further increase of a contribution previously increased, but not above the actual cost of the benefit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>Make no further change to the benefit or contribution.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6.</td>
<td colspan="2">When making a decision under subsection 3 or subsection 4 the CDF must consider the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The remaining period of imprisonment, detention or custody.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The impact that reducing or ceasing a benefit or increasing a contribution would have on the member's resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Any other relevant circumstance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>7.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is not eligible for a benefit that they were not eligible for immediately before their imprisonment, detention or custody.</td>
</tr>
</table>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The part of the member's salary calculated using the following formula<i>,</i> is forfeited to the Commonwealth<i>.</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">[image: Start formula forfeited salary equals A minus B end formula]</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

<td><b>A</b></td>
<td>is the member's rate of salary.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

###### 1.7.6 Salary and DFRT allowances – member imprisoned or in custody

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member’s salary, DFRT allowances and Language allowance are forfeited to the Commonwealth during a period of imprisonment or custody.<br><b>Note:</b> Language allowance is payable under DFRT Determination No. 10 of 1992, <i>Language allowance.</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">For the purpose of subsection 1 the forfeit period is one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">For a single period of imprisonment or custody.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Commencing at the start of the first full day that the member is imprisoned or held in custody.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Ending at the end of the last full day the member is imprisoned or held in custody.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">For periodic imprisonment or custody.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Commencing at the start of the first day for each period that the member is imprisoned or held in custody.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Ending at the end of the last day of each period that the member is imprisoned or held in custody.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">If a member is held in custody for less than a full day, or 2 consecutive part days, the member does not forfeit any salary, DFRT allowances or Language allowance.<br><b>Note:</b> If the member is absent from duty without leave while being held in civil custody, action under section 29 of the Defence Regulation may apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">A period of imprisonment or custody does not count as qualifying service for the purpose of eligibility for DFRT allowances.</td>
</tr>
</table>

<table>
<tr>

<td colspan="3">This section applies to a member who is, or was, in detention or imprisonment and any of the following occurs.</td>
</tr>

<tr>

</tr>

<td colspan="3">If the member had part of their salary forfeited under section 1.7.5, the member is to be paid all of the following.</td>

<td colspan="2">An amount of salary calculated using the following formula.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">[image: Start formula amount of salary repayable equals A minus B end formula]</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td><b>A</b></td>
<td>is the amount of salary that the member would have received during the period had the member not been in detention.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td><b>B</b></td>
<td>is the amount of salary that the member received during the period the member was in detention.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">An amount equal to the DFRT allowances and Language allowance which were forfeited during the period the member was in detention.<br><b>Note:</b> Language allowance is payable under DFRT Determination No. 10 of 1992, <i>Language allowance.</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">If the member's salary, DFRT allowances and Language allowance were forfeited under section 1.7.6, the member is to be paid an amount equal to the salary, DFRT allowances and Language allowance that were forfeited during the period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">If a member's contribution for a benefit was increased under section 1.7.4, the member is to be reimbursed an amount calculated using the following formula.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">[image: Start formula amount of contribution reimbursed equals A minus B end formula]</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>A</b></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>B</b></td>
<td colspan="2">is the contribution amount that would have been paid by the member during the period of imprisonment, detention or custody.</td>
