<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="3">If a member's eligibility for a reimbursement was ceased under section 1.7.4, the member is to be paid the amount that the member would have been reimbursed had the member not been imprisoned, in detention or held in custody.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6.</td>
<td colspan="3">If a member’s service was ended during a period of imprisonment, detention or custody, the member is to be paid any salary, DFRT allowances and Language allowance that would have been payable from the date of forfeiture up until the member's last day of service.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 1: Leave

###### 1.7.8 Purpose

|  | This Division sets out what happens to a member’s leave during a period of imprisonment, detention or custody.<br>**Note:** The general rule in section 1.7.4 does not apply to any type of leave. |
|---|---|

###### 1.7.9 Recreation leave

| 1. | A member is not eligible to take recreation leave during a period of imprisonment or detention. |
|---|---|
| 2. | A period of imprisonment, detention or custody is non-effective service for the purpose of recreation leave accrual. |
| 3. | A member is credited recreation leave credits that would have accrued during a period of detention if the decision is quashed or set aside.<br>**Note:** This subsection does not apply to imprisonment or custody. |

###### 1.7.10 Short absence and medical absence from duty

|  | A member is not eligible to take short absence or medical absence from duty during a period of imprisonment, detention or custody. |
|---|---|

###### 1.7.11 Maternity leave

| 1. | A member is not eligible to take maternity leave during a period of imprisonment, detention or custody. |
|---|---|
| 2. | If a member is imprisoned, detained or held in custody during the required absence provided under Chapter 5 Part 6 Division 3, the required absence period is reduced by the by the number of days the member was imprisoned, in detention or custody during that period. |
| 3. | If a member is in periodic imprisonment or weekend imprisonment, the member may take maternity leave when not serving a period of imprisonment during the period in which maternity leave can be taken. |

###### 1.7.11A Premature birth leave

|  | A member is not eligible to take premature birth leave during a period of imprisonment, detention or custody. |
|---|---|

###### 1.7.12 Parental leave

|  | If a member is in periodic imprisonment or weekend imprisonment, the member may take parental leave when not serving a period of imprisonment during the period in which parental leave may be taken. |
|---|---|

###### 1.7.13 Long service leave

| 1. | A period of imprisonment, detention or custody is non-effective service for the purpose of accruing long service leave credits under Chapter 5 Part 5 Division 3. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The member is not eligible to take long service leave during a period of imprisonment, detention or custody. |

###### 1.7.14 Other forms of leave with or without pay

|  | A member is not eligible to take any other forms of leave with pay provided under Chapter 5 during a period of imprisonment or detention.<br>**Note:** This section does not apply to custody. |
|---|---|

##### Division 2: Housing, removals and storage

###### 1.7.15 Purpose

|  | This Division sets out what happens to a member’s housing, removals and storage benefits during a period of imprisonment, detention or custody.<br>**Note:** The general rule in section 1.7.4 does not apply to the contribution rate payable for any type of housing. |
|---|---|

###### 1.7.16 Member occupying a Service residence or rent band choice property

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">During a period of imprisonment, detention or custody a member is required to pay the market rent rate for the Service residence or rent band choice property for the following period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Commencing on the first full day of the member’s imprisonment, detention or custody.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Ceasing on the earlier of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The last full day the member is in prison, detention or custody.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The day the member vacates the property.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">Note: If the member is not in receipt of salary during this period, the payments will be considered a debt to the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">Subject to subsection 4, if the member is in financial hardship the CDF may reduce the market rent rate payable under subsection 1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">If the member’s eligibility for a Service residence or a rent band choice property is ceased by the CDF under section 1.7.4, the member is eligible for a removal under Chapter 6 Part 5 within 28 days to a location within Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">If the member or the member's resident family or recognised other persons do not vacate the residence within the 28 day period under subsection 3, all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s contribution is the equivalent of market rent rate for the residence until the residence is vacated.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is not eligible for any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>A removal under Chapter 6 Part 5.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>A reduction in the market rent rate under subsection 2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="3">If the member chooses to vacate a Service residence or rent band choice property and their eligibility for the accommodation has not ceased, the member is not eligible for a removal under Chapter 6 Part 5.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member is not eligible for housing assistance for their resident family if any of the following applies.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member's eligibility for a Service residence or rent band choice property is ceased by the CDF under section 1.7.4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member chooses to vacate a Service residence or rent band choice property.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>7.</td>
<td colspan="3">If a member is required to vacate their Service residence or rent band choice property and the member is unable to remove their property due to their imprisonment, detention or custody, the member’s property may be removed and stored under Chapter 6 Part 5 until the member’s release or an agent appointed by the member takes possession of the property.<br><b>Note 1:</b> The member may be responsible for the cost of storage under section 1.7.19.<br><b>Note 2:</b> If the member appoints an agent to take possession of their property, this appointment must be in writing.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>8.</td>
<td colspan="3">If a member’s possessions have been removed to another location or to storage, the member is not eligible for a removal under Chapter 6 Part 5 on their release from imprisonment, detention or custody unless they are posted to a new service location.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.7.17 Member occupying a rent allowance property

| 1. | A member ceases to be eligible for rent allowance on the first full day of the member's imprisonment, detention or custody. |
|---|---|
| 2. | If the member chooses to vacate the rent allowance property during a period of imprisonment, detention or custody, Chapter 6 does not apply. |

###### 1.7.18 Member occupying living-in accommodation

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member ceases to be permitted to occupy living-in accommodation if the CDF revokes the member's licence to live in.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">When making a decision under subsection 1, the CDF must take the following into consideration.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The duration of the member’s imprisonment, detention or custody.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The pattern of the member’s imprisonment, detention or custody.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The type of living-in accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Whether the accommodation is needed for a member who is required to live in.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> If the member’s licence to live in is revoked under subsection 1, the member may be eligible for housing assistance upon release from imprisonment, detention or custody.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member’s property remains in the living-in accommodation, the member is eligible for one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Storage of the member's property in the living-in accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Removal and storage of the member's property under Chapter 6 Part 5.<br><b>Note:</b> The member may be responsible for the cost of storage under section 1.7.19.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.7.19 Storage costs

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member's possessions have been removed and stored under Chapter 6 Part 5, section 1.7.16 or section 1.7.18, the CDF may recover the cost of the storage from the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">When making a decision under subsection 1 the CDF must take the following into consideration.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The amount of property put into storage.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Any special storage requirements that resulted in an increased cost to the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The number and type of vehicles that required storage.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.7.20 Contribution for meals

|  | If the member is on a continuous period of imprisonment, detention or custody — the member is not required to make a contribution for meals under Chapter 7 Part 9 Division 1. |
|---|---|

###### 1.7.21 Food allowance

|  | A member ceases to be eligible for food allowance under Chapter 7 Part 9 Division 2 during a period of imprisonment, detention or custody. |
|---|---|

##### Division 3: Other benefits

###### 1.7.22 Purpose

|  | This Division sets out the effect on other benefits that a member may or may not be eligible for during a period of imprisonment, detention or custody. |
|---|---|

###### 1.7.24 Travel in Australia

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member is required to travel to or from the place of detention, the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member is not eligible for meal allowance or incidentals for the journey to the place of detention but the member will be provided a reasonable meal having regard to the length and time of the journey.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member is eligible for meal allowance and incidentals payable under Chapter 9 Part 5 for the return journey to the member's service location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> Travel relating to the start and end of a period of detention is duty travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member is required to travel to or from the place of imprisonment or custody, the member is not eligible for travel benefits under Chapter 9 Part 5.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 1.7.25 Funeral costs

|  | The Director General Defence Member and Family Support may approve funeral benefits in exceptional circumstances under subsection 11.4.6.2. |
|---|---|

### Chapter 2: ADF career

#### Part 1: Joining the ADF

###### 2.1.3 Purpose

|  | This Part provides assistance to a person who has applied to join the ADF. This includes travel costs, allowances and accommodation costs. |
|---|---|

###### 2.1.4 Travel, accommodation and meals

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies to a person who has applied to be appointed to, or enlisted in, the ADF and all the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are requested to attend a Defence Force Recruiting Centre for an interview or examination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They attend a Defence Force Recruiting Centre for the interview or examination requested.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are required to travel from their normal place of residence to the Defence Force Recruiting Centre and back to their normal place of residence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">They live outside of an area serviced by the metropolitan transport system of the city or town where the Defence Force Recruiting Centre is located.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A person who travels to attend a Defence Force Recruiting Centre is eligible for one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If they use a private vehicle — an amount calculated under section 9.6.25.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If they use public transport by a regional transport provider, including air travel — the lesser of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The fares that the member would be eligible for if they held a rank of Colonel or lower.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The fares that they paid.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">The person is eligible for the allowance under subsection 4 for accommodation and meals if they meet all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The person has to be absent from their normal place of residence overnight to attend the Defence Force Recruiting Centre and return home.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Their meals and accommodation are not provided by the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">The allowance is the lowest of the following amounts.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The amount the accommodation and meals would have cost if they had been provided under this Part.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The amount the person paid for accommodation and meals.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The amount the person would be eligible for under table item 2 of section 9.5.35.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="3">The person is eligible for meal allowance under section 4.5.9 if all the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The person will not be absent from their normal place of residence overnight.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The period of their absence includes a meal period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">A meal is not provided under this Part.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 2.1.5 Prepaid fares

| 1. | A country applicant who travels to or from a recruiting centre is eligible to either a prepaid fare or an allowance under section 2.1.4. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The applicant must repay any prepaid amount they do not spend, including if the journey is cancelled. |

###### 2.1.6 Baggage

|  | Persons eligible for travel under this Division are not eligible for assistance under this Part for excess baggage. |
|---|---|

###### 2.1.7 Loss of wages or salary

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a person who is not a member of the ADF and who has applied to join the ADF. They may be compensated for loss of wages or salary if they meet all these conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are employed.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are required to have an examination or interview to see if they are suitable to join the ADF.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>They attend a recruiting centre to be examined or interviewed.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>They lose salary or wages because of that attendance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The applicant is eligible for the lesser of these two amounts.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The wages or salary they would have earned during the period they are reasonably required to be absent from the employment because of the attendance. This does not include any payment for overtime.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The salary that would be payable for that period to a normal entry recruit during basic training.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The applicant is not eligible if they have not disclosed in their application a significant fact that makes them ineligible to join the ADF.</td>
</tr>
</table>

#### Part 2: Career transition

###### 2.2.1 Purpose

|  | This Part provides benefits for a member to assist them with training and financial advice in preparation for civilian life when they change service category or cease service with the ADF. |
|---|---|

###### 2.2.2 Definitions

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">In this Part the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Employment</b> means any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Full-time work.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Part-time work.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Casual work.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Self-employment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Meaningful Engagement</b> means activities that improve social interaction and community inclusion, including, study, volunteer activities with sporting and recreation associations and clubs, retirement activities or unpaid work.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Member</b> includes a former member.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 2.2.3 Member this Part applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">This Part applies to the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member of the Permanent Forces who becomes a member of the Reserves.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> A member may become a member of the Reserves under sections 16 or 21 of the Defence Regulation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member of the Reserves who transfers to service category 2 if one of the following occurs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They cease service in service category 3, 4 or 5.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They complete a fixed period of continuous full-time service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member, including a member of the Reserves, who is in one of the following situations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They have been given a notice under section 100 of the Act or subsection 24(2) of the Defence Regulation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They are 12 months or less away from their retirement age.<br><b>Note:</b> Retirement ages are provided under subsection 23(4) of the Defence Regulation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>They are 3 months or less away from completing a fixed period of service.<br><b>Note 1:</b> A member may change their period of service under section 18 of the Defence Regulation.<br><b>Note 2: Change a period of service</b> is defined in subsection 18(3) of the Defence Regulation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iv.</td>
<td>They have been dismissed under the <i>Defence Force Discipline Act 1982</i>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">A former member who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They were in one of the situations under paragraph c. before they ceased to be a member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>It has been 2 years or less since their last day of service in the ADF.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 2.2.4 Member this Part does not apply to

|  | This Part does not apply to a member who is leaving the Permanent Forces who will immediately become a member of the Reserves on continuous full-time service. |
|---|---|

###### 2.2.5 Career transition training

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subject to subsection 3, a member is eligible on application for career transition training if all of the following apply and the CDF is satisfied that the training is aligned to a post-transition employment career path or meaningful engagement.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The application is approved within 24 months of the member’s transition date.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The training commences within 24 months of the member’s transition date.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1A.</td>
<td colspan="2">Despite subsection 1, a member is eligible for an additional 12 months to apply for and undertake training provided under subsection 1 if the CDF is satisfied of all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They have been given a notice under subsection 24(2) of the Defence Regulation because of being medically unfit for service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member is unable to access training because of their medical condition or injuries.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> A member’s service may be ended under paragraph 24(1)(a) of the Defence Regulation if they are medically unfit for service in the Defence Force.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1B.</td>
<td colspan="2">If subsection 1A applies, the member must not commence the approved training unless the CDF is satisfied that the member is medically fit to undertake it.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Career transition training cannot occur during a period the member is on duty and undertaking Reserve service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">A benefit under subsection 1 can be made as a reimbursement to the member or provided to the service provider.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is not eligible for assistance under this section if any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member has secured employment or achieved meaningful engagement related to their post-transition goals.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The training could be considered a capital investment in a new or existing business.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">In this section, <b>career transition training</b> means training for a member up to a cumulative lifetime total of $5,320.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 2.2.6 Assistance for professional financial advice

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is eligible on application for professional financial advice within 24 months of the member’s transition date if the financial advice meets the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">It is provided by one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>A professional financial advisor who holds a current Australian Financial Services Licence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>An authorised representative of a holder of an Australian Financial Services Licence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The advice is not for routine tax or accountancy services.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A benefit under subsection 1 can be made as a reimbursement to the member or provided to the service provider.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">In this section, <b>professional financial advice</b> means financial advice for a member up to a cumulative lifetime total of $1,000.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 2.2.7 Travel and accommodation

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for travel costs within Australia if the CDF is satisfied that the member must travel to attend the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Career transition training activities under section 2.2.5.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>ADF Member and Family transition seminars.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Travel costs provided under subsection 1 are limited to the travel costs payable under Chapter 9 Part 5, Payment of Travel costs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is eligible to occupy one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Service accommodation in the location where the activity is to be held.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Normal accommodation stock, as defined in section 9.5.15, if the CDF is satisfied that Service accommodation is not suitable for the member to use.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 2.2.8 Transition absence

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section does not apply to a member of the Reserves, other than a member of the Reserves on continuous full-time service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">Subject to subsection 3, a member who has a transition date is eligible for a cumulative total of 25 days of transition absence for any of the following activities.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Defence Force transition program activities.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Employment-related activities, career transition training or education courses that relate to one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member’s post-transition employment career path.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member’s post‑transition meaningful engagement.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">Transition-related administrative activities.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">All of the following apply to a transition absence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF must be satisfied that service requirements can be met while the member is absent.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">It can be taken as a full or a half day and must be within the cumulative total of 25 days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">If it is for a transition-related administrative activity under paragraph 2.c, it must not exceed the cumulative total of 5 days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member has been granted a period of transition absence and one of the following occurs, any unused portion of the approved period of absence will not be debited from the member’s transition absence credits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The activity finishes early.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The activity is cancelled.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 2.2.9 How to apply for transition assistance and transition absence

|  | A member must use the approved form to apply for any assistance under this Part. |
|---|---|

#### Part 3: Leaving the ADF

##### Division 1: Redundancy

###### 2.3.3 Purpose

|  | The purpose of this Division is to provide financial benefits for a member who given a notice under subsection 24(2) of the Defence Regulation because of redundancy. |
|---|---|

###### 2.3.4 Member this Division applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Division applies to a member who meets all of the following conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member’s service in the ADF is ending under paragraph 24(1)(b) of the Defence Regulation because of redundancy.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member has completed more than 2 years of continuous full-time service.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 2.3.5 Benefit

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">On the day the member ceases to be a member of the Permanent Forces as a result of redundancy, the member is entitled to any of the following amounts.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">A fortnight’s salary and allowances for each completed year of service that is recognised for long service leave under Chapter 5 Part 5.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">A pro rata payment for each part-year of such service completed.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">A fortnight’s salary and allowances for each completed year of continuous full-time service in the ADF that is not recognised for long service leave accrual.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">A pro rata payment for each completed part year of ADF service that is not recognised for long service leave accrual.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">Certain periods must be excluded from the calculations in subsection 1. These periods are those included by the Commonwealth or any employer in the calculation of a payment of a special benefit, redundancy payment, or management initiated early retirement benefit, however described.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">The amount payable under subsection 1 must not be more than 48 weeks’ salary and allowances.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">If the member's retirement age is less than 48 weeks from the day the service of the member is to end, the amount payable is for the period up to the member's retirement age.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="3">For the purpose of this section, <b>allowances</b> means any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Higher duties allowance when the period of higher duties was for 12 continuous months or more on the day the notice of redundancy was received.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Any of the following under DFRT Determination No. 6 of 2024.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>A Special Forces Disability Allowance under Part B Division 2 Subdivision 5.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>

##### Division 3: Special benefit payment

###### 2.3.20 Purpose

| 1. | The purpose of this Division is to provide the payment of a special benefit to certain members of the Permanent Forces who are compulsorily transferred to the Reserves under section 16 of the Defence Regulation. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The payment is not a performance management tool. |

##### Division 4: Extension of medical support on ceasing continuous full-time service

###### 2.3.26 Purpose

|  | This Division enables a member to be reimbursed the costs of medical, psychological and dental services incurred up to 4 months after they stopped being a member performing continuous full-time service if there are exceptional circumstances. |
|---|---|

###### 2.3.27 Definitions

|  | In this Division, the following apply. |
|---|---|
|  | **Decision maker** means the Director General Military Personnel Branch. |
|  | **Member** includes a former member of the Permanent Forces. |

###### 2.3.28 Member this Division applies to

|  | This Division applies to a member who has ceased continuous full-time service. |
|---|---|

###### 2.3.29 Reimbursement of medical expenses

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is eligible for the reimbursement of the cost they incur for medical, psychological and dental services if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The medical, psychological and dental services were unable to be provided before the member ceased continuous full-time service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF or decision maker is satisfied that there are exceptional circumstances to provide the benefit after the member has ceased continuous full-time service having regard to the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The personal circumstances of the member and their family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The reason the member has ceased continuous full-time service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The member’s medical, psychological and dental requirements.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iv.</td>
<td>The degree to which any of the factors in subparagraphs i. to iii. are beyond the member’s control.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>v.</td>
<td>Whether the medical, psychological and dental services can be funded by another means.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>vi.</td>
<td>Any other relevant factors.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">Despite subsection 1, reimbursement of costs cannot be provided for medical, psychological and dental services received more than 4 months after the member ceased continuous full-time service.</td>
</tr>
</table>

#### Part 4: ADF careers referral scheme

###### 2.4.1 Simplified outline of this Part

This Part sets up an incentive scheme to encourage members to refer people to join the ADF. This scheme provides a $1,000 payment to an ADF member who refers a person to join the ADF who then completes 12 months of service as a member of the Permanent Forces.

</tr>

<td></td>
<td>a.</td>

</tr>

<tr>

</tr>

|---|---|

### Chapter 3: ADF salaries and bonuses

#### Part 2: Administration of salaries

##### Division 1: About salaries

###### 3.2.1 Simplified outline of this Part

This Part provides the principles for the administration of salary for members of the Permanent Forces and Reserves. This includes when the payment of salary commences and ends during the course of a members service (see Division 1), how salary will be paid (see Division 1) and how to work out the rate of salary that applies to a member at various points of their career (see Division 2).

Rules relating to when and how a member will receive additional increments to their salary are provided for at Division 3. There are specific rules about additional salary increments, promotion and competency requirements for specified specialist officers, such as chaplains, aviation members, nuclear qualified submariners and cyber warfare members, (see Divisions 4, 4A, 4B, 4C).

Division 5 sets out when and how a member’s salary can be preserved for a period where it otherwise would have been reduced. The members to who a salary non-reduction period apply are identified in the annexes to the Division. The Division does not apply to members in particular circumstances, such as when a member’s performance of duty is not satisfactory (see section 3.2.51).

This Part should be read in conjunction with DFRT Determination No. 2 of 2017, *Salaries*, and other relevant determinations made by the DFRT under section 58H of the Act.

###### 3.2.5 Time for payment of salary for a member on continuous full‑time service

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Subject to section A.1.4 of DFRT Determination No. 2 of 2017, <i>Salaries</i>, the salary of a member starts on the day on which they begin continuous full-time service and ends at midnight on whichever of the following days is relevant to their situation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>For a member who ceases service — on the day on which the member ceases continuous full-time service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>For a member who is seconded for service with another Government department or civil employment — on the day before the member starts the secondment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>For a member who transfers to the Reserves — on the day immediately before the transfer.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 3.2.6 Method of payment of salary for a member on continuous full-time service

| 1. | Salary may be paid to members every 14 days (a fortnight). |
|---|---|
| 2. | Payment of salary and allowances to a member is made by electronic funds transfer into a financial institution advised by the member. |

<td>2.</td>

</tr>
</table>

###### 3.2.9 Death or presumed death of member

|  | If a member dies or is missing and presumed dead, the member may be taken to have ceased continuous full-time service. |
|---|---|

###### 3.2.13 Reserve member taken to be attending for duty

|  | A member of the Reserves who meets a circumstance in column A of the following table is taken to be on duty from the day in column B and taken to finish duty on the day in column C. |
|---|---|

| Item | Column A<br>Circumstance | Column B<br>Commencing | Column C<br>Concluding |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. | The member is directed to attend away from their service location. | The day the journey starts from where the member normally lives. | The day the member commences duty in the other location. |
| 2. | The member is returning to the place they normally live after attending for duty away from it. | The day the return journey starts to the place where the member normally lives. | The day the member arrives at the place they normally live. |
| 3. | The member is admitted to hospital while parading for approved duty. | The day that the member is admitted to hospital. | The earlier of the following days.<br>a. The day when they are discharged from hospital.<br>b. The first day that one of dates in item 4 occurs. |
| 4. | The member is on a period of medical absence due to illness or injury arising out of and immediately following a period of Reserve duty. | The day that the Commanding Officer approves as the first day of the medical absence. | The earliest of the following days.<br>a. The day that meets all of the following:<br>i. The period of medical absence authorised has passed.<br>ii. The member has been cleared for duty by a service medical officer.<br>b. The day the Department of Veterans' Affairs commences payment to the member.<br>c. The day the member starts civilian employment or receives sick leave payment from a civilian employer.<br>d. A day for which sick leave is payable by the member's employer.<br>e. The day the member receives unemployment or a similar benefit from Centrelink.<br>f. The day the member has recovered from their injury and parades with their unit.<br>g. The day the Department of Veterans' Affairs notifies the member that it has rejected the claim. |

<tr>

<td></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>

<table>

###### 3.2.17 Method of payment of salary and allowances for a member on Reserve service

| 1. | Salary may be paid to a member on Reserve service every 14 days (a fortnight). |
|---|---|
| 2. | A Commanding Officer may approve a salary payment outside of the fortnightly pay cycle, if the Reserve member can demonstrate exceptional circumstances or hardship. |
| 3. | Payment of salary and allowances to a member is made by electronic funds transfer into a financial institution advised by the member. |

##### Division 2: Commencement salary

###### 3.2.18 Purpose

|  | The Division describes how to work out the rate of salary that may apply to a member at various points in their career. |
|---|---|

###### 3.2.18A Member this Division does not apply to

|  | This Division does not apply to a member who is paid salary as an Officer Aviation member under Division 4A. |
|---|---|

###### 3.2.18B Definitions

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">In this Division the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Specialist level</b> means any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Competency level.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Dental level.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Military medical level.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Legal level.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 3.2.19 Salary on enlistment or appointment

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">The rate of salary on the day a member is enlisted or appointed is one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is a trainee, the rate specified in Schedule B.13 of DFRT Determination No. 2 of 2017, <i>Salaries.</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If paragraph a. does not apply to the member, the rate of salary is the higher of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The rate of salary set by the CDF.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> A member’s service commences on the day they are first required for duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member does not hold an entry level rank of Officer Cadet in the Army or Air Force.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 3.2.20 Salary on promotion – general

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The minimum rate for their new rank at the relevant pay grade.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The rate of salary set by the CDF.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Another rate if a non-reduction provision under Division 5 applies to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">For the purpose of paragraph 1.b, the CDF must believe that a higher rate of salary is reasonable having regard to the member's experience, qualifications and skills.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 3.2.21 Salary on change of pay grade or specialist level

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member's pay grade or specialist level changes.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The change is for a reason other than disciplinary action or an administrative sanction.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The change is not related to the member becoming eligible for salary in a different pay grade scale under another salary Schedule in DFRT Determination No. 2 of 2017, <i>Salaries</i>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s salary rate is the rate for the new pay grade or specialist level that corresponds to the rank increment the member held at their former pay grade or specialist level.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">Despite subsection 2, if salary non-reduction arrangements apply to the member under Division 5, then the member's rate of salary is the rate for the member's rank increment of their former pay grade or specialist level.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 3.2.22 Salary on ceasing to be a specialist officer

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member who ceases to perform duty as a specialist officer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is to be paid one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The salary rate for the new pay grade that corresponds to the rank increment the member held in their former specialist officer competency level.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A salary rate above the minimum increment that the CDF is satisfied is reasonable having regard to the member’s relevant experience, qualifications and skills.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 3.2.23 Member with previous service – commencement salary

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">In this section <b>relevant military service</b> means service that meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">It was service in, or with, any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>In the ADF, including ADF service with the United Nations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>In a force of a Commonwealth country.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>In a force of the United States of America.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">It is relevant to the kind of work the member enlisted or is appointed to do.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">It was performed at a rank equivalent to the rank the member enlisted or is appointed to, or at a higher rank.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section does not apply to members on promotion.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member may have previous relevant military service at the time they enlist or are appointed to a rank. The CDF may grant the member a commencement salary between the following two amounts.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The minimum rate.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The rate the member would have been paid if the member's service had been in the ADF.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">The CDF must consider all of the following factors.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member's previous relevant military service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">What incremental salary rate the length of the member's relevant military service would place them at in the salary scale.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">For a member being reappointed or re-enlisted – whether the qualifications, skills or training requirements for the rank have changed since the member last served.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">Other matters relevant to periods of service for salary advancement.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="3">This table sets out what the CDF considers in working out the period of relevant military service if there is a break in service between two periods of continuous full-time service.</td>
</tr>
</table>

| Item | If the break in service is… | then the CDF may disregard… |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | 5 years or less | any service before an earlier break in service. |
| 2. | more than 5 years | any service before the break. |

###### 3.2.24 Recognition of service in the Reserves

| 1. | The CDF may approve a salary above the minimum rate in the salary scale for the member's rank, for a member who served in the Reserves before they enlisted or were appointed to the Permanent Forces. This also applies to any other service that is not continuous full-time service. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The CDF must consider the nature and period of the previous service, having regard to any relevant matters set out in Division 3 or Division 4. |

</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">A Service Chief may approve an extended period of payment under subsection 2 for a member who has completed training. The Service Chief must specify the period of the extension.</td>

<table>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>

<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">For members undergoing a course of officer training and paid in accordance with item 6 of Part 1 of Schedule B.13 of DFRT Determination No. 2 of 2017, <i>Salaries</i>, the date of increase to the next year's rate is the date that corresponds to the member's month of entry to the course, set out in paragraph a or b.</td>

<td>For the January entry — the date of commencement of the second term.</td>

##### Division 3: Increments

###### 3.2.27 Purpose

|  | This Division describes advancement through a rank, based on the passing of time. |
|---|---|

###### 3.2.28 Definitions

|  | In this Division the following apply. |
|---|---|
|  | **Increment anniversary date** means the day that is 12 months after the member's most recent appointment, enlistment, promotion or last increment advancement date. |

###### 3.2.29 Member this Division does not apply to

|  | This Division does not apply to a member whom Division 4, Division 4A, Division 4B or Division 4C applies. |
|---|---|

###### 3.2.30 Increment advancement

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is to be given an additional increment of salary if all of the following conditions are met.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member's rate of salary is below the top increment for the member's rank.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member meets all of the following.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is not a senior officer paid salary under Schedule B.1 of DFRT Determination 2 of 2017, <i>Salaries</i>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member ordinarily carries out duties at the standard of competence for the member's rank, experience, pay grade and employment category, including any applicable classification.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> Senior officers paid salary under Schedule B.1 of DFRT Determination 2 of 2017, <i>Salaries</i>, do not need to meet subparagraph i.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="3">In the year since their most recent appointment, enlistment, last promotion, or last increment advancement date, the member has completed the following amount of service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td colspan="2">For a member of the Permanent Forces – 12 months of continuous full-time service.<br><b>Note:</b> This includes ADF service with the United Nations, regardless of whether they are paid by the ADF or the UN.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td colspan="2">For a member of the Reserves on Reserve service or continuous full-time service – 20 days or more of service in a 12-month period.<br><b>Note:</b> For the increment following 1 July 2015, special transitional rules apply for some members.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td colspan="2">For a member who served in both the Permanent Forces and Reserves in a 12‑month period – 20 days of service, made up of the sum of the service in both Forces.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="4">A member may not receive more than one increment advancement under this section in any 12‑month period, except as a result of their initial transition to the 2 July 2015 salary structure.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="4">This subsection applies to a member of the Reserves. The following table sets out how part days of duty count toward the amount of service needed to qualify for an increment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
</tr>
</table>

<table>
<tr>
<td>Item</td>
<td>If a member</td>
<td>then</td>
</tr>
<tr>

###### 3.2.33 Increment deferral

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member does not meet the conditions for incremental advancement under paragraph 3.2.30.1.b, the member's Commanding Officer may defer the payment of an increment for up to 12 months.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The decision to defer an increment must meet all the following conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>It must be in writing.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The period of the deferral must be specified.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>A copy must be provided to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The decision to defer an increment must be reviewed within 4 months of the date of deferral. If the member is assessed having carried out their duties and responsibilities at the standard expected during that 4 months, the increment will be granted at the end of that review period.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 3.2.34 Effect of pay increases on increments

|  | A salary increase that is not a salary increment under subsection 3.2.30.1 does not affect the date for the next increment. |
|---|---|

###### 3.2.35 Effect of pay grade changes on increments

|  | A member keeps the increment level for their rank when their pay grade changes. |
|---|---|
|  | **Note:** Section 3.2.38 provides the effect a reduction in rank for disciplinary reasons, or an administrative sanction, has on a member’s salary. |

###### 3.2.36 Promotion after previous service at temporary or acting rank

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The purpose of this section is to set out how earlier service in a higher rank can affect a member's increment when they are promoted to a new substantive rank.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member is promoted while in service. It is not to be confused with provisions dealing with salary on appointment or enlistment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member has previously served at their new substantive rank, or a higher one.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">Periods of service must add up to full years of service to be counted towards an increment under this section. Periods of service that add up to part-years (that is, less than 1 year of service) do not count for salary increments in the higher rank.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">Periods of earlier service that meet any of the following can count towards increments.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A period of service at temporary or acting rank that is continuous with service in the member's new substantive rank. The whole period of continuous service counts towards the date of the member's next increment. There must be no break at all between the two periods of service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Periods of service at temporary or acting rank that are not continuous with service in the member's new substantive rank. This service must be within an overall period of double the number of years needed to qualify for the particular salary increment in that rank. Periods of service can be added together, provided they are within that overall period.<br><b>Note:</b> This is sometimes known as the 'one in two' rule, that is, one year in the last two years, two years in the last four, three years in the last six, etc.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 3.2.37 Salary – Private Proficient

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies to an Army member who holds the rank of Private and meets all the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They have completed their initial employment category training.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are proficient in their military trade or skill.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member is eligible to be paid as Private Proficient if they meet one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are a member of the Permanent Forces and they have completed at least 12 months of service since finishing their initial employment category training.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are a member of the Reserves and all the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>At least 12 months have passed since they finished initial employment category training.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They have provided 20 days of service in a year after completing their initial employment category training.<br><b>Note:</b> Service includes Reserve service and continuous full-time service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">For the purpose of subsection 2, only days for which the member is eligible for salary are counted.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 3.2.38 Salary on reduction of rank

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">If a member’s rank is reduced, they are entitled to salary at a rate approved by CDF in the salary scale of the lower rank. CDF must consider all the following factors in setting the member's new salary rate.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Their previous service at the lower rank.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Relevant service in the higher rank.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The circumstances of the reduction in rank.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 3.2.39 Salary on promotion to rank previously held

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The purpose of this section is to set out how earlier service in a previously held rank can affect a member's rate of salary on promotion.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member must meet all the following conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They have been reduced in rank.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are later promoted to the rank that they held substantively before the reduction in rank.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The actions in paragraphs a and b occur within a single period of service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may approve earlier periods of the member's service in the higher rank to be counted towards the member's increment in the higher rank if the reduction in rank was not due to inefficiency.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 4: Specialist Officer – increment and competency arrangements

###### 3.2.40 Purpose

<table>
<tr>

<td colspan="2">This Division sets out provisions for advancement through ranks and competency arrangements for the following specialist officers.</td>
</tr>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>

<td></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>

</tr>

</tr>
</table>

###### 3.2.41 Chaplain, Maritime Spiritual Wellbeing Officers and dental officers – increment advancement, promotion and advancement

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A Chaplain or Maritime Spiritual Wellbeing Officer is eligible for incremental advancement in the specialist officer salary structure 12 months after the later of the following dates.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The day the member is posted to a position requiring a higher competency level than the member previously held.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The day the member advances to a higher division or class.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The day of the member's last increment advancement.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">A dental officer is eligible for incremental advancement in the specialist officer salary structure 12 months after the later of the following dates.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The day the member is assessed as holding a higher dental level than the member previously held.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The day the member is promoted to a higher rank.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The day of the member's last increment advancement.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">A dental officer in the specialist officer salary structure is eligible for increment advancement 12 months after the day they become eligible for payment under that structure.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">On advancement to a higher division or class a Chaplain or Maritime Spiritual Wellbeing Officer is paid the lowest increment for the competency level for their new division or class.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4A.</td>
<td colspan="2">On promotion a dental officer is paid the lowest increment for the dental level for their new rank.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4B.</td>
<td colspan="2">Despite subsections 4 and 4A, a member will be paid a higher increment of salary set by the CDF if the CDF believes it is reasonable, based on the member's relevant experience, qualifications and skills.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">On advancement to a higher competency or dental level under section 3.2.44 or 3.2.45, the member's increment level is the lowest increment for that competency or dental level.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 3.2.42 Medical officers – increment advancement and promotion

<table>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">A medical officer is eligible for an increment advancement in the specialist officer salary structure (up to the maximum increment level in the relevant Part of Schedule B.8 in DFRT Determination No. 2 of 2017 that applies to the medical officer) on their increment anniversary.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3A.</td>
<td colspan="3">For the purpose of this section, increment anniversary means the day 12 months after the later of the following days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The day that the member begins to be paid salary under one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Schedule B.8, Specialist officer salary rates – medical officer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Schedule B.15, Senior officer specialist salary rates – medical officer</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The day the member last advanced to a higher military medical level.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The day of the member's last increment advancement.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> The placement of a member from a medical level to a military medical level is not an increment advancement.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="3">On promotion from rank to rank, a medical officer retains the same military medical level (MML1, 2A, 2B, 3, 3A or 4) and the same increment level they held before promotion.<br><b>Note:</b> The member's increment advancement date will remain unchanged.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6.</td>
<td colspan="3">If a member advances to a higher military medical level under section 3.2.47, the member's increment is the lowest increment for that military medical level.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6A.</td>
<td colspan="3">Despite subsection 6, if one of the following applies, the member’s increment level is the increment that has the next higher salary than their salary immediately before they advanced.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member advances to MML3A.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member advances from MML3A to MML4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>8.</td>
<td colspan="3">For medical officer who becomes eligible to be paid under Schedule B.8 Part 2 or 4 of DFRT Determination No. 2 of 2017, <i>Salaries</i>, the medical officer's initial increment level is the higher of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The entry level increment for their Force and rank.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">An increment level approved by Surgeon General Australian Defence Force above the entry level increment for the medical officer because of their qualifications, clinical experience, and currency of skills.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 3.2.42A Salary on promotion – senior medical officers

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">If a member is promoted to one of the following ranks, the member’s rate of salary is the rate payable under Schedule B.15 of DFRT Determination No. 2 of 2017, <i>Salaries</i> for the lowest increment for their new rank.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Brigadier.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Major General.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 3.2.43 Legal Officers – increment advancement and promotion

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A legal officer in the specialist career structure becomes eligible for an increment level advancement (up to the maximum increment level for their legal level) on the later of the following dates.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The day that is 12 months after the legal officer entered the specialist career structure.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The day that is 12 months after the legal officer advanced to a higher legal level.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The day that is 12 months after the legal officer was promoted to a higher rank.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The day that is 12 months after the legal officer's last increment level advancement date.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">A legal officer who is promoted retains the competency element of their legal level.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2A.</td>
<td colspan="2">A legal officer who is promoted is to be paid one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The rate of the lowest increment for their legal level at the new rank.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The rate of an increment level above the minimum for their legal level that the CDF is satisfied is reasonable having regard to the member’s relevant experience, qualifications and skills.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">On advancement to a higher legal level under paragraph 1.b, the legal officer's increment level is the bottom increment for that legal level.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 3.2.44 Competency levels – Chaplain and Maritime Spiritual Wellbeing Officer

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A Chaplain or Maritime Spiritual Wellbeing Officer is placed in a competency level by the CDF based on the member's relevant experience, qualifications and skills.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">A Chaplain or Maritime Spiritual Wellbeing Officer may be placed in or advanced to a higher competency level if the CDF is satisfied that the officer meets the requirements for that competency level.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">A Chaplain or Maritime Spiritual Wellbeing Officer may advance to competency level 3 if the CDF is satisfied that the officer meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The officer meets the requirements for competency level 3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The officer is posted to a position that requires competency level 3.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 3.2.45 Dental levels – dental officer

| 1. | A dental officer is placed in a higher dental level if the CDF is satisfied it is reasonable after considering the member’s relevant experience, qualifications and skills. |
|---|---|
| 2. | A dental officer may only advance to a higher dental level if the CDF is satisfied that the officer meets the requirements for that dental level. |

###### 3.2.46 Legal levels – legal officer

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may approve the qualification, skill and experience requirements for a legal level for legal officers.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may designate a position as requiring a specific legal level.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">A legal officer holding legal level 1 or 2 may only advance to a higher legal level if the CDF is satisfied that the legal officer meets the professional requirements for the legal level.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">A legal officer holding legal level 3 or 4 may only advance to a higher legal level if the officer meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The CDF is satisfied that the legal officer meets the professional requirements for the legal level.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The Chief of the member's Service is satisfied that the legal officer is posted to a position that requires that legal level.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 3.2.47 Military medical levels – medical officer

| 1. | A medical officer is placed in a higher military medical level by the CDF based on the member’s relevant experience, qualifications and skills. |
|---|---|
| 2. | A medical officer advances to a higher military medical level if the CDF is satisfied that the officer meets the requirements for that military medical level. |

<table>
<tr>

The member is placed in the relevant pathway and competency stream.</td>

<td></td>

###### 3.2.47F Entry placement – Other Rank member transfers to the Officer Aviation Pay Structure

|---|---|
| 2. | The member retains the rate of salary payable immediately before the transfer until the salary payable for the member's Officer Aviation increment for their rank, pathway and competency stream is equal to or greater than the retained rate of salary. |

<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>

###### 3.2.47L Entry placement – Officer transferring from other salary structures

<table>
<tr>

<tr>
<td>3.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td>3A.</td>
<td colspan="2">An officer in the Navy is placed in the Command Pathway, Remote Pilot Warfare Officer competency stream at Officer Aviation increment OA6 on the day the member has completed remote pilot warfare officer training.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">An officer of the Army who holds the rank of Lieutenant is placed in the Generalist Pathway, Rotary Wing Pilot competency stream at the relevant of the following Officer Aviation increments on the day that the member completes the Regimental Officers Basic Course – Program (aviation).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the member has less than 12 months experience as a Lieutenant — the member's Officer Aviation increment is OA1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the member has 12 months or more experience as a Lieutenant — the member's Officer Aviation increment of OA1 is increased by one for each 12 months completed as Lieutenant, up to a maximum increment of OA4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">An officer of the Army who holds the rank of Captain or above is placed in the Generalist Pathway, Rotary Wing Pilot competency stream at the relevant of the following Officer Aviation increments on the day that the member completes the Regimental Officers Basic Course – Program (aviation).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the member has less than 12 months experience as an aviation officer — the member's Officer Aviation increment is the minimum increment for their rank.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the member has 12 months or more experience as an aviation officer — the member's Officer Aviation increment is the minimum increment for their rank that is increased by one increment as set out in Annex B.3.D of DFRT Determination No. 2 of 2017, <i>Salaries,</i> for each 12 months completed as an aviation officer, up to the maximum increment for their rank but not including the command increment levels.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6.</td>
<td colspan="2">An officer of the Air Force who transfers from an employment category is not specified in section 3.2.47K or from the air traffic control employment category is placed in the Command Pathway, the relevant competency stream for their qualifications and the minimum Officer Aviation increment for their rank on the day they are awarded a Category D qualification or Air Traffic Controller primary endorsement.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>7.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subsection 8 applies to an officer who meets all of the following on the day immediately before their transfer into Officer Aviation Pay Structure.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Their rate of salary was administered by section B.2.5 table item 1.c, 2.a.ii or 2.b.ii of DFRT Determination No. 2 of 2017, <i>Salaries.</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td>8.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member retains the rate of salary payable immediately before the transfer until the salary payable for the member's Officer Aviation increment for their rank, pathway and competency stream is equal to or greater than the retained rate of salary.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 3.2.47M Entry placement – CDF discretions

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section does not apply to an Officer Cadet.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">When a member enters the Officer Aviation Pay Structure the CDF may decide to place the member on an Officer Aviation increment that is between the minimum and maximum Officer Aviation increment for the member’s rank, pathway and competency stream.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF must consider the following when making a decision under subsection 2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member’s experience, qualifications and skills.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member’s previous relevant military service<i>.</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The Officer Aviation increment the member would otherwise have been placed on in the Officer Aviation Pay Structure.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>If an officer is reappointed — whether the qualifications, skills or training requirements for the rank have changed since the member last served.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>If a member was reduced in rank — the reason for the reduction in rank.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td>If a member was reduced in rank and is later promoted to the rank they held previously before the reduction in rank — the periods of the member's service at the higher rank.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>g.</td>
<td>Any other matters relevant to the periods of service for increment advancement.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 3.2.47O Increment on promotion

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section does not apply to the following members.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member in the Navy who is promoted to Acting Sub Lieutenant, Sub Lieutenant or Lieutenant.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member in the Army who is promoted to Second Lieutenant or Lieutenant.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member in the Air Force who is promoted to Pilot Officer or Flying Officer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">On the day that an Officer Aviation member is promoted, the member has the lowest Officer Aviation increment for their rank, pathway and competency stream.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">Despite subsection 2, the member may be placed on a higher Officer Aviation increment for their rank, pathway and competency stream that is decided by the CDF when the member has a period of service that meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The service was performed by the member at the rank the member is promoted to, or a higher rank.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The service was performed by the member at the standard of competence expected for the member's pathway and competency stream for the rank the member is promoted to, or a higher rank.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The service was performed by the member was for one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>For a member in the Navy or Air Force — the service is performed for a cumulative period of at least 12 months and the CDF is satisfied it is relevant to the member's ability to contribute to capability at the rank to which the member is promoted.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>For a member of the Army— the service was performed at the rank the member is promoted to or at a higher rank for a continuous period of at least 12 months.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">On the day that a member in the Army Specialist Pathway is promoted, the relevant of the following applies.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is promoted to a rank below Colonel and their increment before the promotion is below the lowest increment for their promoted rank — the member has the minimum Officer Aviation increment for their promoted rank.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is promoted to a rank below Colonel and their increment before the promotion is equal to or above the lowest increment for their promoted rank — the member has an Officer Aviation increment that is one above the increment they held before their promotion.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is promoted to Colonel — the member is transferred to the Generalist pathway and placed on Officer Aviation increment OA35.</td>
</tr>
</table>

<tr>

<td colspan="3">On the day that a Navy or Army Officer Aviation member loses their Command appointment for one of the following reasons, the CDF may decide the member's Officer Aviation increment within the increment range for the member's rank, pathway and competency stream, excluding the command increment levels.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member was imposed with a censure or formal warning.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member was convicted of any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>An offence under the <i>Defence Force Discipline Act 1982.</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>A civilian criminal offence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member was suspended from duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The CDF must take the following into consideration when making a decision under subsection 1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s previous service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The circumstances of the loss of the command appointment.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 3.2.47S Increment advancement

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">For the purposes of subsections 3 and 4, the advancement period is any of the following periods of service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">For a member in the Permanent Forces — 12 months of service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">For a member in the Reserves (providing Reserve service and continuous full-time service) — 20 or more days of Reserve service in a 12 month period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">For a member who served in both the Permanent Forces and the Reserves — 20 days of service in a 12 month period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note 1:</b> The advancement period commences on the later of one of the dates set out in paragraph 4.b.<br><b>Note 2:</b> A day of Reserve service is calculated based on the proportion of the daily rate the member is paid for the duty under section A.1.5 of DFRT Determination No. 2 of 2017, <i>Salaries</i>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">For the purpose of calculating the advancement period under subsection 1, the advancement period is extended by any period when the member is on leave without pay or is absent without leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member whose Officer Aviation increment is below the top increment for the member's rank, pathway and competency stream will advance to the next Officer Aviation increment within the member’s rank, pathway and competency stream at the end of the advancement period when one of the following is met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>

<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The day of the member's appointment as an officer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The day of the member's most recent promotion.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The day of the member's last increment advancement in the Officer Aviation Pay Structure.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is in the Navy at the rank of Sub Lieutenant or Lieutenant and all of the following have been met.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Commencing on the day they completed operational flying training on a military aircraft, they have performed their duties for 12 months at the standard of competence for their rank, pathway and competency stream.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>ba.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member completed remote pilot warfare officer training.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member has completed 4 ½ years of service since either graduating from the Australian Defence Force Academy or, if the member is a direct entry officer, completing officer training.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is in the Navy Command pathway or the Army Generalist pathway with a command appointment and has performed their duties at the standard of competence for their rank, pathway and competency stream for 12 months commencing from the date of the member's command appointment.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>

<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The day they entered the Officer Aviation Pay Structure.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The day of their last increment advancement in the Officer Aviation Pay Structure.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> Subsections B.3.8.5 and B.3.8.6 of DFRT Determination No. 2 of 2017, <i>Salaries,</i> limit the increment range for the following members and must be read in conjunction with these provisions.<br>a. A member in the Navy in the Command Pathway.<br>b. A member in the Army in the Generalist Pathway.</td>
</tr>
