| 2. | Private | Private Proficient |
| 3. | Aircraftman | Leading Aircraftman |
| 4. | Acting Sub Lieutenant | Sub Lieutenant |
| 6. | Second Lieutenant | Lieutenant |
| 7. | Pilot Officer | Flying Officer |

##### Division 2: Eligibility

###### 4.1.5 Eligibility for higher duties allowance

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">Subject to subsection 2, a member is eligible for higher duties allowance if the approver is satisfied of all the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is capable of performing the required duties attributed to the higher rank.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The duties being performed are duties that would ordinarily be performed by a person holding a higher rank than the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is not on leave, a medical absence, or short absence on the day the payment of higher duties allowance would commence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">There is a capability reason to pay higher duties other than the position or role being temporarily unfilled.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is in the Reserves, that they are performing the majority of their work in the higher duties role.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">An approver must not approve higher duties allowance for any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">A period where a member has been directed to perform higher duties for less than 5 consecutive days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">A period that exceeds one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>If the member has been posted to the position in which the higher duties is being performed — the duration of the member’s posting to that position.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>If subparagraph i does not apply — 12 months.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">For the purpose of subsection 2.a, consecutive days are not broken by any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">A day a member of the Reserves or Permanent Forces is not required to attend for duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member is on a flexible service determination, a nonworking period that is 14 days or less.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.1.6 Rate of higher duties allowance

| 1. | The rate of higher duties allowance that applies to the member is the rate set out in Division 3. |
|---|---|
| 2. | If a member is eligible for more than one rate of higher duties allowance on a day, the member is to be paid the higher rate for that day. |

###### 4.1.7 End of higher duties allowance

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">A member ceases to be eligible for higher duties allowance on the earlier of the following days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The day the approval to be paid higher duties allowance ends.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The day on which the member is directed to cease performing the higher duties.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is posted to a position for which they have been approved higher duties allowance, the day they cease to be posted to that position.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">The day the member commences unpaid leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td colspan="2">The day that is 2 months after the commencement of any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member commences paid leave that continues for more than 2 months.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member commences another duty that causes them to be unable to fulfil the primary duties that they have been directed to do for which higher duties allowance is payable.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td colspan="2">The day the member is promoted.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 3: Rate of higher duties allowance

###### 4.1.8 Higher duties position within member’s pay schedule

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are not eligible for a rate of higher duties allowance set under another section in this Division.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are directed to perform duties of a position that is normally performed by a member at a higher rank that attracts a salary from within the same schedule that applies to the member under DFRT Determination 2 of 2017.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The rate of higher duties allowance is the difference between the following rates of salary.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The salary payable to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The lowest rate of salary payable to a member holding one rank higher than the member in the same pay grade.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.1.9 Higher duties position outside member’s pay schedule

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are not eligible for a rate of higher duties allowance set under another section in this Division.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are directed to perform duties of a position that is normally performed by a member at a higher rank that attracts a salary from outside the pay schedule that applies to the member under DFRT Determination 2 of 2017.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The rate of higher duties allowance is 5% of the salary payable to the member.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.1.10 Higher duties within the Officer Aviation Pay Structure

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies to an officer aviation member who is directed to perform higher duties.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> Section 4.1.4 provides that all of the following are not eligible for higher duties allowance.<br>a. Aviation specialists.<br>b. Air Force officer aviation members in the specialist pathway or Stream.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The rate of higher duties allowance is one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member’s salary, inclusive of any non-reduction arrangement, is less than the lowest rate of salary payable under DFRT Determination 2 of 2017 to a member holding one rank higher than a member in the same pathway or competency stream — the difference between the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The current salary payable to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The lowest rate of salary payable under DFRT Determination 2 of 2017 for the member’s competency stream within one of the pathways that would apply if the member were to be promoted to one rank above their current rank.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member’s salary, inclusive of any non-reduction arrangement, is more than the lowest rate of salary payable under DFRT Determination 2 of 2017 to a member holding one rank higher than a member in the same pathway or competency stream — 5% of the current salary payable to the member.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.1.11 Higher duties within the specialist career structure

<td></td>

<tr>

</tr>

<td></td>

<td colspan="2">The duties of a position that is normally performed by a higher rank in a position in a foreign military force.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The rate of higher duties allowance for a member performing the duties of an SES Band 1, 2 or 3 position is the difference between the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The salary payable to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">One of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>If the member is performing the duties of an SES Band 1 position — the lowest rate of salary payable to a member holding the rank of Brigadier.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>If the member is performing the duties of an SES Band 2 position — the lowest rate of salary payable to a member holding the rank of Major General.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>If the member is performing the duties of an SES Band 3 position — the base salary component of pay point 1 in Schedule B.1 Part 3 of DFRT Determination No. 2 of 2017.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">The rate of higher duties allowance for a member performing the duties of an APS position or an ASD position not described in subsection 2 or a position in a military force is the difference between the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The salary payable to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The rate of salary that would apply to the member if they were one rank higher than their rank in the ADF.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">In this section, <b>SES</b> means Senior Executive Service.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.1.18 Higher duties for officers within the Cyber Warfare Pay Structure

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies to a cyber warfare officer who is directed to perform duties of a position that is normally performed by a member holding a higher rank.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The rate of higher duties allowance is one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member’s salary, inclusive of any non-reduction arrangement, is less than the lowest rate of salary payable under DFRT Determination No. 2 of 2017 to a member holding one rank higher than a member in the same pathway — the difference between the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The salary payable to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The lowest rate of salary payable under DFRT Determination No. 2 of 2017 to the member within their pathway that would apply if the member were to be promoted to one rank higher in their pathway.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">In any other circumstances — 5% of the salary payable to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> Subsection 2 applies regardless of whether the incumbent of the higher position is paid under a different schedule or pathway within DFRT Determination No. 2 of 2017.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.1.19 Higher duties for other ranks within the Cyber Warfare Pay Structure

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies to a cyber warfare specialist who is directed to perform duties of a position that is normally performed by a member holding a higher rank.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The rate of higher duties allowance is the greater of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The difference between the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The salary payable to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The rate of salary payable for the increment that applies under section 3.2.47AK if the member were to be promoted to one rank above their rank.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">5% of the salary payable to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">If subsection 2 does not apply to the member, the rate of higher duties allowance is 5% of the salary payable to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> Subsection 2 or 3 applies regardless of whether the incumbent of the higher position is paid under a different schedule or pathway within DFRT Determination No. 2 of 2017.</td>
</tr>
</table>

#### Part 3: Qualification and occupation based allowances

##### Division 1: First Nations’ language allowance

###### 4.3.1 Purpose

|  | This Division provides an allowance to Australian First Nations’ language speakers who utilise their language, interpreting skills, and application of traditional knowledge in support of named operations, Regional Force Surveillance Group on-country patrols or stakeholder negotiations on behalf of the ADF and multinational partners. |
|---|---|

###### 4.3.2 Definitions

|  | In this Division, the following apply. |
|---|---|
|  | **First Nations’ language skills** means the ability to gather and convey information to and from an Australian First Nations’ person in a First Nations’ language understood by the person in a culturally appropriate manner. |

###### 4.3.3 Member this Division applies to

|  | This Division applies to a member who has First Nations’ language skills. |
|---|---|

###### 4.3.4 Eligibility for allowance

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is eligible for First Nations’ language allowance if they meet all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member has completed an interpreter language assessment confirming the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member’s ability to interpret accurately in the target language.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member’s ability to maintain confidentiality of information received while interpreting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The member’s ability to be impartial in their interpretation of information.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF is satisfied that the member’s use of their First Nations’ language skills was essential to perform adequately any of the following to meet an operational need.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The duties of the position in which the member is employed.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The duties of a task.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">Operational needs do not include incidental, ceremonial or personal uses of First Nations’ language skills that are not undertaken as a part of an operation need.<br><b>Note:</b> Uses of First Nations’ language skills that will not meet operational needs alone are greetings and Welcomes to Country.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.3.5 Rate of allowance

|  | The rate of the First Nations’ language allowance is $1,410. |
|---|---|

###### 4.3.6 Payment of allowance

| 1. | The First Nations’ language allowance is payable as soon as practicable after the CDF signs the approved form. |
|---|---|
| 2. | First Nations’ language allowance cannot be paid more than once within a 12 month period. |
| 3. | For the purpose of subsection 2, the 12 month period starts on the day the member first uses their First Nations’ language skills to meet an operational need. |

###### 4.3.7 How to apply for First Nations’ language allowance

|  | A member must use the approved form to apply for a benefit under this Division. |
|---|---|

#### Part 4: Location allowances

##### Division 1: ADF district allowance – general and rates

###### 4.4.3 Purpose

|  | District allowance compensates for service in a location in Australia that involves hardship caused by remoteness, harsh climate and cost of living. |
|---|---|

###### 4.4.4 Definitions

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">In this Division the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Continuous period</b> means the period that the member stays in the remote location, including any period they leave the remote location while any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are not required for duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are on a nonworking period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Grade</b>, for a remote location, means the grade specified for it in Annex 4.4.A.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Harbour craft</b> means a vessel that is not liable, in the ordinary course of duty with the ADF, to be ordered to sea.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Remote location</b> means a location mentioned in Annex 4.4.A.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.4.5 Members who are eligible

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is eligible for ADF district allowance if they meet any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Their primary service location is a remote location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They serve on temporary duty at a remote location for a continuous period of more than 21 days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are posted for service in a seagoing ship based at a remote location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF recognises the member meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They are performing duty at a location that is not listed in Annex 4.4.A.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They serve at an isolated location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>Their duty is for a continuous period of more than 21 days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member on Reserve service is eligible for ADF district allowance if they meet all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They serve on temporary duty at a remote location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Their temporary duty is for a continuous period of more than 21 days.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.4.6 Members who are not eligible

|  | A member is not eligible for ADF district allowance for any period they are eligible for Antarctic allowance under Division 5. |
|---|---|

###### 4.4.7 Period of benefit

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">Subject to subsection 2, the member is eligible to receive ADF district allowance for one of the following periods.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member’s primary service location is a remote location ― the following period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Starting on the later of the day the member commences duty in the location or the day the member arrives in the location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Ending on the day before they leave the location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is serving on temporary duty at a remote location for a continuous period of more than 21 days ― the following period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Starting on the day the member begins the period of temporary duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Ending on the day before they leave the location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member on a flexible service determination is not eligible for the allowance for any continuous nonworking period of more than 28 days.<br><b>Note:</b> The period for which a member who is away from the remote location on temporary duty or is posted for service in a seagoing ship or submarine that is away from its remote location may be paid the allowance provided under section 4.4.11.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.4.8 Grading of locations

| 1. | Remote locations are graded A, B, C, D and E according to how difficult they are. Annex 4.4.A contains a list of currently approved locations and grades. |
|---|---|
| 2. | Members who are eligible under paragraph 4.4.5.1.d are paid at the grade of the remote location in Annex 4.4.A that the CDF decides is in the general area of the isolated location of duty. The CDF must have regard to the conditions expressed in section 4.4.3. |

##### Division 2: ADF district allowance – movement to or from remote location

###### 4.4.11 Absence for temporary duty

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies if a member on ADF district allowance is away from a remote location for any of the following reasons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are serving a period of temporary duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are serving in a harbour craft temporarily commissioned as a seagoing ship.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>They are serving in a seagoing ship or submarine.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>They have an approved alternate located work agreement and they are required to attend for duty in the location to which they are posted for duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The following table sets out the circumstances where a member may be eligible for district allowance under this section.</td>
</tr>
</table>

| Item | If the member | then they may be paid ADF district allowance for an absence from location that is for a period of |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | returns to the remote location immediately after the absence | 30 days or less. |
| 2. | meets all of the following:<br>a. They have accompanied resident family.<br>b. The accompanied resident family stays at the remote location for the duration of the member’s absence. | more than 30 days. |
| 3. | meets all of the following:<br>a. one of the following applies:<br>i. they have unaccompanied resident family<br>ii. they have no resident family living at the remote location<br>b. they perform temporary duty in another remote location | more than 30 days. |
| 4. | is posted to another location (away from the remote location) while on temporary duty | the period of temporary duty, up to the day the posting begins in the location that is not remote. |

|  | **Note:** The following sections may affect the payment of ADF district allowance under this section.<br>Section 4.4.12 if a member goes on a period of leave.<br>Section 4.4.13 if a member is absent from duty due to a reason set out in subsection 4.4.13.1.<br>Section 4.4.14 if a member’s primary service location changes from one remote location to another.<br>Section 4.4.15 if a member’s primary service location changes from a remote location to non-remote location. |
|---|---|

###### 4.4.12 Payment during a period of leave

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is on one of the following types of leave and the member, or at least one of their resident family, continues to live in the remote location.<br><b>Note:</b> The remote location must be the location that the member received the allowance for prior to taking the leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Long service leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Unpaid maternity leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>Unpaid parental leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is on one of the following types of leave and they are to return to duty at the remote location at the end of their leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Recreation leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Personal leave for a compassionate reason or carer’s leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>Medical absence from duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iv.</td>
<td>Paid maternity leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>v.</td>
<td>Premature birth leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>vi.</td>
<td>Paid parental leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member who is on a period of leave without pay is not eligible to receive ADF district allowance during their leave.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.4.13 Payment when not on duty

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member to whom any of the following apply during or immediately after the end of a period of duty at a remote location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They take a period of recreation leave, including any short absence for travelling.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are absent from duty for illness.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>They are hospitalised.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>They are unable to use the number of recreation leave credits they accrued in the remote location for Service reasons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is eligible for ADF district allowance for one of the following periods.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If paragraph 1.a applies — the period of recreation leave up to what the member accrued for service in the remote location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If paragraph 1.b or c applies — the period of absence or hospitalisation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>If paragraph 1.d applies — the period that is equal to the leave they accrued in the remote location but did not take while at the remote location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">If subparagraph 2.c applies, the member may be paid a lump sum.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.4.14 Primary service location changes from one remote location to another

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This subsection applies if a member’s primary service location changes from one remote location to another remote location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section does not apply to a member who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is approved an alternate located work agreement to a remote location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">One of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member's resident family join the member in the remote location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member's resident family already live in the remote location and the location is a location where benefits are not provided.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s primary service location changes, and their resident family remain in the remote location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member is eligible for ADF district allowance at the rate for the previous primary service location until the beginning of their period at the new primary service location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">Despite subsection 3, subsection 5 applies if a member meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Their primary service location changes from one remote location to another remote location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They have unaccompanied resident family because their resident family remain in the first remote location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member is eligible for ADF District allowance at the rate that is the greater of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The rate the member received at the remote location that was the member’s primary service location before they were posted.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The rate the member would receive at the remote location which is their new primary service location if they were a member who had accompanied resident family at that that location.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.4.15 Primary service location changes from a remote location to non-remote location

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies if a member meets all these conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s primary service location changes from a remote location to another location that is not a remote location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They have unaccompanied resident family because their resident family remain in the remote location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section does not apply to a member who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is approved an alternate located work agreement to a remote location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">One of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member's resident family join the member in the remote location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member's resident family already live in the remote location and the location is a location where benefits are not provided.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s primary service location changes, and their resident family remain in the remote location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member is eligible for ADF district allowance for the period their resident family stay at the remote location.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.4.16 Member serving a period of detentions

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member who has accompanied resident family and no unaccompanied resident family who is serving a period of detention under Service law.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is eligible for the allowance they would have been paid if they meet all these conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The allowance was payable to them immediately before they began to serve a period of detention.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>At that time, they were eligible for the allowance at the full rate under section 4.4.9 table item 2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Their resident family continue to live in the location that the allowance was payable for.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 3: Port Wakefield allowance

###### 4.4.17 Purpose

|  | Port Wakefield allowance compensates a member for the isolation, harsh climate and cost of living involved in serving at the Port Wakefield establishment. |
|---|---|

###### 4.4.19 Benefit

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subject to subsection 1A, a member is eligible for Port Wakefield allowance if the member is posted to the Proof and Experimental Establishment at Port Wakefield and must live there.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1A.</td>
<td colspan="2">Port Wakefield allowance is not payable during a nonworking period that exceeds 28 days under a member's flexible service determination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The rate of allowance is one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the member has at least one of their resident family living at the establishment — $3,420.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>In any other case — $1,710.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">Port Wakefield allowance is paid from the date the member takes up residence at the Proof and Experimental Establishment at Port Wakefield and ends when they leave it.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.4.20 Member not eligible

|  | A member serving at the Proof and Experimental Establishment at Port Wakefield on temporary duty is not eligible for the allowance. |
|---|---|

###### 4.4.21 Absence from the Proof and Experimental Establishment at Port Wakefield

|  | The conditions for absence from a remote location under Division 2 apply to a member's absence from the Proof and Experimental Establishment at Port Wakefield. |
|---|---|

##### Division 4: Scherger allowance

###### 4.4.22 Purpose

|  | Scherger allowance recognises hardship at RAAF Scherger caused by the generally poor state of the unsealed road to Weipa. |
|---|---|

###### 4.4.23 Member who is eligible

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for Scherger allowance if they meet all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are posted in a caretaker role to RAAF Scherger for at least 12 months.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are required for operational reasons to live on the base.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>They live on the base for the period of the posting.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.4.23A Member not eligible

|  | A member on a flexible service determination is not eligible for the allowance for any continuous nonworking period of more than 28 days. |
|---|---|

###### 4.4.24 Rate of allowance

|  | The rate of Scherger allowance is $7,425 a year. |
|---|---|

##### Division 5: Allowances for services in Antarctica

###### Subdivision 1: General provisions

###### 4.4.25 Definitions

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">In this Division the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>ADF amount</b> means the sum of the amounts of salary and maritime disability allowance that the member would be eligible for if the duty was for an ADF posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Antarctica</b> means the area south of the Antarctic Convergence, and includes Macquarie Island.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Antarctic Convergence</b> has the same meaning as in the Convention on the Conservation of Antarctic Marine Living Resources, as set out in the Schedule to the <i>Antarctic Marine Living Resources Conservation Act 1981.</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>APS amount</b> means the sum of the amounts of salary and allowance instead of overtime that the member would be eligible for in the APS position.<br><b>Note:</b> If the member is not an APS employee, this amount will always be zero.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Day of embarkation</b> means one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the ship sails from a port at or before 1200 — the day of embarkation is the day the ship sails.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the ship sails from a port after 1200 — the day of embarkation is the day after the ship sails.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Day of disembarkation</b> means one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the ship docks in a port at or before 1200 — the day of disembarkation is the day before the ship docks.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the ship docks in a port after 1200 — the day of disembarkation is the day the ship docks.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Expedition</b> means an Australian National Antarctic Research Expedition to Antarctica.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Port</b> means the port specified in the expedition itinerary as the port of embarkation or disembarkation of the expedition.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### Subdivision 2: Antarctic allowance

###### 4.4.29 Purpose

|  | Antarctic allowance compensates a member for the demands of service in Antarctica. |
|---|---|

###### 4.4.30 Eligibility for Antarctic allowance

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">A member is eligible for Antarctic allowance for the period of eligibility under section 4.4.32 if any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">All of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They are directed to undertake duties as an integral part of an expedition.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They are expected to remain on duty with, or to support, the expedition during the summer or winter season in Antarctica.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They travel to Antarctica with an expedition but are not part of the expedition.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> Under subsection A.1.6.2 of DFRT Determination No. 6 of 2025, Antarctic allowance may not be payable if the member is receiving a maritime crew B-F allowance that is not in connection with their posting and the rate of that allowance is higher than Antarctic Allowance.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.4.31 Rate of allowance

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">The rate of the allowance is one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If paragraph 4.4.30.a applies — $17,071.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If paragraph 4.4.30.b applies — $9,405.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.4.32 Period of eligibility

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subject to subsection 1A, a member is eligible for Antarctic allowance for the following period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>From 0001 hours on the day of embarkation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>To 2359 hours on the day of disembarkation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1A.</td>
<td colspan="2">Antarctic allowance is not payable during a nonworking period that exceeds 28 days under a member's flexible service determination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member does not return directly to Australia immediately after service in Antarctica, payment of the allowance ends at 2359 on one of the following days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the member takes recreation leave after duty in Antarctica — the last day they are eligible for Antarctic allowance under section 4.4.35.<br><b>Note:</b> Section 4.4.35 provides the period a member is eligible to continue to receive Antarctic allowance when they are granted a period of recreation leave after duty in Antarctica.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the member does not take recreation leave after duty in Antarctica — the last day they serve in Antarctica.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.4.34 Member on long service leave

|  | The allowance is not included in a member’s salary during a period of long service leave unless they remain in Antarctica during the period. |
|---|---|

###### 4.4.35 Recreation leave after duty in Antarctica

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies to a member who completes service in Antarctica and is granted a period of recreation leave before beginning duty in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member is eligible for Antarctic allowance for the number of days of recreation leave credits they accrued for service in Antarctica at the rate payable at the time the leave credits accrued under section 4.4.31.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">Subsection 1 applies to recreation leave granted immediately after any of the following periods.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">A period of hospitalisation or absence from duty for an illness that began on or before the day the member completed service in Antarctica.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">A period of duty that meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>It is performed by the member before recreation leave can be granted.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>It is performed immediately after the member's period of service in Antarctica.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section does not apply to Antarctic parity allowance under Subdivision 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> Short absence for travel provided under this Subdivision may be available under Chapter 5 Part 11 Division 6.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### Subdivision 3: Common duties allowance

###### 4.4.35A Purpose

|  | Common duties allowance provides for payment to a member who performs duties that are in addition to the duties they ordinarily perform in an expedition. |
|---|---|

###### 4.4.36 Eligibility

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for common duties allowance if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are eligible for Antarctic allowance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The officer-in-charge of an expedition directs them to perform duties that are additional and unrelated to their ordinary duties.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>They perform the duties for a period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The rate of common duties allowance is $9,405 a year.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### Subdivision 4: Antarctic parity allowance

###### 4.4.37 Purpose

|  | Antarctic parity allowance provides for payment to a member who volunteers for service in Antarctica in an APS position as a member of an expedition. |
|---|---|

###### 4.4.40 Eligibility for allowance

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for Antarctic parity allowance for the same period they are eligible for Antarctic allowance under section 4.4.32 if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are serving with an expedition in a voluntary capacity in an established APS position.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are not entitled to the full APS salary and allowances that apply to the position.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>They are not posted to a ship or establishment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>They are not on leave without pay.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Antarctic parity allowance is equal to the difference between the APS amount and the ADF amount payable in a pay period.</td>
</tr>
</table>

#### Part 5: Meal allowance

###### 4.5.2 Purpose

|  | Meal allowance assists a member to buy a meal if a Service-provided meal is not available. |
|---|---|

###### 4.5.2A Definitions

|  | In this Part the following apply. |
|---|---|
|  | **Meal period** for a member who occupies living-in accommodation means a period that the mess at the location of their living-in accommodation provides meals for them. |

###### 4.5.3 Member this Part applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Part applies to a member who meets one of the following, unless section 4.5.4 applies.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are serving in Australia. This includes a member on Reserve service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are an applicant for entry into the ADF and section 2.1.4 applies to them.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.5.4 Meal allowance not payable

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Meal allowance is not payable for a meal period when any of the following conditions are met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member is eligible for travelling allowance or use of the Defence travel card.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The Commonwealth makes a meal available to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Subject to subsection 2, a meal is included in the fare for a journey or is otherwise provided by the transport operator.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">An in-flight meal on a commercial aircraft does not count as a meal for purpose of this Part.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.5.6 Member who occupies living-in accommodation

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies to a member who occupies living-in accommodation and pays a contribution for meals under Chapter 7 Part 9 Division 1. The member must meet one of these conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are on duty away from their service location during a meal period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are performing duty at their service location during a meal period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">They perform extra duty before or after normal duty and one of these conditions is met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They get a meal break between the normal duty and the extra duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They do not get a meal break after the normal duty. The extra duty runs until after the next meal period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">Their service location is in a capital city. This applies for lunch only.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member is eligible for a meal allowance for the meal period. This is only if it is not reasonably practical for them to do one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Return to their normal mess during the meal period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Get a meal at Commonwealth expense during the meal period.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.5.7 Member who lives out

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies to a member who lives out and buys a meal during a meal period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member is eligible for a meal allowance for the meal period if they cannot go home for the meal for any of these reasons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They perform extra duty before or after normal duty and one of the following happens.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They get a meal break between the normal duty and the extra duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They do not get a meal break and the extra duty extends through the next meal period after the normal hours of duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are on duty at a place where the Commonwealth does not provide a meal and the duty meets one of these conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>It starts 3 or more hours before their rostered time for starting duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>It finishes 3 or more hours after their rostered time for finishing duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">All of these circumstances prevent the member going home for lunch.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They begin normal duty after a period of extra duty overnight.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They cannot go home before starting the normal duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>They finish the normal duty at or after 1400 hours.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.5.9 Rates of allowance

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">The rate of meal allowance for a meal period is one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the meal period is breakfast — $31.15.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the meal period is lunch and paragraph 4.5.6.1.d applies — $14.20.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>If the meal period is lunch and paragraph 4.5.6.1.d does not apply — $35.55.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>If the meal period is dinner — $61.30.</td>
</tr>
</table>

#### Part 6: Additional benefits for star rank officers

###### 4.6.1 Purpose

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">The purpose of this Part is threefold.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>To recognise and reward the professional contribution of star rank officers in meeting the greater internal and external demands involved in giving effect to the Government’s Defence policy.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>To provide employment conditions that reflect contemporary management practices.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>To retain highly skilled star rank officers.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.6.2 Member this Part applies to

| 1. | This Part applies to a member who holds a rank of Brigadier or higher. |
|---|---|
| 2. | Section 4.6.5 also applies to a member of the Reserves who holds a rank of Brigadier or higher. |

###### 4.6.5 Mobile telephones and hand held devices

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is eligible for a mobile telephone or other handheld device.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The Department of Defence will meet the cost of providing and operating the telephone or device, including limited personal use.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member of the Reserves is only eligible under this section when all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member has 100 days of expected liability to serve in the financial year.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member’s commanding officer or manager approves that the benefit be made available, having regard to the duties that the member is required to perform.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.6.7 Parking space or permit

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A parking space at or near their service location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A parking permit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member may be required to make a contribution towards the parking space or permit under Part 11.</td>
</tr>
</table>

#### Part 7: Victoria Cross for Australia representational duties

###### 4.7.1 Purpose

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Part has two purposes.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>To recognise and reward the contribution of Victoria Cross for Australia recipients.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>To provide a package of benefits for Victoria Cross for Australia recipients to allow them to perform the representational duties associated with the award.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.7.2 Persons this Part applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Part applies to any of the following persons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A member who has been awarded the Victoria Cross for Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A member who has been approved to perform chaperone duties for a Victoria Cross for Australia holder.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The family of a member posthumously awarded the Victoria Cross for Australia.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.7.3 Nominated family of member posthumously awarded

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Assistance may be provided to the family of a member posthumously awarded the Victoria Cross for Australia, to attend representational activities. All the following limits apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The CDF must decide that it is reasonable in the circumstances for family to represent the Victoria Cross recipient, having regard to the advice of the relevant Service Chief.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The Victoria Cross recipient's family may nominate a maximum of 2 family members to attend an activity.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Benefits may only be provided up to 5 years from the date of investiture of the Victoria Cross for Australia.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.7.4 Expenses related to representational duties

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">For the purposes of this section the term member also applies to a family member of a posthumously awarded Victoria Cross recipient, who has been nominated under section 4.7.3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The CDF may approve the payment or reimbursement of costs for the following expenses that are directly related to the member's representational duties.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The purchase of civilian clothing for the member or the member's resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The hire of civilian clothing for the member or the member's resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">Laundry and dry cleaning costs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">Babysitting costs for a child who is the member’s resident family, if any of the following are attending a representational activity.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member and their partner.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>If the member does not have a partner, the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2A.</td>
<td colspan="3">The CDF must only approve a payment or reimbursement under subsection 2 if satisfied that the costs and the frequency of the payment or reimbursement are reasonable for the member's representational duties.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">The CDF may approve any additional costs not listed in subsection 2 that relate directly to the member's representational duties.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">The CDF may approve reimbursement of the cost of clothing hire for the member performing chaperone duties who must attend representational events with the Victoria Cross for Australia recipient.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.7.5 Business class travel

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may approve travel for the member and their chaperone for travel to and from Victoria Cross for Australia representational activities.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may approve business class travel for the following people for travel to and from Victoria Cross for Australia representational activities.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member's partner.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member's resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The family of a member posthumously awarded the Victoria Cross for Australia, nominated under section 4.7.3.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.7.6 Travel allowance

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Travel costs or travel allowance rates, specified in Annex 9.5.A Part 1 column B and Part 4, are payable to the member and the following people for travel on Victoria Cross for Australia representational activities.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member's resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A member performing chaperone duties.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Up to 2 nominated family members of a member posthumously awarded the Victoria Cross for Australia.</td>
</tr>
</table>

#### Part 8: Training payments

##### Division 1A: Trainee’s dependant allowance

###### 4.8.3 Purpose

|  | Trainee's dependant allowance supplements a trainee's salary when they are supporting one or more eligible dependants. |
|---|---|

###### 4.8.5 Member this Division applies to

|  | This Division applies to a trainee in the Permanent Forces whose salary is less than the salary of a Private in Pay Grade 1. |
|---|---|

###### 4.8.6 When this Division does not apply

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This Division does not apply if any of the following criteria are met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If any of the trainee’s eligible dependants has an expected income of $52,398.36 or more in the current financial year.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The trainee is not entitled to salary.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is on Reserve service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">In this section, <b>eligible dependant</b> means one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The trainee’s resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">A person who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They are under 16 years of age.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They are living with the trainee.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>They are wholly or substantially dependant on the trainee.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.8.6A Applying for trainee’s dependant allowance and notification of change in expected income

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A member must use the approved form to do any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Apply for the trainee’s dependant allowance under this Division.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Notify of any change in an eligible dependant’s expected income.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.8.7 Rate of benefit

| 1. | The rate of trainee's dependant allowance is the difference between their rate of salary and the annual rate of salary for a Private in Pay Grade 1. |
|---|---|
| 2. | Trainee's dependant allowance is paid fortnightly based on the annual amount. |
| 3. | If the trainee is on a flexible service determination, the trainee is to be paid trainee's dependant allowance on a pro rata basis as calculated under section 3.2.7A. |

###### 4.8.8 Dual entitlement

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">If the trainee's partner is a member and is also eligible for the trainee's dependant allowance, the rate for each member is one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the trainee and their partner have the same rate of salary — half the difference between their individual rate and the salary of a Private in Pay Grade 1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the trainee and their partner have different rates of salary — half the difference between the lower individual rate and the salary of a Private in Pay Grade 1.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 2: Medical residency – additional salary

###### 4.8.9 Purpose

| 1. | This Division supplements the salary for a member who works as a resident medical officer at a civilian hospital. |
|---|---|
| 2. | A member is paid additional salary to equal the salary and allowances they would have received if they had been a civilian resident medical officer at the hospital. |

###### 4.8.10 Members this Division applies to

|  | This Division applies to a member who undertakes a period of compulsory residency at a civilian hospital with the approval of the CDF. |
|---|---|

###### 4.8.11 Rate of additional payment

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for an additional payment at the end of each 3-month period calculated using the following formula.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">[image: Start formula additional payment equals start fraction A minus open bracket B plus C close bracket over 4 end fraction end formula]</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>A</b></td>
<td>The annual salary the member would have received if they were paid by the hospital.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>B</b></td>
<td>The member’s annual salary.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>C</b></td>
<td>The annual rate of district allowance payable to the member, if applicable.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.8.12 Payment for accrued leave

|  | The member is eligible for payment for any leave accrued but not granted during their period of compulsory residency, less any payment instead of leave made by the hospital. |
|---|---|

###### 4.8.13 Conditions of entitlement

| 1. | The sponsored member works full-time at the hospital providing the training. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The member remains in ADF service. They work under an arrangement agreed between the hospital and the Commonwealth. The member will not become an employee of the hospital. |
| 3. | The member retains all the conditions of service of full-time members. |

##### Division 3: Former medical or dental officer – refresher training

###### 4.8.14 Purpose

|  | Refresher training assistance assists a former member who served as a medical or dental officer with the costs of training to better equip them for civilian practice or employment. |
|---|---|

###### 4.8.15 Definition

|  | In this Division, the following apply. |
|---|---|
|  | **Refresher training course** means an approved course of study to be undertaken by a former member in aspects of medical or dental practice that are not normally found in the ADF. |

###### 4.8.16 Members this Division applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Division applies to a former member who served on a fixed-term appointment as a medical or dental officer, if they meet all of these criteria.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They were appointed before graduation or within 2 years after first registration as a medical or dental practitioner.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They completed at least 4 years’ continuous full-time service as a medical or dental officer before ceasing to be a member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>They begin a refresher training course within 12 months of ceasing service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>They have not, on the day they begin the training course, been appointed as an officer on an indefinite appointment.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.8.17 Conditions for refresher training payment

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The former member is eligible for a payment for the refresher training course if the CDF considers it reasonable for them to undertake it.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">For the purpose of subsection 1, the CDF must consider the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>How much the length and nature of the former member’s service has impaired their ability to undertake civilian medical or dental practice or employment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>How much the former member’s completion of the refresher training course would remedy any impairment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Any other factor relevant to the former member’s ability to undertake such practice or employment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">Payment is available for the period of a refresher training course to a maximum of 90 days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">Only one payment can be made to a member under this Division.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.8.18 Amount of payment

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">The former member is eligible for a daily payment calculated using the following formula.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">[image: Start formula payment equals start fraction A minus B over C end fraction end formula]</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>A</b></td>
<td>is the rate of salary the former member would have received, including any higher duties allowance, on the day the refresher training course begins at the rank they held on the day before they left the ADF.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>B</b></td>
<td>is the salary, excluding overtime or penalty rates, a civilian employer would pay them on the day the refresher training course begins.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>C</b></td>
<td>is the period of the refresher training course up to a maximum of 90 days.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 4: Australian Defence Force Academy learning materials

###### 4.8.19 Purpose

|  | This Division provides members who are trainees and undertaking undergraduate studies at the Australian Defence Force Academy with a benefit to cover the costs of certain learning materials required for their studies. |
|---|---|

###### 4.8.20 Member this Part applies to

|  | This Part applies to a trainee who is an undergraduate posted to the Australian Defence Force Academy. |
|---|---|

###### 4.8.21 Learning materials

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible to be reimbursed the costs of compulsory learning material purchased by the member if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The compulsory learning materials have not been provided to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The compulsory learning materials have been approved by the Commandant Australian Defence Force Academy.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 5: In-service medical officers – refresher training

###### 4.8.22 Purpose

|  | In-service training assistance is provided to serving medical officers to allow them to undertake refresher training or experience, except where the training is a Service requirement. |
|---|---|

###### 4.8.23 Members this Division applies to

|  | This Division applies to a medical officer serving on an indefinite appointment. |
|---|---|

###### 4.8.24 Conditions of training

| 1. | The CDF may approve the member to undertake refresher training for a maximum of 12 months on full salary after each completed 6 years of service. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The CDF may approve the member to do the training in one or more periods over the member's service, subject to Service requirements. |

###### 4.8.25 Refresher training allowance

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for an allowance payable at the end of each 3-month period if all of the following are met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member’s refresher training takes place at a civilian hospital.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member’s salary is less than the salary the member would have received if they were paid by the hospital.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The allowance payable under subsection 1 is calculated using the following formula.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">[image: Start formula allowance equals start fraction A minus B over 4 end fraction end formula]</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>A</b></td>
<td>The annual salary the member would have received if they were paid by the hospital.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>B</b></td>
<td>The member’s annual salary.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.8.26 Expenses associated with training

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is to be reimbursed for these costs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Compulsory fees for the training.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The cost of textbooks prescribed for a course.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The ADF may make available, for the duration of the training, medical instruments the member must use in the training.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is responsible for costs of any travel or removal needed to complete the training.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 6: Army dental officer professional development scheme

###### 4.8.27 Purpose

|  | The Division sets out the reimbursement a dental officer may get when they participate in approved professional development activities. |
|---|---|

###### 4.8.29 Member this Division applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This Division applies to a member who meets all of the following conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member is an Army dental officer who provides a clinical dental capability.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member is on either continuous full-time service or Reserve service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>If the member is required to be fit for operational deployment — they are Army Individual Readiness Notice (AIRN) compliant on the day the expense is incurred.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">This Division ceases to apply to all members on 30 June 2026.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.8.30 Payment

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member may be reimbursed the cost of approved professional development activities up to a maximum amount.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Professional development activities are described in section 4.8.31.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The process for calculating the maximum amount of reimbursement for a member is set out in section 4.8.32.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Costs for professional development activities must be paid in full before reimbursement may be paid.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The maximum under section 4.8.32 applies to a single financial year. Unused funds cannot be paid to the member or carried over to future financial years. If the costs reimbursed are less than the maximum, the member is not eligible for the difference.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">Incurred costs must be paid for and reimbursed in the same financial year.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member can be provided financial support under this Division by direct payment to a supplier for an approved professional development activity. Any amount paid directly is counted as part of the costs that may be reimbursed within the maximum under section 4.8.32.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6.</td>
<td colspan="2">Travel costs for professional development activities are included as part of the costs that may be reimbursed within the maximum under section 4.8.32.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>7.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member may use their Defence travel card for travel associated with an approved professional development activity.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.8.31 Professional development activities

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may approve activities, travel or the purchase of equipment as professional development activities. The CDF must consider all the following criteria.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Whether the activity will enhance the member's clinical and professional skills.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Whether the activity could be funded by other means.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The cost of the activity.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The interests of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>Any other factors relevant to the member's personal development.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The following activities cannot be approved as professional development activities under this Division.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Membership of groups that have a primary purpose that is political in nature.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Activities associated with Specialist officer career structure competency-based training.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Activities that can be accessed through the Defence Assisted Study Scheme.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The purchase of non-dental specific computer hardware, software or internet access.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.8.32 Calculation of the maximum

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section sets out how to calculate the maximum reimbursement that may be paid to a member under section 4.8.30.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The maximum for a member of the Permanent Forces is $10,000 in a financial year.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">This subsection applies to a member of the Army Reserve on continuous full-time service. The member's maximum claim is as follows.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The maximum is $833.33 for each period of 30 consecutive days of service in a financial year.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The financial year reimbursement may not exceed $10,000.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Any period of less than 30 consecutive days of service in a financial year does not count towards the maximum.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Unused days of service not claimed in a financial year cannot be carried over to the next financial year.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>A member who has worked both permanent service and Reserve service cannot claim more than $10 000 in a financial year.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">This subsection applies to a member of the Reserves on Reserve service. The member's maximum is calculated as follows.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The maximum is $27.39 for each day of service. The days do not need to be consecutive. A day of service is a minimum of 6 hours of duty on a day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The financial year reimbursement may not exceed $10,000.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Twenty days or more of Reserve service must be served within a financial year before a claim can be made.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Any total of less than 20 days of Reserve service in a financial year does not count towards the maximum.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>Unused days of service not claimed in a financial year cannot be carried over to the next financial year.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">This subsection applies to a Reserve member who has worked both continuous full-time service and Reserve service in a financial year.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member's maximum is the sum of the limits as calculated under each type of service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member cannot combine unused days from continuous full-time service and Reserve service to be eligible for a claim.</td>
</tr>
</table>

#### Part 9: Reserves

##### Division 1: Legal officer sessional fee

###### 4.9.3 Purpose

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Legal officer sessional fee compensates Reserve legal officers for the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>For certain professional work they perform for the ADF.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>For practice costs associated with the duties in paragraph a.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.9.4 Definitions

|  | In this Division, the following apply. |
|---|---|
|  | **Commission of Inquiry** means an inquiry made under the *Defence (Inquiry) Regulations 2018.* |

###### 4.9.5 Members this Division applies to

|  | This Division applies to a legal officer who is a member of the Reserves. |
|---|---|

###### 4.9.6 Duties attracting a sessional fee

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A legal officer is eligible for a sessional fee if all the following conditions are met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The legal officer performs legal duties in the ADF when they would otherwise be working in a private professional capacity as a barrister or solicitor.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Any of the following persons approves a period of the duty described in the table at paragraph c, before it is performed.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>CDF.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Director General Australian Defence Force Legal Services.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The legal officer performs one or more of the duties described in the following table.</td>
</tr>
</table>

| Item | Duties |
|---|---|
| 1. | Military duty as a counsel or assistant counsel performing any of the following duties.<br>a. Appearing before a summary authority.<br>b. Any of the following duties performed in relation to a Court Martial or Defence Force Magistrate proceeding.<br>i. Appearing in the proceeding.<br>ii. Participating in a pre-trial directions hearing.<br>iii. Participating in a case management conference.<br>iv. Participating in a stay application in relation to a punishment or order.<br>c. Providing legal services related to paragraphs a and b.<br>d. Providing legal services relating to a petition or request for review to a reviewing authority, including a punishment review pursuant to the *Military Justice (interim Measures) Act No. 2 2009*. |
| 2. | Military duty as a Judge Advocate or Defence Force Magistrate in a disciplinary proceeding. |
| 3. | Providing legal services relating to the preparation or provision of a report under section 154 of the *Defence Force Discipline Act 1982*. |
| 4. | Military duty as a legal officer assisting a Commission of Inquiry. |
| 5. | Military duty as a legal officer representing or assisting in the representation of a person, including a person who has died, before a Commission of Inquiry. |
| 6. | Providing legal services to an ADF commander if all of the following requirements are met.<br>a. The services are of any of the following types.<br>i. Providing legal advice.<br>ii. Providing dispute resolution services.<br>iii. Acting as an inquiry officer or as an inquiry assistance under section 11 of the *Defence (Inquiry) Regulations 2018.*<br>b. The services require legal skills.<br>c. The services relate to duties and responsibilities of a member in that command. |
| 7. | Giving legal advice to a member on matters arising from their service in the ADF.<br>**Note:** Preparation time is not paid for this duty. |
| 8. | Giving legal advice to a defence civilian or former member in any of the following circumstances.<br>a. The defence civilian or former member is being investigated in connection with disciplinary action or possible disciplinary action under the *Defence Force Discipline Act 1982.*<br>b. The defence civilian or former member has been charged with an offence under the *Defence Force Discipline Act 1982.*<br>In this item, defence civilian has the same meaning as in the *Defence Force Discipline Act 1982.*<br>**Note:** Preparation time is not paid for this duty. |

<table>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">For the purpose of subsection 1, the sessional fee is payable for preparation time in connection with duty performed for an item in paragraph 1.c. unless the duty is in connection with any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Providing legal advice under table item 6.a.i.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Giving legal advice to a member on matters arising from their service in the ADF under table item 7.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Giving legal advice to a defence civilian or former member under table item 8.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.9.7 Sessional fee and Reserve salary

| 1. | This section applies in any period for which a legal officer is entitled to pay as a Reserve member and also performs duties that meet conditions for payment of the sessional fee set out in section 4.9.6. |
|---|---|
| 2. | If the member's Reserve salary for the period is less that the amount of sessional fee that would be payable for the same period, the member may elect in writing to be paid the higher amount of sessional fee under this Division instead of the salary.<br>**Note 1:** To avoid doubt, a member may be paid a combination of salary and sessional fee for a day, but is not entitled to payment for more than 6 hours’ duty in total for that day.<br>**Note 2:** If the member is approved to perform a period of duty for Reserve salary and not also given an express approval for that period of duty for the purpose of this Division, the member cannot later elect to be paid legal officer sessional fee under this section. |

##### Division 3: Health support allowance – Reserves

<table>

</tr>
<tr>

<td></td>
