##### Division 4: Reserve service payment – infectious diseases

###### 4.9.19 Member this Division applies to

|  | This section applies to a member of the Reserves not on continuous full-time service. |
|---|---|

###### 4.9.20 Payments for periods of isolation associated with military service

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subject to section 4.9.24, a member of the Reserves is eligible for a Reserve service payment if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Their Commanding Officer reasonably believes the member was exposed to an infectious disease in the course of their service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are required to isolate themselves.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note 1:</b> Commanding Officers should work with members to establish work from home arrangements if possible.<br><b>Note 2:</b> A member who subsequently becomes ill may be eligible for a payment of salary under section 3.2.13.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The rate of the Reserve service payment is equal to the salary the member would receive if they rendered service on each day of the isolation period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member must not receive more than the equivalent of 10 days’ salary for a pay period.<br><b>Note:</b> This may consist of a combination of salary and a Reserve service payment.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.9.21 Payment following a Defence activity

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subject to section 4.9.24, a member is eligible for a Reserve service payment if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They have completed a Defence activity.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are required to isolate themself at the end of the Defence activity.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The rate of the Reserve service payment is equal to the salary the member would receive if they rendered service on each day of the isolation period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member must not receive more than the equivalent of 10 days’ salary for a pay period.<br><b>Note:</b> This may consist of a combination of salary and a Reserve service payment.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.9.22 Payment for an inability to work a pattern of Reserve service

| 1. | Subject to section 4.9.24, a member is eligible for a Reserve service payment if their Commanding Officer reasonably believes the member is unable to work their pattern of Reserve service for a reason relating to the control of COVID-19. |
|---|---|
|  | **Note 1:** Commanding Officers should work with members to establish work from home arrangements if possible.<br>**Note 2:** A member who is subsequently diagnosed with COVID-19 may be eligible for a Reserve service payment under section 4.9.23. |
| 2. | The rate of Reserve service payment is equal to the salary they would receive for the pattern of Reserve service. |

###### 4.9.23 Payment for COVID-19

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subject to section 4.9.24, a member is eligible for a Reserve service payment if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are diagnosed with COVID-19.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member is not receiving a payment as a consequence of section 3.2.13.<br><b>Note:</b> A member may be eligible for Reserve salary under section 3.2.13 as a result of an injury or illness acquired in the course of Reserve service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The payment is equal to the amount of salary the member would receive for the pattern of Reserve service.</td>
</tr>

###### 4.9.24 Periods of non-payment

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is not eligible for a Reserve service payment for the same period that any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member is receiving income by way of salary or wages.<br><b>Note:</b> Salary includes salary payable under DFRT Determination 2017 No. 2, <i>Salaries.</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member is on a medical absence.</td>

#### Part 10: Life insurance – additional risk insurance

###### 4.10.1 Purpose

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A member may be reimbursed the part of a life insurance policy premium they pay because of the additional risk involved in doing their duties. This includes a member on Reserve service. This additional risk premium is the difference between these two amounts.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The premium the member would pay for life insurance if their duties did not involve additional risk.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The premium they pay because of the nature of their duties.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.10.2 Members eligible

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A member may be reimbursed their additional risk insurance costs if they do any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They pay more than a normal yearly life insurance policy premium because of the nature of their duties.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They pay a higher premium on a life insurance policy they take out on their resident family because of the nature of their duties.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.10.3 Members not eligible

|  | A member will not be reimbursed their additional risk insurance costs if they pay additional premiums only because of the location they are serving in. |
|---|---|

###### 4.10.4 Amount of reimbursement

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is eligible to be reimbursed the cost of an additional risk premium for a life insurance policy.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1A.</td>
<td colspan="2">The maximum amount of the reimbursement is a combined total of $3,709 paid in a financial year.<br><b>Note:</b> The member may have more than one life insurance policy, but the combined total must not exceed the maximum amount.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may grant an additional reimbursement, up to the amount of the additional risk premium. The CDF must consider all these criteria.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member's rank and duties.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The nature of the policy and the commencement and maturity dates of the policy.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The value of the policy.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The reason for the additional risk premium.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>The additional risk premium offered by other insurers.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td>Any other factor relevant to the member’s life insurance.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 4.10.5 Timing of reimbursement

| 1. | A member is eligible for reimbursement once a year. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The premium for the additional risk insurance must be paid in full before reimbursement can be made.<br>**Note:** The member must provide evidence of the payment. It is the member’s responsibility to provide enough detail to allow the benefit to be verified. |

#### Part 11: Parking

###### 4.11.1 Purpose

|  | This Part sets out the contribution for a parking space, or a parking permit, if one is allocated to a member at a specified location. |
|---|---|

###### 4.11.2 Contributions for parking and parking permits

<table>
<tr>

<td colspan="3">This section applies to a member when all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is allocated one of the following.</td>

<td></td>

<td>A parking space at or near their primary service location.</td>

<td></td>

<td>A parking permit instead of a specific parking space.</td>
</tr>

<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member chooses to take the parking space or permit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

<td colspan="2">The posting location is a location for which the CDF decides that a contribution is payable for a parking space or permit.</td>

<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The contribution only commences on the first payday after the member has been in the temporary or acting position.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>

#### Part 12: Operation COVID-19 ASSIST allowance

###### 4.12.1 Purpose

|  | This Part provides an allowance to members who are force assigned to Operation COVID‑19 ASSIST in Australia, recognising the increased risk of exposure to the COVID-19 virus and the disruption to usual working patterns, the uncertainty and duration of the commitment, and additional unique pressures faced while duties are being undertaken by members during the operation. |
|---|---|

###### 4.12.2 Member this Part applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>

### Chapter 5: Leave and absences

#### Part 1: General provisions

###### 5.1.1 Purpose

|  | This Part gives a general outline of leave for ADF members and describes the various kinds of leave available. |
|---|---|

###### 5.1.1A Definitions

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">In this Chapter the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Senior officer who transitioned</b> means a member who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They hold a rank specified in items 2 or 3 in Schedule 1 of the Act.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They have been transferred to a pool position.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>They are required to undertake activities that support their resignation, retirement or transfer to the Reserves.</td>
</tr>
<tr>

<td colspan="2"><b>Start date</b> means the first day of the member’s absence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The day the member is transferred to a pool position.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The day the member ceases to be a member of the Permanent Forces.</td>
</tr>
</table>

#### Part 2: Leave for travel to restricted destinations

###### 5.2.1 Purpose

|  | This Part specifies the restrictions on the granting of leave for members who travel to restricted destinations and the consequences of travelling to a restricted destination while on approved leave. |
|---|---|

###### 5.2.2 Member this Part applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Part applies to members who have applied, or have been approved, for any of the following types of leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Recreation leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Long service leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>War service leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Personal leave for compassionate reasons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>Leave without pay.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td>Maternity leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>g.</td>
<td>Premature birth leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>h.</td>
<td>Parental leave.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.2.3 Definitions

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">In this Part the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Transiting through a restricted destination</b> means the member enters a restricted destination and all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member remains in the port or airport.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

###### 5.2.4 Restriction on the grant of leave

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A member must not be granted leave to travel to a restricted destination unless any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member has been granted a leave travel waiver for that restricted destination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member will only transit through the restricted destination.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.2.5 Cancellation of leave in a restricted destination

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">If a member is on leave and travels to a restricted destination, the member’s leave is cancelled unless one of the following applies.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member has been granted a leave travel waiver for that restricted destination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member is only transiting through the restricted destination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The member’s presence in the restricted destination is beyond their control.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The member was in transit in the restricted destination and required to leave the port or airport for a reason beyond their control.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> A member’s leave is not restored once the member leaves the restricted destination.</td>
</tr>
</table>

#### Part 3: Medical absence from duty

###### 5.3.1 Purpose

|  | This Part provides a member with paid time away from duty when they are unfit for health reasons. For a member on continuous service, this time away from duty is a type of leave. |
|---|---|

###### 5.3.2 Member this Part applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Part applies to the following members.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A member of the Permanent Forces.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A member of the Reserves on a period of continuous full-time service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Subject to the conditions in section 3.2.13, a member of the Reserves who is unable to work due to an illness or injury arising out of their Reserve duty may be provided with benefits in accordance with section 5.3.5.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> A Reservist not on a period of continuous full-time service can access the arrangements in this Part only if they meet the additional conditions for eligibility in section 3.2.13. In some cases, the Reservist may be eligible for payment under section 3.2.13.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.3.2A Member this Part does not apply to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Part does not apply to a member who meets any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are on a form of unpaid leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are on a flexible service determination during their nonworking period.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.3.3 How to apply for a medical absence

|  | A member must use the approved form to apply for leave to be absent from duty under this Part unless the supervisor is satisfied the member is unable to apply for leave on the approved form due to their illness or injury. |
|---|---|

###### 5.3.4 Medical absence without recommendation from a health professional

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">For the purpose of this section, a supervisor must be at one of these ranks or higher.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Warrant Officer Class 2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>APS 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member may apply to take a day of leave to be absent from duty as a medical absence without providing a medical certificate for that day, if they provide a statement that they are unfit to work on that day for health reasons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">A supervisor may grant a day of medical absence under this section to the member on a day-to-day basis for a maximum of 3 consecutive days, for a period of illness or injury.<br><b>Note:</b> Each day must be granted separately by the supervisor. An aggregated period of several days of medical absence can only be granted under section 5.3.5.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">In relation to the decision under subsection 3, the supervisor may take any of the following actions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The supervisor may make the decision without the advice of an authorised health professional.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The supervisor may seek advice from an authorised health professional before making the decision.<br><b>Note:</b> Personal or health information directly related to the member must not to be provided without the consent of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The supervisor may at any time direct the member to seek assessment by a health professional, in relation to the reason for the leave.<br><b>Note 1:</b> If medical absence is granted under this section, the direction is to be taken as a condition on the grant of the medical absence.<br><b>Note 2:</b> If medical absence is refused under this section, the direction ensures that the member seeks prompt advice from a health professional, who may recommend a medical absence for the purpose of section 5.3.5.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The supervisor may decide not to approve the leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is being treated under a crisis management plan, the supervisor must only approve leave as recommended by a health professional under section 5.3.5.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.3.5 Medical absence on recommendation from a health professional

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A supervisor may approve a member's application to be absent from duty for a period of 1 day or more, having regard to all of the following circumstances.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The period of leave that the member has applied for.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Any recommendation of a health professional. This could include recommendations as to the member's care, remaining in a health facility or undertaking follow-up treatment. The supervisor may make the grant of leave conditional on these recommendations being followed.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Any other relevant matter.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The supervisor may direct the member to seek further assessment by a Defence health professional, in relation to the reason for the leave. The direction may be given at any time in relation to the grant of medical absence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">Up to 3 days of absence can be recommended by a health professional who does not provide services for Defence. If the application relates to an absence of more than 3 days, then the recommendation of a Defence health professional is required to support the application.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note 1:</b> Regulation 35 of the Work Health and Safety Regulations 2011 requires Defence to identify risks and hazards and to eliminate or minimise any risks to health and safety.<br><b>Note 2:</b> A Defence member may provide written consent for health information to be released to specific individuals in their chain of command.<br><b>Note 3:</b> If the member's consent is not provided, then information can only be disclosed in accordance with the exemptions to the Privacy Act 1988.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.3.6 Refusal to grant a medical absence

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">If a health professional has recommended that a member is unfit for duty, the supervisor may only refuse to grant the member a medical absence for the period of unfitness in any of the following circumstances.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">There are alternate duties available that a health professional has confirmed that the member is fit to perform.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">There are no alternate duties that the member is fit to perform and the supervisor has performed a written risk assessment setting out how the risks related to the member's attending for duty can be eliminated or minimised, having regard to all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The risk to the health of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The risk to any other people.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The risk to operational requirements of the mission for which the member is performing duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iv.</td>
<td>Any relevant requirement to provide medical or dental treatment to the member<i>.</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> The risk assessment in paragraph 1.b would require operational imperatives to be weighed against any adverse outcomes to the member or other members resulting from the sick or injured member continuing to work, rather than being placed on medical absence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A risk assessment made under paragraph 1.b must document all the following matters.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The reasons the recommendation for leave was made.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Any risks to health and safety that may foreseeably arise if the leave is not granted as recommended.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The work-related activities that may involve an increased risk to health and safety in relation to each of subparagraphs 1.b.i to 1.b.iv.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">Consultation between the supervisor and the health professional who has recommended the member's leave, or with a Defence medical officer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">A copy of a risk assessment made under paragraph 1.b must be provided to the supervisor's Commanding Officer as soon as practicable after it has been made.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.3.7 Granting a medical absence without an application form

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A supervisor may grant a period of leave under section 5.3.4 or section 5.3.5 for a member who has not made a formal application, if all of the following are met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The supervisor has regard to any statement from the member, a person who is responsible to care for the member while they are unfit for duty, or a health professional.<br><b>Note:</b> An absence of more than 3 days should only be approved with the recommendation of a Defence health professional.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The supervisor is satisfied that the member is unable to formally apply for leave to be absent under this Part within a reasonable period due to their unfitness for duty.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.3.9 Payment of salary and allowances on a medical absence

| 1. | Any salary, allowance or benefit for which a member was eligible for immediately before a medical absence may continue to be paid during the medical absence as long as the member continues to meet conditions required for eligibility, other than attending for duty. |
|---|---|
| 2. | To avoid doubt, if the rates of a benefit or contribution that the member is eligible for while on a medical absence change, that change applies in relation to the member. |
| 3. | A member may cease to be eligible for an allowance or benefit during a period of medical absence if they cease to meet a condition required for eligibility, other than attending for duty. |
| 4. | A member's medical absence is conditional on the member only engaging in paid work outside the ADF (as an employee, under a contract or otherwise) if that external work is part of an ADF-approved convalescence or career transition activity. |
| 5. | An absence ceases to be a medical absence if the condition in subsection 4 is not met by the member. No salary or allowances are payable under this Part for the absence and the absence may be an absence without leave. |

###### 5.3.10 Interaction between medical absence and other forms of leave

| 1. | A member who could reasonably apply for a medical absence because they are unfit for duty must apply for that type of leave and not another form of leave. |
|---|---|
| 2. | A member who is being actively managed on a crisis management plan may access leave under this Part only and must not be required to access their recreation leave or other accrued leave credit while the crisis continues. |
| 3. | A member may apply for a medical absence if they become unfit for duty while on a period of recreation leave or long service leave.<br>**Note:** Sections 5.4.35 and 5.5.12 provide that a member who has been approved a medical absence while on recreation leave or long service leave will be re-credited their leave if specific criteria are met. |

###### 5.3.11 Travel for medical purposes

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Travel costs may be provided in the following circumstances, to assist with medical needs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If a member must travel to an appointment relating to a medical or dental condition for which treatment is provided under section 49 of the Defence Regulation, they may be eligible for their travel costs.<br><b>Note:</b> The costs are payable as if the trip was duty travel and any means of travel recommended by a health professional were the most economical means of travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If a member leaves hospital to recover or waits to return to hospital, they may be provided with travel costs under section 9.2.25 if a Defence health professional considers that the travel is necessary to assist the member's recovery.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The CDF may approve other travel costs if satisfied that the senior medical advisor in the member's region recommends the travel as in the best interests of the member's recovery.</td>
</tr>
</table>

|---|---|

###### 5.4.4 Members this Part applies to

</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The Vice Chief of the Defence Force.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>

</tr>

</tr>
<tr>

<td></td>

</tr>

</tr>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Peacetime training</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Periods of warlike service</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>Field operations</td>
</tr>

<td>Activities similar to the above</td>

</tr>
<tr>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

##### Division 2: Basic recreation leave

###### 5.4.7 Purpose

|  | This Division sets out basic recreation leave entitlements and conditions. |
|---|---|

###### 5.4.8 Basic recreation leave credit

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member may accrue up to a maximum credit of 25 days basic recreation leave a year.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Leave credit accrues fortnightly and is credited on each payday.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">Fortnightly leave credits for a member not subject to a flexible service determination are calculated using the following formula.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">[image: Start formula forghtnightly leave credits equals start fraction 25 over 365 end fraction times open bracket 14 minus A close bracket end formula]</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>A</b></td>
<td>is the number of calendar days in a fortnight of non-effective service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">Fortnightly leave credits for a member subject to a flexible service determination are calculated using the following formula.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">[image: Start formula fortnightly leave credits equals open brackets 14 times start fraction 25 over 365 end formula close bracket times open bracket start fraction A minus B over 80 end fraction close bracket end formula]</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>A</b></td>
<td>is the number of hours in a fortnight in the member’s pattern of service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>B</b></td>
<td>is the number of hours in a fortnight of non-effective service.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 3: Additional recreation leave

###### 5.4.9 Purpose

|  | Additional recreation leave is to provide members with recreation leave credits to enable recovery from the environmental effects of certain types of service over time. |
|---|---|

###### 5.4.9A When leave credit accrue

|  | Leave credits accrued under this Division are credited on each payday. |
|---|---|

###### 5.4.10 Members eligible for a Military Factor framework allowance

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="4">A member is eligible to accrue additional recreation leave credits on a day they are eligible for an allowance under DFRT Determination No. 6 of 2024.<br><b>Note:</b> Allowances under DFRT Determination No. 6 of 2024 are not paid for a period of leave without pay.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>

<td></td>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">[image: start formula daily rate of accrual equals start fraction 10 over 365 end fraction end formula]</td>

<td></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td><b>A</b></td>
<td>is the number of hours in the member’s pattern of service for the fortnight.<br><b>Note:</b> The number of hours in a member’s pattern of service is specified in their flexible service determination made under section 23 of the Act.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="3">In any other circumstance — 0.1 of a credit of additional recreation leave.</td>
</tr>

##### Division 5: Purchased recreation leave

###### Subdivision 1: General provisions

###### 5.4.21 Simplified outline of this Division

This Division sets up two different methods for members to increase the amount of recreation leave credits available to them. The member can purchase up to 20 days in a financial year, depending on the method the member uses to purchase recreation leave credits.

 Recreation leave credits can be purchased under the pay-as-you-go method, in which recreation leave credits accrue as they are paid for. Up to 20 days can be purchased over 26 pay periods under this method.

 Recreation leave credits can be purchased as credit in advance method, in which recreation leave credits are received following approval of their application and paid for later. Up to 10 days can be purchased over of 13 pay periods under this method.

###### Subdivision 2: Application to purchase recreation leave credits

###### 5.4.22 Application to purchase recreation leave credits

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is eligible to purchase recreation leave credits in one of the following ways if the CDF is satisfied that subsection 3 is met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The pay-as-you-go method.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The credit in advance method.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">To apply to purchase recreation leave credits, the member must do the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Use the approved form.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Specify the number of pay periods over which they will pay for the recreation leave credits, subject to the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The pay-as-you-go method — up to 26 pay periods.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The credit in advance method — up to 13 pay periods.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> The calculation for the amount to be paid is provided under section 5.4.26C.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">For subsection 1, service requirements are unlikely to prevent the member using the purchased recreation leave credits.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.4.23 Members not eligible to purchase recreation leave credits

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is not eligible to purchase recreation leave credits under this Division if they are performing any of the following kinds of service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Warlike service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Non-warlike service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Foreign service, as defined by subsection 23AG(7) of the <i>Income Tax Assessment Act 1936</i>, which could reasonably be expected to be exempt from tax under section 23AG of that Act.<br><b>Note:</b> To qualify for the tax exemption, a member must be engaged in foreign service for a continuous period of not less than 91 days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is not eligible to purchase recreation leave credits if the member’s recreation leave credits balance will exceed 50 days after the purchase.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is not eligible to purchase recreation leave credits under the credit in advance method unless the member has 10 days or less of recreation leave credits at the time of application.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is not eligible to purchase recreation leave credits if any of the following apply at the time of application.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are already purchasing credits under a pay-as-you-go arrangement.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are already paying for recreation leave credits under the credit in advance method.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.4.24 Limitations on purchasing recreation leave credits

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The maximum amount of recreation leave credits the member can purchase in an application is one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the member is using the pay-as-you-go method — up to 20 days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the member is using the credit in advance method — up to 10 days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> The maximum amount is not reduced for a member on a flexible service determination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">Recreation leave credits must be purchased in whole days.<br><b>Note:</b> Eight hours is the equivalent of one day of leave.</td>

###### Subdivision 4: Credit in advance method

###### 5.4.26A Credit of purchased recreation leave credits

|  | If recreation leave credits have been purchased under the credit in advance method, the member’s recreation leave credit balance is increased by the number of days the member purchased on the day the first payment is deducted from the member’s fortnightly salary.<br>**Note:** The calculation for the amount of each payment is provided in Subdivision 5. |
|---|---|

###### 5.4.26B Recovery of purchased recreation leave credits

|  | If the member is no longer receiving salary, the unpaid payment balance will be recovered as a debt.<br>**Note:** If a debt needs to be recovered under this section, section 1.5.4A will apply. |
|---|---|

##### Division 6: Additional recreation leave for training ('trainee leave')

###### 5.4.27 Purpose

|  | Additional recreation leave for training is for a member who must take a break from a course and who does not have enough recreation leave credit to cover the absence. The leave is sometimes called trainee leave. |
|---|---|

###### 5.4.28 Member eligible for trainee leave

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member who meets all of these conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are required by their Service to attend a training course, or a series of courses.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are not required to attend the course during a course break.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>They do not have enough recreation leave to cover the period of the course break.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is able to take trainee leave for the period of the course break not covered by recreation leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">Recreation leave credits must be used before trainee leave may be granted.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.4.29 Member on a flexible service determination

|  | A member on a flexible service determination may only be granted trainee leave for a period in the member's pattern of service. |
|---|---|

##### Division 7: Administration and payment for recreation leave

###### 5.4.30 Purpose

|  | This Division sets out how recreation leave may expire or be re-credited. It also provides other recreation leave administration rules. |
|---|---|

###### 5.4.30A Definitions

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">In this Division, the following apply.</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Division 3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Chapter 14 Part 6 Division 1 subdivision 2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Chapter 16 Part 3A.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Chapter 17 Part 7 Division 3.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.4.31 How leave may be taken

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">Recreation leave may be taken in any of the following ways.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is not on a flexible service determination, any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>A full day of recreation leave at full pay.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ia.</td>
<td>A full day of recreation leave at half pay.<br><b>Note:</b> Recreation leave at half pay cannot be taken in half days, part days or for less than 7 consecutive days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>A half day of recreation leave at full pay.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>A part day of recreation leave if the remaining day is taken as war service leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is on a flexible service determination, any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The period of duty specified in the member’s flexible service determination for the day in the member’s pattern of service at full pay.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ia.</td>
<td>The period of duty specified in the member’s flexible service determination for the day in the member’s pattern of service at half pay.<br><b>Note:</b> Recreation leave at half pay cannot be taken in part days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Half the period of duty specified in the member’s flexible service determination for the day in the member’s pattern of service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> Section 5.4.38 may affect a member’s ability to take leave if they are seconded or attached for duty outside of the ADF.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.4.32 Taking recreation leave

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is eligible to take recreation leave if their supervisor is satisfied of all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member has leave credits to cover the period of leave at the end of the pay fortnight in which the member ceases to be on leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s absence from duty will not adversely affect capability.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is taking the leave at half pay, all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The leave is for a minimum of 7 consecutive days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member does not have excess leave credits as defined under subsection 5.4.33A.3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A supervisor must not approve a member to take leave if the member is a senior officer who transitioned and the total amount of recreation leave to be taken in their transition period is more than 2 weeks.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">In this section, <b>supervisor</b> means a person who meets one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are in the member’s chain of command and hold a minimum rank of Warrant Officer Class 2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are in the member’s line management and hold a minimum APS classification of APS 4.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.4.33A Leave credits

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member’s leave credits are reduced if any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They have taken recreation leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They have been directed not to attend for duty for the purpose of reducing the member’s excess leave credits.<br><b>Note:</b> The direction to take leave is an exercise of command power.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1A.</td>
<td colspan="2">Leave credits for a member not subject to a flexible service determination are reduced for each day on which leave is taken in accordance with the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If a full day of leave is taken at full pay — by 1 day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>aa.</td>
<td>If a full day of leave is taken at half pay — by 4 hours.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If a half day of leave is taken at full pay — by 4 hours.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> Section 5.4.31 details how leave may be taken at less than a full day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1B.</td>
<td colspan="2">Leave credits for a member subject to a flexible service determination are reduced for each day on which leave is taken in accordance with the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If a full day of leave is taken at full pay — by the number of hours in the member’s pattern of service on that day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>aa.</td>
<td>If a full day of leave is taken at half pay — by half the number of hours in the member’s pattern of service on that day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If a half day of leave is taken at full pay — by half of the number of hours in the member’s pattern of service for that day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> Section 5.4.31 details how leave may be taken at less than a full day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">A grant of recreation leave reduces a member's combined recreation and war service leave credit balances in the following order.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>War service leave credits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Recreation leave credits donated under Division 9.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Purchased recreation leave credits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Recreation leave credits, including additional recreation leave, and basic recreation leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">In this section, <b>excess leave credits</b> means having more than 50 recreation leave credits.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.4.34 Expiration of recreation leave credits ('leave lapsing')

| 1. | If a member has a recreation leave credit that exceeds 90 days on the lapsing day, the recreation leave credit that exceeds 90 days expires on the lapsing day. |
|---|---|
| 1A. | For the purpose of subsection 1, the lapsing day is the last payday before 30 June each year. |
| 2. | The expiration of the member’s leave credit is deferred by one additional year at a time if the CDF is satisfied that leave could not to be granted because the Commanding Officer needed the member to stay on duty to meet Service needs during the previous 3 years. |
| 4. | For the purposes of this section, decisions about the CDF's own recreation leave may be made by the Minister. |
| 5. | A member who holds a statutory appointment and who applies to have their recreation leave credit deferred and treated as recreation leave under this Part, is not eligible to have the leave credited as special leave under Part 9 Division 4, Special leave for private purposes. |

###### 5.4.35 Re-credit of recreation leave

<table>
<tr>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>

<td></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They were admitted to hospital.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member on recreation leave may be re-credited any day's leave that was granted which they did not take if any of the following occurs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are formally recalled to duty from the leave for operational reasons, for not less than 1 day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member wishes to return to duty early. Management accepts the return to duty.<br><b>Note:</b> The member's unit must pay the costs of any recall to duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>ba.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are required to isolate themself on return to Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">They die.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 8: Payment or transfer of recreation leave credit

###### 5.4.40 Purpose

|  | This Division sets out how recreation leave may be paid out or transferred to another Commonwealth entity instead of taken when a member ceases continuous full-time service. |
|---|---|

###### 5.4.41 Member this Division applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Division applies to the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A member who ceases continuous full-time service, including the CDF.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A member who has died, but limited to calculate the amount payable under section 1.6.4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>A member who has been diagnosed with a terminal illness before ceasing continuous full-time service.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.4.42 Definitions

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">In this Division the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Accrued leave credit</b> means the sum of leave credits accrued from the following types of accruable leave (measured in days).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Additional recreation leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Overseas additional recreation leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Basic recreation leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Extra recreation leave as granted under this determination before 1 August 2023.<br><b>Note:</b> Extra recreation leave was repealed by Defence Determination, Conditions of service Amendment (Employment offer modernisation) Determination 2022 (No. 2).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>War service leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Annual allowance</b> means a DFRT allowance or an allowance paid under this Determination, other than the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Rent allowance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Higher duties allowance that has been paid to the member on a continuous basis for less than a year.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Commonwealth entity</b> has the same meaning as given in section 10 of the <i>Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013</i>, as in force from time to time.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Daily rate</b> means the annual rate of any of the following divided by 365.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Salary.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>An annual allowance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Purchased recreation leave credit</b> means a member's purchased recreation leave credit measured in days, including part days.<br><b>Note:</b> 1 hour equals 0.125 day.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.4.43 Election for payment or transfer of leave credit

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member may elect to take their accrued leave credit and purchased recreation leave credit in any of the following forms on ceasing continuous full-time service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">A payment for the full amount of their accrued leave credit and purchased recreation leave credit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Transfer to their new Commonwealth entity, one of the following amounts.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>All their accrued leave credit and purchased recreation leave credit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Part of their accrued leave credit and purchased recreation leave credit.<br><b>Note:</b> For remaining credits that are not transferred, their leave credit will be a payment to the member under paragraph 1.a.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The election must be submitted in writing at least 30 days before ceasing continuous full‑time service.<br><b>Note:</b> If the member has not made an election 30 days before ceasing continuous full-time service, their leave credit will be a payment to the member under paragraph 1.a.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">Once a member has made an election under subsection 1 it cannot be changed.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member's offer of employment with the new agency is withdrawn.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The Commonwealth entity does not agree to the transfer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">Despite subsection 3, the member’s leave is to be a payment for the full amount of their accrued leave credit and purchased recreation leave credit if any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member's offer of employment with the new agency is withdrawn.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The Commonwealth entity does not agree to the transfer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.4.43A Payment of leave credits to a member diagnosed with a terminal illness

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member who has been diagnosed with a terminal illness before ceasing continuous full-time service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is eligible for a payment for their leave balance if the CDF is satisfied that making the payment is reasonable in the circumstances.<br><b>Note 1:</b> The payment amount is calculated under section 5.4.44.<br><b>Note 2:</b> There is no limit to the number of times a member can receive payment under this section.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The amount of payment under subsection 2 can be for all or part of the member’s leave balance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member's accrued leave credits and purchased recreation leave credits is reduced by the number of credits for which they received a payment under subsection 2 in the order provided in section 5.4.33A.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">In this section, the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Leave balance</b> means the amount of all of the following types of leave that the member has on the day the decision under subsection 2 is made.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Accrued leave credit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Purchased recreation leave credit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> Section 5.4.42 provides the definition of accrued leave credit and purchased recreation leave credit.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.4.44 Payment to member for leave credit

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies to a member, other than a senior officer who transitioned, who meets any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They have elected to receive payment under paragraph 5.4.43.1.a.<br><b>Note:</b> Under Section 5.4.43 a member may elect to receive payment for their accrued leave credit and purchased recreation leave credit on ceasing continuous full-time service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are eligible to receive payment under 5.4.43A.<br><b>Note:</b> Section 5.4.43A provides payment to a member for their leave when they have been diagnosed with a terminal illness prior to ceasing continuous full-time service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member is to be paid the sum of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">For each day of accrued leave credit and purchase leave credit, all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The daily rate of salary.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The daily rate of an annual allowance the member would be eligible to receive on recreation leave if the recreation leave were taken on their last day of service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">For every 5 days of accrued leave credit, 2 days of salary and annual allowances paid at the daily rate.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">For the purpose of subparagraph 2.a.i, the rate of salary used to calculate the daily rate of salary is one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member’s last promotion was under section 13(1)(a) of the Defence Regulation— the rate of salary of their rank.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If on the member’s last day of service, the member was under a direction to act at a higher rank under section 13(1)(b) of the Defence Regulation and has held that rank for less than 1 year — the rate of salary for their rank had the direction not applied.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">If on the member’s last day of service, the member was under a direction under section 13(1)(b) of the Defence Regulation to act at a higher rank and has held that rank for 1 year or more — the rate of salary for the higher rank.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.4.44A Payment to senior officer who transitioned for leave credit

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies to a senior officer to whom all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The senior officer has become a senior officer who transitioned.</td>
</tr>

<td></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The senior officer is to be paid an amount calculated using the following formula.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">[image: Start formula A times open bracket B plus C close bracket plus D times open bracket E plus F close bracket minus open bracket A times G close Bracket end formula.]</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Where:</td>

<td></td>

<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

<td>is the amount of accrued leave credits (in days) the senior officer used during their transition period.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
</tr>

###### 5.4.45 Transfer of leave credits and payment to new Commonwealth entity

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member who elects to transfer all or part of their accrued leave credit and purchased recreation leave credit under paragraph 5.4.43.1.b and the new Commonwealth entity has agreed to the transfer.</td>

</tr>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

<td>If the member’s last promotion was under section 13(1)(a) of the Defence Regulation, — the rate of salary of their rank.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If on the member’s last day of service, the member was under a direction to act at a higher rank under section 13(1)(b) of the Defence Regulation and has held that rank for less than 1 year — the rate of salary for their rank had the direction not applied.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>If on the member’s last day of service, the member was under a direction under section 13(1)(b) of the Defence Regulation to act at a higher rank and has held that rank for 1 year or more — the rate of salary for the higher rank.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>

##### Division 9: Sharing recreation leave – Dual serving couples

###### 5.4.46 Purpose

|  | This section sets out how recreation leave is donated from one member to another if the members are part of a dual serving couple. |
|---|---|

###### 5.4.47 Definitions

|  | In this Division, the following apply. |
|---|---|
|  | **Donor member** means a member who donates recreation leave credits to their partner under section 5.4.50. |
|  | **Receiving member** means the partner of the donor member who is to receive the donated recreation leave credits under section 5.4.50. |

###### 5.4.48 Member this Division applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Division applies to a member and their partner who meet all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are part of a dual serving couple.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are both on continuous full-time service.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.4.49 Member this Division does not apply to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Division does not apply to a member who meets any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member or their partner have 6 months or less until they cease continuous full-time service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>There has been less than 12 months since the last time the member or their partner donated recreation leave credits under this Division.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.4.50 Donating recreation leave

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A donor member can donate their recreation leave credits to a receiving member if the CDF is satisfied all of the following conditions have been met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The donor member will have a recreation leave balance of at least 10 days after the donation has occurred.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The leave credits being donated are not purchased leave credits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The donor member and the receiving partner are not expected to cease continuous full-time service within 6 months of the leave credits being donated.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The request to donate leave credits must be submitted using the approved form at least 4 weeks before the date the donor member requests the donation to occur.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">Leave credits can only be donated in whole days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">On the day the leave credits is donated the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The donor member’s recreation leave credits is reduced by the number of credits approved to be donated under subsection 1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The receiving member’s donated recreation leave credits are increased by the number of credits donated under subsection 1.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.4.51 Ceasing continuous full-time service

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">If a receiving member ceases continuous full-time service, the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The donor member’s recreation leave credits are increased by the number of donated recreation leave credits not used by the receiving member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The receiving member’s donated recreation leave credits are reduced by the number of donated recreation leave credits returned to the donor member.</td>
</tr>
</table>

#### Part 5: Long service leave

##### Division 1: General provisions

###### 5.5.1 Purpose

|  | Long service leave is intended to give an extended period away from work to a member who has served for 10 years or more. |
|---|---|

###### 5.5.4 Member this Part applies to

|  | This Part applies to a member on continuous full-time service. |
|---|---|

###### 5.5.5 Definitions

|  | In this Part the following apply. |
|---|---|
|  | **Long Service Leave Act** means the *Long Service Leave (Commonwealth Employees) Act 1976*. |

###### 5.5.6 Administrative concepts

| 2. | Long service leave credits are expressed in months and decimal parts of a month. |
|---|---|
| 3. | A month is measured from the start date to the day before the same date in the next month. This rule applies no matter how many days there are in that month. |
| 4. | When working out parts of a month, a month is taken to have 30 days. |
| 6. | Leave may be granted in months and whole days. |
| 8. | For the purpose of payment instead of long service leave, a month's salary is one-twelfth of a year's salary. This rule applies no matter how many days there are in that month. |

###### 5.5.7 Applying for long service leave

|  | A member must use the approved form to apply for long service leave. |
|---|---|

##### Division 2: Entitlement to long service leave

###### 5.5.8 Long service leave entitlement

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="4">A member is entitled to a long service leave credit once the member has completed 10 years of accrued service.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="4">Long service leave credits are credited to a member on the completion of the following.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">10 years of accrued service.</td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Each full year of accrued service thereafter.</td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="4">Annual long service leave credit is calculated on the following basis.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="3">If the member is not on a flexible service determination for any period during a completed year of accrued service, the member earns 0.3 of a month long service leave credit.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="3">If the member is on one or more flexible service determinations during a year of accrued service, the member’s long service leave credit for the year is the sum of the long service leave credit for each period.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="4">For the purposes of paragraph 3.b, a member's long service leave credit is calculated using the following formula.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="4">[image: Start formula long service leave credit equals start fraction Days over 365 end fraction times start fraction Hrs over 40 end fraction times 0.3 end formula]</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td colspan="4">Where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td><b>Days</b></td>
<td colspan="3">is the numbers of days in the period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td><b>Hrs</b></td>
<td colspan="3">is the number of hours worked each week calculated using the following.<br>– Eight hours for any full day of duty.<br>– The number of duty hours under the flexible service determination for any part day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.5.9 Eligibility to take leave

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is eligible to take leave using long service leave credits if the CDF approves an application and all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member applies for leave using the approved form.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The application for leave has been submitted not less than 30 days before the day on which the leave is to start.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The period of leave applied for is not less than the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>If leave is taken at full pay — 7 days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>If leave is taken at half pay — 14 days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>If the CDF is satisfied that there are compassionate reasons — 1 day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member has previously taken leave using long service leave credits, the member has been available for duty for a least 14 days from the last day of the previous period of leave taken using long service leave credits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td colspan="2">The period of leave does not include a part day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">For the purpose of paragraph 1.d, a member is available for duty if they are not on any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">A type of leave other than short absence leave, a medical absence or examination leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The Christmas stand-down.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">Paragraphs 1.b and 1.d do not apply if the CDF is satisfied it is reasonable in the circumstances.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.5.10 Taking leave and long service leave credits

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member takes leave using long service leave credits, the member’s long service leave credits are reduced in accordance with the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the leave is taken at full pay — by the period of leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the leave is taken at half pay — by half the period of leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">A period of leave includes weekends and public holidays.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.5.12 Re-credit of long service leave

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is to be re-credited long service leave for any day all of the following are met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member was on a period of long service leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">One of the following applies.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Illness or injury made the member unfit for duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member was admitted to hospital.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member has been approved a medical absence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">A medical certificate has been provided.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">If the member meets the condition in subsection 1 for less than a full day, long service leave is not re-credited.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member on a period of long service leave is to be re-credited for the leave on any day they are recalled to duty for operational reasons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">The CDF may extend a member's period of leave by the amount of long service leave re-credited.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 3: Accrual of service for long service leave

###### 5.5.13 Accrued service

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">In this Part, a member's accrued service is the sum of these periods.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Their period of continuous full-time service.<br><b>Note:</b> This includes ADF service with the United Nations, regardless of whether they are paid by the ADF or the UN.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Prior Reserve service, measured under section 5.5.14.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Any prior service described in sections 5.5.15 or 5.5.16.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> Section 5.5.16 provides how overlapping prior service is treated if a member has recognised prior service with two different employers at the same time.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.5.14 Prior Reserve service

| 1. | Subject to subsection 5.5.15.2, a member’s long service leave accrues on a day they perform 6 or more hours of Reserve service. |
|---|---|
| 2. | Thirty days of Reserve service counts as a month of service. |

###### 5.5.15 Prior service

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A period that could be counted as service under the <i>Long Service Leave (Commonwealth Employees) Act 1976</i>, on or after 1 January 1973, is accrued service under this Part.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1A.</td>
<td colspan="3">The following are not recognised as prior service under this Part.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Periods of ineffective service with a prior employer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Service with the armed forces of another country.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">Unless one of the following apply, if there is a gap of more than 12 months between any two periods of service, the earlier period of service cannot be recognised.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF is satisfied of all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The prior period of service or employment was ceased due to illness.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>After considering the member’s duties before their illness, the member has returned to, or commenced, suitable duties in the ADF within 1 year of their recovery.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The break was due to Service-approved full-time vocational training.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">Service with another employer may only be recognised if it has ended.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member's credit is reduced by any of the following events.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Long service leave granted during prior service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Any payment instead of long service leave during prior service.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.5.16 Overlapping prior service

| 1. | This section applies to a member who has recognised prior service with two different employers at the same time. |
|---|---|
| 2. | A member cannot have more than 1 day of service for long service leave purposes recognised for a calendar day. |
| 3. | If a member has part-time service with two employers at the same time, the weekly hours are added together to determine service for long service leave. The member is subject to the limit in subsection 2. |

###### 5.5.17 Effect of part-time prior service

<table>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Members with part-time prior service need to have these periods converted to full-time equivalents.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Subsection 3 gives the method for adjusting the period of part-time service to the<br>full-time equivalent.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Subsection 5 gives the method for adjusting the period of part-time leave to the<br>full-time equivalent.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">Prior part-time service counts as accrued service but the period of service is adjusted to reflect the part-time hours worked. This table shows the method.</td>
</tr>
</table>

| Step | Action |
|---|---|
| 1. | Work out the length of the member's part-time prior service, in days. |
| 2. | Work out the member's average weekly hours during that period. If the member had different periods at different weekly rates, these should be calculated separately. |
| 3. | Multiply the two figures together. |
| 4. | Divide this total by 36.75. This figure is the number of days of prior service that may be recognised. |
| 5. | If the member had different periods at different weekly rates, steps 1 to 4 should be worked out separately for each period. The periods are added at the end to give the total part-time prior service. |
| 6. | The total should be included in the member's period of service for when working out their credit. |

<table>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">The difference between the following periods is recorded as non-service days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The calendar days in the period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The number of days to be recognised as a result of the calculations in subsection 3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">Prior part-time leave should be adjusted to its full-time equivalent before being deducted from a member's long service leave credit. This table shows the method.</td>
</tr>
</table>

| Step | Action |
|---|---|
| 1. | Work out the periods of long service leave that were paid at part-time rates.<br>**Note:** This includes payment instead of long service leave. It does not include half-pay long service leave if the amount paid was half of the person's full-time hours. |
| 2. | Work out weekly hours the person was paid for the leave. If the member had different periods of leave at different weekly rates, these should be calculated separately.<br>**Note:** If the person took the leave at half pay, use their weekly part-time hours, not the half part-time hours that they were paid. |
| 3. | Divide their weekly part-time hours (Step 2) by 36.75. |
| 4. | Multiply Step 1 by Step 3. |
| 5. | If any of the periods of leave were at half pay, divide Step 4 by 2. |
| 6. | If the member had different periods of leave at different weekly rates, steps 1 to 5 should be worked out separately for each period of leave. The periods are added at the end to give the total leave taken in respect of part-time service during the prior work. |

###### 5.5.18 Periods that are not accrued service

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">In this Part, these periods are not accrued service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Any period the member is absent without leave for more than a day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">A period of unpaid leave of more than 3 months. There are two exceptions to this rule.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Leave without pay for illness.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Leave without pay under the <i>Defence (Parliamentary Candidates) Act 1969.</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">Any period of more than 1 day that the member is not entitled to salary or allowances under Chapter 1 Part 7.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.5.19 Member's responsibilities

| 1. | A member should ask for recognition of their prior service as soon as reasonably practical after starting continuous full-time service. This includes prior Reserve service. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The member must give the CDF written evidence of their prior service. If not, the periods will not be counted as accrued service. |

###### 5.5.20 Working out the total period for a member’s long service leave credit

| 1. | This table shows how to work out the total period that a member's long service leave credit is assessed on. |
|---|---|

| Step | Action | See |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | Work out the member's total period of accrued service. This includes the member's current service, prior full days of Reserve service and other prior service. | Sections 5.5.13 to 5.5.17 |
| 2. | Work out their total long service leave credit for completed years of service. | Division 2 section 5.5.8 |
| 3. | Subtract any leave that they have already taken as leave or been paid for instead of leave. |  |

<table>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">For a grant of long service leave, the entitlement to the actual credit is set out in section 5.5.8.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">For a payment instead of long service leave, the entitlement to the actual credit is set out in the following sections.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Section 5.5.26 for a member who has an established long service leave credit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Section 5.5.28 for a member who does not have an established long service leave credit, but has at least 1 year's service. They must be leaving the ADF for a reason stated in that section.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 4: Salary and allowances during long service leave

###### 5.5.21 Salary during long service leave

| 1. | A member is eligible to receive the salary payable to them while on long service leave. |
|---|---|
| 2. | If a member was under a direction to act a higher rank under section 13(1)(b) of the Defence Regulation before the start date of their long service leave, the member’s salary is paid at the rate of the higher rank at which they were directed to act. |

###### 5.5.23 DFRT allowances during long service leave

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible to receive a DFRT allowance during long service leave if they were eligible for the allowance on the day immediately before the member commences long service leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>

#### Part 6: Maternity leave

##### Division 1: Overview

###### 5.6.1 Simplified outline of this Part

This Part provides a member with up to 52 weeks of maternity leave, which consists of both paid and unpaid leave. Maternity leave recognises the physical aspects of pregnancy, childbirth and recovery after childbirth and in particular circumstances where the pregnancy ends other than by birth of a live child. It also provides time for the care of a child once it is born.

Paid maternity leave is available to members who have completed their qualifying service (see section 5.6.4).

Members who have not completed their qualifying service may be eligible for a lesser period of paid maternity leave (see section 5.6.14).

Maternity leave may also be taken in connection with other types of paid leave (see section 5.6.18).

Division 3 specifies the periods leading up to and immediately following the birth of a child that the member is required to be on maternity leave. It also provides options if the member wishes to continue to work during the required absence.

###### 5.6.4 Definitions

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">In this Part the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Birth</b> means the birth of a child that occurs from 20 weeks before the expected date of the birth.<br><b>Note:</b> A multiple birth is a single event under this Part.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Premature birth</b> has the meaning given under section 5.6A.2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Qualifying service</b> means a continuous period of 12 months of any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Continuous full-time service in the ADF.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Any other employment recognised for the purpose of the <i>Maternity Leave (Commonwealth Employees) Act 1973</i>, subsection 6(4).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Required absence</b> means a period of absence under Division 3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Termination</b> means an event that results in a pregnancy ending, without the birth of a live child. The event must occur from 20 weeks before the expected date of the birth.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.6.5 Members this Part applies to

|  | This Part applies to a member whose pregnancy ends by a birth or a termination. |
|---|---|

###### 5.6.6 Required absence and maternity leave

| 1. | Two key concepts in this Part are required absence and maternity leave. |
|---|---|
| 2. | Required absence is the period that a member is required to be away from duty. It usually covers the later stages of pregnancy and the first few weeks after the birth. It can be reduced if the member has medical approval. Maternity leave is granted to cover the period of required absence. |
| 3. | Maternity leave is leave granted to a member who is pregnant or who has recently given birth. It has paid and unpaid components, for eligible members. |

###### 5.6.7 Termination of pregnancy – overview

| 2. | If a member's pregnancy terminates 20 weeks or later before the expected date of the birth, the member is entitled to maternity leave. |
|---|---|
| 3. | If the member's pregnancy terminates earlier than 20 weeks before the expected date of birth, the member is not entitled to maternity leave. If the member is unfit for duty, normal fitness for duty arrangements apply. |

###### 5.6.8 Leave without pay and maternity leave

|  | The unpaid component of maternity leave is a different leave type to leave without pay. The two leave types are both unpaid, but in other respects are quite different. Unpaid maternity leave cannot be refused for any reason. Unpaid maternity leave is administered under this Part. |
|---|---|

###### 5.6.10 Notice

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member must report to an ADF health facility when they believe they are pregnant.</td>
</tr>

<td></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

</tr>
</table>
