##### Division 3: Required absence

###### 5.6.23 Purpose

|  | This Division provides the period a member must be away from duty due to pregnancy.<br>**Note:** Division 4 provides the effect being on leave without pay has on required absence and maternity leave. |
|---|---|

###### 5.6.24 Period of required absence

|  | This table sets out the period a member must be absent. |
|---|---|

| Item | If the member… | then the member must be absent… |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | has a birth or termination earlier than 6 weeks before the expected date of the birth | for 6 weeks starting on the date of the birth or termination. |
| 2. | is still pregnant 6 weeks before the expected date of the birth | **from** 6 weeks before the expected date of the birth,<br>**until** 6 weeks after the actual date of the birth or termination. |
| 3. | meets all of these conditions<br>a. The member is still pregnant 6 weeks before the expected date of the birth.<br>b. The member is given permission by the CDF to continue to perform duty under section 5.6.26.<br>c. The member **is able** to continue working until the date approved by the CDF. | **from** the end of the day immediately after the day they have permission to work to,<br>**until** 6 weeks after the date of the birth or termination. |
| 4. | meets all of these conditions<br>a. The member is still pregnant 6 weeks before the expected date of the birth.<br>b. The member is given permission by the CDF to continue to perform duty under section 5.6.26.<br>c. The member **is not able** to continue working until the date approved by the CDF, because the birth or termination happens before that date. | for 6 weeks starting on the date of the birth or termination. |
| 5. | is given permission by the CDF to return to duty early under section 5.6.27. | for the period up to the end of the day they have permission to return to duty. |

###### 5.6.25 Fitness for duty and the required absence

| 1. | A member cannot be made to go on maternity leave earlier than 6 weeks before the expected date of birth. |
|---|---|
| 2. | A medical officer or doctor may declare a member unfit for duty for reasons related to their pregnancy. In this case, the normal ADF fitness for duty arrangements must apply. They apply until the member is declared fit for duty or their required absence starts. |
| 3. | The member may be considered fit for other duties. |
| 4. | One of the purposes of maternity leave is to recognise that a member may not be fit for duty because of their pregnancy. If a member is placed on convalescence at the same time as this Part provides for maternity leave, they should happen at the same time. |

###### 5.6.26 Continuing to perform duty during the required absence

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member may apply to perform duty during the period that would otherwise be their required absence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member must provide a doctor's certificate that states that they will continue to be fit for duty until a nominated date.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The certificate must be provided at any of the following times.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>At least 6 weeks before the expected date of birth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>If they have previously been given permission under this section — on or before the day they already have permission to work to.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The CDF may permit a member to continue to perform duty during what would have been their required absence. The permission must be in writing and state the day the permission ends.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">If the CDF considers it necessary, the CDF may require a supporting certificate by an ADF medical officer. It should state that the member will continue to be fit for duty until a nominated date.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">A doctor may certify a member unfit for duty for reasons related to their pregnancy. The member may later produce a medical certificate stating that they are fit for duty until a nominated date. In this case, the CDF may consider that certificate under subsection 1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="3">If the CDF has approved a member to continue to perform duty under subsection 2, the member may be granted other leave not related to their pregnancy during that period.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.6.27 Resuming duty during the required absence

| 1. | A member may apply to resume duty during the period that would otherwise be their required absence. The member must provide a doctor's certificate. It should state that the member will be fit to resume duty on a nominated date. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The CDF may permit a member to resume duty during what would have been their required absence. The permission should be in writing and state the day the member may resume duty. |
| 3. | If the CDF considers it necessary, the CDF may require a supporting certificate by an ADF medical officer. It should state that the member will continue to be fit to resume duty on a nominated date. |
| 4. | After the required absence has begun, the member may want to return to duty on a day different from the one already approved. In this case, the member must apply to the CDF, for a new decision under subsection 2. The application must be in writing. |
| 5. | The CDF must make a decision under subsection 2 on an application under subsection 1 within 7 days of receiving it. The member must be told of the decision in writing.<br>**Note:** The CDF may also allow a member to resume duty on a date after their required absence is completed. |

#### Part 6A: Premature birth leave

##### Division 1: General provisions

###### 5.6A.1 Simplified outline for this Part

Premature birth leave provides a period of paid leave to a member who has given birth prematurely, or to a member whose partner has given birth prematurely. This period of leave is in addition to a period of paid maternity leave or parental leave that the member may be eligible for.

A child is born prematurely if they are born alive and before they have reached 37 weeks’ gestation.

If a member has given birth prematurely, the member may take premature birth leave after they have taken their paid maternity leave (see Division 2).

If the member’s partner has given birth prematurely, the member may take premature birth leave before they access any parental leave (see Division 3).

###### 5.6A.2 Definitions

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">In this Part, the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Period of premature birth leave</b> means the period calculated using the following formula.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">[image: start formula period of leave equals 37 minus A end formula]</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>A</b></td>
<td>is the number of weeks’ gestation the child was at birth.<br><b>Note 1:</b> The number of weeks’ gestation can include partial weeks and cannot be less than 20 weeks.<br><b>Note 2:</b> The period of premature birth leave a member is eligible for may be affected under section 5.6A.4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Premature birth</b> means the birth of a live child that occurs between the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>20 weeks before the expected date of the birth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>37 weeks’ gestation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Qualifying service</b> has the same meaning as section 5.6.4.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.6A.3 Member this Part applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Part applies to a member on continuous full-time service who meets one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They have had a premature birth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They have a partner who has had a premature birth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note 1:</b> If a member is part of a dual serving couple, both members may be eligible under this Part.<br><b>Note 2:</b> The application of this Part is not affected by the death of the child for which the member is eligible for premature birth leave.</td>
</tr>
</table>

| 1. | A member who has not completed their qualifying service is not eligible for premature birth leave. |
|---|---|
| 2. | Despite subsection 1, if the member completes their qualifying service during the period they would be eligible to take their premature birth leave, the member is eligible for the period of premature birth leave remaining after they have completed their qualifying service.<br>**Note:** The period of premature birth leave is not extended. |

##### Division 2: Premature birth leave – member who gives birth

|---|---|

| 1. | A member is eligible for the period of premature birth leave commencing immediately after the member completes their period of paid maternity leave if they have notified of the premature birth.<br>**Note 1:** The period of premature birth leave is calculated under section 5.6A.2.<br>**Note 2:** The period of paid maternity leave is provided under section 5.6.14. |
|---|---|
| 2. | Eligibility for premature birth leave is not affected if the notification under section 5.6A.8 is made after the period of premature birth leave has commenced. |

###### 5.6A.10 Member this Division applies to

|---|---|
| 2. | The member must provide evidence of the date of birth and the expected date of birth with their application. |

###### 5.6A.12 Eligibility for premature birth leave

| 1. | A member is eligible for the period of premature birth leave unless exceptional operational requirements exist.<br>**Note:** The period of premature birth leave is calculated under section 5.6A.2. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The period of premature birth leave is taken before paid parental leave under Part 7. |

</tr>
</table>

###### 5.7.4E Member this Division applies to

<tr>

<td colspan="2">One of the following.</td>

</tr>

###### 5.7.5 Paid parental leave

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="4">A member is eligible for up to 40 days of paid parental leave if they are not eligible for paid maternity leave.<br><b>Note:</b> The child does not have to be recognised as resident family of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="4">The following conditions apply to a grant of paid parental leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="3">Paid parental leave may be taken at full pay or half pay.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="3">The minimum period of paid parental leave that may be taken at a time is one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>

<td></td>
<td>i.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>

<td colspan="2">If the leave is taken at half pay — 7 consecutive days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

<td colspan="3">Paid parental leave under subsection 1 is reduced by the following for each day the member would otherwise be required for duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">i.</td>
<td>For each day taken at full pay — 1 day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">ii.</td>
<td>For each day taken at half pay — 0.5 day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="4">Paid parental leave counts as effective service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 3: Special paid parental leave

###### 5.7.6 Purpose of special paid parental leave

|  | Special paid parental leave is to provide members with a type of leave in the early days of becoming a parent of a child in circumstances when the other parent is not available to be the primary caregiver of the child during that leave period. |
|---|---|

###### 5.7.6A Members this Division applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">This Division applies to a member if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They are not eligible for paid maternity leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They will be the primary caregiver of the child for the duration of the special paid parental leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>They have completed their qualifying service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The child in relation to whom special paid parental leave will be taken meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They are a member’s resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They have lived with the member for less than 66 weeks.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.7.6B Members this Division does not apply to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Division does not apply to a member if the child’s other parent is on any of the following types of leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Paid parental leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Unpaid parental leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>A type of leave of provided to the member’s partner by their employer, however described, for similar purposes.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.7.6C Special paid parental leave – dual serving parent

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subject to subsection 2 and section 5.7.6E, a member who is a dual serving parent is eligible for up to 10 weeks of special paid parental leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subsection 1 does not apply if the other parent of the child for whom special paid parental leave will be taken is on maternity leave unless the CDF is satisfied that the child’s other parent is not capable of providing care for the child for any of the following reasons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Disability or impairment which impacts their ability to provide care for the child.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Hospitalisation, serious illness or very serious illness.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The child has been removed by court order from the birth parent’s care.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>They are deceased.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.7.6D Special paid parental leave – other circumstances

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subject to subsection 5.7.6E, a member who is not a dual serving parent is eligible for special paid parental leave if the CDF is satisfied that the other parent, if any, of the child for whom special paid parental leave will be taken is not capable of providing care for the child for any of the following reasons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Disability or impairment which impacts their ability to provide care for the child.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Hospitalisation, serious illness or very serious illness.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The child has been removed by court order from the birth parent’s care.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>They are deceased.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">For the purpose of subsection 1, the amount of special paid parental leave for the member is an amount set by CDF that is not more than 10 weeks, having regard to the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The age of the child.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Any special needs of the child.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The amount of time the child has been living with the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Any other compelling reasons.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.7.6E How special paid parental leave must be taken

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">All the following apply to special paid parental leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The leave must be taken within 18 weeks of one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The birth of a child of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The adoption of the child by the member or the day the child will enter the member’s home in anticipation of being adopted by the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The child being placed in the member’s or their partner’s care under a permanent care order issued by a court or statutory authority or the day the child will enter the member’s home in anticipation of being placed in the member’s or their partner’s care under a permanent care order issued by a court or statutory authority.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The leave must be taken in a single continuous period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The leave may be taken in any combination of full pay or half pay that is not more than the equivalent amount of full-time leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The time limit under paragraph 1.a is increased by 1 day for each day of special paid parental leave taken at half pay.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.7.6F Special paid parental leave and effective service

|  | Special paid parental leave counts as effective service. |
|---|---|

###### 5.7.6G Member this Division applies to

###### 5.7.7 Unpaid parental leave

| 1. | A member is eligible for unpaid parental leave. |
|---|---|
|  | **Note 1:** A member is not eligible to receive salary under DFRT Determination 2017 No. 2 for periods of unpaid leave.<br>**Note 2:** The child does not have to be a member’s resident family. |
| 2. | Unpaid parental leave does not count as effective service. |

#### Part 8: War service leave

###### 5.8.1 Purpose

|  | War service leave is an additional leave benefit to provide relief from an operational area for a member who is on warlike service. It also allows them to adjust to living back in Australia and to recover from the demands of that service. |
|---|---|

###### 5.8.3 Members this Part applies to

|  | This Part applies to a member who performs warlike service in an operational area. |
|---|---|

###### 5.8.4 War service leave credit

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member may accrue war service leave credit for any day they perform warlike service in an operational area.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">Credit accrues at the rate of 18 days a year, on a pro rata basis. It is processed at the end of each fortnightly pay period, calculated using the method in subsection 3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">The amount of war service leave credit for a fortnightly pay period is calculated using the following formula and rounded to the nearest 2 decimal places.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">[image: Start formula leave credit equals start fraction A plus B over 365 end fraction times 18 end formula]</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">Where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>A</b></td>
<td colspan="2">is the number of days the member spent in an operational area while on warlike service during a fortnightly pay period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>B</b></td>
<td colspan="2">is any of the following part days which count as a full day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Any part day at the beginning or the end of the period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Any part day when the member is absent from the operational area.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.8.5 Granting leave

| 1. | The CDF may grant war service leave to a member for a period up to the period of the member's war service leave credit. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The member may only be granted a part day of war service leave in combination with a part day of recreation leave. |

###### 5.8.6 War service leave and other leave

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member takes leave after warlike service, they must take war service leave before recreation leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member does not accrue any of the following leave types while on warlike service in an operational area.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Additional recreation leave in a remote location under section 5.4.17.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Additional recreation leave in a hardship location under Chapter 16 Part 3A.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Additional recreation leave for non-warlike service under Chapter 17 Part 7 Division 3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">If eligible, the member may continue to accrue additional recreation leave under Part 4 Division 3 for sea, field or flying service.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.8.7 Debiting leave credit

| 1. | At the end of a period of war service leave, a member’s war service leave credit must be reduced by the number of days of leave granted. Weekends, public holidays and nonworking periods are not counted. |
|---|---|
| 2. | If the member takes payment instead of leave under section 5.8.9, their war service leave credit reduces by the number of days they took pay for instead of leave. |
| 3. | If a member has a part-day of war service leave credit, it can be combined with a part day of recreation leave credit in order to provide the member with a whole day of leave credit to take. |

###### 5.8.9 Payment instead of leave — during ADF service

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may approve payment instead of war service leave to a member who meets all of the following.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member is not permitted to take the leave for Service reasons.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member applies for payment instead of leave.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">If payment instead of war service leave is approved under subsection 1, the member is eligible for the sum of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">For every 5 days of war service leave credit — 7 days of salary and allowances that are payable under sections 5.4.36 and 5.4.37.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">For every remaining whole day of war service leave credit — 1 day of salary and allowances that are payable under sections 5.4.36 and 5.4.37.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.8.10 Payment instead of leave — leaving continuous full-time service

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member must be paid an amount instead of their war service leave credit in the following situations.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member leaves the Permanent Forces.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member is a Reserve member and ends a period of <b><i>continuous full-time service</b></i>.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">For the purpose of subsection 1, the member is paid the sum of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">For every 5 days of war service leave credit — 7 days of salary.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">For every remaining whole day of war service leave credit — 1 day of salary.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">For the remaining part day of war service leave credit — salary for the part of the day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.8.11 How to apply for war service leave

|  | A member must use the approved form to apply for war service leave. |
|---|---|

#### Part 9: Other leave with pay

##### Division 1: General provisions

###### 5.9.3 Purpose

|  | A range of leave types are available to a member for specific events that happen during a financial year. |
|---|---|

###### 5.9.4 Member this Part does not apply to

|  | This Part does not apply to a member on Reserve service. |
|---|---|

###### 5.9.5 Leave not to accrue under this Part

|  | Leave under this Part does not accrue. Leave or other absence that is not taken at the time of the specific event does not attract a credit for later use. |
|---|---|

###### 5.9.6 Member on a flexible service determination

|  | For a member on a flexible service determination, leave under this Part can only be taken during the member’s pattern of service. |
|---|---|

###### 5.9.7 How to apply for leave

|  | A member must apply for leave using the approved form. |
|---|---|

##### Division 2: Personal leave

###### 5.9.8 Purpose

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Personal leave is available to members who needs to attend to any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Personal matters of a compassionate nature.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Urgent personal matters if no other form of paid leave is appropriate.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.9.9 Eligibility for personal leave

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is eligible for personal leave if the CDF is satisfied of all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The personal leave is for one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>A compassionate reason.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>To attend to an urgent personal matter.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>There are exceptional circumstances that are in the interest of the ADF that warrant the granting of leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Granting the member personal leave is reasonable in the circumstances.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">In this section, <b>compassionate reason</b> means any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">One of the following applies to a close relative.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They are seriously ill.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They are very seriously ill.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>They have died.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s or their partner’s pregnancy ends other than by birth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member or a person in their household has been subject to family and domestic violence.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.9.10 Limitations on personal leave

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">A member cannot be granted personal leave if any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They have previously had personal leave for the same factual circumstances unless the CDF is satisfied it is reasonable to grant a second period of leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The period of leave is for less than one of the following periods.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>If the member is not subject to a flexible service determination — half a day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>If the member is subject to a flexible service determination — half the member’s pattern of service on the day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The leave is in relation to family and domestic violence and the CDF is satisfied that the member is the perpetrator of the violence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">The leave is in relation to the ending of a pregnancy and any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member has had a medical absence in relation to the ending of the pregnancy</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member is eligible for maternity leave in relation to the pregnancy.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td colspan="2">The leave is for attending to an urgent personal matter and all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The use of recreation leave for the absence from duty would be more appropriate.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member has sufficient recreation leave to cover the absence from duty.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 3: Carer's leave

###### 5.9.11 Purpose

|  | The purpose of carer's leave is to provide a member leave to care for and support their close relatives when they are sick or injured, or affected by an unexpected emergency. |
|---|---|

###### 5.9.12 Carer's leave

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member may be granted carer's leave by a supervisor in their direct chain of command. The supervisor must be at one of these ranks or higher.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Warrant Officer Class 2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>APS 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Carer's leave may be granted to a member who is to provide direct care and support to a close relative in any of the following circumstances.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The close relative is sick or injured.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The close relative is affected by an unexpected emergency.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">These conditions apply to a grant of carer's leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A member may be granted up to 10 working days of carer's leave in a financial year.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Only days that would otherwise be duty count towards the 10 days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Leave may be taken in broken periods.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Documentary evidence must be provided to support any application for a period of carer's leave that is longer than 3 consecutive working days, for the circumstance under paragraph 2.a.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>The member's supervisor may request supporting documents for a period of carer's leave of less than the 3 days to confirm that the use of the carer's leave is consistent with the circumstances for which it was granted.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td>Carer's leave for an unexpected emergency under paragraph 2.b, may only be granted for a maximum of 2 days for each occurrence.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.9.12A Additional carer’s leave

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">A member is eligible for additional carer’s leave if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They have used all of their carer’s leave benefit under section 5.9.12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are required to care for and support their close relative who is sick or injured, or affected by an unexpected emergency.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF is satisfied that the additional carer’s leave is reasonable having regard to the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Other forms of paid leave available to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Alternative carer arrangements.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.9.12B Additional carer’s leave – dual serving couples

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member who is a part of a dual serving couple.<br><b>Note:</b> This section does not prevent a member in a dual serving couple from being eligible for additional carer’s leave under section 5.9.12A.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member (the first member) is eligible for additional carer’s leave if all for the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They have used all of their carer’s leave benefit under section 5.9.12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are required to care for and support their close relatives who is sick or injured, or affected by an unexpected emergency.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Their partner (the second member) has a benefit to carer’s leave under section 5.9.12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The CDF is satisfied that the second member cannot return to the first member’s location to provide the required care.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The number of days of additional carer’s leave available to the first member is 10 days.</td>
</tr>
</table>

#### Part 10: Leave without pay

###### 5.10.3 Purpose

|  | Leave without pay allows a member to take leave when no other leave type is suitable. |
|---|---|

###### 5.10.4 Grant of leave without pay

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may grant a member a period of leave without pay on the member's application.<br><b>Note:</b> For a member on Reserve service, this means permission to interrupt their training obligations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">A period of leave without pay must not be longer than 2 years, unless section 5.10.5 applies.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">For subsection 1, the CDF must consider all of these criteria.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The purpose and length of the period of leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The operational efficiency of the ADF.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The member’s length of service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The extent and appropriateness of any other leave available to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>The nature of any training or study that the member intends to undertake during the period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td>The likelihood of the member resuming continuous full-time service at the end of the period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>g.</td>
<td>The personal circumstances of the member or their resident family, recognised family or recognised other persons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>h.</td>
<td>Any approved employment to be undertaken by the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Any other factor relevant to the application for leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">Leave without pay must not be used for unpaid maternity leave.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.10.5 Leave without pay to accompany partner on posting

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member who meets all these conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They have a partner.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member's partner is also a member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The member is granted a period of leave without pay to accompany their partner to a new housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member's period of leave ends on the earlier of these two days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The day a suitable posting becomes available for the member at that location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The day their partner's posting ends.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.10.5A Leave without pay to attend a court or tribunal proceeding

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member who is appearing in civilian court or tribunal proceedings for a person other than the Commonwealth.<br><b>Note:</b> A member appearing for the Commonwealth is on duty and is not required to take leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for leave without pay to attend a court or tribunal proceeding if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member has not been approved a short absence under section 5.11.30 to attend the court or tribunal proceedings.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The CDF is satisfied that it is reasonable in the circumstances.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.10.6 Allowances during leave without pay

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member granted leave without pay under this Division is not eligible for an allowance during the period of leave. This is unless subsection 2 applies.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may approve payment of an allowance during all or part of a period of leave without pay.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">For subsection 2, the CDF must consider all of these criteria.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Whether it would severely disadvantage a member, their resident family or recognised other persons if the member ceased to be eligible for an allowance during a period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member’s eligibility for the allowance immediately before the period of leave and whether the allowance would have continued if they were not on leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The personal circumstances of the member, their resident family, or their recognised other persons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The nature and status of any claim by the member against the Commonwealth for compensation or veterans’ entitlement.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>Any other factor relevant to the member’s eligibility for the allowance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">In this section, allowance includes reimbursement for costs paid.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.10.7 Effects on other conditions of service – summary

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A period of leave without pay does not count as qualifying service for any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">a.</td>
<td>Salary increments under Chapter 3 Part 2 Division 3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">b.</td>
<td>Recreation leave under section 5.4.8 if the leave without pay is for longer than 24 hours.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">c.</td>
<td>Long service leave under section 5.5.18 if the leave without pay is not for illness and is for more than 3 months.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">This subsection applies to any of the following periods of leave without pay.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">A period longer than 21 consecutive days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">A period totalling more than 21 days, if the member takes leave without pay immediately before or after another period that salary is not payable for.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">The periods in paragraphs 2.a and 2.b do not count as qualifying service for any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Defence Force Retirement and Death Benefit (DFRDB) purposes. There is still cover for invalidity benefits during the period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">A Defence Service Home Loan, for a member who must serve an initial qualifying period to get a loan.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">A benefit under the <i>Veterans’ Entitlements Act 1986</i>. After qualifying for benefits under the Act, a member has no cover under the Act for an injury or illness that happens during leave without pay.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">Leave without pay may affect maternity leave entitlements.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="3">Continuity of service for a particular benefit will not be broken by leave without pay if the conditions for the benefit are met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member continues to be entitled to medical and dental treatment while they are on leave without pay. They are not entitled to salary while they are in hospital, undergoing medical treatment, or on convalescence or absence for illness.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>7.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is not covered by compensation legislation for injuries they suffer during a period of leave without pay.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>8.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member’s furniture and effects are not to be stored for the period of leave without pay.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>9.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member on leave without pay has no eligibility for compassionate or carer's leave. This is because they are already on leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>10.</td>
<td colspan="3">Leave without pay may affect qualifying service for the Military Superannuation and Benefits Scheme (MSBS) retention benefit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>11.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member on leave without pay is not required to stay fit or deployable.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.10.8 Payment of charges

| 1. | A member must continue to pay for services or facilities they continue to receive while they are on leave without pay. |
|---|---|
| 2. | A member who has been granted leave without pay must notify the Defence Housing Australia in writing. This allows the member to arrange housing contribution payments during the leave. |

#### Part 11: Short absence

##### Division 1: Short absence for rest and recovery

###### 5.11.3 Purpose

|  | Short absence for rest and recovery provides a member with the opportunity to rest and recover from long or arduous periods of duty.<br>**Note:** A member of the Reserves on reserve days may be eligible for salary to rest and recover from long or arduous periods of duty if they meet the requirements of section 3.2.14. |
|---|---|

###### 5.11.5 Approval of absence

| 1. | A member is eligible for up to 5 consecutive days’ short absence if the CDF is satisfied that the member needs to rest and recover from a period of long or arduous period of duty. |
|---|---|
| 3. | If a member is on a flexible service determination, leave under this Part can only be granted a short absence from duty for a period during the member's pattern of service. |

###### 5.11.7 Short absence relating to Service event or activity

| 1. | A short absence under this Division granted in relation to a Service event or activity must be taken as soon as Service requirements allow after the event or activity has ended. |
|---|---|
| 2. | Only one period of short absence can be granted for an activity or event. |

##### Division 2: Short absence for removal purposes

###### 5.11.8 Purpose

|  | Short absence for removal purposes allows a member time to carry out a variety of removal tasks. |
|---|---|

</tr>

</tr>

<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="4">The person is the member's supervisor in the member's direct chain of command or supervision.</td>
</tr>

<td></td>

<td colspan="3">They are not below the following rank or APS classification.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>

<td>i.</td>
<td colspan="2">Warrant Officer Class 2.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>

<td colspan="2">APS 4.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>

<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>

###### 5.11.10 Conditions on grant of absence

<table>
<tr>

<td colspan="2">The CDF must consider whether it is reasonable to grant the absence under section 5.11.9, having regard to operational needs.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The maximum amount of short absence leave for each removal is one of the following.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>

<td colspan="2">If the removal is between one housing benefit location and another location — 2 consecutive days at each location.</td>

<td></td>

<td></td>

##### Division 2A: Short absence – not required for duty

###### 5.11.10A Purpose

|  | A short absence when not required for duty provides members with a type of short absence from duty outside of normal working hours. |
|---|---|

###### 5.11.10B Short absences – not required for duty

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A member is on a short absence for a period outside of their normal working hours if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are not required for duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are not under a restriction imposed by a Service tribunal that requires them to be on duty outside of normal working hours.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>They are not on another type of short absence under this Part.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> Normal working hours are normally identified in the member’s unit’s standing orders or shift roster.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 3: Short absence – Infectious diseases

###### 5.11.11 Purpose

|  | The purpose of this Division is to enable a member to take a short absence from duty if they are required to isolate themself for purposes relating to the control of an infectious disease. |
|---|---|

###### 5.11.13 Member this Division applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Division applies to a member required to do any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Isolate themself in response to an infectious disease.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Supervise a child who is recognised as resident family, recognised family or as a recognised other person and is required to isolate themself.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.11.13A Member this Division does not apply to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Division does not apply to a member who is required to isolate as a consequence of a private activity or private travel undertaken other than in connection with the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Leave associated with reunion travel under Chapter 9 Part 3 Division 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Leave associated with compassionate travel under Chapter 9 Part 3 Division 8.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.11.14 Short absence from duty – isolation

| 1. | Subject to subsection 2, a member is eligible for a short absence from duty for their isolation period. |
|---|---|
| 2. | If a member is required to perform duty at the place they are completing an isolation period, the member is not eligible for a short absence from duty for that period. |

###### 5.11.15 Short absence from duty – supervision

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subject to subsection 2, a member is eligible for a short absence from duty if they are required to supervise any of the following persons who required to complete an isolation period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A person who is the member’s resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A person who is a recognised other person.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If a member is required to perform duty at the place they are completing an isolation period, the member is not eligible for a short absence from duty for that period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the member has a partner who is eligible for the same benefit or a similar benefit for the same purpose, the member is not eligible for short absence from duty under this section at the same time the partner is receiving the same benefit or a similar benefit.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 4: Short absence – supervision of children

###### 5.11.16 Purpose

|  | The purpose of this Division is to enable a member to take a short absence from duty to supervise their child due to the implementation of COVID-19 control measures as advised by Commonwealth, State or Territory health authorities. |
|---|---|

###### 5.11.16A Definitions

|  | In this Division the following apply. |
|---|---|
|  | **COVID-19 control measure** means a measure taken to limit the spread of COVID-19 issued by the Commonwealth government or a State or Territory government however described.<br>**Note:** A measure may be issued for example, in the form of guidance, a public health order or directive. |

###### 5.11.17 Member this Division applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">This Division applies to a member who has a child who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The child is recognised as resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The child attends one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>A secondary school.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>A primary school.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>A preschool.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iv.</td>
<td>A kindergarten.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>v.</td>
<td>A child care provider.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.11.18 Short absence from duty – school and child care attendance

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subject to subsections 2, 4 and 5, a member is eligible for short absence from duty for an approved period if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Their resident family or recognised other person are unable to attend their school, kindergarten or child care provider because of a COVID-19 control measure.<br><b>Note:</b> This does not include a period the child would not have otherwise attended school, such as school holidays.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member must supervise their resident family or recognised other person.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">An approved period is one of the following, but must not be longer than the duration of the resident family’s or recognised other person’s inability to attend their school, kindergarten or child care provider because of COVID-19 control measure.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A period approved by the member’s Commanding Officer that is less than a total of 28 days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A greater period approved by the CDF that is up to the duration of the closure.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">In approving a period of short absence from duty, the CDF must consider the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The duration of the closure.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member’s ability to find alternative supervisory arrangements.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member is able to perform duty at the place where they are supervising their resident family or recognised other person having regard to the age and welfare of the child, the member is not eligible for a short absence from duty for that period.<br><b>Note:</b> Commanding Officers should work with members to establish suitable work from home arrangements if possible.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member has a partner who is eligible for the same benefit or a similar benefit for the same purpose, the member is not eligible for short absence leave under this section at the same time the partner is receiving the same benefit or a similar benefit.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 5: Short absence – examination attendance

###### 5.11.19 Short absence to attend an exam

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is eligible for a short absence if the CDF is satisfied that the member needs to be absent from duty for any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">To attend an examination in connection with a course of study they are undertaking.<br><b>Note:</b> The period of the short absence is the duration of the examination only.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">For local travel to and from the examination venue.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member cannot take more than 40 hours of short absence under this Division in a financial year.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">In this section, <b>course of study</b> means a course to which any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member receives assistance with the payment of the course fees under the Defence Assisted Study Scheme.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member has one of the following loans to pay their student contribution amount for the course</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>FEE-HELP.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>VET student loan.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is in a Commonwealth supported place.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> A member who is in a Commonwealth supported place may use HECS-HELP to pay their course fees or pay the course fees upfront.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.11.20 Limitations

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A short absence under this Division cannot be taken on any of the following days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A weekend.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A public holiday.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>A day on which the member is taking a full day of leave.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 6: Short absence – travel

###### 5.11.21 Purpose

|  | Short absence for travel is available to members who are granted specific types of travel or leave and have to travel for longer than 12 hours to reach their destination. |
|---|---|

###### 5.11.22 Member this Division applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">This Division applies to a member who meets one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are traveling on any of the following benefits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Recreation leave travel in Australia</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Compassionate travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>Pre-deployment leave travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iv.</td>
<td>Travel for removal purposes within Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are serving overseas and meet all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They travel to Australia at their own expense.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They are on personal leave for a compassionate reason.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>They were overseas before commencing the travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> Serving overseas includes short-term duty overseas, a long-term posting overseas and overseas deployments</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are on a deployment and travel to Australia using relief out-of-country travel fare assistance under Chapter 17 Part 7 Division 4.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.11.23 Short absence for travel

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for a short absence when they arrive at any of the following locations if the duration of the travel is more than 12 hours.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Their destination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the member has travelled to Australia at their own expense — the place where they are serving overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The number of days of short absence a member is eligible for under subsection 1 for a travel period in an item in column A of the following table is the number of days in column B of the same item.</td>
</tr>
</table>

| Item | Column A<br>Travel period (hours) | Column B<br>Number of days of short absence |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | 12 or more but less than 36 | 1 day |
| 2. | 36 or more but less than 60 | 2 days |
| 3. | 60 or more but less than 84 | 3 days |
| 4. | 84 or more but less than 108 | 4 days |
| 5. | 108 or more but less than 132 | 5 days |
| 6. | 132 or more but less than 144 | 6 days |

###### 5.11.24 Calculation of the duration of travel

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">For the purpose of section 5.11.23, the duration of travel is measured using the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the travel is within Australia — the number of hours the member would travel by most economical means between the place of origin and the destination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the leave destination is within Australia but not connected by a commercial flight or a rail service — the shortest journey time of a scheduled coach service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the travel is between an overseas location and Australia — the number of hours the member would travel by most economical means between the following locations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>If the member is travelling to Australia — from the time of departure from the overseas location to the time of entering the first port of call in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>If the member is travelling from Australia — from the time of departure from Australia to the time of entering the overseas location.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.11.25 Limitations for members serving in the Navy

| 1. | This section applies to a member of the Navy who travels on recreation leave travel. |
|---|---|
| 2. | A member is only eligible for a short absence for travel that is more than 48 hours long once in a financial year.<br>**Note:** This does not prevent the member from being granted a short absence more than once in a financial year for travel that is less than 48 hours. |

##### Division 7: Short absence – pre-deployment

###### 5.11.26 Purpose

|  | Pre-deployment leave allows a member going on a deployment overseas to finalise their personal affairs and make their farewells before they leave Australia. |
|---|---|

###### 5.11.27 Short absence before a deployment

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">A member is eligible for up to 7 days of short absence if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">It is expected the member will be in one of the following areas for a minimum of 6 months.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>An operational area.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>A defined area approved by the Minister.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is a member of the Reserves on continuous full-time service, their continuous full-time service commences more than 12 weeks before the member is expected to deploy.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF is satisfied that the short absence is reasonable having regard to the operational situation.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.11.28 When short absence before a deployment can be taken

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A short absence under this Division must be taken within the greater of the following periods before the member is expected to deploy.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>6 weeks.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A greater period set by the CDF.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 8: Short absence – civilian court proceedings

###### 5.11.29 Member this Division applies to

|  | This Division applies to a member who is appearing in a civilian court or tribunal proceedings for a person other than the Commonwealth.<br>**Note:** A member appearing for the Commonwealth is on duty and is not required to take leave. |
|---|---|

###### 5.11.30 Short absence for court appearances

|  | The member is eligible for a short absence to attend a civilian court or tribunal proceeding if the CDF is satisfied that it is reasonable in the circumstances.<br>**Note:** The CDF may also grant leave without pay in these circumstances under section 5.10.6 |
|---|---|

##### Division 9: Short absence – command directed

###### 5.11.31 Purpose

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">The purpose of a command directed short absence is to enable commanders to direct members within their unit to not attend for duty for any of the following purposes.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>To maintain unit effectiveness.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>To maintain the health and welfare of members of the unit.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.11.32 Short absence directed by command

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for a short absence on a day the member has been directed to not attend for duty for any of the following reasons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>To maintain unit effectiveness.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>To maintain the health and welfare of members of the unit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> Failure to follow a direction may result in disciplinary action under the <i>Defence Force Discipline Act 1982</i>.</td>
</tr>
</table>

#### Part 12: Public holidays – Australia

###### 5.12.1 Public holidays

| 1. | A member performing duty in Australia must observe certain days as public holidays, unless required for duty. |
|---|---|
| 2. | A member is eligible for the same public holidays as an APS employee of the Department of Defence, at the location where the member performs duty. |
| 3. | A member might be performing duty away from their primary service location. They observe a public holiday at the location where they are actually performing duty. |
| 4. | A member on recreation leave will not have their leave credit debited for public holidays that occur during the leave period. The public holidays observed will be those at the location where the member normally performs duty. |
| 5. | A member on a flexible service determination may only observe those public holidays that fall within the working days in their pattern of service. |

###### 5.12.2 Substitution of public holidays

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member may apply to the CDF to substitute a different day for a public holiday that they would otherwise observe.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">In deciding whether to grant the member’s application, the CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Any Service requirement that the member remain on duty that day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the substitute day is of cultural or religious significance to the member.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.12.3 Christmas stand-down

|  | A member is on short absence – not required for duty under Part 11 Division 2A for the Christmas stand-down period unless required for duty.<br>**Note 1:** The definition of Christmas stand-down under section 1.3.1 provides the dates of the Christmas stand-down period.<br>**Note 2:** If a day during the Christmas stand-down period is a public holiday section 5.12.1 applies. |
|---|---|

#### Part 13: Cancellation of, or recall from, leave

###### 5.13.1 Purpose

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A member may be paid an amount for costs resulting from any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are recalled from an approved period of leave for operational reasons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Their approved period of leave is cancelled.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> Members should be recalled from leave for operational reasons only. Payments under this Part are an operational cost.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.13.2 Basis

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The basis of this condition is that a member should be reimbursed for costs associated with a recall from leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">There are two types of costs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Travel costs, in some circumstances.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The cost of services that could not be used because of the recall.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member can only be reimbursed the costs of the portion of a holiday that was not used.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member can only be reimbursed costs that were not recoverable in other ways.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">It is not compensation for the inconvenience of the recall.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.13.4 Member is recalled from housing benefit location

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member is on leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member has not left their housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The member is recalled to duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member has no eligibility to recall costs.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.13.5 Member is temporarily recalled from leave location

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies to a member who meets all of these conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is on leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is away from their housing benefit location because of the leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is temporarily recalled to duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member intends to return to the leave location at the end of the recall period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is eligible for a payment set by the CDF towards the following costs associated with the recall.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">For the journey from the leave location to the place of duty and return, all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Transportation costs.<br><b>Note:</b> This travel is duty travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Meal expenses.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>If an overnight break is necessary — accommodation costs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is a parent, and their resident family and recognised other persons travel with the member, all of the following for the resident family and recognised other persons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Transportation costs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Meal expenses.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>If an overnight break is necessary — accommodation costs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">Other holiday items that the member had paid for but was not able to benefit from due to the recall.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">Other unavoidable costs associated with the recall from leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">In assessing the amount of payment under subsection 2, the CDF must consider these criteria.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The time available for the return journey.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The number of people who were required to return.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The amount of money the member had spent on holiday items that the member was not able to benefit from.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the costs are recoverable by other means.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.13.6 Costs if a member is recalled from holiday location

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies to a member who meets all of these conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is on leave, and living away from their housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is recalled to duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member ends the leave to return to duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is eligible for an amount set by the CDF towards the following costs associated with the recall.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">For the member’s return to their place of duty all of the following</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Additional travel costs that were not an expected or an ordinary part of the member’s return to duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Meal expenses.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>If an overnight break is necessary — accommodation costs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member’s resident family and recognised other persons travel with the member, all of the following for the resident family and recognised other persons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Additional travel costs that were not an expected or an ordinary part of the member’s return to duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Meal expenses.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>If an overnight break is necessary — accommodation costs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">Other holiday items that the member had paid for but was not able to benefit from due to the recall.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">Other unavoidable costs associated with the recall from leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">In assessing the amount of payment under subsection 2, the CDF must consider all these criteria.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The time available for the return journey.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The number of people who returned.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The amount of money the member had spent on holiday items that the member was not able to benefit from.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the costs are recoverable by other means.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td colspan="2">Whether it was practical for the member to restart the holiday.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.13.7 Costs if a member's leave is cancelled before it starts

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member may be reimbursed certain costs if their leave is cancelled before it begins. The leave must have been formally approved. The cancellation must be for Service reasons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The costs must not be recoverable by other means.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">These costs may be reimbursed.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Accommodation deposits or tariffs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Fares or fare deposits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Other unavoidable costs to do with a recall from leave.<br><b>Note:</b> No amount can be refunded to compensate a member for lost frequent flyer points. This is because they have no monetary value.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 5.13.8 Claiming reimbursement

|  | A member must use the approved form to claim reimbursement. |
|---|---|

###### 5.13.9 Re-credit of leave

| 1. | A member will be re-credited unused leave under section 5.4.35 when the unused leave is a result of a recall from leave order. |
|---|---|
| 2. | Additional leave travel may be granted if the conditions in Chapter 9 Part 4 Division 1 are met. |

**About this compilation**

**This compilation**

This is a compilation of *Defence Determination 2016/19, Conditions of service*, that shows the text of the law as amended and in force on 10/09/2026 (the ***compilation date***).

The notes at the end of this compilation (the endnotes) include information about amending laws and the amendment history of provisions of the compiled law.

**Uncommenced amendments**

The effect of uncommenced amendments is not shown in the text of the compiled law. The details of amendments made up to, but not commenced at, the compilation date are underlined in the endnotes. Any uncommenced amendments affecting the law are accessible on the Register (www.legislation.gov.au).

**Application, saving and transitional provisions**

If the operation of a provision or amendment of the compiled law is affected by an application, saving or transitional provision that is not included in this compilation, details are included in the endnotes.

**Modifications**

If the compiled law is modified by another law, the compiled law operates as modified but the modification does not amend the text of the law. Accordingly, this compilation does not show the text of the compiled law as modified. Any modifications affecting the law are accessible on the Register.

**Self repealing provisions**

If a provision of the compiled law has been repealed in accordance with a provision of the law, details are included in the endnotes.

### Chapter 6: ADF relocation on posting in Australia

#### Part 1A: General provisions

###### 6.1A.1 Purpose

|  | This Chapter sets out the provisions relating to relocation benefits for members and their resident family and recognised other persons when they are relocating within Australia. |
|---|---|

###### 6.1A.2 Definitions

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">In this Chapter the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Accommodation for which rent allowance is payable</b> includes accommodation where the amount of rent allowance payable is zero.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>ADF gap year</b> means a program on which a member, including a member of the Reserves, provides continuous full-time service in SERVOP G.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Essential household item</b> means an item that meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The absence of the item for more than 72 hours would unduly inconvenience the member, their resident family or a recognised other person.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The item is in everyday use in the normal household.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The member does not have an alternative item in their inventory.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Family court</b> means any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The Family Court of Western Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The Magistrates Court of Western Australia, constituted by a family law magistrate.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Furniture and effects</b> means portable household items ordinarily used for domestic purposes and convenience.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Non-portable item</b> means an item that cannot be carried by two people and would require additional equipment, such as a crane or a forklift, to move it.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Private vehicle</b> means a motor vehicle that is registered in the name of a member, their resident family or a recognised other person.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Suitable own home</b> has the same meaning given by section 7.2.5.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Towable item</b> means a caravan or trailer that is registered in the name of a member, their resident family, or a recognised other person, is roadworthy and is capable of being towed by the member's private vehicle.</td>
</tr>
</table>

#### Part 1: Relocation allowances

##### Division 1: Disturbance allowance

###### 6.1.3 Purpose

|  | A member may be compensated for some of the costs involved in a removal to a new dwelling within Australia. This Division outlines the kinds of costs covered, the conditions of eligibility and the amount payable. |
|---|---|

###### 6.1.4 Members eligible

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">A member is eligible for disturbance allowance if one of the following applies.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They are granted a removal to a new home.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They are on continuous full-time service or cease continuous full-time service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They are a member who has unaccompanied resident family and no accompanied resident family, or a member with no resident family or recognised other persons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They have been deployed for 6 months or longer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The member chose under any of sections 7.4.23, 7.6.38, 7.7.11 or 7.8.31 to leave their accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> Section 1.6.1 applies to this section and may affect the payment of the allowance if a member and an adult who is recognised as resident family are both eligible for disturbance allowance for the same period.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 6.1.5 Members not eligible

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">A member is not eligible for disturbance allowance if any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are moving from living-in accommodation in an establishment, unit or base to different living-in accommodation in the same establishment, unit or base.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are moving overseas from Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are moving between two seagoing ships that have the same home port.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are moving to another home because the combined total of resident family and recognised other persons has changed.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td colspan="2">They meet all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They are a member who has unaccompanied resident family and no accompanied resident.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They are moving to reunite with their resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The location they are moving to is specified in their alternate located work agreement.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are eligible for a removal under Part 5 Division 10.</td>
</tr>
</table>
