##### Division 10: Assistance on breakdown of relationship

###### Subdivision 1: General provisions

###### 6.5.76 Simplified outline of this Division

A relationship between a member and their partner may break down and a removal may be needed. The benefits provided in this Division are available for both a member and their former partner, and may include the removal of furniture and effects, pet relocation and private vehicle removals in Australia. This Division provides all the removal related benefits available following the end of a relationship.

The eligibility requirements that a person seeking a removal needs to meet are provided in Subdivision 2. Each person needs to be eligible in their own right before they can receive a removal.

Removals may be limited in terms of what can be removed, how many removals a person can receive under this Division and where the removals can be effected to (Subdivision 3).

Additional benefits for privately arranged removals and hiring household goods may also be available in specific circumstances (Subdivision 4).

###### 6.5.77 Person this Division applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Division applies to any of the following persons when a relationship breaks down.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A member posted to a location in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A member’s former partner.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### Subdivision 2: Eligibility for a removal

###### 6.5.78 Eligibility for removal

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A person is eligible for a removal if their relationship has broken down and all of the following are met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The person applies for a removal in writing.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF is satisfied that the removal is reasonable, having regard to the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The intention to establish separate living arrangements.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Any relevant orders made by a court.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>If the person is a member — the reason they need to vacate the property.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iv.</td>
<td>Any other relevant factor.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note 1:</b> Both people may be eligible to receive a removal under this Division.<br><b>Note 2:</b> Members receiving a removal under this Division are not eligible for disturbance allowance under Part 1 Division 1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The application for a removal under this Division must be made by the later of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the person is a member — within 90 days of notification of the breakdown of the relationship.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the person is not a member — within 12 months of notification of the breakdown of the relationship.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">A later day that the CDF is satisfied is reasonable.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 6.5.79 Number of removals

| 1. | A member is eligible for one removal under this Division in a 24-month period. |
|---|---|
| 2. | A person is eligible for one removal for the breakdown of a relationship with the same partner.<br>**Note:** Unless subsection 3 applies, if a member and their former partner reunite and separate again, neither person will be eligible for another removal. |
| 3. | The person is eligible for one additional removal if the CDF is satisfied it is reasonable in the circumstances. |

<table>

<tr>
<td>2.</td>

<td>3.</td>

<td></td>

<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>It is registered to a person in the relationship.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>It is roadworthy.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> The rules in subsection 6.5.82 apply to the removal of private vehicles and towable items.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The removal of a private vehicle means one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the person is a member — vehicle allowance as calculated under sections 9.6.25 and 9.6.26, up to the cost of transporting the vehicle.<br><b>Note:</b> Travel by private vehicle for the non-serving partner is provided for under 9.3.21.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The removal of the vehicle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">The removal of a towable item means the transport of the towable item.<br><b>Note:</b> A person may choose to tow their towable item.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a private vehicle has been removed under paragraph 3.b, the person is eligible for the reimbursement of the cost of delivering the vehicle to the transport agency’s depot and collecting the vehicle from the depot if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The person arranges for the vehicle to be delivered and picked up from a depot.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The CDF is satisfied the cost is reasonable.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6.</td>
<td colspan="2">Costs for subsection 5 include, but are not limited to, any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Drainage of fuel tanks.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Unavoidable storage charges.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Fares for the most economical means to and from the depot.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### Subdivision 4: Additional benefits

###### 6.5.83B Removal taken as privately arranged removal

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies to a person who is eligible for a removal of their furniture and effects under section 6.5.78 and takes the removal as a privately arranged removal.<br><b>Note:</b> Items that can be removed under this section may be limited by section 6.5.82.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">If the privately arranged removal is carried out by a commercial removal company, the person is eligible for one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the person is not a member and the CDF is satisfied that the removal was urgent — reimbursement of the costs the CDF considers reasonable.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">In any other circumstance — reimbursement of the lesser of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The amount of the removal had it been carried out by a Commonwealth removalist.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The actual cost of the privately arranged removal.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td><b>Note:</b> A person who takes a privately arranged removal under this paragraph is taken to have used their removal benefit under section 6.5.78.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">If the privately arranged removal is not carried out by a commercial removal company, they are eligible for reimbursement of any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The costs of hire of, and fuel for, a suitable removal vehicle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Vehicle allowance for the use of a private vehicle for the distance between the old and the new location, up to the amount payable under Division 5 of Part 6 of Chapter 9.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 6.5.83C Hire of household items

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The person is eligible to be reimbursed for the costs to hire a replacement item that was lost or damaged in connection with the removal if they meet all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The person is not a member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They received a removal under this Division.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>They live with the member’s recognised family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>They have filed an indemnity or insurance claim for the item.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>The item meets the criteria provided in subsection 6.5.13.1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The person is eligible to be reimbursed the costs of using a laundromat washing machine and dryer if all of the following are met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The washing machine or dryer is lost or damaged during a removal.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The person cannot hire a suitable replacement at the new location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">Eligibility under this section ends when any of the following occur.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The original item is delivered or repaired.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The person receives a payment for the lost or damaged item.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The member’s recognised family member no longer lives with the person.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 11: Removal on death of a member

###### Subdivision 1: General provisions

###### 6.5.84 Purpose

|  | This Division provides benefits for the removal of furniture and effects, and pet relocation when a member dies. |
|---|---|

###### 6.5.84A Definitions

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">In this Division, all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Pet relocation</b> means the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The commercial transportation and boarding of a household pet by a service provider who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They have an Australian Business Number.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They conduct a business for profit in the transportation or boarding of household pets.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>They are registered or licenced to carry out the business, as required under relevant State or Territory law.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Does not include any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The cost of the purchase of equipment or other items used for the transportation or boarding of the pet.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The costs of other goods for continued use, including pet containers.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The costs of other services, including vaccinations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iv.</td>
<td>The relocation of a pet primarily used for economic or business purposes.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 6.5.84B When a benefit must be taken

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A benefit under this Division must be taken before the later of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>15 months after the death of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A later day that the CDF is satisfied is reasonable in the circumstances.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### Subdivision 2: Removal of furniture and effects

###### 6.5.85 Removal benefit for resident family or recognised other persons

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member who met one of the following before they died.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They were a member who has accompanied resident family and no unaccompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They were a member who has recognised other persons and no resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s resident family or recognised other persons are eligible for a removal of furniture and effects limited to one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Within the same location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the member was in the Permanent Forces at the time of death — a location set out in column A of the following table subject to the conditions in column B of the same item.</td>
</tr>
</table>

| Item | Column A<br>Location | Column B<br>Conditions |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | The location within Australia of the permanent residence the member and their resident family or recognised other persons had at the time of enlistment or appointment. | No conditions apply to this location. |
| 2. | The location outside Australia of the permanent residence the member and their resident family or recognised other persons had at the time of enlistment or appointment. | The removal is limited to one of the following.<br>a. If the member was appointed or enlisted from Norfolk Island — Sydney.<br>b. If the member was appointed or enlisted from any other external territory of Australia — a capital city nominated by the resident family.<br>c. If the member was appointed or enlisted from another country — the port at which the member first entered Australia. |
| 3. | Any other location in Australia. | The member’s partner must meet one of the following.<br>a. They have established a permanent home in the location.<br>b. They intend to establish a permanent home in the location. |
| 4. | An overseas country. | The removal is limited to one of the following.<br>a. If all of the following are met — the reasonable costs of removal and travel to a location in a country that the resident family or recognised other persons wish to live.<br>i. The member was enlisted or appointed from another country.<br>ii. The resident family or recognised other persons choose to be removed before the end of the period that the member had agreed to serve in Australia.<br>b. In all other cases — costs up to the amount that would otherwise be payable under items 1 or 2. |

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">If all the following apply — a removal to a location set out in column A of the following table subject to the conditions in column B of the same item.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member was a member of the Reserves on continuous full-time service at the time of death.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member was appointed or enlisted in Australia.</td>
</tr>
</table>

| Item | Column A<br>Location | Column B<br>Conditions |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | The location where the member lived immediately before starting full-time service. | No conditions apply to this location. |
| 2. | Any other location in Australia | The cost of the removal is limited to the amount that would otherwise be payable under item 1. |

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">If all the following apply — a removal to a location set out in column A of the following table subject to the conditions in column B of the same item.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member was a member of the Reserves on continuous full-time service at the time of death.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member was appointed or enlisted from an overseas country.</td>
</tr>
</table>

| Item | Column A<br>Location | Column B<br>Conditions |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | The location of the port where the member first entered Australia. | No conditions apply to this location. |
| 2. | Any other location in Australia | The removal is limited to one of the following.<br>a. The amount that would otherwise be payable to remove the resident family to the location in Australia where the member lived immediately before starting full-time service.<br>b. The cost of a normal service removal if the CDF is satisfied that the member’s resident family have established or intend to establish a permanent home in the location after considering all of the following.<br>i. Whether the resident family have extended family in the location.<br>ii. Whether the resident family have residential property in the location.<br>iii. Employment prospects for the resident family in the location.<br>iv. Whether there is evidence of plans to move to the location made before the member's death. |

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> A removal under this section includes removal of furniture and effects from a store in any location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2A.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member was not living with their resident family at the time of death, items in the member’s possession will be removed to the person legally entitled to receive them.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2B.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s resident family or recognised other persons are eligible for a removal of the following to a location within Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Up to 2 private vehicles.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Up to 2 towable items.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> Vehicles and towable will not be moved into storage facilities.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">Any items in the resident family or recognised other persons’ possession or in storage at the time of the member’s death will be removed in the same way as items would be removed for a member who has accompanied resident family and no unaccompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 6.5.86 Removal in Australia on death of member who has no resident family or recognised other persons

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member who meets all of the following is eligible for a removal of their furniture and effects to the address of the person legally entitled to receive them.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They have no resident family or recognised other persons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They died while serving in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">Storage under subsection 2 is for the lesser of the following periods.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Until the furniture and effects are collected by a person legally entitled to take them.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Three months.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">A longer period if the CDF is satisfied it is reasonable having regard to all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The length of time needed to administer the member’s estate.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The arrangements necessary to hand over the member’s furniture and effects.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### Subdivision 3: Pet relocations on death of a member

###### 6.5.86A Eligibility for pet relocation – accompanied resident family

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member dies, their accompanied resident family is eligible for the cost of pet relocation if the CDF is satisfied the costs are reasonable.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">For the purpose of subsection 1, the CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The nature and number of the pets to be relocated.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The arrangements for the transportation and boarding of the pets.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The availability of discounted transport rates to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The travel time between the member’s housing benefit location and final destination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The pet relocation must meet all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>It is from the member’s housing benefit location to the location the member’s accompanied resident family receive a removal to under section 6.5.85.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>It occurs at the same time the member’s accompanied resident family receive a removal.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 6.5.86B Eligibility for pet relocation and boarding – no accompanied resident family

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member who dies and has no accompanied resident family is eligible for the costs of pet relocation and boarding if the CDF is satisfied the costs are reasonable.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">For the purpose of subsection 1, the CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The nature and number of the pets to be relocated.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The arrangements for the transportation and boarding of the pets.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The availability of discounted transport rates to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The travel time between the member’s housing benefit location and final destination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The pet relocation must be from the member’s housing benefit location to the location of the person legally entitled to take responsibility for the pet.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">The pet relocation must be undertaken as soon as reasonably practicable after the death of the member.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 6.5.86C How a benefit is paid

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The benefit provided under this subdivision may be paid in accordance with the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If a quote or invoice from the service provider for the proposed services is provided —before the pet is relocated.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If a receipt for the services is provided — by reimbursement after the pet is relocated.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the benefit is provided under paragraph 1.a, the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the pet relocation did not occur — the benefit must be repaid.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the cost of the pet relocation was less than the amount paid — the difference between the cost and the amount paid must be repaid.</td>
</tr>
</table>

#### Part 5A: Vehicle removals and travel

##### Division 1: General provisions

###### 6.5A.1 Purpose

|  | This Part provides members, their resident family and recognised other persons with the removal and storage of their private vehicles and travel when they change housing benefit location, family benefit location or the member goes on deployment. |
|---|---|

###### 6.5A.2 Definitions

|  | In this Part the following apply. |
|---|---|
|  | **Recreation or hobby vehicle** has the meaning given in section 6.5A.3. |
|  | **Towable item** has the same meaning as given in section 6.1A.2 and includes a recreation or hobby vehicle that is capable of being towed by the member’s private vehicle. |

###### 6.5A.3 Recreation or hobby vehicle

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A vehicle is a <b>recreation or hobby vehicle</b> if the CDF is satisfied, having considered all of the following, that the vehicle is used as a recreation or hobby vehicle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member bought the vehicle to use it for recreational purposes.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is a member of relevant clubs and associations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a recreation or hobby vehicle under restoration can be moved as a single unit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member has an active interest in restoring the vehicle as indicated by these factors.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The make and model of the vehicle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The date of acquisition.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The vehicle’s state of restoration.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iv.</td>
<td>The time the member has spent restoring the vehicle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>v.</td>
<td>The expected completion date of restoration of the vehicle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>vi.</td>
<td>The final cost of restoration.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>vii.</td>
<td>Whether the member owns special tools or equipment bought solely for restoration.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A recreation or hobby vehicle includes its trailer (if applicable) if all the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They must be moveable as a single unit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They must be capable of being freighted by the normal commercial means for freighting motor vehicles and similar items.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note 1:</b> The recreation or hobby vehicle and its trailer are transported as 1 item.<br><b>Note 2:</b> The trailer of the recreation or hobby vehicle must be registered and roadworthy if it is to be towed.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 6.5A.4 Member this Part applies to

|  | This Part applies to a member who is eligible for a removal under Chapter 6 Part 5. |
|---|---|

###### 6.5A.4A Members this Part does not apply to

|  | This Part does not apply to a member who is eligible for a removal under Chapter 6 Part 5 Division 10. |
|---|---|

###### 6.5A.5 Measurement of distances

|  | For the purpose of this Part, a distance is the number of kilometres to be travelled by the most direct and practicable route. |
|---|---|

##### Division 2: Vehicle removal assistance

###### 6.5A.6 Purpose

|  | This Division assists members, their resident family and recognised other persons to move between housing benefit locations. This may be by driving their own vehicle or travelling by another mode of transport and having the vehicle transported by freight. Whether the vehicle is transported or driven is the choice of the member, but there may be implications on their benefits. |
|---|---|

###### 6.5A.7 Vehicle this Division does not apply to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Division does not apply for a vehicle to which any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The vehicle is not owned by the member, their resident family or recognised other persons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The vehicle is not registered.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The vehicle is not roadworthy.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The vehicle is a recreation or hobby vehicle<b>.</b><br><b>Note:</b> Benefits for the removal of recreation or hobby vehicles are provided in Division 3.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 6.5A.8 Vehicle removal assistance – general

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for vehicle removal assistance for up to 2 vehicles if any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the member is eligible for vehicle removal assistance for a vehicle being driven under section 6.5A.9.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the member is eligible for vehicle removal assistance for a vehicle being transported under section 6.5A.10.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is posted to an external territory or Thursday Island, vehicle removal assistance may be to one of the following locations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member’s housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A location in Australia chosen by the member.</td>
</tr>

### Chapter 7: ADF housing and meals

#### Part 1: General information and indexes

##### Division 1: Introduction

###### 7.1.1 Simplified outline of Chapter 7

This Chapter provides housing assistance and other associated benefits when a member is:

 Posted to a location within Australia.

 Posted to an overseas location and their resident family remain in Australia unaccompanied.

Housing assistance helps members manage the hardships caused by the need to move location regularly or at short notice. Part 1 provides general eligibility to housing assistance, including when a member may or may not be eligible for housing related benefits.

If you own a home

If a member, their resident family or a recognised other person owns a home in the member’s housing benefit location or family benefit location, and the home is considered suitable, access to other forms of housing assistance under this Chapter may be limited. There are various factors provided under Part 2 which will determine if the home is considered suitable.

Housing options

If a member does not have access to a suitable own home where they are posted, or where their unaccompanied resident family lives, they may have access to a number of other housing options, including:

 Living-in accommodation (see Part 4) – This type of housing is available to members when they are undertaking training courses or operational reasons require them to stay on base. Living-in accommodation can also be used by members who have no resident family or recognised other persons living with them in their housing benefit location.

 Service residences (see Part 6) – This type of housing is provided through Defence Housing Australia and is available to members who have resident family. While this is the primary form of housing for members with resident family, if there are no Service residences available, members will still have access to other forms of housing assistance.

 Member choice accommodation (see Part 7) – This is a type of accommodation available to members who have no resident family or members who have resident family who they do not live with. A member can choose to occupy member choice accommodation as an alternative to occupying living-in accommodation or receiving rent allowance.

 Rent allowance (see Part 8) – This is a form of housing assistance that is paid to a member to assist them in paying their rent when they rent a home in the private rental market.

Part 5 provides temporary accommodation allowance for members and their families if they are unable to access housing when they initially arrive in their new housing benefit location or family benefit location. Temporary accommodation allowance assists with the costs associated with alternative accommodation as well as certain other costs, such as meals.

Buying and selling a home

There are also a number of benefits available under this Chapter to assist a member to purchase and sell a home. Part 3 has two types of benefits, one for the initial purchase of a home (HPAS), which provides a one off payment and another for the subsequent sale of that home and purchase of another home (HPSEA), which provides the reimbursement of certain costs associated with selling and purchasing a home. Some of the costs which may be covered under HPSEA include, legal/conveyancing fees, mortgage discharge/legal fees, agent’s commission and mortgage insurance. There is no limit to the number of times a member can use HPSEA.

Related benefits

In addition to housing assistance, Part 9 and Part 10 of this Chapter contain benefits for certain members to assist them with the cost of meals and utilities when they are occupying accommodation because they either have no resident family, or if they do, because they do not live in the same location as their resident family.

###### 7.1.6 Eligibility for housing assistance

|  | Housing assistance may be given to a member who needs suitable accommodation and does not have a suitable own home in their housing benefit location. The choice and type of suitable accommodation will depend on the member's category. |
|---|---|

##### Division 3: Definitions and key concepts

###### 7.1.14 Definitions

<td></td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Agent</b> means a person or organisation who is doing one of the following.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Acting on behalf of an eligible person for the mortgage, purchase or sale of a home.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Contribution</b> means the amount a member pays towards the cost of housing, meals and utilities.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Hotel</b> includes a motel, boarding house or similar accommodation, and does not include a serviced apartment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>HPAS</b> means the home purchase assistance scheme.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>HPSEA</b> means the home purchase or sale expenses allowance.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Land broker or conveyancer</b> means a person licensed or authorised under the law of a state or territory to transact business relating to the registration of titles to land.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Own home</b> means a home that the member, their recognised family or recognised other person holds an interest in as the owner of the home.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Ownership</b> of a home includes when a member, their recognised family or recognised other person holds a legal or equitable controlling interest or equal share through a company, trust, partnership or joint venture.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Rent</b> means a charge for a home for which rent allowance is payable and includes all of the following.</td>

##### Division 4: House-hunting trips

###### 7.1.18 Purpose

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">House-hunting trips allow a member to visit a new housing benefit location to find a Service residence or home for which rent allowance is payable. The ADF and the member benefits in these ways.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A Service residence, or a home that attracts rent allowance, can be arranged before the member starts duty in the new location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Members and accompanied resident family (if any) will spend less time in temporary accommodation at the new location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Costs and stress levels are reduced because members are more likely to have a door-to-door removal.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.1.19 Member who is eligible

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member who has accompanied resident family who meets all of the following conditions may apply for a house-hunting trip.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are relocating to a new housing benefit location within Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are eligible for a full removal under Chapter 6 Part 5.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>They are eligible for a Service residence or a home that attracts rent allowance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Any other member who meets all these conditions may apply for a house-hunting trip.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are relocating to a new housing benefit location within Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They intend to live in a rented home at the new location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>They will be eligible for rent allowance for that home.</td>
</tr>
</table>

<td></td>

<td>If the member travels alone — the member must occupy living-in accommodation, if practicable, and take meals from a mess at the new location.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>

###### 7.1.27 House not chosen during house-hunting trip

| 1. | The rules on accepting and rejecting a reasonable offer of a Service residence or rented home apply to a member on house-hunting trips. |
|---|---|
| 2. | If the member rejects a reasonable offer, they must repay any payment they received for the house-hunting trip. |
| 3. | A member may go on a house-hunting trip but be unable to secure suitable accommodation. Subject to section 7.1.28, they do not have to repay the payment they received for the trip. |
| 4. | If their circumstances change, a member can reject a house that they chose on an earlier house-hunting trip. This must be because it is no longer suitable accommodation. |

###### 7.1.28 Evidence of house-hunting trip costs

| 1. | House-hunting trip payments may be made before the member goes on the trip. |
|---|---|
| 2. | After the trip, the member must give copies of written records of the costs of the trip to the Toll Transitions Removal Administration Services Manager. |
| 3. | The member must repay any payment under this Part for which they do not provide a written record under subsection 2. |

#### Part 2: Suitable own home

##### Division 1: Introduction to suitable own home

###### 7.2.1 Simplified outline of Part 2

This Part provides when a member’s home is considered to be a suitable own home.

If a member or any of their recognised family owns a home in the member’s housing benefit location or family benefit location, and the home is considered suitable, access to other forms of housing assistance under this Chapter may be limited.

There are various factors which will determine if the home is considered suitable.

There are circumstances when a member’s suitable own home will become unsuitable (Division 2 and 3). In this case, there are other forms of housing assistance that can be accessed under Chapter 7.

###### 7.2.5 Suitable own home

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">Subject to section 7.2.9, a home is a suitable own home if it meets all these conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">It is owned by the member, their resident family, adult child or a person with an interdependent relationship with the member under paragraph 1.3.37.1.d.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">It is at the member's housing benefit location or family benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">It has the minimum prescribed number of bedrooms.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1A.</td>
<td colspan="3">For the purpose of paragraph 1.c the minimum number of prescribed bedrooms is the sum of each of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">For a member and their partner, if they have one — 1 bedroom.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">For every 2 children who meet all of the following — 1 bedroom.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They are the member’s resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They are of the same gender.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>They have an age difference of 4 years or less.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iv.</td>
<td>They are in Year 6 or less at school.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">For every person who is one of the following — 1 bedroom.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member’s resident family who is not included in paragraph a or b.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>A recognised other person.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>An adult child.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">Pets are not taken into account in working out whether a home is suitable.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">The CDF may decide that a smaller home is suitable for exceptional reasons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">A suitable own home includes any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">A home for which the member has received assistance under HPAS.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">A home for which the member has received HPSEA.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">A home that the member lives in at the housing benefit location and has a real or equitable interest that is not an equal or controlling interest.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="3">This subsection applies to a member who has a suitable own home that they regard as unsuitable. Their eligibility for housing assistance is assessed on the basis that they have a suitable own home until a decision is made under section 7.2.12 to declare the home unsuitable.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.2.6 Own home bought with Defence assistance

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Despite section 7.2.5, this section applies to a member who buys a home using any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>HPAS.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>HPSEA.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>A Defence Service Home Loan.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Defence Home Owner Scheme.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>Defence Home Ownership Assistance Scheme.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The home is taken to be a suitable own home.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">A home bought using a benefit listed under subsection 1 is a suitable own home if the home is in the member’s housing benefit location or family benefit location unless the home ceases to be suitable for any of the following reasons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The number of the member’s resident family or other persons has increased since the member last occupied the home.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member has an acquired disability and needs to be located near rehabilitation facilities.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The member has an acquired disability that cannot be accommodated in the home.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subsections 2 and 3 apply even if one of these events occurs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member has been approved under section 1.3.11 to have their housing benefit location extended and purchases a home in it using a benefit listed under subsection 1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member's relationship status changes.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.2.9 When a member's home is unsuitable

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">A home is not a suitable own home if any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member's own home is deemed unsuitable because it is rented out.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">All of the following circumstances apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member buys a new home in their housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

#### Part 3: Home sale or purchase

##### Division 1A: General provisions

###### 7.3.1 Simplified outline of Part 3

This Part provides members and their resident family assistance to purchase or sell a home while the member is posted within Australia.

There are two forms of assistance provided under this Part:

 HPAS (see Division 1) – A one-off payment to assist with the purchase of a home. This payment is payable once only. To access this payment the home that is purchased must be lived in and located in either the member’s current or next housing benefit location or family benefit location.

 HPSEA (see Divisions 2 and 3) – A reimbursement for costs associated with selling a home and purchasing another home that will be lived in by the member or their resident family in either the members next housing benefit location or family benefit location. There are no limits to the number of times HPSEA can be used.

A member who purchases their first home under HPAS then enters into the sell-purchase-sell home ownership cycle when they go to sell it. Each time they purchase or sell another home on a posting, they can be reimbursed the reasonable costs involved.

While time limits do apply to the sell-purchase-sell cycle, this does not mean that a home must be sold or purchased following each of the member’s postings. It remains the member’s choice if they sell and buy, however continued eligibility is dependent on a member maintaining the cycle of sell-purchase-sell.

The time limits applied to the sell-purchase-sell cycle will be paused in certain circumstances, such as when the member is posted to an overseas posting location, or to a location where they are required to live in a Service residence or living-in accommodation (see subdivisions 2 and 3 of Division 2).

A home purchased under one of these schemes is likely to be considered a suitable own home under Part 2 of this Chapter.

###### 7.3.2 Member this Part applies to

|  | This Part applies to a member, including a member of the Reserves and a former member. |
|---|---|

<table>

#### Part 4: Living-in accommodation

##### Division 1: General provisions

###### 7.4.1 Simplified outline of Part 4

This Part provides members with living-in accommodation, which is a barracks-style accommodation that is usually offered on base.

Living-in accommodation is an accommodation option available to members when they are traveling for duty purposes, undertaking training courses or when operational reasons require them to stay on base (see Division 2).

Members can also choose to stay in living-in accommodation when they have no resident family or recognised other persons living with them in their housing benefit location (see Division 2).

Members who occupy living-in accommodation do so under a licence to live in. A licence to live in provides the conditions imposed upon members while occupying this kind of accommodation. For a member who occupies living-in accommodation onshore, Annex 7.4.A applies. For a member who lives on board a seagoing vessel or nuship, section 7.4.42 applies.

There are various factors that will determine the level of living-in accommodation that is suitable for a member and whether they will be required to share the accommodation with other members (see Division 3).

Generally, members occupying living-in accommodation are required to pay a contribution (see Division 4). The reason a member is occupying living-in accommodation will determine if the member needs to pay a contribution towards the accommodation or not (see Division 5). Rates of contribution are found in Annex 7.4.B.

There are specific provisions that apply to a member who is posted to a seagoing vessel or nuship and chooses to live on board (see Division 6). A member’s personal circumstances will determine if they are required to make a contribution towards their accommodation and meals while living on board.

###### 7.4.1A Member this Part does not apply to

<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Part does not apply to a member who is in the housing benefit location and on any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A transition location (general) agreement.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A transition location (medical) agreement.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.4.2 Principles for the provision of living-in accommodation

| 1. | Living-in accommodation is provided to meet the operational, training and duty of care responsibilities of the Department of Defence. |
|---|---|
| 2. | Members who occupy living-in accommodation are subject to the responsibilities and conditions that apply under the licence to live in provisions. |
| 3. | Members occupying living-in accommodation make a contribution based on rank, number of beds per room and the level of accommodation. |

###### 7.4.3 Definitions

|  | In this Part the following apply. |
|---|---|
|  | **Accommodation manager** means a person responsible for managing living-in accommodation on behalf of the Department of Defence. |
|  | **Common areas** means areas inside and outside of the accommodation buildings which can be used or accessed any member occupying the accommodation building. |
|  | **Fair wear and tear** means the normal deterioration of an element of the room or building due to the ageing process and use. |
|  | **Key** includes an access card or a keypad access code. |
|  | **Non-fair wear and tear** means the faster deterioration of an element of the room or building caused by neglect or mistreatment. |
|  | **Nuship** means a Navy ship not yet commissioned into naval service. |
|  | **On-board member** means a member who chooses not to keep on-shore accommodation at the ship’s home port or refitting port. |
|  | **Service property** has the meaning given in the *Defence Force Discipline Act 1982*. |
|  | **Shore member** means a member who keeps on-shore accommodation at the ship’s home port or refitting port. |

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member has no unaccompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The member has suitable accommodation in the housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The CDF is satisfied that the member is unable to live in their suitable accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member who meets the conditions in subsection 1 may choose, in writing, to live in accommodation described in subsection 7.4.9.1. They must pay a contribution at the rate for a member on leave without pay.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member who meets all of the following may choose to live in under section 7.4.9 regardless of any other accommodation they own in the housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They have unaccompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They have no accompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.4.11 Living-in accommodation not available

|  | If living-in accommodation is not available to a member, the member may be eligible for rent allowance under section 7.8.5. |
|---|---|

###### 7.4.12 Responsibility for living-in accommodation

| 1. | When the member takes the key to living-in accommodation from an accommodation manager, the member must acknowledge in writing that they will take strict care of the property they live in under the licence.<br>**Note:** If the member fails or refuses to give written acknowledgement that they will take strict care of the living-in accommodation, no licence to live in will be given. |
|---|---|
| 2. | To help minimise the cost of damage to living-in accommodation, a member must immediately notify an accommodation manager of any damage affecting a room they live in or use, or the common areas.<br>**Note:** If the living-in accommodation is damaged while the member is its custodian, then the member may be required to pay the costs related to the damage as a debt to the Commonwealth, unless the member can demonstrate that reasonable steps were taken to prevent the damage. |

###### 7.4.13 Condition reports

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">When a member moves into living-in accommodation, the member must be given a report listing the condition of the accommodation and its contents.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member has 48 hours, or the first working day after the 48 hours, to assess the report, take any of the following actions and return the report to an accommodation manager.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Sign the condition report to show that they agree with it.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If member disagrees with all or part of the condition report – write the reason that they disagree on the report and sign it.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">On receipt of the condition report, if the accommodation manager disagrees with the member's assessment of their allocated room then all of the following items must be placed on file with the report.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Photographs of the room.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A signed document listing the name of the photographer, time, date and location of the photographs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member does not return the condition report within the time specified in subsection 2, it is taken that the member agrees with the condition report.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">All of the following actions must occur before the member's licence to live in ends.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A member's living-in accommodation is inspected in the presence of the member or the member's agent.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The inspection is to be done having regard to the condition report.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6.</td>
<td colspan="2">The accommodation manager may waive a condition report when the member will only be in the accommodation for a short period of time.<br><b>Note:</b> If a condition report has been waived it is at the accommodation manager's and the member's own risk.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>7.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member, whose condition report has been waived under subsection 7, may request a condition report from an accommodation manager.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.4.14 Revoking a licence to live in

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member's licence to live in may be revoked for a period of up to 3 years if the CDF is satisfied any of the following have occurred.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member has deliberately, recklessly or negligently breached the conditions listed in Annex 7.4.A.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member fails, or refuses, to comply with any reasonable request or direction from an accommodation manager relating to their living-in accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The member fails to give notice that the living-in accommodation will be unoccupied for at least 28 consecutive days, unless the absence is due to an emergency, or a situation which is beyond the member’s control has occurred.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1A.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subsection 1 does not apply to a member who is under the age of 18.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">In making the decision in subsection 1, the CDF must have regard to any relevant considerations, including any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The nature and severity of any breach by the member, including any risk assessment of the effect on other members in the living-in accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Any pattern of similar behaviour by the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Whether the member is required to occupy living-in accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Whether revocation would affect the member's ability to perform their duties.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>If any hardship is likely to be caused to the member if their licence to live in is revoked, including the availability of reasonable quality off-base accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF must advise the relevant contract service provider and the member's Service when a member's licence to live in has been revoked.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member whose licence has been revoked under this section is not eligible for living-in accommodation, rent allowance or a Service residence while their licence to live in is revoked.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member may seek redress of a decision to revoke a licence to live in made under this section.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 3: Suitable living-in accommodation

###### 7.4.15 Suitable living-in accommodation

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Living-in accommodation is suitable for a member if it is available and meets all of the following conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>It is in the member's housing benefit location or temporary duty location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>It is fit to live in at the time the member is issued with their room key.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>It is at a level in column B that corresponds with the member's reason for occupying living-in accommodation or rank group in column A of the same item in the following table.</td>
</tr>
</table>

| Item | Column A<br>Reason for occupying living-in accommodation or rank group | Column B<br>Level of accommodation |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | Transit or short visit to the location. | Any available level |
| 2. | Completion of compulsory residency, training or post-graduate work experience by a medical officer, Chaplain or Maritime Spiritual Wellbeing Officer. | Any available level |
| 3. | Exercise or preparation for deployment. | Any available level,<br>including shared rooms,<br>camps and tents |
| 4. | Basic recruit training as a normal entry recruit or Reserve recruit. | Level 1 |
| 6. | Initial employment training in the Infantry Corps of the Army. | Level 1 |
| 7. | Initial Employment Training other than in the Infantry Corps. | Level 3 |
| 8. | Career development training for less than 6 months. | Level 3 |
| 9. | Initial officer training. | Level 3 |
| 10. | Training for a period of 6 months or more for reasons other than those in items 3 to 8. | Level 5 |
| 11. | For an operational purpose for a period of 6 months or more. | Level 5 |
| 12. | To fill a specific position on a base for a period of 6 months or more. | Level 5 |
| 13. | To provide respite for a member posted to a seagoing submarine alongside in port that is not the vessel’s home port. | Level 5 |

| 2. | If suitable living‑in accommodation is not available at the level set out for the member under paragraph 1.c table items 1 to 12, the member may occupy living‑in accommodation that is available closest to the level listed for them in the table. |
|---|---|
| 3. | If suitable living-in accommodation is not available for the member under paragraph 1.c table item 13, suitable living-in accommodation is commercial accommodation provided by the contracted service provider under Chapter 9. |

###### 7.4.17 Change in member's rank group

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member's rank changes, the member's rank group for living-in accommodation may change under section 7.4.16.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member changes rank group, the CDF may take any of the following actions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Offer the member living-in accommodation under section 7.4.9, at a level that corresponds to the new rank group.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>End the member's licence to live in their accommodation in accordance with a notice to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Allow the member to remain in the accommodation they are currently in and pay the relevant contribution for that accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> This may affect the rate at which the member must contribute to the cost of living-in.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.4.18 CDF may decide that accommodation is unsuitable

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may decide that living-in accommodation is unsuitable for a member. The CDF must consider these factors.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Anything that prevents accommodation being lived in. It need not relate to the group level of accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Anything that makes the member's individual situation exceptional when compared with that of other members.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the CDF decides that the accommodation is unsuitable, the CDF may end a member's licence to live in. The CDF should consider whether other accommodation is available.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member's licence to live in has been ended under this section the member may still be eligible for living-in accommodation, rent allowance or a Service residence.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.4.19 Member required to share room

| 1. | Subject to subsection 2, a member occupying living-in accommodation will have their own room. |
|---|---|
| 2. | A member may be required to share living-in accommodation if they are in one of the groups in the following table. |

| Item | A member in this group... | may be required to share... |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | normal entry recruit or Reserve recruit during basic recruit training, in item 4 of the table in section 7.4.15 | with 3 or more other members per room. |
| 3. | initial employment trainee in the Infantry Corps of the Army in item 6 of the table in section 7.4.15 | with at least one other and up to 9 other members per room. |
| 4. | any member the rank of Major (E) or below | by the CDF, when there are not enough rooms for one each. |

###### 7.4.23 Living-in accommodation on deployment – 6 months or longer

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They occupy living-in accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Subject to subsection 1A, they are deployed for 6 months or longer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1A.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section does not apply to a member who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member is deployed for a period of less than 6 months.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>While deployed, the member's deployment is extended.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The total period of a member's deployment is 6 months or longer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member may make a choice between the following options.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>To keep the living-in accommodation for the period of the member's deployment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>To leave the living-in accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The choice in subsection 2 must be in writing to the member's Commanding Officer and made before the member is deployed.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member who fails to make a choice under subsection 2 is taken to have chosen to keep the living-in accommodation under paragraph 2.a.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member who has made a choice under paragraph 2.a must vacate the living-in accommodation if the CDF is satisfied of any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The living-in accommodation is required for other members.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The living-in accommodation requires maintenance or repair.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6.</td>
<td colspan="2">If subsection 5 applies, the member is treated as a member who chose to leave the living-in accommodation under paragraph 2.b.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 4: Contribution for living-in accommodation

###### 7.4.24 Contribution for living-in accommodation

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member must pay a contribution towards the cost of occupying living-in accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member who occupies living-in accommodation for more than 1 day is not required to make a contribution for the last day they occupy the living-in accommodation.<br><b>Note:</b> Additional contributions under section 7.4.30 may apply after the licence to live in ends.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">The rate of contribution a member must pay is one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is paid at a rank listed in items 1 to 4 in column A of the table in Annex 7.4.B and occupies a room with the number of beds in column B of the same item, the contribution is the rate in columns C to G of the same item that applies to the member's accommodation level.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member is paid at a pay grade listed in item 5 in column A of the table in Annex 7.4.B and occupies a room with the number of beds in column B, the contribution is the rate of the contribution per fortnight specified for the same item.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member meets one of the following and is paid at a rank in items 1 to 4 in column A of the table in Annex 7.4.B, the contribution is the amount in column E that corresponds with the number of beds in the room that the member occupies in column B of the same item.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member is a medical officer occupying living-in accommodation during compulsory residency.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member is in training as a Chaplain and is occupying living-in accommodation at a seminary or theological college.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The member is a Maritime Spiritual Wellbeing Officer occupying living-in accommodation at an educational institution during compulsory post‑graduate work experience.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">If paragraphs a. to c. do not apply and the member meets one of the following, the contribution is the rate specified in columns C to E of the table in Annex 7.4.B that applies for the members rank in items 1 to 4 of column A of the table for a member holding the same rank and occupying a room with 1 bed.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>A medical officer who is required to occupy living-in accommodation during compulsory residency.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>A Chaplain in training who is required to occupy living-in accommodation at a seminary or theological college</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>A Maritime Spiritual Wellbeing Officer who is required to occupy living-in accommodation in at an educational institution during compulsory post‑graduate work experience.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member who chooses to occupy living-in accommodation goes on a period of leave without pay, the contribution is the rate specified in subsection 7.4.27.2 for the type of living-in accommodation they occupy.<br><b>Note:</b> Section 7.4.9 provides that a member may choose to live in if the CDF approves based on there being accommodation available that is not required for members who are required to live in.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.4.27A Member on a flexible service determination

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="4">This section applies to a member who meets all of the following conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member is on a flexible service determination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member has no unaccompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member occupies living-in accommodation at the gaining location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="4">Subject to subsection 3, a member pays the rate of contribution that applies to the member’s circumstances under Annex 7.4.B for living-in accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="4">The rate of contribution is 150% of the rate that would have been payable by the member under subsection 2 for one of the following periods.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="3">Unless subsection b applies, the period commencing on the 29th day of a continuous nonworking period and ending on the last day of the same nonworking period.<br><b>Note:</b> This applies to each nonworking period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="3">The whole period of the member's flexible service determination if the total number of days that are the member's pattern of service in the member's flexible service determination is one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a period in the flexible service determination is 1 year — less than 130 days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a period in the flexible service determination is part of a year — less than the number of days calculated using the following formula.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">[image: Start formula number of days equals 130 times start fraction FSD over 365 end fraction end formula]</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td><b>FSD</b></td>
<td>is the number days in the period of the member's flexible service determination that is less than 1 year.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="4">If the member's pattern of service changes for a reason specified in the flexible service determination and the member has an incomplete cycle, one of the following applies.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="3">If the member's contribution decreases, the member must be reimbursed the difference between the following two amounts.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td colspan="2">The contribution that the member has paid for the member's cycle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td colspan="2">The contribution that the member would have paid for the member's incomplete cycle under the changed pattern of service<i>.</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="3">If the member's contribution increases, the member is not required to repay any amount for the incomplete cycle<i>.</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="4">If the member's flexible service determination is varied for Service reasons, the member will be reimbursed the difference between the following two amounts.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="3">The contribution that the member has paid during the period of the variation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="3">The contribution that the member would have paid during the period of the variation.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.4.27B Member who has unaccompanied resident family and no accompanied resident family on a flexible service determination

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="5">This section applies to a member who meets all of the following conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="4">The member meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">i.</td>
<td colspan="2">They have unaccompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">ii.</td>

###### 7.4.30 Vacating living-in accommodation

| 1. | A member ceases to be eligible to occupy living-in accommodation at the end of the day their licence to live in ends. |
|---|---|
| 2. | If any of the circumstances set out in column A of the following table apply to the member on the day they are required to vacate their living-in accommodation, they must pay the contribution set out in column B of the same item. |

| Item | Column A<br>Member Circumstance | Column B<br>Contribution |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | They do not vacate the accommodation when their licence to live in ends. | The rate that applies to the member under section 7.4.24 until they vacate the accommodation. |
| 2. | They vacate the accommodation, but it was not left in its former state, excluding fair wear and tear. | All of the following.<br>a. Costs of repairing non-fair wear and tear.<br>b. Any additional cleaning costs (excluding for fair wear and tear) required to return the room to its former state. |
| 3. | They vacate the accommodation, but do not remove rubbish, items or possessions. | Costs of removing and cleaning required to return the accommodation to its former state, excluding for fair wear and tear. |
| 4. | They do not return the key, even if the accommodation can be reallocated. | Costs of securing the accommodation and controlling access. |
| 5. | The accommodation is not reallocated because they did not return the key. | All of the following.<br>a. The rate applicable to the member under section 7.4.24 until the earlier of the following.<br>i. The date the member returns the key.<br>ii. The date the accommodation is secured and is available to be reallocated.<br>b. If the member does not return the key, the cost of replacing it. |

| 3. | If the member does not pay the contribution under subsection 2, the costs may be recovered from the salary and allowances payable to the member. |
|---|---|

###### 7.4.31 Failure to make contributions

<table>
<tr>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member must pay the amount within a reasonable time of a request.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the member fails to make the payment of contribution for living in accommodation under paragraph a, then the amount may be recovered from any amount of salary and allowances payable to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>If the amount cannot be recovered under paragraph b, it is to be treated as a debt under the <i>Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013.</i></td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 6: Members posted to seagoing ships and nuships

###### 7.4.38 Basis

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Division applies these principles to living-in benefits for members posted to seagoing vessels and Nuships.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Members who have chosen to live on board their ship do not pay for accommodation or meals taken on board.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Members who choose not to live on board their ship are only eligible for meals on board when they are on duty there over a meal period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Members eligible for free meals on board while on duty may be eligible to take those meals in a mess ashore when the ship's galley is not operating.</td>
</tr>
</table>

| 3. | Away from the home port | Less than 6 months | $0. |
| 4. | Away from the home port | 6 months or more | The amount for accommodation, utilities and meals that applies for their rank, level of accommodation and mess arrangements. |

| 2A. | A member posted to an uninhabitable ship who is shore bound in the location in column A of the table for the period in column B of the same table item must pay the contribution in column C of the same table item. |
|---|---|

| Item | Column A<br>Location | Column B<br>Duration | Column C<br>Contribution |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. | At the home port | Any duration | The amount for accommodation, utilities and meals that applies for their rank, level of accommodation and mess arrangements. |
| 2. | Away from the home port | Less than 6 months | $0, while they contribute for living-in accommodation in their home port.<br>Otherwise, the amount for accommodation, utilities and meals that applies for their rank, level of accommodation and mess arrangements. |
| 3. | Away from the home port | 6 months or more | The amount for accommodation, utilities and meals that applies for their rank, level of accommodation and mess arrangements.<br>**Note:** The member is not eligible to keep their living-in accommodation in the ship's home port. |

<table>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">Despite subsection 2 and 2A, the contribution rate for a member who meets all of the following is $0.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They have unaccompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They have no accompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
</table>
