##### Annex 7.4.A: Licence to live in

Part 1: Quick guide

|  | **Note:** The quick guide in this Part must be read in conjunction with the information provided in Part 2 of this Annex, Conditions of licence to live in. |
|---|---|

###### 7.4.A.1 What is a licence to live in?

| 1. | Living-in accommodation is made available for members of the ADF. |
|---|---|
| 2. | You might be required to occupy living-in accommodation, or you might choose to. |
| 3. | When a room becomes available for you, and you are permitted to live in it, you hold a licence to live in. |

###### 7.4.A.2 What you get

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">When you have a licence to live in, you get all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A lockable room in living-in accommodation, other than barrack style accommodation or a shared room that is suitable for your rank and situation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Access to common areas and facilities at the living-in accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Privacy to use the assigned room and facilities without unreasonable interference by Defence, other than in barrack style accommodation or a shared room where accommodation is not private.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Maintenance and repair of the living-accommodation provided in a timely manner by Defence.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.4.A.3 What you must do and not do

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Your licence to live in is conditional on you complying with rules set out in this Annex.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The main conditions that you must comply with are as follows.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>When you take the key to your living-in accommodation from the accommodation manager, you must acknowledge in writing that you will take strict care of the property that you are to live in under the licence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>You must not let another person live in your room without Defence permission.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Ensure that your room remains in the same condition as on the day you first live in it, other than fair wear and tear.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>You must not intentionally, recklessly or negligently cause damage to any part of the accommodation or common areas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>You must avoid any disturbance, nuisance or annoyance to other members.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td>You must tell Defence if you notice a hazard in your room or other part of the accommodation or common areas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>g.</td>
<td>You must not make any alterations to your room without written consent from Defence.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.4.A.4 What happens if you do not comply with the conditions of the licence

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">These circumstances may apply if you fail to comply with the conditions in this Annex.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Defence may revoke your licence and you will have to move out. You will not be eligible for rent allowance or a Service residence while the licence to live in is revoked.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>You might have to pay for cleaning or repairs to damage that you caused.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>You might have to keep contributing to the cost of the accommodation for a period, even though you have moved out.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>You might face disciplinary action.</td>
</tr>
</table>

Part 2: Conditions of licence to live in

###### 7.4.A.5 Member must comply with the conditions in this form

| 1. | A member who is required to occupy living-in accommodation, or who chooses to, may be permitted to occupy living-in accommodation made available by Defence. That permission is the member's licence to live in. |
|---|---|
| 2. | A member of the ADF has a licence to live in when they are permitted to occupy living-in accommodation by Defence. |
| 3. | Living-in accommodation is a benefit made available to members under section 58B of the *Defence Act 1903.* A licence to live in is not an agreement, tenancy or contract between a member and the Commonwealth. |
| 4. | This Annex sets out the conditions upon which a member is permitted to occupy and use living-in accommodation. These are conditions on the licence to live in. |
| 5. | The conditions in Chapter 7 Part 4 do not limit the legal authority of ADF commanders to issue commands or general orders associated with the use of living-in accommodation by ADF members. |

###### 7.4.A.6 Start of a licence to live in

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">When the member takes the key to their living-in accommodation from an accommodation manager, the member must acknowledge in writing that they will take strict care of the property they live in under the licence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member's licence to live in commences from the day they are given the key to the room that they are permitted to live in under subsection 1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">Defence may provide the member with a list of the room's contents, listing the condition of the contents and the condition of the room, fixtures and fittings. This is called a condition report.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member must return the condition report to an accommodation manager within 48 hours of receiving it, or the first working day after the 48 hours, after doing any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Sign the condition report to show that they agree with it.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the member disagrees with all or part of the condition report – write the reason that they disagree with the contents of the report, sign it.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">Failure to return the condition report within the required period will be taken to be an implied agreement by the member of the contents of the report.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6.</td>
<td colspan="2">Defence may decide not to provide a condition report if it is reasonable to expect that the member will only be in the accommodation for a short period of time.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>7.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member may request a condition report if Defence does not provide one.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.4.A.7 Permitted use

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The licence to live in is for the member only. Only the member may use the assigned room as a private residence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Another member can only live in the room if that member is permitted by Defence to access and use it too.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member must not allow another person to live in the room unless any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The room is a shared room and there is a requirement to share the room.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>It is permitted by the accommodation manager or the contracted service provider.<br><b>Note:</b> This would be in exceptional circumstances and for a short period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member may use any of the following common areas and shared amenities.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The common areas and shared amenities allocated to their rank group in the complex in which their assigned room is located.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Other common areas and shared amenities permitted by the accommodation manager.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.4.A.8 Care of the living-in accommodation

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member must ensure that their assigned room remains in essentially the same condition as when they started to occupy the room, other than due to any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Fair wear and tear.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Events outside a member's control, like a flood, earthquake or cyclone.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member must comply with all of the following drawn from the condition in subsection 1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member must not make any alterations to a room they live in or use without written consent from an accommodation manager.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member must not alter, remove or add any lock or security device to or in their assigned room.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The member must not mark, deface or paint a room they live in or use, common areas in the building, or the areas surrounding the building.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member must take care of the room they live in and any common areas they are permitted to use. The member must keep them in a clean and tidy condition.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member must inform an accommodation manager immediately whenever maintenance or repairs are needed. This means that if the member becomes aware of any defect in the water, gas, drainage, sewerage or electrical installations, appliances, furniture, or fittings, they must inform an accommodation manager.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member must not engage a repair person or make repairs without an accommodation manager's permission.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6.</td>
<td colspan="2">Defence will undertake any repairs and maintenance that the member is not required to under the conditions in this section, in a reasonable time.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.4.A.9 Conduct and values

| 1. | A member must comply with the conditions of conduct specified in this Annex while they occupy living-in accommodation. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The member must also comply with conditions of conduct set out in any instructions made under section 10 of the *Defence Act 1903* which are relevant to conduct and behaviour. |
| 3. | Additional conditions for use of the accommodation may be set from time to time by the accommodation manager, Senior Australian Defence Force Officer or the Commanding Officer/Officer Commanding. A copy must be given to the member. The member must comply with the conditions, as long as they are lawful. |
| 4. | If the member does not comply with the conditions of conduct, the CDF may revoke the licence to occupy living-in accommodation. |

###### 7.4.A.10 Conduct – animals

|  | The member must not keep animals in the living-in accommodation. |
|---|---|

###### 7.4.A.11 Conduct – damage

| 1. | The member must not intentionally, recklessly or negligently cause damage to any part of the living-in accommodation, furniture, fixtures or fittings, or common areas. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The member must immediately notify the accommodation manager of any damage affecting the living-in accommodation or common areas. |

###### 7.4.A.12 Conduct – disturbance

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A member must not do any of the following</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Cause undue disturbance, nuisance or annoyance to other members.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Throw anything out of windows or off balconies, or place anything on outside window sills.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Hang clothes, washing, equipment or other similar articles in any place not specifically provided for the purpose.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Obstruct or impair access to accommodation or common areas.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.4.A.13 Conduct – lighting, heating and cooking

| 1. | The member must not use any means of lighting, heating, or cooking in a room they live in or use, or common areas of the building, except in the place and the manner provided for by Defence in the room or building, unless the use of additional appliances is approved by the accommodation manager. |
|---|---|
| 2. | If a member triggers a false fire alarm, the member may have to pay Defence for the cost of any emergency services called out if Defence has been charged for the call out. The member's action may have caused a debt under the *Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013.* |

###### 7.4.A.14 Conduct – security

| 1. | The member must notify an accommodation manager as soon as possible after they become aware that an accommodation key they have been issued is lost. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The member must pay Defence for the cost of replacing the key or lock, or resetting the access code. |

###### 7.4.A.15 Conduct – smoking

| 1. | The member must not smoke in any room they live in or use, or common areas of the building. |
|---|---|
| 2. | If a member triggers a false fire alarm, the member may have to pay Defence for the cost of any emergency services called out if Defence has been charged for the call out. The member's action may have caused a debt under the *Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013.* |

###### 7.4.A.16 Conduct – vehicles

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member must not keep a vehicle at the living-in accommodation if any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>It is not roadworthy.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>It is unregistered, unless the car’s registration expires while the member is on an overseas deployment.<br><b>Note:</b> The member must register their car as soon as practicable on their return to their accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Members may conduct any of the following activities only in areas designated by Defence for that purpose.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Park vehicles.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Wash vehicles.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Maintain vehicles.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">Members must not use the living-in accommodation for vehicle storage or maintenance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3A.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member may store bicycles in their accommodation if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>No lockable storage is provided in connection with the accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The accommodation manager is satisfied it is safe to store the bicycle in the member's accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member must observe all of the following rules relating to neatness.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member must clean up any spills caused by the vehicle at once.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The car park or parking spot must be kept in a tidy condition.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Vehicle parts and engines may not be stored in a car park or parking spot.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.4.A.17 Conduct – visitors

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is not permitted to have a visitor stay overnight in the living-in accommodation unless subsection 2 applies</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The Commanding Officer or accommodation manager may permit any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Grant permission for a visitor to stay overnight.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">In exceptional circumstances, grant permission for a person recognised as one of the following to live with them in the living-in accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>A recognised other person.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> The person must comply with the conditions set out in this Annex.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.4.A.18 Access to a member's room

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is entitled to privacy to use the assigned room and facilities, without unreasonable interference by Defence. However, the member does not have exclusive possession of their assigned room.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The Commanding Officer or a person they authorise may enter a member’s assigned room for reasons of command or discipline, or in an emergency.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">All of the following apply in regard to access to a member's room.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Defence or its contractors may enter the room to undertake cleaning, maintenance or repairs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Prior notice must be given to the member.<br><b>Exceptions:</b><br>1. In an emergency.<br>2. If it is not possible to give prior notice.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>If Defence enters a room without a member’s permission and not in the presence of the member, a notice advising that the room has been entered and the purpose of the entry must be affixed to the member's door (or other highly visible spot).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">Room inventory and condition inspections may occur at least every 6 months during a member's stay in living-in accommodation. An individual’s room may be inspected more frequently as required by the Commanding Officer/Officer Commanding at the living-in accommodation.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.4.A.19 Swapping rooms

| 1. | A member may apply to the accommodation manager for approval to swap their assigned room. If the approval is granted, the member is given a new licence to live in for the new room. The licence to live in for the old room ends. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The member must not transfer the licence to live in to another person. |

###### 7.4.A.20 Moving furniture and fittings

| 1. | The member must get written permission from the accommodation manager before they remove any property, furniture or fittings (with the exception of property owned by the member) from their room to another location, other than to another room on a short-term and temporary basis. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The member must not remove any of the property, furniture or fittings provided for use in other rooms or common areas, such as the dining room, common room, or another living-in room to their assigned room, unless it is equipment provided for short-term use in the member’s room. |

###### 7.4.A.21 Absence from the accommodation

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member must inform the accommodation manager in writing if the member expects the assigned room will be unoccupied for 21 days or longer for reasons other than any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>An emergency.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Another situation beyond the member’s control.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> Section 7.4.14 provides that failure to give notice that the living-in accommodation will be unoccupied for at least 28 consecutive days, unless the absence is due to an emergency, or a situation which is beyond the member’s control has occurred, may result in the members licence to live in being revoked for up to 3 years.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member fails to give that notice, then the CDF may revoke the licence to live in under paragraph 7.4.14.1.c because the member has abandoned their responsibilities under the licence.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.4.A.22 When a licence to live in ends

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A licence to live in ends on whichever of the following dates happens first.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The day set out in a notice given to the member by Defence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The last day of the fixed period of the licence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The day set out in a notice that the member gives to Defence under subsection 2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>

#### Part 5: Temporary accommodation allowance

##### Division 1: General provisions

###### 7.5.1 Simplified outline of Part 5

This Part provides temporary accommodation allowance to members to support them, or a person in their household, when the need to occupy temporary accommodation arises. Temporary accommodation allowance is provided when other accommodation is unable to be accessed. It assists with the costs associated with alternative accommodation as well as certain other costs, such as meals.

Temporary accommodation may be required for various reasons, including as part of a removal, when suitable accommodation is not available, or in an emergency under the SAFE scheme.

The SAFE scheme provides emergency assistance for persons who cannot remain in their home due to a domestic crisis, whether actual or threatened.

There are a number of different kinds of temporary accommodation available (see Division 2). The kind of temporary accommodation used and the period that it is occupied (see Division 3) will determine the rate of temporary accommodation allowance (see Division 4) and the contribution required to be paid towards the cost of the accommodation by the member (see Division 5 and Annex 7.F).

###### 7.5.2 Definitions

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">In this Part the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Accommodation</b> means any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A Service residence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A suitable own home.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>A home for which rent allowance is payable.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Accommodation provided under Part 7.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Suitable accommodation</b> means accommodation that has enough furniture and effects for a member and their resident family and recognised other persons to live in it on a normal domestic basis.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.5.3 Definitions – SAFE scheme

|  | In this Part the following apply in relation to the SAFE scheme. |
|---|---|
|  | **Member** includes any person eligible for a benefit under subsection 7.5.6.3.<br>**Note:** This has the effect of extending the benefits in this Part to a person granted accommodation under the SAFE scheme. |
|  | **The SAFE scheme** means a scheme that provides emergency assistance for persons who cannot remain in their home due to a domestic crisis that may be happening or be threatened. |

###### 7.5.6 Members eligible

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member and their resident family and recognised other persons may be eligible for temporary accommodation allowance if they meet any of these conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are eligible for a removal.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are eligible for housing assistance under this Chapter. They are temporarily unable to live in suitable accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>They notify the Defence Housing Australia Regional Operations Manager that they intend to buy a suitable own home at their housing benefit location or family benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Their furniture and effects are in transit to their housing benefit location or family benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>They are required to isolate in a place specified by State or Territory authorities that is not the member’s or their resident family’s and recognised other person’s usual place of residence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">A deceased member’s resident family and recognised other persons may be eligible for the allowance under section 7.5.10 if they are granted a removal.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">Any of the following persons may be granted emergency assistance under this Part under the SAFE scheme.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A person in the member's household.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The member’s resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The member’s recognised other person.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.5.7 Approval under the SAFE scheme

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may approve emergency assistance for a person who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are a person eligible for a benefit under subsection 7.5.6.3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are under threat of a domestic crisis, or in a domestic crisis.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.5.8 Member not eligible

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A member is not eligible for temporary accommodation if the CDF is satisfied that the member, their resident family, or a recognised other person of the member caused any of the following to occur.</td>
</tr>

<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The furniture and effects not to arrive at the location until one or more days after the member and any resident family or a recognised other persons got there.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member and their resident family and recognised other persons do not have suitable accommodation.</td>
</tr>
</table>

<table>

<td>1.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member and their resident family or recognised other persons may need to move into temporary accommodation for the period of the removal. They are eligible for temporary accommodation allowance for the period. The amount of allowance is worked out under Division 4 section 7.5.21 or 7.5.25.</td>

</tr>

<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member and their resident family and recognised other persons arrive at the new housing benefit location on different days, the period of eligibility includes all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A period at the former housing benefit location or family benefit location that lets the member’s resident family and recognised other persons start the journey and arrive on the same day as the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A period at the new housing benefit location that lets the member complete the journey and reunite with their resident family and recognised other persons.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.5.17 Period of eligibility

| 1. | A member in a situation in column A of the following table is eligible to be paid temporary accommodation allowance up to the maximum period in column B of the same item. |
|---|---|

| Item | Column A<br>Member’s situation | Column B<br>Maximum period of eligibility |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | They are leaving a location to go to another location with at least one of their resident family or recognised other persons. | One of the following.<br>a. If the gaining location is RAAF Base Tindal — 6 weeks at the losing location.<br>b. Any other gaining location — 3 nights at the losing location. |
| 2. | They are arriving at the gaining location with at least one of their resident family or recognised other persons. | One of the following.<br>a. If the gaining location is RAAF Base Tindal — 3 nights at that location.<br>b. Any other gaining location — 6 weeks at the gaining location. |
| 3. | They and their resident family and recognised other persons are being removed within the same housing benefit location. | 3 nights. |
| 4. | They have been granted assistance under section 7.5.7 (the SAFE scheme). | 5 nights. |
| 5. | All of the following applies.<br>a. They are in transit from a long-term posting overseas to a housing benefit location in Australia<br>b. They are on temporary duty at a location in Australia. | The number of nights in the period of temporary duty. |
| 6. | They are going overseas on one of the following.<br>Long-term duty.<br>Deployment for 6 months or longer. | 2 weeks.<br>**Note:** The period can be spent at either:<br>a. the losing location; or<br>b. a combination of the losing location and the place of embarkation. |
| 7. | They rejected a reasonable offer of a Service residence at the housing benefit location. | The number of nights from the first day the member meets the criteria in column A of this item to the day that the CDF is satisfied that they could have completed their removal to the Service residence, if they had accepted the offer. |
| 8. | They are vacating a Service residence. | 2 nights. |
| 9. | All of the following apply.<br>a. They have been granted a removal on a posting that is more than 6 months.<br>b. They rejected or did not apply for suitable accommodation that was available at the new housing benefit location. | The number of nights from the first day the member meets the criteria in column A of this item to the first day they could have occupied suitable accommodation if they had applied for it. |
| 10. | All of the following applies.<br>a. They are required to isolate in a place specified by State or Territory authorities that is not their usual residence.<br>b. They are not eligible for a greater period of temporary accommodation allowance. | The number of nights from the first day the member meets the criteria in column A of this item to the last day the member is required to isolate. |

| 2. | Despite subsection 1, if a suitable Service residence or other long-term accommodation is not available, the member continues to be eligible for temporary accommodation allowance if they are taking all reasonable steps to find suitable accommodation. |
|---|---|

###### 7.5.18 Member buying a home

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Searching for a home that they will get rent allowance for.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>

</tr>

</tr>

<td></td>

<td></td>

#### Part 6: Service residences

##### Division 1: General provisions

###### 7.6.1 Simplified outline of Part 6

This Part provides subsidised housing for members and their families to live in.

Service residences and rent band choice homes are types of housing that are designed to be occupied by members who have resident family and recognised other persons. However, surplus Service residences that are not needed for members with families can be occupied and shared by members who do not live with any resident family or recognised other persons (see Division 7).

Service residences are generally located in specific areas near the location the member is posted. In some areas, the demand for Service residences is high, so members may need to access other types of housing, such as renting a home in the private rental market and receiving rent allowance (see Part 8 of this Chapter).

For a Service residence to be suitable it must meet certain standards (see Division 3). If a member is looking to live in a different standard of housing, they have access to another type of housing called rent band choice (see Division 2).

Rent band choice homes allow members to choose a residence that better suits their lifestyle. This type of housing allows the member to choose to occupy a home that does not meet the minimum standard for a Service residence, however is likely situated in a more attractive location (see Division 5).

A rent band choice home still needs to meet certain requirements.

When a member or their resident family occupies a Service residence or rent band choice home, the member is required to pay a contribution towards the cost of living there. The amount the member contributes depends on a number of factors (see Division 8 and Annex 7.A).

Some members are required to live in specific Service residences, these are called appointment, tied or assigned residences (see Division 6). A member who lives in this kind of accommodation is required to pay a contribution, depending on their personal circumstances.

###### 7.6.3 Definitions

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">In this Part the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Allocate</b> means a home that is allocated under this Part is a home which Defence Housing Australia makes available as a reasonable offer of a Service residence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Defence establishment</b> means a Commonwealth site managed by the Department of Defence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Market rent</b> means rent based on the assessed value of the Service residence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Market-rent-based classification</b> means the system for classifying a Service residence based on a combination of the minimum housing standard and market rent.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Suitable Service residence</b> has the same meaning given in section 7.6.4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Surplus Service residence</b> means those Service residences that are surplus to Defence Housing Australia's needs and meet all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>No member who is eligible under section 7.6.28 requires the residence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>There is no plan for a member who is eligible under Section 7.6.28 to use the residence in the next 12 months.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 2: Suitable Service residence

###### 7.6.4 Suitable Service residence

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A home is a suitable Service residence for a member if the CDF considers that it meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">It is available to the member within one of the following periods.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Six weeks after they arrive at the housing benefit location or family benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>A longer period that the CDF considers reasonable.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">It meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>It is at the member's housing benefit location or family benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>It has the classification listed for the member's rank group in the table at section 7.6.13. or it is a rent band choice home that the member has accepted under Division 5.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>It has the number of bedrooms a member and their resident family and recognised other persons need to live in.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">In assessing whether a Service residence is suitable for a member, the CDF must take account of any other factor relevant to the member's accommodation requirements.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">The CDF may decide that a smaller home is suitable in these cases.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">There are exceptional reasons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member has chosen the smaller home.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.6.13 Rent band for a member's rank group

| 1. | A member who holds a rank in column A of the following table is eligible for a Service residence with the rent band in column B of the same item. |
|---|---|

| Item | Column A<br>Member’s rank | Column B<br>Rent band |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | Corporal or lower<br>Sergeant<br>Staff Sergeant<br>Second Lieutenant<br>Lieutenant | 1 |
| 2. | Warrant Officer Class 2<br>Warrant Officer Class 1<br>Captain | 2 |
| 3. | Major<br>Lieutenant Colonel | 3 |
| 4. | Colonel<br>Brigadier | 4 |
| 5. | Major General or above | 5 |

| 2. | An offer of a Service residence in the rent band listed for the member's rank group is taken to be a reasonable offer of a suitable Service residence, provided that it meets the other conditions for suitability set out in section 7.6.4. |
|---|---|
| 3. | Despite subsection 1, if a Service residence is not available in the rent band listed for the member's rank group, the member may be allocated a Service residence in a rent band that is one rent band above or below the rent band listed for the member's rank group in the table in subsection 1.<br>**Note:** An offer made in accordance with this subsection is usually a reasonable offer for the purposes of section 7.6.33, Acceptance or rejection of reasonable offer. |
| 4. | The CDF may allocate a member a Service residence that is more than one level above the rent band for the member's rank group, if accommodation is not available at a lower rent band. The member's contribution is dealt with in the same way as other members allocated a Service residence above their rank group eligibility.<br>**Note:** A member would not be allocated a Service residence two groups below their rank group eligibility. Rent band choice or housing with rent allowance give alternatives to allocation. |

##### Division 5: Rent band choice homes

###### 7.6.19 Rent band choice

| 1. | Rent band choice is off-base accommodation made available by Defence Housing Australia that falls outside the minimum standard of a Service residence. |
|---|---|
| 2. | A rent band choice home is classified under the rent band that the home's rent falls into. |
| 3. | A member who holds a rank in column A of the following table is eligible for an available rent band choice home with the rent band in column B of the same item. |

| Item | Column A<br>Member’s rank | Column B<br>Rent band |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | Corporal or lower<br>Sergeant<br>Staff Sergeant<br>Second Lieutenant<br>Lieutenant | 1 |
| 2. | Warrant Officer Class 2<br>Warrant Officer Class 1<br>Captain | 2 |
| 3. | Major<br>Lieutenant Colonel | 3 |
| 4. | Colonel<br>Brigadier | 4 |

| 4. | If a member accepts the offer of a rent band choice home, then that offer is taken to be a reasonable offer of a suitable Service residence, regardless of the rent band that the home is in. |
|---|---|
| 5. | A member who refuses a rent band choice home offered to them is taken not to have rejected a reasonable offer. |

<tr>

<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>

<tr>
<td></td>

###### 7.6.21 Member living in rent band choice home below their rank group

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">The CDF may offer a member a rent band choice home that is below the rank group specified for the member in the table in section 7.6.19.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">If the member accepts the offer of a home under this section, the member’s contribution is one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is not on a flexible service determination — the contribution for the rent band that the rent band choice home is in, under Part 1 of Annex 7.A.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is on a flexible service determination — one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>If the member’s pattern of service over each 4 week period is 1 week working, 3 weeks not working — 150% of the rate that applies to them under Annex 7.4.B.<br><b>Note:</b> This contribution is listed under a lower rank group.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>If the member’s pattern of service over each 4 week period is 2 weeks working, 2 weeks not working — 100% of the rate that applies to them under Annex 7.4.B.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>If the member’s pattern of service over each 4 week period is 3 weeks working, 1 week not working, — 100% of the rate that applies to them under Annex 7.4.B.</td>
</tr>
</table>

<td>On the member's relocation to their new primary service location, the member’s resident family elect to remain in the location which they were removed to under subparagraph i.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">All of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>A deployed member's resident family are granted a removal to a location for family support.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member keeps their Service residence in their pre-deployment housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td colspan="2">Their partner was recognised under section 1.3.37.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member who has unaccompanied resident family and no accompanied resident family who is eligible for rent allowance under Part 8 may choose to occupy a surplus Service residence in the housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">Members who occupy a surplus Service residence can only share the residence with other members who are eligible under this section or section 7.6.30.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="3">Despite subsection 4, a member who has a recognised live-in carer may occupy a surplus service residence under this section.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member with unaccompanied resident family and no accompanied resident family may be eligible to live in an appointment, tied or assigned Service residence under Division 2, Appointment, tied and assigned residences.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.6.30 Member with no resident family eligible for a Service residence

| 1. | A member with no resident family or recognised other persons who is eligible for rent allowance under Part 8 may choose to live in a surplus Service residence. |
|---|---|
| 2. | A member who occupies a surplus Service residence can only share the residence with other members who are eligible under this section or section 7.6.29. |
| 3. | A member with no resident family or recognised other persons may be eligible to live in an appointment, tied or assigned Service residence under Division 2, Appointment, tied and assigned residences. |

###### 7.6.33 Acceptance or rejection of reasonable offer

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">An offer of a Service residence by Defence Housing Australia is reasonable if the home meets one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">It is a suitable Service residence under section 7.6.4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">It is at the rent band listed for the member's rank group in section 7.6.13.<br><b>Note:</b> This includes on-base Service residences which are taken to hold a market-rent-based classification.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">If no Service residence is available in the rent band for the member’s rank group under section 7.6.13, it is a Service residence in the rent band above or below the member’s rent band.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">It is rent band choice accommodation which the member accepts.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">If a home at a lower rent band does not have enough rooms for the family's children to occupy using the table in section 7.6.4, it would not be considered a reasonable offer for the purpose of paragraph 1.b.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">To continue to be eligible for housing assistance, the member must accept a reasonable offer or reject it in writing for a reason in section 7.6.34.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="3">If a member rejects a reasonable offer for reasons not in section 7.6.34, all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the CDF does not consider the reasons to be sufficient grounds to reject the Service residence, and Defence Housing Australia cannot offer the Service residence to another member within 1 month — the member's name will be removed from the Service residence waiting list.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member will not be eligible for any of the following for the remainder of their posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Temporary accommodation allowance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Rent allowance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>Storage.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6.</td>
<td colspan="3">In this section, <b>waiting list</b> means a list of members who meet all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are eligible for a Service residence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They have been identified as needing a Service residence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">They do not have a Service residence.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.6.34 Reasons for rejecting a reasonable offer

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies to a member who rejects a reasonable offer of a Service residence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">An offer is not reasonable if the member rejects it for any of the following. This means that the member is still eligible for a Service residence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The home is at the classification that applies two or more groups below the member's rank group.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The home has a swimming pool.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The home and grounds are unsuitable for the member’s pet and all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member’s pet is domestic and not owned for business or commercial purposes.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member’s pet is able to be kept at the location without breaking any relevant laws or body corporate rules.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">The home has 2 bedrooms.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td colspan="2">The home is a rent band choice home and the member does not accept the offer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is a flexible housing trial member under section 7.1.15 and the home is not suitable for the purpose for which their housing benefit location was extended.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.6.35 Changing Service residences

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">The CDF may approve a member changing their Service residence for another Service residence in any of these cases.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member's resident family and recognised other persons have increased in number and they need more bedrooms. These conditions apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>If the member is expecting a child, the change can be approved up to 3 months before the birth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The change can only be approved if the member has at least 6 months more in their current posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The long-term lease on the Service residence is ending and will not be renewed.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The Service residence will no longer be available to the member due to sale or major renovation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">There are serious health, safety or security concerns if the member stays at the Service residence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member has a recognised live-in carer and they need an additional bedroom.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1A.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member whose change is approved under subsection 1 is eligible for a removal of furniture and effects under Chapter 6 Part 5 Division 2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The CDF may approve the change of Service residence at the member’s own expense. The CDF must consider all these circumstances.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The reasons outlined in the application.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Whether other Service residences are available.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The effect on any other member.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.6.37 Ineligible member can apply for surplus Service residence

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section does not apply to a member who has no resident family or recognised other persons who has chosen to live in a Service residence under section 7.6.30.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member who is not eligible for a Service residence may apply to Defence Housing Australia to live in a surplus Service residence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>

<td colspan="2">The concept of suitability outlined in section 7.6.4 does not apply to this arrangement.</td>
</tr>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If paragraph (a) does not apply, then the amount of rent payable is determined by Defence Housing Australia under section 59 of the <i>Defence Housing Australia Act 1987.</i></td>
</tr>
</table>

<table>

###### 7.6.42 Suspended contributions for a member who has no resident family or recognised other persons

|  | A member who has no resident family or recognised other persons and is occupying a surplus Service residence in a situation set out in an item in column A of the following table is not required to make a contribution towards the cost of the home from the day set out in column B of the same item until the day set out in column C of the same item. |
|---|---|

| Item | Column A<br>Member situation | Column B<br>Day contributions ceases | Column C<br>Day contribution recommences |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. | The member is living under field conditions. | The twenty-second day of a continuous period in which the member was living under those conditions.<br>This applies even if the period after that day is broken by any of the following.<br>a. The member returns to their accommodation for up to 7 days.<br>b. The member takes up to 7 days of leave. | The day after the period in which the member was living under those conditions is broken by more than 7 days, provided the member contributes for those 7 days. |
| 2. | The member is living on a seagoing ship. | The twenty-second day of a continuous period in which the member was living under those conditions.<br>This applies even if the period after that day is broken by any of the following.<br>a. The member returns to their accommodation for up to 7 days.<br>b. The member takes up to 7 days of leave. | The day after the period in which the member was living under those conditions is broken by more than 7 days, provided the member contributes for those 7 days. |
| 3. | The member is posted to a seagoing submarine. | The day the posting period starts. | The day the posting period ends. |
| 4. | The member is on one of the following:<br>a warlike deployment<br>a non-warlike deployment. | the day they board a ship or aircraft for the journey from Australia to the operational area. | when they disembark in Australia at the cessation of their warlike or non-warlike deployment.<br>**Note:** Contributions do not recommence for a member who returns part-way through their deployment. They only recommence at the cessation of their deployment. |

###### 7.6.43 Higher contribution scheme, above rank group

|  | If the member chooses to accept a Service residence or rent band choice home with a rent band higher than the one specified for the member's rank group eligibility under section 7.6.13, the member must pay the contribution listed for their rank and the higher rent band under Part 2 of Annex 7.A for the period that they hold the home.<br>**Note:** This is called a 'higher contribution scheme' contribution. |
|---|---|

###### 7.6.44 Contribution for a home chosen at a lower rank group's rent band

| 1. | This section applies to a member who chooses a Service residence or rent band choice home with a lower rent band than the member is eligible for at their rank group. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The member must pay the contribution for the lower rank group listed against the rent band of the home under section 7.6.41 and Annex 7.A. |

###### 7.6.45 Member allocated a Service residence above their rank group

| 1. | This section applies to a member who is allocated a Service residence in a rent band that is higher than the one specified for the member's rank group in subsection 7.6.13.1. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The member must pay the contribution that applies under section 7.6.41 and Annex 7.A. |

###### 7.6.46 Member allocated a Service residence below their rank group

| 1. | This section applies to a member who is allocated a Service residence with a lower rent band than the member is eligible for at their rank group under 7.6.13. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The member must pay the contribution for the lower rank group listed against the rent band of the home in Annex 7.A. |

<td colspan="2">On the date of their promotion, the member's contribution for the Service residence is increased to the rate for their new rank group (relevant to the classification of the Service residence).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member's new rank group is the one specified for the classification of their Service residence or rent band choice home under subsection 7.6.13.1, all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Any requirement for the member to pay a higher contribution scheme amount under Part 2 of Annex 7.A ceases.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member must pay the contribution worked out under Part 1 of Annex 7.A.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member who is notified of a promotion to a higher rank group is able to be allocated a Service residence at the higher rank group before the posting commences. The member may continue to pay the contribution for their substantive rank group until the date the promotion commences. From the date of promotion the member must pay the contribution for their new rank.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member is appointed as an officer and their rank group is lowered, they remain eligible for the rank group they held before they were appointed as an officer until they are eligible for a higher rank group.<br><b>Note:</b> Rank groups are provided in subsection 7.6.13.1.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.6.49 Member reduced in rank

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member who meets all these conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They live in a Service residence that is at or above their rank group eligibility.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are reduced to a rank in a lower rank group.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">On the date their rank is reduced, the member's contribution for an allocated Service residence is reduced to the rate for their new rank group (relevant to the classification of the Service residence).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member paid a contribution for their home under section 7.6.43 (the higher contribution scheme) immediately before they were reduced in rank, they must continue to pay the contribution that applies for their home and previous rank under Part 2 of Annex 7.A.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member who has been reduced in rank must notify Defence Housing Australia in writing. This allows Defence Housing Australia to assess whether the reduction in rank has any effect on the member's contribution.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">On reduction of rank, a member who is paying a contribution under the higher contribution scheme may elect to move out of the home. The removal does not attract any assistance and is at the member's own expense.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.6.50 Member on leave without pay

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is not eligible to live in a Service residence while they are on leave without pay under Chapter 5 Part 10, Leave without pay.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section does not apply to a member on any of the following types of leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Maternity leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Parental leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may decide that the member was granted the leave without pay for exceptional reasons. In this case, they may be eligible for a Service residence in the normal way. They pay their usual contribution.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member who is not eligible for a Service residence under this section may apply to live in a Service residence under Division 7 section 7.6.37. They must pay the Defence Housing Australia rent under section 7.6.37.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.6.52 Member undergoing training

|  | The contribution for a Service residence for a member who has accompanied resident family or recognised other persons is not reduced for any period that the member is a member undergoing training. |
|---|---|

###### 7.6.53 Service residence reclassified

|  | A change in the rent band of a Service residence under Division 3 or 5 does not apply until the end of any current occupancy agreement. |
|---|---|
|  | **Note 1:** This means that a change will not affect a member during the life of their tenancy.<br>**Note 2:** Subsection 7.6.41.2 allows CDF to reduce a contribution in some circumstances, without changing the classification of a Service residence. |

###### 7.6.58 Member buys a suitable own home

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>

</tr>

<td></td>
<td>a.</td>

<td></td>

<td></td>

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>

<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">One of the following.</td>

<td></td>
<td></td>

<table>
<tr>

#### Part 7: Member choice accommodation

##### Division 1: General provisions

###### 7.7.1 Simplified outline of Part 7

This Part provides Member Choice Accommodation, which is a type of accommodation provided as an alternative to living-in accommodation or rent allowance for members who have no resident family or only unaccompanied resident family.

To be able to access Member Choice Accommodation a member must be eligible for rent allowance. Members who have accompanied resident family or have been approved a transition location agreement cannot access this type of accommodation (see Division 1).

Members may share Member Choice Accommodation with other members who are also eligible for this type of accommodation. However, if a member’s circumstances change (e.g. they gain a Defence recognised partner) they may be required to relocate to another form of accommodation (see Division 1).

Contributions towards Member Choice Accommodation (see Division 3) are based on a member’s rank, living arrangements and rent ceiling (see Division 2).

###### 7.7.3 Definitions

|---|---|
|  | **Rent ceiling** has the same meaning given in section 7.8.10. |

#### Part 8: Rent allowance

##### Division 1A: General provisions

###### Subdivision 1: Interpretation

###### 7.8.1 Simplified outline of Part 8

This Part provides members with rent allowance which is a type of housing assistance that helps with the costs of renting in the private housing market and supports members who do not have a suitable own home in their housing benefit location or family benefit location. To access rent allowance, members must apply in writing through Defence Housing Australia (see Division 1).

The amount a member receives for rent allowance (see Division 4) is based on their accommodation needs, the location the housing is required, their family circumstances and their living arrangements. Rent allowance is calculated based on the lower of the actual rent paid or the approved rent ceiling (see Division 2 and Annex 7.E), with specific rules for members who are sharing homes, have house sitters, are subletting, or are employing resident child carers.

Members must report changes, such as new residents or subletting arrangements and change in rank or rank group, to Defence Housing Australia so their rent allowance can be adjusted (see Division 4).

Members eligible for rent allowance must contribute towards their rent based on their circumstances (see Division 3 and Annex 7.D). Factors like family circumstances, sharing arrangements, and specific conditions, such as flexible service determinations, postings to seagoing vessels or submarines may change the amount a member is required to contribute.

A member's eligibility for rent allowance ends when they move to other suitable accommodation, such as purchasing a suitable home, accepting a Service residence or moving into living-in accommodation (see Division 5).

Members who are eligible for rent allowance can also apply for assistance with other costs such as rental bonds, rent in advance, and utility deposits (see Division 6).

<td></td>
<td colspan="2">In this Part, a member is <b>boarding in a home</b> if all of the following are met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member is paying the owner of the home rent to occupy a room.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>An owner of the home resides in the home.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> To avoid doubt, this does not include a boarding house or commercial establishment.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.8.4A Trial member

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Trial member</b> means a member to whom all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They have been approved to participate in the Sydney share-arrangement rental trial under section 7.8.4B.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are living in a home for which rent allowance is payable.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The home is in the housing benefit location, which is not an extended housing benefit location, of a trial location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>They are sharing the home with up to 2 trial members.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>They are not sharing a home with a person who is not a trial member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td>They are not on a flexible service determination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>g.</td>
<td>They enter a share-arrangement on or before 31 December 2027.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> The rent ceilings for a trial member are provided in section 7.8.11B.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### Subdivision 2: Sydney share-arrangement rental trial – key concepts

###### 7.8.4B Approval to participate in the Sydney share-arrangement rental trial

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is approved to participate in the Sydney share-arrangement rental trial if the CDF is satisfied that the member meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are posted to a trial location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> A member is posted to an establishment once the posting order is issued, even if the member has not commenced the posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are posted to any of the establishments, including a combination of establishments, for at least 12 months from when the new sharing arrangements start.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">They do not have any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Recognised other persons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is expected to start a new sharing arrangement in a home with any of the following when they start to share.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>A member approved to participate in the Sydney share-arrangement rental trial.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>A trial member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> All trial members must be subject to a lease with either the property owner or a head tenant.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member cannot be approved to participate in the Sydney share-arrangement rental trial after 31 December 2027.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.8.4C Ceasing to be a Sydney share-arrangement rental trial member

<table>
<tr>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They become a member with any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Recognised other persons.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.8.6 Member not eligible

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is not eligible for rent allowance if they cannot find suitable accommodation because of their own action or failure to act.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is not eligible for rent allowance at their housing benefit location or family benefit location if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>aa.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is not on the early eligibility for rental allowance trial under section 7.8.5AA.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Defence Housing Australia offers them a suitable Service residence. They reject it. The CDF does not consider the reasons to be acceptable under Part 6 Division 7 section 7.6.33 or 7.6.34.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Defence Housing Australia cannot offer the Service residence to another member as a suitable home within 1 month of the offer to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member covered by subsection 2 cannot get rent allowance while they stay in the same housing benefit location or family benefit location. This does not change even if they have repeat postings within the location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is not eligible for rent allowance if they, their resident family or recognised other persons, if any, must live in a rental property if any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They have voluntarily moved out of a Service residence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They must move out of a Service residence as a direct result of their own actions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is not eligible for rent allowance for accommodation for their resident family in any of the following situations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">All of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member and their resident family and recognised other persons, if any, lived together.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member’s resident family and recognised other persons, if any, move to a location for which removal benefits are not provided.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">All of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>A deployed member’s resident family and recognised other persons, if any, are granted a removal to a family benefit location for family support.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>On the member’s return from the deployment the member’s resident family and recognised other persons, if any, elect to remain in the location they were removed to under subparagraph i.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The member has 6 months or more to serve in their primary service location after their return from the deployment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">All of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>A deployed member’s resident family and recognised other persons, if any, are granted a removal to a family benefit location for family support.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member had less than 6 months to serve in their primary service location after their return from the deployment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iv.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">All of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>A deployed member’s resident family and recognised other persons, if any, are granted a removal to a family benefit location for family support.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member keeps their rent allowance residence in their pre-deployment housing benefit location.</td>

<td></td>

##### Division 2: Rent ceilings

###### 7.8.9 Rent ceilings – living in rental accommodation

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies to a member who meets one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They meet all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They have accompanied resident family or recognised other persons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They have no unaccompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>They are occupying accommodation in their housing benefit location for which rent allowance is payable.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They meet all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They have unaccompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They have no accompanied resident family or recognised other persons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>Their resident family are occupying accommodation in their family benefit location for which rent allowance is payable.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">For the purpose of this section, the number of bedrooms a member is eligible for is equal to the number of bedrooms they would be eligible for in a Service residence if Part 6 applied.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">Subject to subsection 5, the member’s rent ceiling is one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is eligible for 3 bedrooms their rent ceiling is the rate for their location in column A that corresponds with their rank in columns B to F of Annex 7.E Part 1.1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is eligible for more than 3 bedrooms their rent ceiling is the rate under paragraph 3.a increased by 10 per cent for each additional bedroom after the third bedroom.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member may choose in writing to have a reduced rent ceiling.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="3">If a member has chosen a reduced rent ceiling under subsection 4 their rent ceiling is the rate for their location in column A that corresponds with their rank in columns B to F of Annex 7.E Part 1.2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6.</td>
<td colspan="3">In this section, <b>location</b> means one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is a flexible housing trial member — the location in column A of the table in Annex 7.E in which they live.</td>
</tr>
<tr>

<td></td>

<tr>
<td></td>

<table>

</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>

<td>a.</td>
<td>Market rents at the location.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The number, age, gender and circumstances of the member’s resident family.</td>
</tr>
</table>

<table>
<tr>

<tr>

###### 7.8.12 CDF may increase rent ceiling

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member may have their rent ceiling increased if the CDF is satisfied that the member cannot rent a home at their housing benefit location for less than their rent ceiling for one of these reasons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Market rent at the location has increased unusually or suddenly.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member's resident family or recognised other persons have particular housing needs and the member cannot find a suitable rental home that meets those needs within their rent ceiling.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is a member who has unaccompanied resident family and no accompanied resident family and cannot rent a home and sufficient furniture for it within the rent ceiling.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member has specific housing needs during rehabilitation or as a result of an acquired disability, which can include, but are not limited to, any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Location of the rental home in relation to rehabilitation facilities.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Additional room for a live-in carer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>Accessibility of the accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">For paragraph 1.b, the CDF must consider all these criteria.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The number, age, and gender of the member’s resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Any disability of the member's resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">Any other factor relevant to the resident family’s housing needs.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.8.16 Reduction in rent ceiling – effect on rent allowance

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A reduction in the rent ceiling for a member's housing benefit location does not apply to the member until the earlier of the following dates.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The day the lease ends.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The day the member, their resident family and recognised other persons, if any, move out of the home.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>

<td>a.</td>
<td>For a member who ceases to have resident family or recognised other persons — the day the member ceases to have any resident family or recognised other persons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>For a member whose primary service location is in a housing benefit location which is adjacent to their previous housing benefit location and the home the member rents remains unchanged — the day the member's posting to the adjacent location commences.</td>

</table>

###### 7.8.18 When rent contribution ceases for a member who has no resident family or recognised other persons

|  | A member who has no resident family or recognised other persons and is usually required to contribute to their rent in a situation set out in an item in column A of the following table is not required to make a contribution towards their rent from the day set out in column B of the same item until the day set out in column C of the same item. |
|---|---|

| Item | Column A<br>Member’s situation | Column B<br>Day contributions ceases | Column C<br>Day contribution recommences |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. | The member is living under field conditions. | The twenty-second day of a continuous period in which the member was living under those conditions.<br>This applies even if the period after that day is broken by any of the following.<br>a. The member returns to their accommodation for up to 7 days.<br>b. The member takes up to 7 days of leave. | The day after the period in which the member was living under those conditions is broken by more than 7 days, provided the member contributes for those 7 days. |
| 2. | The member is living on a seagoing ship. | The twenty-second day of a continuous period in which the member was living under those conditions.<br>This applies even if the period after that day is broken by any of the following.<br>a. The member returns to their accommodation for up to 7 days.<br>b. The member takes up to 7 days of leave. | The day after the period in which the member was living under those conditions is broken by more than 7 days, provided the member contributes for those 7 days. |
| 3. | The member is posted to a seagoing submarine. | The day the posting period starts. | The day the posting period ends. |
| 4. | The member is on one of the following:<br>a warlike deployment<br>a non-warlike deployment. | The day they board a ship or aircraft for the journey from Australia to the operational area. | When they disembark in Australia at the cessation of their warlike or non-warlike deployment.<br>**Note:** Contributions do not recommence for a member who returns part-way through their deployment. They only recommence at the cessation of their deployment. |

<td></td>
<td></td>

<td></td>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td colspan="2">[image: Start formula number of days equals 130 times start fraction FSD over 365 end fraction end formula]</td>

<td></td>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td colspan="2">Where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>

<td>is the number days in the period of the member's flexible service determination that is less than 1 year.</td>

<tr>
<td>3.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>C</b></td>
<td colspan="3">is 50% of the fortnightly contribution rate set for the member's rank and circumstances in Annex 7.D that would apply to the member if they were a member with no resident family or recognised other persons and not on a flexible service determination.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>

##### Division 4: How rent allowance is worked out

###### 7.8.19 Rent allowance – General

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">In this section, <b>rent</b> means the lower of the following amounts.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The fortnightly rent paid by the member for a property.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The approved rent ceiling for the property.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The rate of rent allowance is worked out using this formula.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">[image: Start formula rent allowance equals rent minus A end formula]</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>A</b></td>
<td>is the member’s contribution set out in Division 3.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.8.20 Rent allowance – sharing a home

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies to a member who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>

<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The amount calculated using the following formula.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">[image: Start formula rent equals A divided by B end formula]</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>

<td></td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">[image: Start formula fortnightly rate of rent allowance equals A minus B end formula.]</td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">Where:</td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>A</b></td>

<tr>
<td></td>

<tr>
<td>3.</td>

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the visitor has no permanent home, the member’s rent allowance must be recalculated based on the visitor living in the home from the first day of the visitor’s stay.<br><b>Note 1:</b> Rent allowance is based on the contribution a member is required to make under section 7.8.17 and their rent ceiling under section 7.8.10.<br><b>Note 2:</b> If the visitor has a permanent home at another location, the visitor is not taken to be living in the home and therefore will not affect the member’s rent allowance.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>

<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">If subsection 3 applies, after considering all of the circumstances in which the person is living in the home, the CDF can decide that the person is not sharing the home for the purpose of calculating the members rent allowance under subsection 2.</td>
