###### 7.8.28 Member reduced in rank

| 1. | This section applies to a member who is eligible for rent allowance and is reduced in rank. |
|---|---|
| 2. | If the member's rank group changes, their eligibility for rent allowance would normally change. This is because the contribution rates that apply to the member would be the ones for the lower rank group. However, the rent ceiling would remain at the higher rank group rate. |
| 3. | The contribution the member must make toward the cost of rent is reduced if they belong to a lower rank group after demotion. |
| 4. | The reduced contribution under subsection 3 starts on the day the member's demotion takes effect. |
| 5. | Despite subsection 2, the member does not get a lower rent ceiling from the day that their rank is reduced. |
| 6. | The member may move into another home that they get rent allowance for. In this case, the rent ceiling for the member is reduced to the amount that applies to their new rank group. The reduced rent ceiling applies from the day the member moves out of the home they were living in at the time they were demoted. |
| 7. | A member who has been reduced in rank must notify the Defence Housing Australia in writing. This allows the Defence Housing Australia to assess whether the reduction in rank has any effect on the member's contribution. |

###### 7.8.29 Changing homes at the housing benefit location or family benefit location

| 1. | A member must re-apply for rent allowance if they move to another rented home at their housing benefit location or family benefit location. |
|---|---|
| 2. | A rent ceiling increase approved for a previous home cannot be kept for the new home. |
| 3. | The member can seek a rent ceiling increase for the new home under section 7.8.12. They must include any evidence that section requires. |

##### Division 5: Events that will end or limit eligibility

###### 7.8.38 Rent allowance audit

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Each member’s rent allowance may be audited one or more times in each posting cycle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The purpose of the audit is to check that the member is getting the amount of rent allowance they are eligible for. It checks facts including the address in the housing benefit location or family benefit location and the number of resident family or recognised other persons or other residents.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">To start an audit, the Defence Housing Australia Regional Operations Manager must do all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Write to the member to seek confirmation of information the Manager needs to make the checks.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the member does not respond, give written notice to the member's unit that the member is to be audited.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member must respond within 14 days of receiving the Defence Housing Australia Regional Operations Manager's letter. The response must be in writing.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member may be absent from the location at the time of the audit. The audit must then be suspended until the member returns.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6.</td>
<td colspan="2">This suspension lasts until the Defence Housing Australia Regional Operations Manager gets written notice that the member is in the housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
</table>

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>

<td>The member complies with the request under paragraph 7.8.38.2.a.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The Defence Housing Australia Regional Operations Manager is satisfied that the member has reasonable grounds for not responding within the time provided under paragraph 7.8.38.2.b.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 6: Advances and repayments

###### 7.8.40 Purpose

|  | A member might be unable to pay the bond or other fees for securing a rental property. The member may be eligible for an advance. |
|---|---|

###### 7.8.40A Member this Division does not apply to

|  | A member who accepts an offer of accommodation under Chapter 7 Part 7 of this Determination is not eligible for benefits under this Division. |
|---|---|

###### 7.8.41 Assistance with payments for rental home

| 1. | This section applies to a member who intends to enter into a lease on a rental home for which they will be eligible for rent allowance. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The member may apply for assistance for some of the costs of entering into a rental lease. |
| 3. | A member who must pay the costs in column A of the table is eligible for the assistance in column B of the same table item. |

| Item | Column A<br>Cost | Column B<br>Assistance |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | A rental bond | An advance payment of up to a maximum of twice the member's fortnightly rent ceiling.<br>**Note:** The member may apply for less than the full amount. |
| 2. | Rent in advance | An advance payment of up to a maximum of twice the member's fortnightly rent ceiling.<br>**Note:** The member may apply for less than the full amount. |
| 3. | A utility connection deposit | An advance payment of the cost of the deposit. |
| 4. | Commonwealth, State or Territory stamp duty of the lease | Reimbursement of the amount that was paid.<br>**Note:** This amount is not repayable. |
| 5. | Fees to a lawyer for preparing a lease | Reimbursement of up to $1,000.<br>**Note:** This amount is not repayable. |

|  | **Note:** The member may apply for assistance for the costs under both table items 1 and 2. |
|---|---|
| 4. | A member who received an advance under table items 1, 2 or 3 must repay the amount they received. |

###### 7.8.42 Advance payment of bond when sharing

| 1. | This section applies to a member who shares a rented home with another person and gets rent allowance. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The member can apply for an advance of the money they would be eligible for under section 7.8.41. They can apply for an advance of all or part of the amount. |

###### 7.8.44 Member to give evidence of payment

| 1. | A member who receives an advance payment under this Division 6 must provide the Defence Housing Australia Regional Operations Manager documents to demonstrate that it was spent for the intended purpose. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The documents under subsection 1 must be provided within 14 days of entering into a lease. |

###### 7.8.45 Unused advances to be repaid

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">If any part of an advance is not used for its intended purposes, the member must repay it immediately.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may decide that a member who received an advance has not paid or lodged it. The member must repay the advance immediately.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may decide that a member who received an advance for rent has not entered a lease and paid rent within a reasonable period. The member must repay the advanced amount back immediately.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">In making a decision under subsection 3, the CDF must consider all these factors.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Where the housing benefit location or family benefit location is.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The time of year.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Whether there is suitable accommodation available for the member's rank, status and resident family or recognised other persons’ circumstances.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.8.46 Method of repayment

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">If a member receives any advances under subsection 7.8.41.3, table items 1, 2 and 3, they must comply with all of the following conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They must repay any advances made to them.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Repayments must be made in one of the following fortnightly instalments.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>If the member is on an alternate located work agreement, a transition location (medical) agreement or a transition location (general) agreement — in fortnightly instalments over the period of the agreement up to a maximum of 26 fortnightly instalments.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>For all other members — 26 fortnightly instalments.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member may choose to repay the balance of any advances as a single payment before the end of the period in subparagraph 1.b.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">If the member does not repay the full advance within the first 12 months of the lease commencing, the balance is to be recovered in accordance with the <i>Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013</i>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">On termination of a lease the member may get a refund of a rental bond or utility connection deposit. The following table shows the amount that a member must repay in this situation.</td>
</tr>
</table>

<table>
<tr>
<td>Item</td>
<td>If a member has...</td>
<td>they...</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td>fully repaid the Commonwealth within the first 12 months of the lease commencing</td>
<td>are able to keep the refund.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td>a lease of less than 12 months</td>
<td rowspan="2">must repay any outstanding amounts to the Commonwealth when the member gets a refund through the State or Territory rental board or utility provider.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td>broken the lease within the first 12 months of the lease commencing</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td>a lease of 12 months or less and does not receive a refund</td>
<td>must repay any outstanding amount of the advance to the Commonwealth within 12 months of the lease commencing.</td>
</tr>
</table>

| 5. | If the member gets any interest on bond money refunded to them, they must make a payment to the Commonwealth. The amount of the payment is the portion of interest corresponding to the period and amount of the advance. |
|---|---|

###### 7.8.47 Rent paid before member moves in

<table>

#### Part 9: Meals

##### Division 1A: General Provisions

###### 7.9.1 Simplified outline of Part 9

This Part provides when a member is required to pay for a meal if they eat in a mess and the circumstances in which a member is able to receive food allowance.

When a member eats a meal in a mess, they are generally required to make a contribution towards the cost of that meal. In some circumstances, members may be able to receive meals at no cost (see Division 1).

If a member eats in a mess, they are generally required to pay the casual meal charge unless:

 They are paying a fortnightly meal charge.

 They have unaccompanied resident family.

 They are living under field conditions.

The rates for casual meals are provided under Division 1, with specific rates provided for breakfast, lunch, and dinner.

Members who have unaccompanied resident family and are not paying the fortnightly meal charge may be eligible to receive food allowance to cover food costs (see Division 2).

Rates for food allowance will depend on whether the member is under a flexible service determination or not. Members become ineligible for food allowance during periods when meals are provided as well as during specific types of leave (see Division 2).

#### Part 10: Utilities

##### Division 1: General provisions

###### 7.10.1 Simplified outline of Part 10

This Part provides utilities assistance to members to help manage the costs of maintaining two households due to the nature of their service.

Depending on who a member lives with and the type of accommodation they occupy, some members are able to claim a portion of their utility costs back each fortnight (see Division 1).

If a member is living in a tied residence or in living-in accommodation, they are required to contribute towards energy costs each fortnight (see Division 2). There are some exceptions to this.

Members occupying Service residences are eligible for advances on utility connection deposits, this includes members who are sharing (see Division 3). Evidence is required to verify the use of advances, and any unused funds must be repaid.

##### Division 3: Assistance with utilities connections and bonds

###### 7.10.10 Assistance with utility connection deposits

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for an advance for a utility connection deposit when they occupy a Service residence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The advance is the full amount of the payment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member may ask for assistance for only a part of the utility connection deposit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member receives a refund for the utility connection deposit under subsection 1, the advance must be repaid at one of the following times.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the member no longer occupies the Service residence — immediately after it is refunded.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the member is still occupying the Service residence —the day their eligibility for the Service residence ends.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member gets any interest on money the utility company refunds to them, they must pay the interest to the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.10.11 Advance payment of utility connection deposit when sharing

| 1. | This section applies to member who shares a Service residence with another person. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The member can apply for an advance of the money they would be eligible for under section 7.10.10. They can apply for an advance of all or part of the amount. |

###### 7.10.12 Member to give evidence of payment

| 1. | A member who has been given an advance under section 7.10.10 must give Defence Housing Australia's Regional Operations Manager documents to show that they have used it for the intended purpose. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The documents must be provided within 14 days of occupying the Service residence. |

###### 7.10.13 Unused advances to be repaid

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A member must immediately repay any part of an advance that meets any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>It is not used for its intended purposes.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>It has not been paid or lodged.</td>
</tr>
</table>

#### Part 11: Evacuation assistance

###### 7.11.1 Simplified outline of Part 11

This Part provides evacuation assistance for members and their families who occupy service accommodation on a Defence establishment if the establishment is evacuated due to an actual or imminent emergency.

Evacuation assistance includes:

 If the member occupies a Service residence — the reasonable costs of accommodation for the member and any family that also occupied the accommodation with the member prior to evacuation.

 If the member occupies living-in accommodation — temporary accommodation at another Defence establishment or the reasonable costs of other accommodation.

 Reimbursement of meal costs during the evacuation period. If the member has resident family, these costs are based on the location and age of the family members.

 Vehicle allowance if the member is required to travel more than 50 km to the other accommodation.

 Reimbursement of reasonable additional costs associated with the need to evacuate.

###### 7.11.2 Members this part applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Part applies to a member who occupies one of the following on a Defence establishment immediately before an evacuation order is issued.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A Service residence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Living-in accommodation.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.11.3 Period of evacuation assistance

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is eligible for evacuation assistance from one of the following times.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the evacuation order included a start time, that time.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If no start time was included in the evacuation order, the time the evacuation order was issued.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member ceases to be eligible for evacuation assistance at one of the following times.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the evacuation order included an end time, that time.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If no end time was included in the evacuation order, a time set by the Senior ADF Officer at the establishment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member was occupying a Service residence immediately before an evacuation order is issued, the day all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member is eligible for temporary accommodation allowance under Chapter 7 Part 5.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member is able to occupy the accommodation provided under Chapter 7 Part 5.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 7.11.4 Accommodation assistance

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is not eligible for a benefit under this section if an evacuation centre has been established for the member to evacuate to, unless one of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The evacuation centre is full.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member was occupying living-in accommodation immediately before the evacuation order was issued and other living-in accommodation is made available for them to occupy.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The Senior ADF Officer at the establishment is satisfied that there are special circumstances for the member, their accompanied resident family or recognised other persons not to go to the evacuation centre.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> An evacuation centre includes a centre established by civilian authorities or Defence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member occupying a Service residence immediately before an evacuation order is issued is eligible for the reasonable costs of accommodation for all of the following persons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Each of their resident family and recognised other person who was occupying the Service residence with the member immediately before the evacuation order was issued.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member who was occupying living-in accommodation immediately before the evacuation order was issued is eligible for one the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Living-in accommodation at another Defence establishment within 50 km of the establishment from which the member was evacuated.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If living–in accommodation under paragraph a. is not available — the reasonable costs of other forms of accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> The <i>Acts Interpretation Act 1901</i> applies to the measurement of distance in this section.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">In this section, accommodation means the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the member was occupying living-in accommodation — accommodation that is suitable for the member on a short term basis having regard to the nature of the emergency and the availability of accommodation, including shared accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the person was occupying a Service residence — accommodation that is suitable for the occupants to occupy on a short term basis having regard to the nature of the emergency and the availability of accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">A benefit provided under this section may be paid to the member by way of reimbursement or to the service provider.</td>
</tr>
</table>

<table>

</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>For any resident family who are less than 10 years old and occupying the accommodation with the member — 50% of the amount specified in column C of the same item.</td>

###### 7.11.6 Transport assistance

|  | A member who is required to drive more than 50 km to occupy accommodation under section 7.11.4 is eligible for vehicle allowance at the rate provided in section 9.6.25.<br>**Note:** The *Acts Interpretation Act 1901* applies to the measurement of distance in this section. |
|---|---|

###### 7.11.7 Additional funds

| 1. | Subject to subsection 2, a member is eligible for a reimbursement of up to $500.00 for additional costs if the Senior ADF Officer is satisfied that there are exceptional circumstances for making the payment that arose in connection with the evacuation. |
|---|---|
| 2. | A reimbursement cannot be made under this section for costs relating to accommodation, meals or vehicle allowance. |

### Chapter 8: Assistance for recognised family

#### Part 4: Education assistance

##### Division 1: General information on education assistance

###### 8.4.4 Purpose

|  | Education assistance helps members pay for additional education costs for their children caused by a posting to a location within Australia. |
|---|---|

###### 8.4.5 Definitions

|  | In this Part, the following apply. |
|---|---|
|  | **Compulsory tuition fees** means compulsory amounts levied by a child’s school for educating the child, including compulsory sports levies.<br>**Note:** Boarding fees are not included. |

###### 8.4.6 Changes to eligibility periods

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may bring forward or extend periods of eligibility outlined in this Part, having regard to all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The child's age, school history, educational needs, family circumstances and general welfare.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Facilities offered by schools and educational institutions in the former and gaining locations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The nature of the education system in the gaining location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Staff advice from schools and educational institutions in the former and gaining locations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>The circumstances of the member's posting and the likely location of future postings.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td>Any other assistance available from Defence Member and Family Support to support resident family with special needs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>g.</td>
<td>Any other disabilities of the child.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>h.</td>
<td>The interests of Defence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Any other factor relevant to the child's educational progress.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 8.4.7 Assistance in special circumstances

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for education assistance if they have not received a benefit for education assistance under this Part for the child and the CDF is satisfied of all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The reasons for the member not being eligible for education assistance are beyond the member’s control.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>There are special reasons for providing education assistance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">When making a decision under subsection 1, the CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The special circumstances are reasonable and consistent with the purposes of education assistance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member cannot be provided with any other type of education assistance outlined in this Part.<br><b>Note:</b> The amount of assistance approved must not exceed the amount outlined in this Part for eligible members in similar circumstances.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 2: School students at the gaining location

###### 8.4.8 Purpose

| 1. | If a member's child changes schools due to posting in Australia, their education may be disrupted. This Division assists with the cost of additional educational services. These services help the child meet and maintain their academic standards at the new school so that they don’t fall behind academically due to posting. |
|---|---|
| 3. | Education assistance in this Division is designed to overcome immediate difficulties as a result of posting. Assistance is limited. If the child continues to experience education difficulties beyond the limits, any further costs are the member's responsibility. |

###### 8.4.8A School changes that apply to this Division

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Division applies to a child who moves between the following schools.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The first year of compulsory schooling — primary school.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Primary school — primary school.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Primary school — secondary school.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Secondary school — secondary school.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 8.4.9 Member this Division applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">For this Division, all of the following must be met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is granted a removal to a new housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s child meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They are the member’s resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They are changing school to the new housing benefit location or family benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>They are enrolled full-time in a registered primary or secondary school.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The principal or the child's teacher at the new school provides evidence on the approved form of at least one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The child has not reached, or is unlikely to maintain, a sufficient standard in a subject. They require additional tuition that the school cannot provide.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The school cannot provide a subject. This must be critical to the child's educational progress or career-choice.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The school cannot provide a therapy service. This must be critical to the child's educational progress.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iv.</td>
<td>The child needs to have a special need assessed to develop a suitable educational program. A government agency is not able to do this within 6 months of the child's arrival at the new housing benefit location or family benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>v.</td>
<td>A child with a special need critically needs a program or service. A government school at the location cannot provide it. A non-government school at the location can provide it, or another directly related program or service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>vi.</td>
<td>The child is academically gifted and needs a special education program. A government school at the location cannot provide it.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> Section 1.6.1 applies to this section and may affect the reimbursement provided if a member and their partner, who is also a member, are both eligible for education costs for the same child.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 8.4.10 One‑on‑one tutoring

| 1. | This section applies to a member whose child is resident family and receives tutoring that is conducted in person between the child and the tutor. |
|---|---|
| 2. | A member who has a child who meets a condition in column A of the following table is eligible for the reimbursement of the cost of tuition up to the number of hours under column B of the same item. |

| Item | Column A<br>Conditions | Column B<br>Maximum hours |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | The child has studied the subject before and the subject is offered at the new school. | 14 hours |
| 2. | The child has not studied the subject before and the subject is offered at the new school. | 26 hours |
| 3. | The child meets all of the following and the subject is not offered at the new school.<br>a. The child is in Year 10, 11 or 12.<br>b. The child needs to study the subject, as it is essential to their career aims. | 40 hours |

<td></td>

<td>$138 an hour.</td>

##### Division 3: Loss of scholarship

###### 8.4.16 Purpose

|  | Education assistance in this Division assists a member with educational costs that would have been covered by a scholarship that their child can no longer access as a result of changing schools due to the member’s posting. |
|---|---|

###### 8.4.17 Member this Division applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">For this Division, the member must meet all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is posted to another location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s child meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They are the member’s resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They held a scholarship for education at a school in the losing location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>They could not use the scholarship because they changed schools to the gaining location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is not eligible for any other education assistance outlined in this Part.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> Section 1.6.1 applies to this section and may affect the reimbursement provided if a member and their partner, who is also a member, are both eligible for reimbursement for loss of a scholarship for the same child.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 8.4.18 Loss of scholarship

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is eligible for reimbursement of any of the following educational costs incurred at the gaining location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Compulsory tuition fees.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Textbooks.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The costs incurred by the member under subsection 1 must be for education of a kind that the child would have received under the scholarship.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The total amount of reimbursement must not exceed any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The unused part of the scholarship.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If a sublimit applies to a specified type of expense — the maximum for that sublimit.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 4: School students not at a housing benefit location or family benefit location

###### 8.4.19 Purpose

|---|---|

###### 8.4.20 Member this Division applies to

<table>
<tr>

</tr>
<tr>

<td>a.</td>

<tr>

<td></td>

<td></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iv.</td>
<td>They are not repeating a school year to improve results.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

<tr>
<td>2.</td>

<td></td>

###### 8.4.21 Tuition and accommodation costs

| 1. | Subject to subsection 3 and section 8.4.22, a member who incurs a cost for a purpose in column A in a year is eligible for a reimbursement of the cost incurred up to the amount specified in column B and must pay the contribution specified in column C of the following table. |
|---|---|

| Item | Column A<br>Purpose | Column B<br>Maximum reimbursement | Column C<br>Contribution |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. | Compulsory tuition fees. | $41,077 | The higher of the following.<br>a. $495.<br>b. The amount equal to the contribution they would normally have incurred for their child’s continued attendance at that school. |
| 2. | If in boarding school or a commercial establishment, the cost of board. | $36,302 | One of the following.<br>a. For the first year of boarding — $3,548.<br>b. For every other year of boarding — $3,984. |
| 3. | If accommodated privately, the cost of board. | $19,909 | One of the following.<br>a. For the first year of boarding<br>— $3,548.<br>b. For every other year of boarding — $3,984. |

<table>
<tr>
<td>1A.</td>
<td colspan="2">For the purpose of subsection 1, all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Boarding arrangements do not include supervision of the child in a member’s home.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Private accommodation does not include a home owned by the member or their resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The school may be paid directly the amount the member would otherwise be reimbursed under column B of the table in subsection 1 if the CDF is satisfied that the member is experiencing financial hardship.<br><b>Note:</b> The member will still be responsible for the contribution under column C of the table in subsection 1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member receives other assistance for school tuition and accommodation, the reimbursement or payment under this section must be reduced by any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If other government assistance is being provided to the member for the cost of attendance at school — the total value of the assistance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If assistance for the purchase of textbooks and equipment is being provided to the member — half the value of the assistance.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 8.4.22 Period of reimbursement

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">For this Division, the period of reimbursement to a member begins on the later of the following days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The first day of the child's next school term, after the member is notified of posting.</td>
</tr>

<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The day the child begins to board at the other location.</td>
</tr>

<td>2.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The last day of the child's attendance at the school.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The day the member ceases continuous full-time service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a child is absent from school for 12 weeks or more, the member is not eligible for education assistance for the period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">In certain cases, a child may stop attending the school for reasons beyond the control of the child or member. This includes Service, medical or other compassionate reasons. If the member has paid school fees or accommodation in advance, the member will be reimbursed for the period they have paid for.<br><b>Note:</b> This subsection only applies to a member who cannot be refunded costs by the school.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member receiving education assistance may become ineligible during the reimbursement period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6.</td>

<td>While the child is on school holidays.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

<td>While the member or an adult who is resident family of the member lives within the child’s location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>7.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The child's age, school history, educational needs, family circumstances and general welfare.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Staff advice from schools and educational institutions in the former and gaining locations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The circumstances of the member's posting and the likely location of future postings.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>

</tr>

<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td>Any other disabilities of the child.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>

<td></td>

</tr>

#### Part 5: Emergency Support for Families Scheme

###### 8.5.1 Purpose

|  | The purpose of this section is to support the well-being of a member’s resident family while the member is absent on duty and during an emergency situation. |
|---|---|

###### 8.5.2 Definitions

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Emergency situation</b> means an event meets any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>It is unforeseen.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>It is sudden.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>It exceeds the coping mechanisms of the member’s resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">An emergency situation is not an event that occurs due to a member’s ordinary work situation.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 8.5.3 Emergency support

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">A member is eligible for emergency support for their resident family in an emergency situation if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is in one of the following situations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They are absent from home for Service reasons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They are required to perform duty outside their working hours with less than 48 hours’ notice.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>They are in hospital or unable to provide care to their resident family for a medical reason.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">An application for emergency support has been made through one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The Defence Member and Family Helpline.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member's local Defence Member and Family Support office.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF is satisfied that the grant of emergency support is appropriate, having regard to all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Whether the member's resident family have insufficient immediate family or local support.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The recommendations made by a Defence Member and Family Support social worker.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The needs of the member's resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iv.</td>
<td>Whether the member's resident family have experienced an emergency situation.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 8.5.4 Emergency support

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">For the purpose of section 8.5.3, any of the following persons may apply for emergency support.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s recognised other persons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">The unit commander if any of the following agree to receive the support.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member’s resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The resident family’s authorised representative.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 8.5.5 When emergency support has been approved

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Emergency support includes any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Organisation of professional care and emotional support for the family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Case management services to the family throughout the emergency, with regular feedback to the people who have been agreed upon in the support plan.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Other support measures as required in consultation with the affected family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Development of a longer term strategy to promote the well-being of the family for the remainder of the member's period of absence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>A service provided under section 8.5.6.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 8.5.6 Types of services available

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is eligible for any of the following emergency services for their resident family up to a combined maximum cost of $3,000 for each emergency.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Any of the following services provided by professional providers.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Care of the member’s resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Specialist care of the member’s resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>Housekeeping.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iv.</td>
<td>Child care.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>v.</td>
<td>Respite care.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Travel for immediate family to provide support to the member's resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">Despite subsection 1, if a service under subsection 1 is not available in the resident family's location, the CDF may approve payment of travel and associated costs to a provider sourced from another location.<br><b>Note:</b> The service providers' travel and associated costs are taken into account as part of the cap on assistance payments under subsection 1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">Assistance under this section is only provided to a member's resident family for emergency services recommended in the social worker's support plan.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">The assistance under this section can be paid by any of the following means, up to the maximum cost for the emergency.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the service is paid by the member or their resident family — by reimbursement of the cost of the services on presentation of receipts to Defence Member and Family Support.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the service is provided and an invoice is issued by the service provider — by payment to the service provider on presentation of the invoice.</td>
</tr>
</table>

#### Part 6: Resident family who have special needs

##### Division 1: Assistance on removal

###### 8.6.1 Purpose

|  | The purpose of this Division is to provide assistance to a member who has resident family or recognised other persons with special needs on posting. |
|---|---|

###### 8.6.2 Member this Division applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">This Division applies to a member who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They have any of the following who has special needs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Recognised other persons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They have been granted a removal under Chapter 6 Part 5.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 8.6.3 Limitations on assistance

|  | A member is not eligible for assistance under this Part for services that are provided to them by any other Commonwealth body, State or Territory Government department, or Government funded agencies. |
|---|---|

###### 8.6.4 Payment

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Assistance under section 8.6.6 and 8.6.7 is paid in one of the following ways.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If services were paid for by the member — by reimbursement to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If an invoice was issued by the service provider to the member — by payment to the service provider.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 8.6.5 Special needs pre-posting visits

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is eligible for travel and accommodation for a pre-posting visit to the new housing benefit location or family benefit location if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The visit is supported by the member's Commanding Officer at the losing location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF is satisfied all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The person who has special needs requires direct contact with the relevant departments or institutions in the new housing benefit location or family benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The proposed travel is reasonable in the circumstances.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member applies using the approved form.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> Meals and incidentals are not included under subsection 1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The benefit under subsection 1 may be provided for any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>

<td>a.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member or their partner if they travel with the person family who has special needs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">Any other person whom the CDF is satisfied it is necessary to have accompany the person who has special needs.</td>
</tr>

<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> Special needs pre-posting visits are in addition to approved house-hunting trips under Chapter 7 Part 1 Division 4.</td>

<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">Despite section 9.1.3, travel under this section can be by a means that is not the most economical if the CDF is satisfied it is appropriate after considering the needs of the person who has special needs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">Despite section 9.5.16, accommodation under this section can be by a means that is not the most economical if the CDF is satisfied it is appropriate after considering the needs of the person who has special needs.</td>
</tr>
</table>

<table>

<td></td>

<td>The member applies using the approved form.</td>

<tr>

###### 8.6.7 Assistance with equipment hire

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">Subject to subsection 2, a member is eligible for financial assistance to hire specialist equipment in their housing benefit location or family benefit location if all of the following apply.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The person with special needs was on a waiting list for the equipment at the former housing or family benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The person with special needs is on a waiting list for the equipment at the housing or family benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member has provided all of the following to Defence Member and Family Support.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Evidence of an approved application for placement on waiting lists for Government funded services at the housing or family benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Evidence that the type of equipment applied for was provided at the former housing or family benefit location or that the person was on a waiting list in that location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>

<td></td>

<td colspan="2">The member applies using the approved form.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>

</tr>
</table>

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is eligible for any of the following at their housing or family benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subject to subsection 2, any of the following housing modifications.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>

<td></td>
<td></td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>

</tr>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">Housing located close to the school of the person with special needs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The CDF must be satisfied that house modifications under paragraph 1.a are appropriate and will not significantly alter the structure of the house.</td>

##### Division 2: Assistance when there is no removal to a new housing benefit location or family benefit location

###### 8.6.10 Purpose

|  | The purpose of this Division is to provide assistance to a member who has resident family or recognised other persons with special needs who has not been granted a removal to a new housing benefit location or family benefit location. |
|---|---|

###### 8.6.11 Member this Division applies to

<td>Unpacking assistance under section 8.6.9.</td>

</tr>

#### Part 7: Family assistance for attendance at a Court of Inquiry

###### 8.7.1 Purpose

| 1. | A Court of Inquiry provides a benefit to members as it determines the facts and circumstances surrounding an incident or situation they may have been involved in. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The purpose of this Part is to provide assistance to a member's family for their attendance at a Court of Inquiry involving an injured or deceased member. |
| 3. | This assistance is provided on the basis that a person does not gain or lose financially when attending a Court of Inquiry. |

###### 8.7.2 Definitions used in this Part

|  | In this Part ***Court of Inquiry*** has the same meaning as in regulation 3 of the *Defence (Inquiry) Regulations 1985*. |
|---|---|

###### 8.7.3 Persons who this Part applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This Part applies to any of the following people.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The partner of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A child of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>A parent of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>A parent of the member's partner.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>Resident family of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may approve assistance under this Part for people other than those listed subsection 1 having regard to all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Any recommendation made by the Director General Defence Member and Family Support.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Whether the person has been authorised to appear under regulation 33 or regulation 121 of the <i>Defence (Inquiry) Regulations 1985</i>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Whether the person's presence is necessary to provide support to a person under paragraph b.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 8.7.4 Persons this Part does not apply to

|  | This Part does not apply to a person who is not covered by subsection 8.7.3.1 or subsection 8.7.3.2 even if they have an interest in a Court of Inquiry for any period. |
|---|---|

###### 8.7.5 When assistance under this Part ceases

|  | The assistance under this Part ceases on the day after the close of the Court of Inquiry hearings. |
|---|---|

###### 8.7.5A Assistance for attendance at a briefing

|  | A person is eligible for assistance under this Part after the close of the Court of Inquiry hearings if the CDF considers it reasonable for the person to attend a briefing before the public release of the report. |
|---|---|

###### 8.7.6 Assistance with domestic travel

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section does not apply to a person who lives within 30 kilometres of the location of the Court of Inquiry.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may approve payment of vehicle allowance to a person if the CDF considers it reasonable to assist the person to travel to attend the Court of Inquiry on a daily basis.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a person is eligible for vehicle allowance, they are eligible to be reimbursed any of the following which are incurred for the purpose of attending a Court of Inquiry if an official receipt for the expense is provided.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Parking fees.<br><b>Note:</b> To avoid doubt, parking fees does not include parking or traffic fines.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Road tolls.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the CDF considers it unreasonable for a person to travel to attend the Court of Inquiry on a daily basis, the CDF may approve a return economy class trip within Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">Approval to travel under subsection 4 may include travel on the day before the Inquiry starts and the day after the Inquiry finishes.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6.</td>
<td colspan="2">A person is eligible for a maximum of 3 return journeys home in any 2‑month period if there is a break of more than 5 days between sitting days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>7.</td>
<td colspan="2">The Director General Defence Member and Family Support may approve additional return trips in extenuating circumstances. The Director General Defence Member and Family Support must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The number of times the Court sits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The nature of the evidence being presented.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Family emergency.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>8.</td>
<td colspan="2">A person is to be provided with cab charges for the trip from their home to the airport or station and to their accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>9.</td>
<td colspan="2">A person who makes their own arrangements for travel cannot apply for reimbursement under this section.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 8.7.7 Assistance with accommodation

| 1. | A person is eligible for accommodation costs if the CDF is satisfied, after considering advice from Defence Member and Family Support, that it is unreasonable for the person to travel to attend the Court of Inquiry on a daily basis. |
|---|---|
| 2. | If the CDF considers it unreasonable for the person to walk from the accommodation under subsection 1 to attend the Court of Inquiry the person may be provided with assistance. |
| 3. | A person who makes their own arrangements for accommodation or travel to the Court of Inquiry venue cannot apply for reimbursement under this section. |

###### 8.7.8 Assistance with meals

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subject to subsection 1A, a person receiving accommodation assistance under section 8.7.7 is eligible for one of the following payments for breakfast, lunch and dinner.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the person is less than 10 years old — half the rate set out in section 9.5.35 for the rank of colonel or lower.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the person is 10 years or older — the rate set out in section 9.5.35 for the rank of colonel or lower.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1A.</td>
<td colspan="2">The person is not eligible for assistance for a meal if the meal is provided at no cost to the person.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a child under 18 years of age is eligible for meal allowance under this section, the payment will be made to the parent, adult relative or legal guardian they are travelling with. If the child is travelling alone, the meal allowance will be paid to them.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 8.7.9 Assistance with incidental expenses

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Each family unit of people eligible for accommodation under section 8.7.7 may also be provided with a weekly allowance for incidental expenses. This allowance is to assist in covering incidental expenses such as phone calls and laundry expenses.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">For the purposes of this Part, one family unit includes all of the following people.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The partner and children of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Parents of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>A parent of the member's partner.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">A person nominated by the family unit is eligible for the weekly amount of incidentals allowance payable under paragraph 9.5.41.3.c.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may approve a higher rate of payment for incidental expenses if it is reasonable, on a case by case basis.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 8.7.10 Assistance with resident family or child care

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is eligible for the reasonable cost of assistance to care for their resident family if the CDF is satisfied it is reasonable.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">Assistance under subsection 1 includes any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Defence arranged travel for extended family to provide support to the member's resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Any of the following provided by family members or professional providers.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Care for the member’s resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Specialist care for the member’s resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>Child minding.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iv.</td>
<td>Respite care.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">Travel for extended family provided under paragraph 2.a may be to the home of the member's resident family or the location of the Court of Inquiry.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">If it is not reasonably practicable for the extended family to travel to the home location of the member's resident family or the location of the Court of Inquiry, travel may be provided for the member's resident family to travel to the home location of the extended family.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 8.7.12 Accountability

|  | A person must sign the attendance diary maintained by the Court of Inquiry for each day that they receive benefits under this Part. |
|---|---|

#### Part 7A: Assistance for attendance at a Royal Commission

###### 8.7A.1 Purpose

|  | The purpose of this Part is to provide assistance to a member's nominated support person so they can provide support to a member who attends a Royal Commission hearing as a witness. |
|---|---|

###### 8.7A.2 Definitions

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">In this Part the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Member</b> includes the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A member of the Reserves.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A former member.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Royal Commission</b> has the same meaning as in section 1B of the <i>Royal Commissions Act 1902</i>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 8.7A.3 Persons who this Part applies to

|  | This Part applies to a person nominated by a member, who is summoned as a witness at a Royal Commission hearing, to provide support to the member at the Royal Commission hearing. |
|---|---|

###### 8.7A.4 When assistance under this Part ceases

|  | The assistance under this Part ceases on the day after the conclusion of the Royal Commission hearing. |
|---|---|

###### 8.7A.5 Assistance with transport

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section does not apply to a person who lives within 30 kilometres of the location of the Royal Commission hearing.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A person is eligible for any of the following if the CDF is satisfied it is reasonable to assist the person to travel to attend a Royal Commission hearing attended by the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the person travels by private vehicle — all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Vehicle allowance under Chapter 9 Part 6 Division 5 for the journey to and from the location of the Royal Commission hearing.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Reimbursement of any parking fees and road tolls incurred in connection with attending the Royal Commission hearing, if they provide receipts.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the person travels by air — all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>A return economy class flight within Australia to and from the location of the Royal Commission hearing.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The cost of transport for the journey to and from the airport where the flight arrives or departs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the person travels by any other means of transport within Australia — the cost of the transport.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 8.7A.6 Assistance with accommodation

| 1. | A person is eligible for accommodation costs if the CDF is satisfied it is unreasonable for the person to attend the Royal Commission hearing without the accommodation being provided. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The person is eligible for reasonable transport costs between the accommodation and the location of the Royal Commission hearing if the CDF is satisfied it is unreasonable for the person to walk to and from the accommodation. |

###### 8.7A.7 Assistance with meals

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subject to subsection 2, a person is eligible for an allowance for a meal at one of the following rates if the CDF is satisfied it is reasonable.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the person is less than 10 years old — half the rate set out in Annex 9.5.A Part 4 table item 1 for the relevant meal.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the person is 10 years or older — the rate set out in Annex 9.5.A Part 4 table item 1 for the relevant meal.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The person is not eligible for assistance for a meal if the meal is provided at no cost to the person.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a person under 18 years of age is eligible for assistance under this section the payment is made to one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If they are travelling with a parent, adult relative or legal guardian — to the parent, adult relative or legal guardian.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If they are travelling alone — to the child.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 8.7A.8 Assistance with incidental expenses

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A person is eligible for incidentals allowance if the CDF is satisfied it is reasonable.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The rate of incidentals allowance is one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The amount payable to a member under paragraph 9.5.41.3.c.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If subsection 3 applies, the rate set by the CDF.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The rate of allowance may exceed the limit in paragraph 2.a. if the CDF is satisfied that the maximum amount payable under paragraph 2.a. is not sufficient in the circumstances.</td>
</tr>
</table>

#### Part 8: Partner Employment Assistance Program

##### Division 1: General provisions

###### 8.8.1 Purpose

|  | The Partner Employment Assistance Program provides reimbursement of certain costs associated with professional employment and training services to support the employability of partners. |
|---|---|

###### 8.8.2 Definitions

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">In this Part, the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Eligible partner</b> means a member’s partner who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are the member’s resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They reside in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">One of the following applies.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They are a non-Service partner.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They are a member of the Reserves not on continuous full-time service.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 8.8.3 Member this Part applies to

|  | This Part applies to a member on continuous full-time service. |
|---|---|

###### 8.8.4 Registering for the Partner Employment Assistance Program

| 1. | The eligible person must register for the Partner Employment Assistance Program before they access services under this Part. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The approved form must be used to apply for the Partner Employment Assistance Program. |

###### 8.8.5 Reimbursement of Partner Employment Assistance

| 1. | The member or the eligible partner is eligible to be reimbursed up to $1,500 in a financial year for professional employment and training services under Division 2 provided to the eligible partner.<br>**Note 1:** Any costs above the reimbursement amount for the financial year must be paid by the member or eligible partner.<br>**Note 2:** Any benefit not used in a financial year lapses and cannot be used in the following financial year. |
|---|---|
| 2. | Reimbursement must be applied for within 3 months of the services being paid for using the approved form. |

#### Part 9: ADF family health program

###### 8.9.1 Purpose

|  | This Part provides reimbursement for health costs incurred within Australia by resident family and certain recognised other persons registered under the ADF family health program. |
|---|---|

###### 8.9.2 Definitions

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">In this Part the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Allied health service</b> has the same meaning given under section 4 of the <i>Health Insurance (Section 3C General Medical Services</i> – <i>Allied Health Services) Determination 2024.</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Claimant</b> means any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member’s eligible dependant.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>A legal personal representative of the member or an eligible dependant.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Eligible dependant</b> has the meaning given by section 8.9.2A.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Family health program</b> means the ADF family health program.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Medicare benefit</b> means an item for which a rebate is payable under the <i>Health Insurance Act 1973.</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Out-of-pocket expense</b> means the difference between the amount that is charged for a service or a product for which a reimbursement may be made under this Part and the amount of Medicare or private health insurance rebate that may be paid for that item.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Specialist</b> means a person who meets the definition of specialist under section 3 of the <i>Health Insurance Act 1973.</i></td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 8.9.2A Eligible dependant

<table>
<tr>

<tr>
<td></td>

|  | The registration day of a newborn in the family health program is their date of birth if they are registered in the family health program within 3 months of their date of birth. |

|  | A claimant must apply for reimbursement under this Part within 12 months of the services or products being provided. |

#### Part 10: Reserve Assistance Program

###### 8.10.1 Overview

###### 8.10.3 Counselling sessions

| 1. | Persons this Part applies to are eligible for counselling sessions with a Defence contracted service provider. |
|---|---|
| 2. | No more than four sessions may be claimed for each issue the person wishes to address. |
| 3. | The CDF may grant the person up to four additional sessions for an issue. The CDF must consider the contracted service provider's recommendation about whether more sessions are needed to resolve the issue. |
| 4. | The CDF may make the decision in subsection 3 without knowing the identity of the person. |
| 5. | If more than one person attends the same session, that session is still only counted once. It is counted against the limit of the person who requested the session. |

###### 8.10.4 Multiple benefits

|  | A person's number of sessions under this Part is reduced by any Employee Assistance Program benefit that they are provided with because they are an APS employee employed in the Department of Defence. |
|---|---|

###### 8.10.5 Benefits

|  | The only other benefit a member may get under this Determination for attendance at the session is set out in section 3.2.15. |
|---|---|

### Chapter 9: ADF travel in Australia

#### Part 1A: General provisions

###### 9.1A.1 Definitions

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">In this Chapter, the following definitions apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Air travel for travel on duty</b> means air travel booked under the Department of Defence travel contract.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Allowable travel time</b> has the meaning given by section 9.1A.2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Contracted service provider</b> refers to the AOT Group (ABN No. 23 106 495 498), the service provider contracted to provide the Commonwealth with accommodation services for its employees and members of the ADF.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Most economical means of travel</b> refers to the means of travel the Commonwealth considers most efficient, practical or appropriate in terms of a range of factors which include, but are not limited to, the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Cost to the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Availability of transport.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Time taken to travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Normal departmental liability</b> has the same meaning given by subsection 9.1.7.1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Travel document</b> means a ticket (including a Miscellaneous Charges Order, travel warrant, movement requisition or other document) that gives a person who holds it travel at Commonwealth expense.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.1A.2 Allowable travel time

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Allowable travel time is worked out on the basis of the actual distance in kilometres for the shortest practicable route, divided by one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If a member is towing a towable item — 360.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If a member, resident family or recognised other person has a special need — the number of kilometres the CDF believes the person with special needs can travel in a day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>In all other cases — 480.</td>
</tr>
</table>

<tr>

<td></td>

###### 9.1.5 Lowest practical fare

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">Lowest practical fare is the lowest fare for the day of travel when the travel is booked, having regard to whether all of the following conditions are met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">It meets the business needs of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">It is for a regular scheduled flight.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">It is for travel that is scheduled to leave within 45 minutes of either of the following times.<br><b>Note:</b> The times do not include travel time to and from the airports, check-in times or security checks.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The latest possible departure flight time for departure flights.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The earliest possible return flight time for return flights.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A person who travels by air must travel using the lowest practical fare at the class of travel for which they are eligible.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">Flexible fares may only be used when either of the following could occur.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The scheduled meeting or event may not go ahead.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The meeting or event times are likely to change.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">The following may not be considered when looking for the lowest practical fare.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The airline.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Type of aircraft.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The provision of in-flight meals.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">Access to airline flight lounges.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td colspan="2">Airline reward, frequent flyer or loyalty points.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member who travels by a fare that is not the lowest practical fare must provide their reasons in writing.</td>
</tr>
</table>

<td></td>

###### 9.1.7 Normal departmental liability

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Normal departmental liability is what the Commonwealth would pay for a journey made by a member, their resident family and recognised other persons authorised to travel to a place at Commonwealth expense. It includes these costs.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The cost of travel to the place by the most economical means.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The costs of travel to and from the relevant airports, railway stations and coach terminals.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Any taxes or levies on the travel.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member travels by means that are not the most economical then the member is eligible for one of the following.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">For travel by means that are cheaper than the most economical means — the actual cost of their journey.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">For travel by means that are more expensive than the most economical means — up to the amount of the normal departmental liability.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member may travel as a passenger in a private vehicle or non-commercial aircraft when they are eligible for travel at Commonwealth expense. In this case, they are only eligible for meal and travel allowance up to what the Commonwealth would have paid for a journey by the most economical means.<br><b>Note:</b> The passenger may be travelling in a private vehicle belonging to another member. In this case, the member may have the rate of vehicle allowance increased for the distance they carry the passenger.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member who travels on personal frequent flyer points will not be reimbursed the cost of their fare.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">The Commonwealth will not pay any amount based on normal departmental liability for a child under 2 years old who is transported by private vehicle.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member might choose to travel by a less direct route than the most direct route available. In this case, they must pay any excess costs to the Collector of Relevant Money in the Department of Defence.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>7.</td>
<td colspan="2">The following conditions apply to travel documents.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The Commonwealth may give a travel document to a specific person and permit them to use it for travel.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If a travel document is used by a person who has not been permitted to use it under paragraph a, the person must repay the Commonwealth for any travel they have taken using the travel document.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The Commonwealth may seek to recover the cost of any travel taken without its permission under paragraph b.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>8.</td>
<td colspan="2">The Commonwealth will not pay for a chaperone that a carrier requires to accompany a member's child.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.1.9 Class of travel

| 1. | If a member is approved to travel by air, the class of travel is economy class air travel unless one of the following applies. |
|---|---|

| Item | If the member... | the class of travel is business class when... |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | holds the rank of Brigadier or higher | a. they are accompanying a Minister, senior Government official or foreign delegation and collaborative work is required during the flight.<br>b. the flight is part of a connecting flight for a longer domestic journey.<br>c. they have a recognised medical condition which precludes them from travelling in economy class.<br>d. the scheduled flight time is for longer than 90 minutes at the time of booking. |
| 2. | holds the rank of Regimental Sergeant Major of the Army | a. they are travelling on Defence business and accompanying a Minister, senior Government official or foreign delegation and collaborative work is required during the flight.<br>b. they are travelling on Defence business and the flight is part of a connecting flight for a longer domestic journey.<br>c. they have a recognised medical condition which precludes them from travelling in economy class.<br>d. they are travelling on Defence business and the scheduled flight time for longer than 90 minutes at the time of booking. |
| 3. | is a staff officer | they are required to travel with a member who holds the rank of Lieutenant General or higher who is travelling business class. |

<table>
<tr>
<td>1A.</td>
<td colspan="2">If resident family or recognised other persons are approved to travel by air, the class of travel is the same as the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member, their resident family or recognised other persons travel by coach or rail, they are eligible for travel at one of the following class.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the travel is by coach — the highest class available.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the travel is by rail — the highest available class.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>If the travel is by rail and continues after midnight — a sleeping berth, if available.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member who travels at a lower class than one listed in the table above is not eligible for any difference in cost between the fares.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>

###### 9.1.10 Baggage – general

| 1. | A member travelling by the most economical means may take baggage up to a maximum weight. This table shows the baggage limits. |
|---|---|

<table>
<tr>
<td>Item</td>
<td>If a member travels on…</td>
<td>and their rank is…</td>
<td>then their maximum baggage limit is…</td>

<td>temporary duty of less than 6 weeks</td>
<td>any rank</td>
<td>78 kg.</td>

<tr>
<td rowspan="2">2.</td>
<td rowspan="2">a. temporary duty of more than 6 weeks, or<br>b. posting, or<br>c. ceasing continuous full-time service</td>
<td>officer or warrant officer</td>
<td>260 kg.</td>
</tr>
<tr>

<td>156 kg.</td>

<table>
<tr>

<tr>

<td></td>

<tr>
<td></td>

<tr>
<td>4.</td>

The Commonwealth will pay no more for baggage than it would have paid for the most economical means and class of travel. The cost of any approved excess baggage will be included in working out the cost of travel by the most economical means.</td>

<tr>

<td colspan="3">A member is not eligible for the cost of insuring baggage.</td>

###### 9.2.5 Purpose

###### 9.2.6 Travel by the most economical means

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member who travels by the most economical means may have these benefits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Travel under Part 1 section 9.1.9, Class of travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Baggage under Part 1 section 9.1.10, Baggage – general.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
