###### 9.2.7 Travel by means that are not the most economical

| 1. | A member may apply to travel by means that are not the most economical. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The CDF may allow the member to travel by the less economical means. The CDF should consider the member's wishes and the needs of the ADF. |
| 3. | This table sets out benefits and conditions when the member travels by the alternative means. |

| Item | If the member chooses to travel by… | then… |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | air rather than rail | a. they must pay any additional cost of travelling by the method they choose before approval is given.<br>b. travel may be approved for all or part of the journey.<br>c. the benefit is to the lesser of allowances and travelling time when the two means of travel are compared.<br>d. they may be eligible for travelling allowance and meal allowance under Part 5, Payment of travel costs. |
| 2. | rail rather than air | a. they must pay any additional cost of travelling by the method they choose before approval is given.<br>b. travel may be approved for all or part of the journey.<br>c. travelling time will be as if the journey was by air. If it is on a working day, any excess travelling time should be taken as leave.<br>d. they may be eligible for travelling allowance and meal allowance under Part 5, Payment of travel costs. |
| 3. | a private vehicle rather than any other form of transport. | a. they may be eligible for vehicle allowance up to the cost of the most economical means of travel.<br>b. travelling time will be as if the journey was by the most economical means of travel. If it is on a working day, any excess Travelling time must be taken as recreation leave.<br>c. they may be eligible for to travelling allowance and meal allowance under Part 5, Payment of travel costs. |

##### Division 4: Travel on posting

###### 9.2.13 Purpose

|  | This Division sets out a member's eligibility for travel, baggage and accommodation expenses on their removal on posting. |
|---|---|

###### 9.2.14 Rail as the most economical means of travel

|  | This table sets out benefits and conditions when a member travels on posting and rail is the most economical means of travel. |
|---|---|

| Item | If the member... | the member... |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | travels by rail as the most economical means | a. is expected to transfer baggage with their furniture and effects. If the baggage is carried by rail, the restrictions in section 9.1.10 apply.<br>b. is eligible for reasonable costs for accommodation and meals for themselves, their resident family and recognised other persons.<br>c. is eligible for reasonable door-to-door travel costs.<br>d. will not be reimbursed costs of accommodation and meals if travelling allowance is paid. |
| 2. | chooses to travel by air rather than rail | a. may be approved air travel for all or part of the journey.<br>b. will not be approved air travel until the member has paid any additional cost of travelling by air rather than by rail.<br>c. must pay any excess baggage costs. |
| 3. | chooses to travel by private vehicle rather than rail | and their resident family and recognised other persons may be authorised to travel and may be eligible for vehicle allowance up to the cost of first class rail travel. Both of the following conditions apply.<br>a. The member's rank does not matter.<br>b. Any cost of sleeping berth accommodation is used in working out the cost of rail travel. This applies whether it is included in the fare or available as an additional cost.<br>**Note:** If the travel is on a working day, any time greater than the time it takes to travel by rail should be taken as leave. |

###### 9.2.15 Air as the most economical means of travel

|  | This table sets out benefits and conditions when a member travels on posting and air is the most economical means of travel. |
|---|---|

| Item | If the member... | the member... |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | travels by air as the most economical means with their resident family and recognised other persons | a. may have their baggage limit increased by:<br>i. one piece for each adult who is resident family or as a recognised other person, and<br>ii. up to 2 pieces for children.<br>b. is eligible for reasonable costs, for accommodation and meals for themselves and their resident family and recognised other persons.<br>c. is eligible for reasonable door-to-door travel costs. |
| 2. | travels alone by air as the most economical means | a. may have their baggage limit increased by:<br>i. up to 3 pieces for journeys to or from Darwin; between a remote location and the nearest capital city; or between a place in an external territory and a place in Australia.<br>ii. 1 piece for any other journey.<br>b. is eligible for reasonable costs for accommodation and meals.<br>c. is eligible for reasonable door-to-door travel costs. |
| 3. | chooses to travel by private vehicle rather than air | a. and their resident family and recognised other persons may be authorised to travel.<br>b. The member may be eligible for vehicle allowance up to the cost of air travel.<br>**Note:** If the travel is on a working day, any time greater than the allowable travelling time should be taken as leave. |

###### 9.2.16 Coach as the most economical means of travel

|  | This table sets out benefits and conditions when a member travels on posting and coach is the most economical means of travel. |
|---|---|

| Item | If the member... | the member... |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | travels by coach as the most economical means | a. may be eligible for travelling allowance and meal allowance.<br>b. is eligible for reasonable costs, for accommodation and meals for themselves and their resident family and recognised other persons.<br>c. is eligible for reasonable door-to-door travel costs.<br>d. must pay any additional baggage costs over the eligible maximum baggage limit under section 9.1.10. |
| 2. | chooses to travel by private vehicle rather than coach | a. and their resident family and recognised other persons may be authorised to travel.<br>b. may be eligible for vehicle allowance up to the cost of coach travel.<br>**Note:** If the travel is on a working day, any time greater than the time it takes to travel by coach should be taken as leave. |

###### 9.2.17 Reimbursement of personal expenditure on travel

| 1. | This section applies to a member eligible for travel under this Division who elects to travel at their own expense. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The member is eligible to be reimbursed the actual travel costs of their travel up to the value of the travel based on the most direct route the member could have taken. |
| 3. | If the member does not travel by the most direct route, the reimbursement is limited to the amount they would have received under subsection 2, unless the CDF is satisfied there are exceptional circumstances for not following the most direct route. |

###### 9.2.18 Members travelling without resident family or recognised other persons

|  | A member who has resident family or recognised other persons but travels on posting without them has the same benefits as a member on temporary duty under Division 2. |
|---|---|

###### 9.2.23 Rejoining a ship that has sailed

| 1. | A member is eligible for travel to rejoin a seagoing ship they have missed on sailing. There must be a need for the member to travel to rejoin the ship at another port. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The member may apply to the Commanding Officer of the nearest ADF establishment for a duty travel warrant to enable them to rejoin the ship. |
| 3. | If the member cannot get a duty travel warrant, they are eligible for a reimbursement of the actual amount they had to spend on fares to rejoin the ship. |
| 4. | Travel under this section is limited to the cost of the member’s transport from the port the ship sailed from to the port where they are to re-join their ship. |

###### 9.2.24 Recall for emergency duty

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member who has left their primary service location after working a normal day may be reimbursed the cost of their travel if they are later recalled to duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may approve reimbursement of costs if satisfied on both these criteria.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member has paid for travel fares or use of a private vehicle that they would not normally have to pay for.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member could not reasonably have used an alternative means to go back to the place of duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The amount of reimbursement is limited to whichever of these costs is relevant.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>For travel by public transport, including taxi — the cost of the fares beyond what the member would usually pay to attend work.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>For travel by private vehicle — vehicle allowance worked out for the journey under Part 6 of this Chapter.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.2.25 Travel during a medical absence

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member is eligible for travel if the CDF is satisfied the travel is for any of the following purposes.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">To assist the member to leave hospital to recover.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">To assist the member to reach a location where they are able to wait to go back to hospital.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">To assist the member to reach a location that the senior medical advisor recommends to assist the member’s recovery.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">In making a decision under subsection 1, the CDF must be satisfied that the following conditions are met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The travel is to the member's home or, if care is not available at their home, an alternative location. The CDF must have regard to any senior medical advisor recommendation about whether the care at the location is adequate for the member's needs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The senior medical advisor for the location has recommended both the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>That the member should undertake the travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>That the means of travel is safest for the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">The CDF may approve the travel at a higher class or by means that are not the most economical, if satisfied it is necessary for the member's safety and consistent with the recommendation under subsection 2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member may apply to travel at Commonwealth expense, including travel costs for meals, incidentals and accommodation on the journey. The member can be provided assistance up to the amount that would be payable if they were eligible for travel costs on Defence business for the same period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member may be approved to travel at Commonwealth expense but pay for it themself. In this case, the CDF may reimburse up to a maximum of what the Commonwealth would have paid under subsections 3 and 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 6: Travel on ceasing continuous full-time service – general

###### 9.2.27 Purpose

|  | This Division sets out a member's travel, baggage and accommodation benefits when they travel in Australia on ceasing continuous full-time service. |
|---|---|

###### 9.2.28 Members this Division applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A member, their resident family and recognised other persons may be eligible for travel to a location they are removed to in any of these circumstances.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>On ceasing continuous full-time service for any reason.<br><b>Note:</b> Eligibility is limited for a member whose service is terminated or ended through their own fault and who is not eligible for a removal.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>In advance of ceasing continuous full-time service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>In anticipation of ceasing continuous full-time service for compassionate reasons.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.2.29 Members this Division does not apply to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Division does not apply to members, their resident family or recognised other persons if they are eligible for any of the following benefits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Travel for candidates for election.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Travel on death of a member under Part 3 Division 10.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.2.30 Additional baggage for travel on ceasing continuous full-time service

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">If a member's resident family or recognised other persons travel by rail, they must take no more baggage than the railway authority carries for free.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">If the member, their resident family and recognised other persons travel by air as the most economical means, they may take additional baggage up to these limits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">For these journeys, up to 3 more pieces of baggage for the member and 2 more for each adult who is resident family or as a recognised other person.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>To or from Darwin.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>To or from Tasmania.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>To or from a remote location and the nearest capital city.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>iv.</td>
<td>Between a place in an external territory and a place in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">For journeys to other places, one more piece of luggage for the member and one more piece for each adult who is resident family or as a recognised other person.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member is not eligible for insurance costs relating to additional baggage under this section.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.2.31 Meals and accommodation

| 1. | A member, their resident family and recognised other persons will be reimbursed the cost of their meals and accommodation during their journey up to the maximum amount that they would have received if they were eligible for travel costs under Annex 9.5.A. |
|---|---|
| 2. | For the purpose of section 1, if the journey includes an isolation period the member, their resident family or recognised other persons are required to complete before they arrive at the location where they receive a removal to. |
| 3. | If the member, their resident family and recognised other persons choose not to travel by the most economical means, they will be reimbursed only up to the amount payable under subsection 1 for travel by the most economical means. |
| 4. | If the member, their resident family or recognised other persons are required to isolate in a place that is not their residence, subsection 3 does not apply to the isolation period. |
| 5. | If the member, their resident family or recognised other persons are eligible for travelling allowance for the journey, they are not eligible for the reimbursement of their costs. |

###### 9.2.33 Dual benefit

|  | If a member’s partner is also a member, the family unit has only one benefit on each occasion of a posting. |
|---|---|

##### Division 7: Travel on ceasing continuous full-time service – specific circumstances

###### 9.2.34 Travel in advance of ceasing continuous full-time service

| 1. | A member may take up their travel benefit up to 12 months before they cease continuous full-time service. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The member must sign an undertaking to refund the cost of the travel if they do not complete their service within the 12 months. This is unless the travel corresponds with a posting during the final 12 months of service. |

##### Division 8: Members of the Reserves – duty travel

###### 9.2.40 Purpose

|  | This Division sets out the benefits for a member of the Reserves travelling on duty. |
|---|---|

###### 9.2.41 Benefits under this Division

| 1. | A member on Reserve service who must travel for duty purposes has the basic benefits set out in Part 1 of this Chapter. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The CDF may approve a member's travel by means that are not the most economical. The CDF must consider the interests of the ADF and the member. |

###### 9.2.42 Limit on Commonwealth expense

| 1. | A member of the Reserves who is eligible for travel may choose to pay for the travel themselves. In this case, they may be reimbursed the cost of any part of the journey they take by public transport. They can be reimbursed an amount up to what the Commonwealth would have paid for the journey. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The member is not eligible for the reimbursement of their costs if they are eligible for vehicle allowance or any other form of allowance or reimbursement. |

#### Part 3: Travel and resident family

##### Division 1: Travel on recognition of a relationship

###### 9.3.3 Purpose

|  | This Division sets out a member's travel benefits when they have a partner recognised under section 1.3.36, while serving on a long-term posting in Australia. |
|---|---|

###### 9.3.4 Overview

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Having a relationship recognised does not create a travel benefit for the member personally.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member may be eligible for assistance for the member's partner and any other resident family to travel within Australia, subject to these limits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The benefit arises on recognition of a relationship.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The travel is for the journey from where they normally lived at the time the relationship is recognised, to the member's housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member’s resident family travel, their travel benefit is one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If travel is by the most economical means — a one-way ticket.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If travel is by private vehicle — vehicle allowance for the trip up to the amount of the normal departmental liability.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td><b>Note:</b> The increased rate for passengers is not payable under Part 6 Division 5 section 9.6.26.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> Any allowances for the resident family’s travel are paid to the member.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.5 Basic benefits

| 1. | Members and their resident family travelling under this Division are eligible for the basic travel benefits set out in Part 1 of this Chapter other than the baggage benefits provided under section 9.1.10 and 9.1.11.<br>**Note:** Baggage over the transport operator’s free limit must be included in personal effects as part of the removal benefit provided under. |
|---|---|
| 2. | If a member chooses a means of travel for their resident family that is not the most economical means, the member is only eligible for the costs up to the cost of travel by the most economical means. |
| 3. | The member may travel by a means that is not the most economical If the CDF approves |
| 4. | If subsection 3 applies, the member must pay the difference between the amount they would have been paid under subsection 2 and the cost of the travel under subsection 3 before commencing the travel. |

###### 9.3.6 When a member travels at their own expense

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member who is eligible to travel on recognition of a relationship and they choose to pay for the travel themselves.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member will be reimbursed in line with the basic benefits in Part 1 of this Chapter if they meet both of the following conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The means of travel under subsection 1 is authorised.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They have no eligibility for vehicle allowance or other forms of reimbursement for the travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member and their resident family who are authorised to travel in a private vehicle may be eligible for vehicle allowance up to the cost of travel by the most economical means.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.7 Member's partner also a member

|  | When a member’s partner is also a member, the family unit has one benefit only. |
|---|---|

###### 9.3.8 Marriage planned or common household started before posting

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for travel for their partner if they provide documentation under subsection 2 and either of these circumstances applies to them.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They have planned to be married but are posted before their planned marriage happens.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They have planned to apply to have their relationship with a person recognised but are posted before the application is granted.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">To qualify, the member must provide documentary evidence that they had completed arrangements for the marriage or had started maintaining a common household before they received the posting authority.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The travel is for the journey from the place of the marriage or common household to the new housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.9 Travel from other location in Australia

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies to a member if all the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The person became the member’s partner in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">At the time the event in paragraph a. occurs, one of the following applies.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They are away from their housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Their primary service location was a seagoing ship or seagoing submarine.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The marriage or the application for recognition or registration of the partner was not arranged before the start of the member's posting period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">They have at least 12 months left to serve on continuous full-time service when the benefit under this section is approved.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td colspan="2">They would have been eligible for travel benefits if they had a partner before they commenced their posting period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member is eligible for their resident family to travel from the place where the partner lived when they became the member’s resident family to the member's housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">For the purpose of this section a town includes a city, suburb or other distinct residential area.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.10 Travel from outside Australia

| 1. | If a member serving in Australia marries or has an ADF recognised partnership in a location outside Australia, section 9.3.9 applies. This includes a member serving in a seagoing ship or seagoing submarine deployed outside Australia. |
|---|---|
| 2. | For the purpose of subsection 9.3.9.2, the place where the partner lived when they became the member’s resident family is taken to be the person’s point of entry into Australia. |
| 3. | In this section, a person’s **point of entry into Australia** means the international terminal in Australia that is closest to the member’s housing benefit location that has flights available from the person’s normal country of residence, either direct or indirect. |

###### 9.3.11 Change of family status in special circumstances

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A member may change their family status in circumstances other than those in the sections above. In this case, the CDF may approve travel benefits and reimbursements for them or their resident family. The CDF must consider these factors.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Any compassionate grounds.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The nature of the person’s relationship to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Whether it is practical for the member to make private arrangements for the travel.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.12 Travel for a child

|  | If the member’s partner has a child at the time the relationship is recognised, and the child is resident family for travel purposes, the member is eligible for the cost of a fare for the child. |
|---|---|

###### 9.3.14 Travel on next posting

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member who becomes a member who has resident family before commencing a new posting period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">On their next posting, the member is eligible for their resident family to travel from a location in paragraph a to the location in paragraph b.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A location from which the member is eligible for a removal under section 6.5.71.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member's new housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member is removed from a location under section 6.5.71 table item 1.f or table item 2.b, the benefit is limited to the lesser of the following amounts.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The cost of the travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The cost of a travel from the member's housing benefit location or ship's home port at the time the person was recognised as resident family.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 2: Travel on breakdown of relationship

###### 9.3.15 Purpose

|  | This Division provides travel benefits for a non-Service partner following the breakdown of their relationship with a member posted to a location within Australia. |
|---|---|

###### 9.3.17 Members this Division does not apply to

| 1. | A member is not eligible for travel under this Division when they cease to have any resident family or recognised other persons. |
|---|---|
| 2. | This Division does not apply to travel benefits for resident family or recognised other persons on death of a member. |

###### 9.3.18 Travel on breakdown of relationship

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">On breakdown of a relationship, a non-Service partner and their resident family are eligible for travel to the same location for which they are eligible for a removal under Chapter 6 Part 5 Division 10.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1A.</td>
<td colspan="3">A recognised other person is eligible for travel to the same location for which they are eligible for a removal under Chapter 6 Part 5 Division 10 if the CDF approves it after considering the individual circumstances of the recognised other person.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The cost of travel is limited to the cost of travel by the most economical means determined by the CDF under the basic benefit in Part 1 of this Chapter.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">The non-Service partner is eligible only once to travel assistance on the breakdown of a relationship.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">The non-Service partner is eligible for travel costs if they travel by air for reasons other than those provided in section 9.1.4 if all the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF approves the travel by air.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Both the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The non-Service partner pays any additional costs of travelling by air rather than rail.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The non-Service partner pays any excess baggage costs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="3">The non-Service partner may require a child to travel by themselves. If the carrier requires the child to be chaperoned, the non-Service partner must pay for an adult to accompany them.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.19 Accommodation during travel

|  | This table sets out how much a non-Service partner may be reimbursed for reasonable overnight accommodation costs. |
|---|---|

| Item | If the person is… | then the most they will be reimbursed is… |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | the non-Service partner | the amount payable for accommodation at the location to a Colonel or lower under Annex 9.5.A. |
| 2. | resident family or a recognised other person of a non-Service partner who is:<br>a. more than 5 years old, and<br>b. occupies a separate room | the amount payable for accommodation at the location to a Colonel or lower under Annex 9.5.A. |
| 3. | resident family or a recognised other person of a non-Service partner who is less than 5 years old | 10% of the amount worked out under item 1. |
| 4. | other resident family or recognised other persons of the non-Service partner who share a separate room with a person described in item 2 | 20% of the amount worked out under item 1. |

###### 9.3.20 Meals during travel

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A non-Service partner who is recognised family of a member is eligible to be reimbursed the cost of meals for themselves and the member’s resident family or recognised other persons travelling with them during travel up to the following amounts.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the person is aged 10 or more — the amount payable for meals under Part 5, Payment of travel costs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the person is aged under 10 — 50% of the amount payable for meals under Part 5, Payment of travel costs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">In all cases, the person will be paid at the rate payable for the relevant location below.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Where they began the journey, if it takes less than a day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Where they stay overnight, if the journey takes more than a day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The non-Service partner may be reimbursed for each meal period that begins at these times during the journey.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Breakfast: 0700 hours</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Lunch: 1300 hours</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Dinner: 1900 hours.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the journey begins after the start of a meal period, the non-Service partner is not eligible for reimbursement for that meal period.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.21 Travel by private vehicle

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A non-Service partner, resident family and recognised other persons who are authorised to travel by private vehicle may be reimbursed the cost of travel. This also applies if they tow a towable item.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The amount they may be reimbursed is the lesser of the two amounts at a. and b.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The sum of these three amounts (if they apply).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Vehicle allowance worked out under Part 6 of this Chapter as if the non‑Service partner were an eligible member for the purposes of that Part.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Accommodation and meal costs worked out under sections 9.3.19 and 9.3.20.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>If it has been approved that the vehicle can be transported for a part of the journey:<br>A. the cost of transporting the vehicle and towable item (if that applies), plus<br>B. the fares for the non-Service partner, resident family and recognised other persons for that part of the journey.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The sum of these three amounts (if they apply).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The fares of the non-Service partner, resident family and recognised other persons for travel by the most economical means.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The cost of removing the vehicle and a towable item if the removal has been approved under Chapter 6 Part 5 Division 5.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>Accommodation and meal costs for travel by the most economical means, worked out under sections 9.3.19 and 9.3.20.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">It is expected that a person will complete the journey at a daily driving rate of:</td>

<td colspan="2">480 km, or</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">360 km if towing a towable item under a removal benefit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.22 Baggage

| 1. | A non-Service partner is eligible for the cost of carrying up to 156 kilograms of baggage that cannot be removed with furniture and effects. |
|---|---|
| 1A. | Baggage benefits under this section are subject to the same conditions that apply under sections 9.1.10 and 9.1.11. |
| 2. | The baggage must be transported by the most economical means. However, the non‑Service partner can carry some baggage with them as accompanied baggage. In this case, it does not matter if it is excess accompanied baggage or included in the fare. This table sets out the amount of baggage they can carry in this way. |

| Item | If the person travels by… | then the amount of baggage they can carry is… |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | rail | a. one piece of baggage per family unit, and<br>b. one additional piece of baggage each for the non-Service partner and any adults who are recognised as resident family or as a recognised other person. |
| 2. | air | a. up to 2 pieces of baggage per family unit, and<br>b. one additional piece of baggage each for the non-Service partner and any adults who are recognised as resident family or as a recognised other person. |

##### Division 3: Travel on maternity leave

###### 9.3.24 Purpose

|  | This Division provides a travel benefit for a member who travels to access extended family support during a period of maternity leave. |
|---|---|

###### 9.3.25 Member this Division applies to

| 1. | This Division applies to a member who has no resident family who is pregnant. |
|---|---|
| 2. | For the purpose of the return trip, this Division continues to apply to the member after the pregnancy ends. |

###### 9.3.26 Travel on maternity leave

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member this Division applies to is eligible for a return trip to a location in Australia. The trip must be in connection with the member's maternity leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Maternity leave travel is limited to both the following amounts.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The cost of travel by the most economical means.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Door-to-door travel costs.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.27 Transfer of benefit

| 1. | The pregnant member may choose to transfer their benefit to their nominated family. This is to allow one or more of the nominated family to travel from their home to the member’s housing benefit location, and back again. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The maximum benefit under this section is the value of the benefit that the member is eligible for under section 9.3.26. |

##### Division 4: Reunion travel

###### Subdivision 1: General provisions

###### 9.3.28 Purpose

|  | The purpose of reunion travel is to reunite a member with resident family or non-resident family who do not reside in the member’s housing benefit location.<br>**Note:** The travel may be used for the member to visit their family, or for the family to visit the member. |
|---|---|

###### 9.3.29 Limits on reunion travel within a 12‑month period

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">The combined maximum number of reunion travel credits a member can use under this Division within a 12‑month period is one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the member has unaccompanied resident family only — 6 credits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the member has unaccompanied resident family and non-resident family — 6 credits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>If the member has accompanied resident family only and is posted to a seagoing ship, seagoing submarine or seagoing flight.— 6 credits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>If the member has accompanied resident family and non-resident family and is posted to a seagoing ship, seagoing submarine or seagoing flight — 6 credits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>If the member has accompanied resident family and non-resident family — 2 credits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td>If the member has non-resident family only — 1 credit.<br><b>Note:</b> Recreation leave travel is also provided to members who have no resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> The number of reunion travel credits a member is eligible for is provided under the following:<br>a. For reunion travel to see resident family, one of the following.<br>i. For a member on a flexible service determination — section 9.3.33E.<br>ii. For any other member — section 9.3.33D.<br>b. For reunion travel to see non-resident family, section 9.3.39J.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.31 Using reunion travel credits

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member's reunion travel credits may be used by the member or one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If using a reunion travel credit under subdivision 2 — the member’s resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If using a reunion travel credit under subdivision 3 — any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member’s resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member’s non-resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A reunion travel credit cannot be used for a member’s resident family or non-resident family to travel if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The resident family or non-resident family will travel to or from a location that will result in them being required to isolate.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The requirement to isolate is known before the travel commences.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">If the member is to be absent from duty on the days they travel using a reunion travel credit, the member must be on one of the following to use a reunion travel credit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">A type of leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">A type of short absence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">A nonworking period.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.32 How reunion travel credits are reduced

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member's reunion travel credits are reduced by all the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the benefit is taken using subsection 9.3.33.1 — one credit for each person who travels using the member’s reunion travel credits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the benefit is taken using subsection 9.3.33.3 — the number of credits used.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">If all of the following apply — one credit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member serves on temporary duty in the same location as their resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member is not required for duty for 2 or more days in a row.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">For the purpose of paragraph 1.c, <b>location</b> means the location that would be the member’s housing benefit location if the temporary duty location was the member’s primary service location.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.33 Benefit for each reunion travel credit

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">If the travel is booked by Defence, the reunion travel credit is all the following between the locations specified in subsection 2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Door-to-door travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">A return economy class airfare.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">Travel under subsection 1 or 3 is to be between a location in paragraph a. and a location in paragraph b.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">One of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The location the member is performing duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>If the member’s primary service location is a seagoing ship, seagoing submarine or seagoing flight — the port in Australia where the member is.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">One of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>If the resident family or non-resident family live in Australia, the location of their home.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>If the resident family or non-resident family do not live in Australia, the nearest international terminal in Australia to the member's primary service location that has flights to or from the country where the resident family or non-resident family live.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">If travel is not booked by Defence, a reunion travel credit is the lesser of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The value of the benefit provided is one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>If the travel includes air travel — the value of the benefit provided under subsection 1 and calculated under section 9.1.8.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>If the travel does not include air travel — an amount up to the normal departmental liability under section 9.1.7 that would have been payable.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The actual total cost of door-to-door travel and airfares for the person travelling on the reunion travel credit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note 1:</b> A member may use one reunion travel credit under this subsection for multiple people to travel if it does not exceed the value of the benefit that would be provided for one person to travel under section 9.1.8.<br><b>Note 2:</b> The benefit under this subsection is paid by reimbursement.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.33A Using multiple reunion travel credits

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A member may use more than one reunion travel credit under this Division at the same time if all the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The CDF is satisfied that the use of more than one reunion travel credit at a time is reasonable.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Two or more of the member’s resident or non-resident family are travelling to the member’s duty location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The member has the required number of reunion travel credits.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.33B Additional benefits for each reunion travel credit – COVID-19

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies to a member if they use a reunion travel credit under this Division and are required to isolate as a consequence of being in a place that is in connection with the reunion travel.<br><b>Note:</b> This section does not apply to resident family or non-resident family travelling on a member’s reunion travel credit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is eligible for additional benefits if they have not used a reunion travel credit under section 9.3.31 in the lesser of the following periods.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The period 6 months before the reunion travel credit is to be used.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the CDF is satisfied there are exceptional circumstances — a period less than 6 months before the reunion travel credit is to be used.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member cannot receive additional benefits under this section more than twice within a 12‑month period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member is not eligible for a payment for a meal that has been provided to the person at no cost.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="3">In this section, <b>additional benefits</b> means any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the place of isolation is directed by State or Territory authorities and is not the member’s usual residence — the cost of the accommodation in which the member is required to isolate.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the place of isolation is not directed by State or Territory authorities and it is not practical for the person to complete the isolation period at their usual residence, one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>If available — access to a quarantine residence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>If a quarantine residence is not available — travelling allowance payable under section 9.5.35.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subject to subsection 5, if a member is occupying a quarantine residence, the sum of the amounts for the following meals that corresponds with the location of the member in column A of the table in Annex 9.5.A Part 4 that the member is eligible to receive meal supplement allowance for.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>For breakfast — the amount in column B.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>For lunch — the amount in column C.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>For dinner — the amount in column D.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member is required to isolate in a place that is not their usual place of residence, the amount for incidentals for the location of the member in column A of the table in Annex 9.5.A Part 4 that is specified in column E.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note 1:</b> There is no benefit under subsection 2 for a member who is required to isolate in their usual residence.<br><b>Note 2:</b> Additional benefits under subsection 2 may be reimbursed to the member or paid to the service provider.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### Subdivision 2: Reunion travel — reuniting with resident family

###### 9.3.33C Member this Subdivision applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">This subdivision applies to a member performing duty in Australia who meets one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They have unaccompanied resident family and no accompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They meet all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They have accompanied resident family and no unaccompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They are posted to a seagoing ship, seagoing submarine or seagoing flight that is not in its home port.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note 1</b>: Subdivision 3 provides reunion travel for members to reunite with their non-resident family.<br><b>Note 2:</b> Section 1.3.1 defines resident family as meaning a member’s accompanied and unaccompanied resident family.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.33D Reunion travel credits — general

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member who is not the subject of a flexible service determination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for the following number of reunion travel credits under this subdivision.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If they are expected to be separated from their resident family for 12 months —6 credits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If they are expected to be separated from their resident family for less than 12 months — 1 credit for every 2 months they expect to be separated from their resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member who is separated from their resident family for less than 2 months is not eligible for a reunion travel credit under this subdivision.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.33E Reunion travel credits — member on a flexible service determination

| 1. | This section applies to a member who is the subject of a flexible service determination. |
|---|---|
| 2. | A member who has a percentage of full time duty set out in column A of the following table is eligible for the percentage of a reunion travel credit set out in set out in column B of the same item for every 2 months of separation from their resident family. |

| **Item** | **Column A**<br>**Percentage of full time duty** | **Column B**<br>**Percentage of a reunion travel credit** |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | Less than 25% | 33% |
| 2. | 25% to 50% | 50% |
| 3. | More than 50% and less than 75% | 66% |
| 4. | 75% to less than 100% | 83% |

<table>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member’s percentage of full time duty is calculated using the following formula.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">[image: Start formula percentage of full time duty equals start fraction A plus B over C end fraction times 100 end formula]</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>A</b></td>
<td>is the number of full days of duty in the member's pattern of service over the duration of the flexible service determination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>B</b></td>
<td>is the number of part days of duty in a fortnight that when combined add up to 8 hours, over the duration of the flexible service determination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>C</b></td>
<td>is the total number of days over the duration of the flexible service determination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">The number of reunion travel credits a member is eligible for under this section is calculated using the following formula, rounded to the nearest whole number.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">[image: Start formula number of credits under this section equals A time B end formula]</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>A</b></td>
<td>The percentage of a reunion travel credit the member is eligible to receive for each 2‑month period of separation under subsection 2 column B.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>B</b></td>
<td>The number of 2‑month periods the member will be separated from their resident family within a 12‑month period.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.33F Reunion travel credits — when flexible service determination is varied

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">If a member’s pattern of service is varied for more than 28 days continuous days, the number of reunion travel credits is to be recalculated in accordance with section 9.3.33E.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member’s reunion travel credits are increased to 6 if they meet one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">All of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member’s flexible service determination is ended for Service reasons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>When the member last received a reunion travel credit they were expected to be separated from their resident family for at least 12 months.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>There is at least 3 months remaining in the period of separation under subparagraph ii.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">All of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member ends their flexible service determination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>When the member last received a reunion travel credit they were expected to be separated from their resident family for at least 12 months.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>There is at least 6 months remaining in the period of separation under subparagraph ii.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.33G Crediting of reunion travel credits

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Reunion travel credits under this subdivision are credited to the member on one of the following days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the separation period occurs immediately after the member was living with their resident family — the day the separation period commences.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the separation period is expected to continue for more than 2 months immediately after the member's reunion travel credits have expired under subsection 2 — the day after the reunion travel credits expire.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.33H Expiry of reunion travel credits

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Reunion travel credits under this subdivision expire on one of the following days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the expected period of separation is 12 months or more at the time of giving the credits — the day that is 12 months after they were credited.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the expected period of separation is less than 12 months at the time of giving the credits — the day that is the last day of the expected period of separation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The day the member is no longer separated from their resident family.<br><b>Note:</b> There is no requirement for a member to repay any used credits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The period under subsection 1 may be extended if the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The CDF is satisfied the member could not use the credits due to Service reasons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member continues to be separated from their resident family after their reunion credits would have expired.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> Credits may be used at any time during the period of separation, subject to section 9.3.31.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### Subdivision 3: Reunion travel — reuniting with non-resident family

###### 9.3.33I Member this subdivision applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This subdivision applies to a member who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are performing duty in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They have non-resident family who live outside of the member’s housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.33J Reunion travel credits

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subject to subsection 2, a member is eligible for the following number of reunion travel credits under this subdivision.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the CDF is satisfied that at least one of the member’s non-resident family is expected to live outside of the member’s housing benefit location for 12 months — 2 credits in that period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the CDF is satisfied that at least one of the member’s non-resident family is expected to live outside of the member’s housing benefit location for more than 6 months, but less than 12 months — 1 credit in that period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The number of reunion travel credits a member is eligible for under subsection 1 is reduced by one if the member is eligible for recreation leave travel under Chapter 9 Part 4 Division 1.<br><b>Note:</b> Recreation leave travel is provided to members who have no resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member’s partner is also a member, only one member is eligible for reunion travel credits under this subdivision with respect to the person who is non-resident family.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.33K Crediting of reunion travel credits

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">An initial grant of reunion travel credits under this subdivision occurs on the earlier of the following days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the member has non-resident family not living in their housing benefit location — the day a person is recognised as non-resident family of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The day the member’s non-resident family cease to live in the member’s housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">A grant of reunion travel under this subdivision that is consecutive with a grant of travel leave credits under this section occurs on one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If paragraph 9.3.33J.1.a applied to the previous grant — 12 months after they last received reunion travel credits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If paragraph 9.3.33J.1.b applied to the previous grant — 6 months after they last received reunion travel credits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> If a member has a break in eligibility for reunion travel credits, upon becoming eligible for reunion travel credits again they would receive their next reunion travel credits under subsection 1.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.33L Expiry of reunion travel credits

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Reunion travel credits under this subdivision expire on one of the following days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the expected period that the member will have non-resident family that live in a location that is not the member’s housing benefit location is 12 months or more — the day that is 12 months after they were received the credit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the expected period that the member will have non-resident family that live in a location that is not the member’s housing benefit location is less than 12 months — the day that is the last day of the expected period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>If the member ceases to have non-resident family living outside of their housing benefit location — the last day the member has non-resident family living outside of their housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The period under paragraphs 1.a or 1.b may be extended by up to 12 months if the CDF is satisfied all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member could not use the credits due to Service reasons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member continues to be eligible for reunion travel under this subdivision.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 5: Reunion travel for school students

###### 9.3.34 Purpose

|  | This Division assists a school student to be reunited with their parents. This is because the child did not accompany the member to the new housing benefit location, and continues their education at another location. |
|---|---|

###### 9.3.35 Member this Division applies to

|  | This Division applies to a member who is receiving education assistance for a child. The child must be studying away from the member's housing benefit location. |
|---|---|

###### 9.3.36 Benefit

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is eligible for one return journey for the child in each calendar year. The journey is provided on a door-to-door basis from where the child lives in the school location to the parent’s home in the housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The benefit cannot be carried forward from one calendar year to the next.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may approve 3 additional return journeys for the child in that calendar year.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">For subsection 3, the CDF must consider all these factors.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The age of the child and year of education.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Any relevant school reports on the child's progress.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The availability of board and lodging at the child's school.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The availability and cost of suitable childcare arrangements for the child.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>The period of separation between reunion visits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td>The period of reunion.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>g.</td>
<td>The number of official term breaks operating at the child's school.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>h.</td>
<td>Any other relevant factor, including the continued well-being of the child.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a child's eligibility for education assistance ends, the child's journey home to the parents' location counts as one of 3 additional journeys.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.37 Mode of travel

|  | Travel must be by the most economical means, using student concession fares whenever possible. |
|---|---|

##### Division 6: Student reunion travel to members in remote locations

###### 9.3.38 Purpose

|  | The purpose of this Division is to enable children to be reunited with their parents who are living in a remote location. |
|---|---|

###### 9.3.39 Member this Division applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Division applies to a member who meets both these conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are serving in a remote location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They have a child receiving primary or secondary education outside the remote location. The child must be living away from their parents.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.40 Benefit

| 1. | The member is eligible for 2 return journeys for the child each calendar year. The journey is provided on a door-to-door basis from where the child lives in the school location to the parent’s home in the remote location. |
|---|---|
| 2. | If the child commences school outside the remote location on or after 1 July, only one benefit may be used before 30 November in that school year. |
| 3. | If the member is also eligible for reunion travel for the child as set out in Division 5, the combined number of reunion benefits is limited to 4 a year. |
| 4. | The benefit cannot be carried forward from one calendar year to the next. |
| 5. | Children may travel to a destination other than the remote location to join a member or the member's partner. The cost cannot exceed the cost of travel to the member's remote location. |
| 6. | If the child turns 18 during the last year of secondary school, at the end of the school year the member is eligible for a journey for the child to the member's remote location. Travel is to the remote location at the completion of the school year. |
| 7. | ADF reunion travel does not apply if travel is already provided by a community-based scheme. |

###### 9.3.41 Period of eligibility

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">Eligibility for a benefit under this Division commences on one of the following.</td>
<td></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="3">If the student departs the remote location to attend school — the date of departure from the remote location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="3">If the student does not accompany the member to the remote location — the later of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td colspan="2">The day the member departs for the remote location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td colspan="2">The day the member’s resident family depart for the remote location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.42 Additional travel beyond benefit

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the child has already used the benefit for the calendar year, the CDF may approve one additional journey. This would be for special circumstances only.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The child must be attending a school with four term breaks in the school year.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">Before approving an additional journey, the CDF must consider all these factors.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The age of the child and year of education.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Any relevant school reports on the child's progress.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The availability of board and lodging at the child's school.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The availability and cost of suitable childcare arrangements for the child.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>The period of separation if this additional reunion visit did not occur.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td>The period of reunion.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>g.</td>
<td>Whether severe detriment to the child would result if not allowed this visit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>h.</td>
<td>Any other relevant factor.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.43 Mode of travel

|  | Travel must be by the most economical means, using student concession fares whenever possible. |
|---|---|

##### Division 7: Reunion travel for tertiary students

###### 9.3.44 Purpose

|  | This Division assists a tertiary student to be reunited with their parents in some cases. |
|---|---|

###### 9.3.45 Member this Division applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Division applies to a member who meets either of these conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are eligible for education assistance under Chapter 8 Part 4 Division 5 for a child or adult child who is a tertiary student.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They would have been eligible for education assistance, but is not incurring costs for the student's accommodation.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.46 Benefit

| 1. | The member is eligible for 2 return journeys for the tertiary student each calendar year. The journey is provided on a door-to-door basis from where the student lives in the location of their educational institution to the parent’s home in the housing benefit location. |
|---|---|
| 2. | If the member has a removal to the new location on or after 1 July, only one journey may be taken in that calendar year. |
| 3. | The benefit cannot be carried forward from one calendar year to the next. |
| 4. | ADF reunion travel does not apply if travel is already provided by a community-based scheme. |
| 5. | The benefit ends when the member ceases to be eligible for education assistance for the student. |

###### 9.3.47 Mode of travel

|  | Travel must be by the most economical means, using student concession fares whenever possible. |
|---|---|

##### Division 8: Compassionate travel

###### 9.3.48 Purpose

|  | This Division provides for the cost of the journey to visit a person with a serious or very serious illness, or who has died. |
|---|---|

###### 9.3.49 Overview

| 1. | Compassionate travel may be made available for the death, serious illness or very serious illness of a person described in section 9.3.52. |
|---|---|
| 2. | Compassionate travel may also be available in other exceptional circumstances. |
| 3. | Personal leave for a compassionate reason may not attract a compassionate travel benefit. Compassionate travel can be taken with other types of leave. |
| 4. | A partner may be eligible for compassionate travel in their own right. Special conditions apply. |

###### 9.3.50 Who this Division does not apply to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Division does not apply to these members.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A member who has claimed a benefit for a journey under the Australians dangerously ill scheme.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A member on leave without pay.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>A member posted overseas.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.52 Who may be visited

| 1. | A member is eligible for compassionate travel to visit a person in an item in column A of the following table subject to the conditions in column B of the same item if the CDF approves the travel.<br>**Note:** The person in column A is not required to normally live with the member. |
|---|---|

| Item | Column A<br>Person | Column B<br>Condition |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | A person who is recognised family. | The person is seriously ill. |
| 2. | A person who is any of the following.<br>a. The member's brother or sister.<br>b. The member's parent or guardian.<br>c. Resident family.<br>d. A recognised other person. | Both the following are met.<br>a. The person is seriously ill.<br>b. The member has to be there because no-one else in the family is available and able to help. |
| 3. | A person who is any of the following.<br>a. Recognised family.<br>b. The member's brother or sister.<br>c. The member's parent or guardian.<br>d. Resident family.<br>e. A recognised other person. | One of the following is met.<br>a. The person is very seriously ill.<br>b. The person has recently died. |

| 2. | A member’s partner is eligible for compassionate travel to visit a person in an item in column A of the following table subject to the conditions in column B of the same item if the CDF approves the travel.<br>**Note:** The person in column A is not required to normally live with the member. |
|---|---|

| Item | Column A<br>Person | Column B<br>Condition |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | A person who is any of the following.<br>a. The member.<br>b. The member's child.<br>c. The child of the member's partner. | The person is seriously ill. |
| 2. | A person who is any of the following.<br>a. The parent or guardian of the member's partner.<br>b. The brother or sister of the member's partner.<br>c. A dependant of the member's partner. | Both the following conditions are met.<br>a. The person is seriously ill.<br>b. The partner has to be there because no-one else in the family is available and able to help. |
| 3. | A person who is any of the following.<br>a. The member.<br>b. The child of the member's partner.<br>c. The parent or guardian of the member's partner.<br>d. The brother or sister of the member's partner.<br>e. A dependant of the member's partner. | The person is very seriously ill. |
| 4. | A person who is any of the following.<br>a. The member.<br>b. The child of the member's partner.<br>c. The parent or guardian of the member's partner.<br>d. A dependant of the member's partner.<br>e. The brother or sister of the member's partner. | The person has recently died. |

| 3. | If the member and their partner both qualify for travel for the same event, both may be granted travel. |
|---|---|
| 4. | There is no travel benefit if the person applying to travel is already at the location of the person to be visited. |

###### 9.3.52A Attendance at memorial services – COVID-19

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a person who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are eligible for compassionate travel under section 9.3.52 to visit a person who recently died (“the deceased person”).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They were unable to visit the deceased person due to COVID-19 restrictions that prevented the person from attending a funeral or memorial service for the deceased person.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subject to subsection 3, the person is eligible for compassionate travel to attend a memorial service for the deceased person if approved by the CDF.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">Compassionate travel in subsection 2 must be taken between the following days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The day the COVID-19 restrictions ceased to prevent the person from travelling to a location where the memorial service is to be held.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The day 12 months after the day in paragraph a.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">For the purpose of this section, <b>COVID-19 restrictions</b> include restrictions that apply in the person’s location and in the location of the funeral or memorial service.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.53 Exceptional reasons

|  | The CDF may grant travel for the member or partner if satisfied that other exceptional reasons make their presence essential.<br>**Note**: A relationship with a person who is not listed under section 9.3.52 is not considered to be an exceptional reason. |
|---|---|

###### 9.3.54 Eligibility of member's partner – extra conditions

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">These additional conditions apply to compassionate travel for a partner.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The cost of their travel is limited if they are temporarily absent from their normal place of residence. It must be no more than the cost of return travel from their normal place of residence to the compassionate destination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The CDF is satisfied that the travel would be approved if the member were to travel in the same circumstances.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.55 Travel overseas

| 1. | A member or their partner may apply for assistance with compassionate travel to an overseas location. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The CDF may approve return travel to and from the nearest appropriate international terminal in Australia.<br>**Note:** The member or their resident family are not eligible for assistance for the overseas portion of the journey. |

###### 9.3.56 Compassionate travel and leave

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Compassionate travel may be approved for absence or leave other than personal leave for a compassionate reason.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for personal leave for a compassionate reason each time compassionate leave is granted if they meet all these conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member is in their first year of service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member was under 17 years old at the start of training.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The member needs to travel to visit a person in respect of whom leave has been granted under section 9.3.52.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.57 Means of travel

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member and any resident family are eligible to use these means of transport for compassionate travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>For the forward journey – the fastest available public transport.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>For the return journey – the most economical means of transport.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1A.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>

<td>The member’s ability to travel safely.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The time involved.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The urgency of the situation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> Short absence for travel is not available for travel by private vehicle.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.58 Reimbursement of member's costs

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A member may be reimbursed their costs of using private transport for compassionate travel. They will be reimbursed whichever is the lesser of these two amounts.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The cost of the most economical means of travel for the journey.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Vehicle allowance for the journey.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.59 Transfer of benefit

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member may transfer a benefit for compassionate travel to their partner if Service reasons prevent the member from travelling.<br><b>Note:</b> A member cannot transfer their benefit unless the CDF has approved one for them to transfer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Service reasons may prevent a member from being present when their partner is seriously ill, very seriously ill or otherwise needs support. The CDF may transfer the member's compassionate travel benefits to another family member. The CDF must consider both these factors.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The needs of the member's partner.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The ability of the other person to provide care and support.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.60 Children accompanying the member or partner

<table>
<tr>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

<td>The child cannot be cared for and supervised while their parent or parents are away.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The child will travel with the member, or with the member's partner.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.60A Additional benefits for compassionate travel – COVID-19

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies to a member or their partner who is eligible for compassionate travel under section 9.3.52 and they are required to isolate as a consequence of being in a place in connection with the compassionate travel.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>

<td>For breakfast — the amount in column B.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>

<tr>
<td></td>
