##### Division 9: Australians dangerously ill scheme – within Australia

###### 9.3.63 Purpose

|  | The purpose of this Division is to provide the support of an approved visitor to a member who is hospitalised in Australia with a very serious or serious illness. The visit from an approved visitor is for the benefit of the member. |
|---|---|

###### 9.3.64 Definitions

|  | The following terms are defined for the purposes of this Division. |
|---|---|
|  | **Approved period** has the meaning given in section 9.3.68. |
|  | **Approved visitor** has the meaning given in section 9.3.67. |

###### 9.3.65 Member this Division applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">The CDF may approve a member as eligible for support under this Division when they meet both of the following conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>A member of the Permanent Forces.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>A member of the Reserves on continuous full-time service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>A member of the Reserves who falls ill or is injured while on duty or in uniform.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The medical authority has recommended that a visit will benefit the member in any of the following circumstances.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member has been classified as very seriously ill and is likely to remain so, or may not recover.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member has been classified as seriously ill.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The member has been classified as suffering a serious medical condition and is hospitalised outside of the housing benefit location to receive specialist treatment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.66 Members who this Division does not apply to

|  | This Division does not apply if the member’s visitor normally lives in the location where the member is in hospital. |
|---|---|

###### 9.3.67 People who may be an approved visitor

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may approve one of the following persons as the approved visitor to visit the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A person identified by the member and recorded on PMKeyS as the primary emergency contact in the event of a casualty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Recognised family of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Resident family of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>A parent of the member, if the member has no resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The approved visitor must meet both of the following conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They must live in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They must be fit to travel.<br><b>Note:</b> An approved visitor who has a medical condition that may be affected by travel must obtain written certification from a qualified medical practitioner that they are fit to travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the approved visitor is incapable or unable to travel and provide support to the member, the approved visitor may nominate another person from one of the classes in subsection 1 to be considered.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">In exceptional circumstances, the CDF may approve any of the following people to accompany the approved visitor.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A second parent of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>One or more children of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>A chaperone for the member's child.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>A carer of the approved visitor.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.68 Approved period for visit

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member may have a visit at Commonwealth expense from an approved visitor for a period of up to 7 consecutive days.<br><b>Note:</b> The 7 consecutive days is inclusive of the return travel time.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may approve additional benefits in relation to a visit when both of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The medical authority recommends that a longer period will significantly benefit the member</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>One of the circumstances in the following table applies.</td>
</tr>
</table>

<table>
<tr>
<td>Item</td>
<td>Length of recommended visit...</td>
<td>when...</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td rowspan="2">1.</td>
<td rowspan="2">up to 21 consecutive days</td>
<td>the member has had major surgery and the post-operative recovery is to last longer than 7 consecutive days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>the member is undergoing specialist treatment in hospital that will last longer than 7 consecutive days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td>21 or more consecutive days</td>
<td>the member has been assessed by the medical authority as likely to remain very seriously ill or seriously ill for longer than 21 consecutive days.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.69 Long term illness

|  | A member ceases to be eligible for assistance under this Division from the day they are provided a sustainable welfare management plan. This does not affect the return travel benefit for any approved visitor. |
|---|---|

###### 9.3.71 Assistance with domestic travel

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may approve return economy class air travel within Australia for the approved visitor.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">If air travel is not available to the location where the member is hospitalised, assistance with the cost of other modes of transport, such as rail or road, is provided to the approved visitor.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">Costs incurred by the approved visitor for public transport, including taxi fares, between any of the following locations may be reimbursed on the production of receipts.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member's hospital.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The approved visitor's accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The airport, bus or train terminal.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The approved visitor's home.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may approve the reimbursement of the lower of the following costs if the approved visitor arranged their own travel prior to the benefit being approved.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The amount incurred by the approved visitor. The approved visitor must produce receipts for the travel to allow for reimbursement.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The amount that would have been incurred if the travel had been taken by a member and the travel had been arranged by Defence Member and Family Support.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is not eligible for the travel costs for more than one trip by the approved visitor during the approved period unless all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The approved visitor is required to return to their home location during the approved period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The CDF is satisfied there are exceptional circumstances to approve more than one trip.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6.</td>
<td colspan="2">The approved visitor may choose to stay beyond the approved period. The costs that may be reimbursed for travel after the approved period are limited. The CDF may only approve the lesser of the following costs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The cost of the return journey incurred by the approved visitor. The approved visitor must produce receipts for the travel to allow for reimbursement.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The cost that would have been incurred if the travel had been taken by a member and if the return journey had been arranged by Defence Member and Family Support.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.72 Travel by private vehicle

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">The CDF may approve travel by private vehicle when both the following conditions are met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The approved visitor wishes to travel by private vehicle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.73 Assistance with accommodation

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may approve commercial accommodation up to the relevant rate in Annex 9.5.A Part 1 column C.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>

<td>The accommodation is located near the member's hospital.</td>

<td></td>

<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The cost of the accommodation that would have been incurred if the visit has been arranged by Defence Member and Family Support.</td>

###### 9.3.74 Assistance with meals

<table>
<tr>

<td colspan="2">The CDF may approve the reimbursement of the lesser of the following meal costs.</td>

<td>The cost of meals incurred by the approved visitor. The approved visitor must produce receipts for the meals to allow for reimbursement.</td>

###### 9.3.75 When the member's condition changes

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member's condition improves and their condition is no longer classified by a medical authority as very seriously ill or seriously ill, the benefits provided under this Division ceases 24 hours after the approved person is informed of the member's reclassification.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may approve an extension of the period for which benefits provided under this Division when both of the following conditions are met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The approved visitor has made reasonable efforts to arrange return travel within the 24 hours.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Return travel is unavailable due to circumstances beyond the approved visitor's control.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may approve another visit for the member. The member must meet both of the following conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member was previously classified by medical authority as no longer very seriously ill or seriously ill.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member is reclassified as very seriously or seriously ill.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 10: Travel for resident family on death of a member

###### 9.3.76 Purpose

|  | This Division describes travel, baggage and accommodation benefit for resident family of a member who dies while serving in Australia. This includes a member who dies while serving in a seagoing ship or seagoing submarine. |
|---|---|

###### 9.3.77 Basic benefit

|  | If a member dies while serving in Australia, their resident family may be granted travel from their location to one of the locations in this table. |
|---|---|

<table>
<tr>
<td>Item</td>
<td>The resident family may be granted travel to…</td>
<td>with the condition that…</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="3"><i>Member of the Permanent Forces at the time of death</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td>the location of the last permanent residence of the member and their resident family at the time of enlistment or appointment</td>
<td>travel is limited if appointment or enlistment was from outside Australia.<br>a. If the member was appointed or enlisted from Norfolk Island, travel is to Sydney.<br>b. If the member was appointed or enlisted from any other external territory of Australia, travel is to the capital city nominated by the resident family.<br>c. If the member was appointed or enlisted from another country, travel is to the port at which the member first entered Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td>any other location in Australia</td>
<td>One of the following:<br>a. If the CDF is satisfied that the resident family have established or intend to establish a permanent home there — there are no conditions imposed on the travel.<br>b. In all other cases — the payment will be no more than the cost of the travel benefit in item 1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="3"><i>Member of the Reserves on continuous full-time service at the time of death</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td>the location where the member lived immediately before starting full-time service</td>
<td>–</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td>any other location in Australia</td>
<td>the cost of the travel is no more than the benefit in item 1.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.77A Recognised other persons

|  | A recognised other person is eligible for the travel benefits under this Division that would apply if they were resident family if the CDF approves it after considering the individual circumstances of the recognised other person. |
|---|---|

###### 9.3.78 Member not living with their resident family at time of death

|  | If a member is not living with their resident family at the time of death, the basic travel benefits in Part 1 of this Chapter apply to the resident family. |
|---|---|

###### 9.3.79 Deceased member's partner also a member

|  | The travel benefits in this Division apply when the deceased member’s partner is a member. |
|---|---|

###### 9.3.80 Means of travel

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Resident family travelling on the death of a member are eligible for travel by the most economical and practical means.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member’s resident family travel by means that are not the most economical both the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The maximum benefit is the cost of travel by the most economical means.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member must pay any costs in excess of the amount in paragraph a. before the travel is undertaken.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.81 Travel by coach

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Travel by coach may only be approved as the most economical means for one of these reasons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>It is the only means available.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The resident family request it as the most appropriate.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">In all other instances travel by coach should be limited. It can be used if it is the only way resident family can be taken to or from the transport used for the major part of the journey.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.3.83 Baggage

|  | If baggage is included with furniture and effects, the insurance provisions for removal on death of a member under Chapter 6 Part 5 Division 11 will apply. |
|---|---|

###### 9.3.84 Deferral of a resident family's travel

|  | Resident family may defer travel for no more than 12 months from the date of the member’s death. |
|---|---|

##### Division 11: Travel for representational purposes

###### 9.3.85 Member accompanied on business travel within Australia

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is not eligible to have their partner accompany them on Defence business travel within Australia using a benefit provided under this Determination unless the CDF is satisfied that, considering the purpose of the travel, it is demonstrably in the interests of the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the CDF approves accompanied travel on Defence business within Australia, the member is eligible for all the following, as applicable.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The reasonable additional cost of accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The partner's transportation cost by the same mode and class of travel as the member. This is the only transportation cost payable for the member's partner.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Costs incurred for meals, up to the same daily limit as the member’s eligibility for meals under Annex 9.5.A Part 4 for travel on Defence business within Australia.</td>
</tr>
</table>

#### Part 4: Leave travel

##### Division 1A: General provisions

###### 9.4.1 Overview

|  | This Part details the travel benefits that a member can use with their leave. |
|---|---|

###### 9.4.3 Nominated family

| 2. | This table shows who a member's nominated family is. |
|---|---|

| Item | If the member... | then... |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | has no partner and no children | their nominated family is their parents, or another person the CDF approves under section 9.4.4, as their closest relative. |
| 2. | has no partner but has children who are resident family living with them | the member is not eligible for recreation leave travel. |
| 3. | has no partner, and has children not living with them | their nominated family is their children, or another person the CDF approves under section 9.4.4 as their closest relative. |
| 4. | has a partner, but has no resident family because the couple do not live together | their nominated family is their partner. |

| 3. | If the member's nominated family normally live at separate locations, the member may alternate between those locations. |
|---|---|
| 4. | The member must notify any relevant change in family circumstances. A relevant change is one which could affect their eligibility for recreation leave travel. |

###### 9.4.4 CDF approval of closest relative

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member whose nominated family would be a parent or child under table item 1 or 3 of the table in subsection 9.4.3.2. It applies only if the CDF is satisfied on either of these two grounds.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>It is not practical for the member to visit the relative, or the member is estranged from the relative.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member has closer ties to a person other than the relative.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may approve a person as the member's closest relative. The CDF must consider the nature and length of their relationship. Any of these relationships could apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Blood.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Law.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Traditional kinship.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> An approval under this section is expected to apply long-term. The member should only seek a new approval after a significant change in family circumstances.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.4.4A Interaction with other travel and reunion benefits

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">The combined total number of the following types of travel must not exceed 7 in the same 12-month period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Recreation leave travel under Division 1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Remote location leave travel under Division 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Reunion travel for members under Part 3 Division 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> For the purpose of counting the number of trips, one reunion travel credit is equal to one trip.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 1: Recreation leave travel

###### 9.4.5 Purpose

|  | This Division enables a member who has no resident family, including a trainee, to travel away from their housing benefit location while on leave or during course breaks to visit their nominated family, or in limited circumstances, another location. |
|---|---|

###### 9.4.5A Members this Division applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">This Division applies to a member who meets the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are a member who has no resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are on recreation leave or a course break.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are not on one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>A long-term posting overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Short-term duty overseas.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.4.6 Eligibility for recreation leave travel within Australia

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">Subject to subsection 2, a member is eligible for recreation leave travel if the CDF is satisfied of any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">All of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member’s nominated family is in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member’s nominated family is not at the member’s housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The member is going to visit their nominated family during the period of leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member has no nominated family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member must not knowingly use recreation leave travel to travel to a place that would require them to isolate on their return to their housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.4.7 Recreation leave travel benefit

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">Recreation leave travel is the return travel for a member from the location they are performing duty to one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member’s nominated family is in Australia — the location where their nominated family live.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member has no nominated family — one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The nearest capital city.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>If the member is performing duty in a capital city — the next nearest capital city.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">Despite subsection 1, a member who takes their recreation leave travel in connection with a removal under Division 4 of Part 5 to Chapter 6 can use their return travel to travel to one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The location they took the travel from.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Their new housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">Recreation leave travel is limited to the following costs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The cost of travel by the most economical means.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Door-to-door travel costs.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.4.8 Number of recreation leave travel trips

| 1. | A trainee may be provided with up to 3 return trips in a financial year, including any graduation trip. |
|---|---|
| 2. | Any other eligible member, including a member undergoing training, may be provided with one return trip in a financial year. |
| 3. | If a member cannot be granted their recreation leave travel benefit for Service reasons, they may apply for the CDF to defer it once only, into the following financial year. They must still meet all the conditions for eligibility in that following year. |
| 4. | A member may be recalled from leave for Service reasons while using a recreation leave travel benefit. In this case, they are taken not to have used their travel benefit. |

###### 9.4.9 Travel in advance of eligibility

| 1. | A member who is expected to be eligible for recreation leave travel trips in the next year is eligible to use that recreation leave travel in advance of becoming eligible for it, if the CDF approves it. |
|---|---|
| 2. | If a member uses a recreation leave travel benefit under subsection 1, the number of recreation leave travel trips the member is eligible for in the next year is reduced by 1 for each trip taken in advance. |

###### 9.4.10 Excess travel costs

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A member who chooses to travel by means that are not the most economical must do both the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Pay any travel costs above the normal departmental liability.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Pay those excess costs before the booking is finalised. They pay them to the Collector of Relevant Money.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.4.11 Offset of benefit for travel to alternative destination

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member can put the value of their benefit towards the cost of travel to meet their nominated family in a destination alternative to the place where the nominated family normally lives in Australia. One of these conditions must be met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The CDF is satisfied that their nominated family is located at the alternative destination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member’s benefit under section 9.4.3 is to the capital city nearest their housing benefit location, and they wish to go somewhere else.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The maximum benefit is the lesser of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The cost of the actual travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The cost of Defence travel to where the nominated family normally live, by the most economical means.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.4.12 Vehicle allowance for trip to transport terminal

| 1. | A member is eligible for vehicle allowance for the trip their vehicle makes from their residence to a transport terminal and back again. They do not have to be present for the whole of that journey. They could have been dropped off at the terminal to continue their journey on recreation leave travel at Commonwealth expense. |
|---|---|
| 2. | Payment of vehicle allowance under subsection 1 must not be more than the normal departmental liability. |

###### 9.4.13 Transfer of benefit

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subject to subsection 2, a member may transfer their benefit to their nominated family to provide for one or more of their nominated family with return travel between their home and the member’s service location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The following conditions apply to the transfer of a benefit under subsection 1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The cost of the travel is limited to what the member would have been eligible for under section 9.4.7.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member cannot transfer their benefit if the nominated family would be required to isolate on entering the service location.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.4.14 Member with family overseas

| 1. | The CDF may grant recreation leave travel under this Division to a member whose nominated family is living overseas. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The member is eligible for return travel to an international terminal in Australia. The terminal must be the one nearest their housing benefit location from which a flight goes to where the nominated family lives. The travel must be by the most economical means. |

###### 9.4.15 Recreation leave travel – trainees

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may approve recreation leave travel under this Division for a trainee on all the following conditions, in addition to relevant conditions in this Division.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The travel is during a course break, or on graduation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Approval is subject to Service requirements and course structures.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Travel may be refused for disciplinary reasons, or because of unsatisfactory academic progress, or for any other reason related to the member's training.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 2: Pre-deployment leave travel

###### 9.4.16 Purpose

|  | This Division allows a member to travel when a short absence – pre-deployment has been granted. |
|---|---|

###### 9.4.17 Benefit

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for pre-deployment leave travel if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member has been granted a short absence – pre-deployment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the member has nominated family — the nominated family is not at the member’s housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The member will not be going to a place that would require the member to isolate on their return to their housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1A.</td>
<td colspan="2">Pre-deployment leave travel is the cost of travel from the member’s location in Australia to one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the member’s nominated family is in Australia — to the location of their nominated family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the member has no nominated family — to the nearest capital city.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Pre-deployment leave travel is provided on a door-to-door basis.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.4.18 Member not eligible

|  | If a member has a recreation leave travel benefit, it must be used instead of a pre‑deployment leave travel benefit. |
|---|---|

###### 9.4.19 Offset of benefit

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">A member can put the cost of their benefit towards the cost of travel to somewhere other than their housing benefit location or family benefit location. Both these conditions must be met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member pays any excess costs involved.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The authorised person is satisfied on both these counts.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Special circumstances exist.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member's need for travel is consistent with purpose of a short absence – pre-deployment</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 3: Post-deployment leave travel

###### 9.4.20 Purpose

|  | This Division provides a member with travel within Australia when leave has been granted on return from a deployment. |
|---|---|

###### 9.4.21 Benefit

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for post-deployment leave travel if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member has returned to Australia from an area that attracted a short absence – pre-deployment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the member has nominated family — the nominated family is not at the member’s housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The member will not be going to a place that would require the member to isolate on their return to their housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1A.</td>
<td colspan="2">Post-deployment leave travel is the cost of travel from the member’s location in Australia to one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the member’s nominated family is in Australia — to the location of their nominated family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the member has no nominated family — to the nearest capital city.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>

</tr>
</table>

###### 9.4.22 Member must use recreation leave travel if available

|  | For travel to be granted under section 9.4.21, the member must have no recreation leave travel benefit left. If a member has a recreation leave travel benefit, they must use it instead of post-deployment travel. |
|---|---|

##### Division 4: Remote location leave travel

###### 9.4.23 Purpose

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Remote location leave travel enables all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Members and their resident family the opportunity to seek relief from living in the remote location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Close family members to visit the member or their resident family at the remote location.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.4.25 Definitions

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">The following terms are defined for the purposes of this Division.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Close family member</b> means any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member’s child, parent, grandparent, grandchild, brother or sister.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The child, parent, grandparent, grandchild, brother or sister of a member’s partner.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The member's partner who lives outside the remote location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Transfer</b>, in relation to the transfer of a benefit, includes the transfer of any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Eligibility for transportation benefits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Eligibility for the member to be paid vehicle allowance for travel by another specified person in a private vehicle.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.4.25A Conditions on using remote location leave travel benefits

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">All of the following apply to a remote location leave travel benefit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A member can only use a benefit during a period they are not required for duty.<br><b>Note:</b> To avoid doubt, this does not prevent a transferred benefit from being used during a period the member is required for duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A person can only use one benefit for each journey.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.4.25B Value of remote location leave travel benefit

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">The value of remote location leave travel benefit is one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the travel is booked by Defence — the best fare of the day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the travel is not booked by Defence — the lesser of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The actual cost incurred by the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The normal departmental liability as described under section 9.1.8.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.4.26 Scheme A – member who has no resident family

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies to a member who has no resident family who is posted to a remote location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">Remote location leave travel benefit is one of the following between the locations specified in subsection 2A and subject to subsection 2B.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member flies — return flights.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member drives — vehicle allowance up to the value of the flights had the member flown.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2A.</td>
<td colspan="3">Remote location leave travel is between the following locations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">From one of the following locations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member’s housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

###### 9.4.32 Scheme A – offset of benefit to another destination

<table>

<td></td>
<td>b.</td>

<td></td>
<td></td>

<td>It contains commercially provided travel to the destination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>

<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The nearest capital city.</td>
</tr>

<td></td>

<td>ii.</td>
<td>If the remote location is in the Northern Territory — Adelaide.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">For the purpose of paragraph 2.a, if the member’s primary service location is one of the following locations, the maximum amount payable under subsection 2 is the amount relevant for the location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Tindal, the amount that may be paid includes.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The lesser of either vehicle allowance or the cost of motor vehicle hire for return travel between Tindal and Darwin.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The cost of return air fare for travel between Darwin and Adelaide.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Woomera, the amount that may be paid includes.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The cost of vehicle allowance for return travel between Woomera and the airport at Olympic Dam.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The cost of return air fare for travel between Olympic Dam and Adelaide.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">A remote location that does not have a commercial airport, the amount that may be paid includes.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The lesser of either vehicle allowance or the cost of public transport for return travel between the housing benefit location and the closest airport.<br><b>Note:</b> The closest airport is the one closest by travel time to the remote location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The cost of return air fare for travel between the closest airport and the nearest capital city.<br><b>Note:</b> For remote locations in the Northern Territory, the nearest capital city is taken to be Adelaide.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">A remote location leave travel benefit that is used to fund an offset is taken to have been used by the member or their resident family who the benefit originally accrued for.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.4.33 Schemes A and B – advances of benefit

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member who has a remote location leave travel benefit that Scheme A or Scheme B conditions apply to.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member or their resident family may be granted an advance of one remote location leave travel benefit if the CDF approves having regard to all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The operational requirements relevant to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The likelihood that the benefit will accrue.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member or their resident family who advance a remote location leave travel benefit do not have to repay the value of that travel, should the benefit not accrue.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.4.34 Schemes A and B – lapsing of benefit

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies to a member who has a remote location leave travel benefit. The remote location leave travel benefit may have Scheme A or Scheme B conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">Remote location leave travel benefits lapse on the following days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the benefit a member has accrued is for themselves — the earlier of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The day before the member accrues the next remote location leave travel benefit for themselves.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The last day of the remote location is the member’s primary service location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the benefit a member has accrued is for their resident family — the earlier of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The day before the member accrues the next remote location leave travel benefit for their resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The day before the person recognised as resident family leaves the remote location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The day the person ceases to be recognised as resident family of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">Despite subsection 2<b>,</b> a benefit that has been deferred under section 9.4.35 does not lapse during the period of deferral.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.4.35 Schemes A and B – deferral of benefit

| 1. | A member may apply to defer a remote location leave travel benefit that Scheme A or Scheme B conditions apply to. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The CDF may defer the lapsing of a benefit under subsection 9.4.34.2 for 1 year, having regard to operational requirements relevant to the member. |

###### 9.4.36 Schemes A and B – change in family circumstance

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Changes to a member’s resident family has the following effects on remote location leave travel benefits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>On the date of the change, all outstanding remote location leave travel benefits for the member and their resident family lapse.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>On the date of the change, the member and resident family (if any) do not have to repay any advances of remote location leave travel benefits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The member and resident family, if any, accrue new remote location leave travel benefits on the date of the change, as provided for under sections 9.4.26, 9.4.27 or 9.4.29.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The member's and resident family’s (if any) next accrual of remote location leave travel is on the anniversary of the member's commencement in the remote location, unless section 9.4.37 applies.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.4.37 Schemes A and B – partner is a member

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies to a member who has a remote location leave travel benefit that either Scheme A or Scheme B conditions apply to, in the following circumstances.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member has a partner.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s partner is a member of the ADF.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member and their partner are posted to the same remote location on different dates.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">Despite subsection 9.4.29.3, the member who arrives in the remote location second accrues remote location leave travel benefits at the following times.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s first benefit accrues on the day they arrive in the remote location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s second and subsequent benefits accrue on the same day as the member who arrived in the remote location first.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member accrues remote location leave travel benefits at the following rate.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member or their resident family have a Scheme A remote location leave travel benefit — one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>If the member is serving in a location that attracts ADF District allowance at the Grade A rate — one travel benefit per person.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>If the member is serving in any other remote location — 2 travel benefits per person.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member or their resident family have a Scheme B remote location leave travel benefit — one travel benefit per person.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.4.38 Schemes A and B – partner is a Defence APS employee

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member whose resident family meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They have a remote location leave travel benefit that either Scheme A or Scheme B conditions apply to.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>They are an APS employee of the Department of Defence, who performs duty in the remote location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>They are eligible for assisted leave fares allowance, as an APS employed by the Department of Defence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member accrues one less remote location leave travel for their partner than is provided for in section 9.4.29.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.4.40 Schemes A and B – Tindal travel arrangements

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member if they or their resident family need to travel to or from Tindal as part of remote location leave travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member may be paid whichever of these costs is less.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Vehicle allowance, for the journey between Tindal and Darwin.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Motor vehicle hire costs, as provided for under subsection 3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">For the purpose of paragraph 2.b, motor vehicle hire costs comprise these costs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The cost of motor vehicle hire for the journey between Tindal and Darwin.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Reasonable insurance costs associated with the hire of the motor vehicle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Fuel costs for the journey between Tindal and Darwin.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Reasonable additional compulsory charges.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.4.40A Schemes A and B – additional travel arrangements

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies to a member if they or their resident family need to travel outside of their housing benefit location to access commercial air travel as a part of their remote location leave travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member is eligible for vehicle allowance for return travel by private vehicle between Woomera and the airport at Olympic Dam if all of the following apply.</td>

<td>The member’s primary service location is in Woomera.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">b.</td>
<td>The member does not drive to Adelaide.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">If the member’s primary service location is a location other than Woomera or Tindal — the member is eligible for the lesser of the following for return travel between the housing benefit location and the closest airport.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Vehicle allowance, if the member or their resident family travel by private vehicle.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>

<td></td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.4.41 Schemes A and B – resident family under the age of 18

| 1. | Resident family under the age of 18 may not make choices under this Division. |
|---|---|

#### Part 5: Payment of travel costs

##### Division 1: Members eligible and definitions

###### 9.5.3 Purpose

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Division has two purposes.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>It explains special terms used in this Part.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>It sets out who may be eligible for assistance with the cost of travelling.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.5.4 Member this Part applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This Part applies to a member who is required to travel in one of these situations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">On Defence business and one of the following applies.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They are away overnight.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They are away from their housing benefit location for more than 10 hours on a day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subject to subsection 2, when travelling to their new housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">In preparation or immediately following the end of their continuous full-time service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">This Part only applies to a member who has been approved an alternate located work agreement if, under the agreement, travel would be provided to their new housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.5.5 Member this Part does not apply to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">This Part does not apply to a member who meets any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are undertaking official travel and are eligible for travel benefits under a determination made by the Remuneration Tribunal for that travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are travelling for any of the following purposes.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Compassionate travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Pre-deployment leave travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>Post-deployment leave travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iv.</td>
<td>Recreation leave travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>v.</td>
<td>Remote location leave travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>vi.</td>
<td>Reunion travel.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.5.8 Definitions

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">In this Part, the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>High‑cost country centre</b> means a location mentioned in Annex 9.5.A Part 2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Meal period</b> means a one-hour period that meets both of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">It starts during a travel period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">It starts at one of the following times.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Breakfast – 0700.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Lunch – 1300.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>Dinner – 1900.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Medium‑cost country centre</b> means a location specified in Annex 9.5.A Part 3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Other country centre</b> means a location in Australia that is not one of the following locations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">A capital city.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">A high‑cost country centre.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">A medium‑cost country centre.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Private vehicle</b> means one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">For travel on removal by a member, their resident family or recognised other person — a motor vehicle owned by the member, their resident family or recognised other person that is to be removed.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">For other travel by a member — a motor vehicle they own, hire or borrow.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Rank</b> means the rank a member was promoted to under paragraph 13(1)(a) of the Defence Regulation and does not include any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The rank the member is directed to act in under paragraph 13(1)(b) of the Defence Regulation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The rank of a position in which a member is performing higher duties.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.5.9 Travel period – business travel

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">For this Part, a travel period for a member on business travel is the period when all these conditions apply to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member has been directed to travel to a location in Australia to perform duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The location for duty is not the member's primary service location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The member is absent overnight from their normal place of residence to do the duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The travel period for a member in a situation set out in an item in column A of the following table starts from the day in column B of the same item and ends on the day in column C of the same item.</td>
</tr>
</table>

<table>
<tr>
<td>Item</td>
<td>Column A<br>Member situation</td>
<td>Column B<br>Start day</td>
<td>Column C<br>End day</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td>The member travels direct to the duty location by the most economical means.</td>
<td rowspan="2">The day the member leaves their housing benefit location</td>
<td>The day the member returns to their housing benefit location</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td>The member travels by another means that takes longer than the most economical means for a Service reason.</td>
<td>The day the member returns to their housing benefit location</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td>The member travels by another means that takes longer than the most economical means for a non-Service reason.</td>
<td>The day the member would have left their housing benefit location if they had travelled by the most economical means</td>
<td>The day the member would have returned to their housing benefit location, if they had travelled by the most economical means.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td rowspan="2">4.</td>
<td rowspan="2">The member takes a break unnecessarily or for private reasons during the period.</td>
<td>The day the member leaves their housing benefit location.</td>
<td rowspan="2">The day the member returns to their housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>The day the member resumes the travel for Service reasons.</td>
</tr>
</table>

|  | **Note:** A member may be required to isolate before they return to their housing benefit location. Their travel period includes the isolation period. |
|---|---|

###### 9.5.10 Part-day travel period

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member who meets all of the following conditions is eligible for part-day travelling allowance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member is required to travel outside their housing benefit location on Defence business.</td>

<td></td>

<td></td>

<td>The member is absent from their housing benefit location for 10 hours or more.</td>

<td></td>

<td>The member is not absent from their housing benefit location overnight.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1A.</td>

<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The rate of allowance is $63.60 a day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>

</tr>

###### 9.5.11 Travel period – in connection with change in primary service location

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">In this Part, a <b>travel period</b> for a member travelling in connection with a change in their primary service location is the period when all of the following apply to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member changes from one primary service location in Australia to another.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member must travel to get to their new housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The travel extends overnight.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The travel period for a member in a situation set out in an item in column A of the following table starts from the day in column B of the same item and ends on the day in column C of the same item.</td>
</tr>
</table>

<table>
<tr>
<td>Item</td>
<td>Column A<br>Member situation</td>
<td>Column B<br>Start day</td>
<td>Column C<br>End day</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td>The member travels direct to the duty location by the most economical means.</td>
<td rowspan="3">The day the member leaves their housing benefit location at the losing location.</td>
<td>The day the member arrives at the new housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td>The member travels by another means that takes longer than the most economical means, for a Service reason.</td>
<td>The day the member arrives at the new housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td>The member travels by another means that takes longer than the most economical means, for a non-Service reason.</td>
<td>The day the member would have arrived at the new housing benefit location, if they had travelled by the normal means.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td rowspan="2">4.</td>
<td rowspan="2">The member takes a break unnecessarily or for private reasons during the period.</td>
<td>The day the member leaves their housing benefit location at the losing location.</td>
<td>The day the member returns to their housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>The day the member resumes the travel for Service reasons.</td>
<td>The day the member arrives at the new housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td rowspan="2">5.</td>
<td rowspan="2">The member travels by another means that takes longer than the normal means, because they go on leave between the former housing benefit location (the "losing location") and the gaining location.</td>
<td>The day the member leaves their housing benefit location at the losing location.</td>
<td>The day the member returns to their housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>The day the member resumes the travel to the new housing benefit location.</td>
<td>The day the member arrives at the new housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
</table>

| 3. | If a member is required to isolate on arrival in their housing benefit location in a place other than their residence, the member’s travel period does not end until the isolation period has ended. |
|---|---|

###### 9.5.12 Travel period – ceasing continuous full-time service

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member who meets all these conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are preparing to cease, or have just ceased, a period of continuous full-time service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are not ceasing the continuous full-time service on disciplinary grounds.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>They are not ceasing the continuous full-time service because they have caused themselves to be medically unfit for duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">In this section, a member’s travel period is the period when all these conditions apply to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member is travelling from their last primary service location, or the location where their service ended to another location in Australia. In this section, the destination is called the final location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member is not travelling in a vehicle that they own or hire.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The travel extends overnight.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The travel period for a member in a situation set out in an item in column A of the following table starts from the day in column B of the same item and ends on the day in column C of the same item.</td>
</tr>
</table>

<table>
<tr>
<td>Item</td>
<td>Column A<br>Member situation</td>
<td>Column B<br>Start day</td>
<td>Column C<br>End day</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td>The member travels direct to their final location by the most economical means.</td>
<td>The member leaves one of these places.<br>a. Their last housing benefit location.<br>b. The location where their duty ended.</td>
<td>The day the member arrives at their final location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td rowspan="2">2.</td>
<td rowspan="2">The member takes a break unnecessarily or for private reasons during the period.</td>
<td>The member leaves one of these places.<br>a. Their last housing benefit location.<br>b. The location where their duty ended.</td>
<td>The day the member returns to their housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>The member resumes the travel for Service reasons</td>
<td>The day the member arrives at the final location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td>is required to isolate in their final location in a place that is not their residence</td>
<td>when the member leaves one of these places.<br>a. Their last housing benefit location.<br>b. The location where their duty ended.</td>
<td>when the member has finished their isolation period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td>is required to isolate in a place that is not in their final location</td>
<td>when the member leaves one of these places.<br>a. Their last housing benefit location.<br>b. The location where their duty ended.</td>
<td>when the member arrives in their final location.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 2: Travel on Defence business

###### 9.5.13 Purpose

|  | This Division sets out basic benefits and limitations on use of the travel card. |
|---|---|

###### 9.5.14 Member this Division applies to

| 1. | This Division applies to a member (including a member on Reserve service) who has a Defence travel card and is required to travel on Defence business. |
|---|---|
| 2. | A member who uses a travel card under this Division has no eligibility under Division 3 for travel on Defence business, except as provided by this Division. |

###### 9.5.15 Meaning of normal accommodation stock

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Normal accommodation stock</b> means any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Accommodation that is made available through the contracted service provider for the period required.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the member is required to isolate and it is available — a quarantine residence.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.5.16 Accommodation while living out on a journey

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member who lives out for up to 21 days during a travel period must use normal accommodation stock unless any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They occupy temporary accommodation under section 9.5.18.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are eligible for payments under Division 3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1A.</td>
<td colspan="2">For the purpose of calculating the number of days in the travel period in subsection 1, a day on which the member is required to isolate in a place that is not their residence is not counted.<br><b>Note:</b> A day a member is required to isolate may be included in the travel period under section 9.5.9 but not included for this purpose.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may approve use of accommodation provided by the contracted service provider that is not normal accommodation stock. The CDF must consider the following criteria.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Whether normal accommodation stock is available.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Whether normal accommodation stock is suitable.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may approve the use of accommodation that is not provided by the contracted service provider. The CDF must consider the following criteria.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Whether the contracted service provider is able to supply accommodation at the location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The attempts made by the member to source accommodation from the contracted service provider.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Whether it is possible to cancel or defer the travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Whether the decision is consistent with the Whole-of-Australian Government (WoAG) travel services arrangements and the Commonwealth procurement rules.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> The Commonwealth has a contract with the contracted service provider to provide accommodation services to the whole of Government. Under that contract the contracted service provider is the sole provider of those services. Defence has promised to use accommodation from the contracted service provider.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member who uses accommodation under this section must use the travel card to pay for it.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section ceases to apply to a member from midnight on the 21st day of their travel period.<br><b>Note:</b> Travel costs for travel after the 21st day are provided in section 9.5.22.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.5.17 Meals and incidentals while living out on a journey

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to the following members.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A member who lives out for up to 21 days with accommodation supplied under section 9.5.16.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A member who lives out for up to 21 days in non-commercial accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1A.</td>
<td colspan="2">For the purpose of calculating the number of days in the travel period in subsection 1, a day on which the member is required to isolate in a place that is not their residence is not counted.<br><b>Note</b>: A day a member is required to isolate may be included in the travel period under section 9.5.9 but not included for this purpose.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The maximum daily limits for meals and incidentals are the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>For meals — the sum of rates for each meal period specified for the location in Annex 9.5.A Part 4, columns B, C and D for each day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>For incidentals — the rate in Annex 9.5.A Part 4, column E for each 24 hours of the travel period and for any part-day at the end of the journey.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member is entitled to receive an amount of field allowance determined by the DFRT in the travel period they are not eligible to be paid incidentals for the period the allowance relates to.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section ceases to apply to a member from midnight on the 21st day of their travel period.<br><b>Note:</b> Travel costs for travel after the 21st day are provided in section 9.5.22.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.5.18 Limits on payment for meals and accommodation

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member must not use their travel card to pay for any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a meal has been provided to the member at no cost during the meal period — a meal.<br><b>Note 1:</b> An in-flight meal provided by a commercial carrier is not considered a meal for the purposes of this paragraph.<br><b>Note 2:</b> A member who resides privately with family or friends is still eligible to use their travel card for meals.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If any of the following apply — accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Accommodation is provided to the member at no cost, not including accommodation supplied under section 9.5.16.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member's travel continues overnight without a break for accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The member is ranked Major or lower, and living-in accommodation is available to them.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> If living-in accommodation is available but the member chooses to stay off‑base, they are not eligible to use their travel card for meals or accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">Despite subparagraph 1.b.iii, a member may use their travel card to pay for accommodation if the CDF considers that occupying living‑in accommodation would make the member less efficient in the performance of their duties.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">For the purposes of accommodation, a member is not eligible for any of the following accommodation costs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The difference between what the member actually paid and the maximum allowable amount if they stay in accommodation that is commercially provided.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Any amount if they stay in accommodation that is provided on a non-commercial basis.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">For the purposes of meals, if a member visits more than one location in a day, the location for working out the amount they are eligible for is one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">For a meal that is on the last day of their journey — the location they are at the beginning of the day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">For any other meal — the location they are at the end of the day.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.5.19 When there is no eligibility for incidentals

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is not eligible for incidentals for any part of a travel period when they meet any of these conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are in hospital in a location that is not the location where they have been performing duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are serving in a seagoing ship on temporary duty and performing duty necessary to the proper working of the ship.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are serving in the field as a member of a force on exercise.<br><b>Note:</b> Subsection 2 may make the member eligible for incidentals.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are serving in the field as a member of a survey party and using camping accommodation, but they are not entitled to field allowance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They are part of a survey party but are not on exercise.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They are part of a survey party and are not camping out, but are housed at a Service establishment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are doing a period of recruit training in the Reserves and are not entitled to field allowance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are on a journey related to discharge or dismissal for any of these reasons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Misconduct.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Disciplinary reasons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>Medical unfitness they caused.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>g.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are attending a live-in training course in the member’s housing benefit location, unless the member is eligible for Incidentals under section 9.5.25.<br><b>Note:</b> Subsection 2 may make the member eligible for incidentals.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">Despite subsection 1, the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is serving in the field as a member of a force on exercise and housed at a Service establishment that is not a camp set up for the exercise, the member is eligible for incidentals.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is on a live-in training course that is longer than 21 consecutive days, the member is eligible for incidentals from the 21st day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.5.20 Member occupying living-in accommodation

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies to a member who occupies living-in accommodation during a travel period at a location that is not their housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member is eligible for the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Compulsory mess charges.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Living-in accommodation charges.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">Meals provided in the living-in accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">The following for incidentals.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>For each day of the travel period up to the end of the 21st day — the rate specified in Annex 9.5.A Part 4 column E.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>For each 24 hours of the travel period after the first 21 days and for any part-day at the end of the journey — $12.25 per day.<br><b>Note:</b> If the last day of the member's journey is for a part day, the full rate of incidentals applies for that day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">For the purpose of calculating the number of days in the travel period in subsection 2, a day on which the member is required to isolate in a place that is not their residence is not counted.<br><b>Note:</b> A day a member is required to isolate under section 9.5.9.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.5.21 Keeping accommodation while occupying living-in accommodation on temporary duty

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member who has no resident family who meets all of these conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They live out at their housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>For Service reasons, they must occupy living-in accommodation during the travel period at a location that is not their housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>They occupy living-in accommodation for a continuous period of more than 21 days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is eligible for the reimbursement of the reasonable cost of keeping their accommodation at their housing benefit location for the period beyond 21 days.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.5.22 Travel for more than 21 days

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies to a member who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They live continuously in a location for 21 days or more in one of the following circumstances.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>During a travel period.<br><b>Note:</b> The member can occupy living-in accommodation or stay off-base in another type of accommodation, during the travel period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They normally live out and are required to occupy living-in accommodation in their housing benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They continue to live at the location for a further travel period after the 21st day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member is eligible for all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Accommodation on each night in the travel period at the rate set out in Annex 9.5.B Part 1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Meals for each meal period at the rate set out in Annex 9.5.B Part 2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">Incidentals for the travel period at the rate of $12.25 per day.<br><b>Note:</b> This item also applies to a member who lives out, if they are required to occupy living‑in accommodation beyond 21 days during a course of training at their primary service location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">For the purpose of subsection 1, none of the following are counted as days in the travel period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">A day on which the member is eligible for field allowance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">A day on which the member is required to isolate.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">If the member leaves the location to return to their housing benefit location on one of the following days, their eligibility under this section ends at one of the following times.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The 22nd day – midnight on that day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Any later day – midday on the day they leave the location.</td>

<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="3">If a member is required to isolate on return to their housing benefit location in a place that is not their residence, they are eligible for the following benefits for their isolation period.</td>

<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Accommodation under section 9.5.16.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>

<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for incidentals under the table in section 9.5.17 if they are on Reserve service in either of these circumstances.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>During the period of a bivouac or camp of continuous training with their unit or<br>sub-unit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>During a Reserves activity comparable to those described in paragraph a.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.5.28 Recall from recreation leave or long service leave

| 1. | If a member on recreation or long service leave is recalled to duty, they are taken to be on duty from the time they start travel to return to duty. |
|---|---|
| 2. | If the member travels by private vehicle or private aircraft, their eligibility under sections 9.5.16 and 9.5.17 will be limited to the amount of allowance that would be payable if they returned to duty by the most efficient and economical means of travel. |

###### 9.5.29 Additional payment toward travelling costs

<table>

</tr>
<tr>

</tr>
<tr>

<tr>
<td></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

<td></td>
