###### 9.5.30 End of eligibility

|  | A member ceases to be eligible for any unused amount provided for meal and incidentals in connection with travel at the end of their travel period. |
|---|---|

##### Division 3: Travelling allowance

###### 9.5.32 Purpose

|  | The purpose of this Division is to provide an allowance for accommodation, meals and incidentals for member in certain circumstances when undertaking Defence approved travel within Australia. |
|---|---|

###### 9.5.33 Member this Division applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">This Division applies to a member, including a member on Reserve service, who meets any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are travelling on Defence business and any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They have not been issued a Defence Travel Card.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They are eligible for part-day travelling allowance under section 9.5.10.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are travelling in connection with a change in their primary service location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are travelling on ceasing continuous full-time service.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.5.34 Members this Division does not apply to

| 1. | This Division does not apply to a member who is travelling on Defence business and who has a travel card. |
|---|---|
| 2. | This Division does not apply to travel for which a member is eligible for vehicle allowance or aircraft allowance under Part 6 or 7 of this Chapter, except to the extent allowed for under those Parts. |

###### 9.5.35 Travel costs while living out on a journey

|  | A member who lives out for up to 21 days during a travel period is eligible for travelling allowance for accommodation, meals and incidentals. This table sets out their benefits. |
|---|---|

<table>
<tr>
<td><b>Item</b></td>
<td><b>If the member's rank is…</b></td>
<td><b>then they are eligible for travelling allowance for…</b></td>
<td><b>at this rate…</b></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td rowspan="3">1.</td>
<td rowspan="3">Brigadier or higher</td>
<td>accommodation on each night in the travel period</td>
<td>the rate specified in Annex 9.5.A Part 1 column B for the location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>meals for each meal period</td>
<td>the sum of relevant rates specified in Annex 9.5.A Part 4 columns B, C and D.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>incidentals for each 24 hour period of the journey, and for any part-day at the end</td>
<td>the rate specified in Annex 9.5.A Part 4 column E.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td rowspan="3">2.</td>
<td rowspan="3">Colonel or lower</td>
<td>accommodation on each night in the travel period</td>
<td>the rate specified in Annex 9.5.A Part 1 column C for the location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>meals for each meal period</td>
<td>the sum of relevant rates specified in Annex 9.5.A Part 4 columns B, C and D.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>incidentals for each 24 hour period of the journey, and for any part-day at the end</td>
<td>the rate specified in Annex 9.5.A Part 4 column E.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.5.35A Quarantine residence while living out on a journey

|  | A member who is required to isolate is eligible to occupy a quarantine residence for the isolation period if one is available. |
|---|---|

###### 9.5.36 Limits on travelling allowance for meals and accommodation

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is not eligible for travelling allowance when any of the following conditions are met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">For the purpose of meals — if any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>A meal is provided to the member at no cost.<br><b>Note 1:</b> An in-flight meal provided by a commercial carrier is not considered a meal for the purposes of this paragraph.<br><b>Note 2:</b> A member who resides privately with family or friends is still eligible for meal allowance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The meal period begins before the member's journey.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The meal period begins after the member's journey.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">For the purpose of accommodation — if any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Accommodation is provided to the member at no cost, not including accommodation supplied under section 9.5.16.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member's travel continues overnight without a break for accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The member is ranked Major or lower, and living-in accommodation is available to them.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> If living-in accommodation is available but the member chooses to stay off‑base, they are not eligible for travelling allowance for meals or accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">Despite subparagraph 1.b.iii, a member may receive travelling allowance for accommodation if the CDF considers that occupying living–in accommodation would make the member less efficient in the performance of their duties.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">For the purposes of meals, if a member visits more than one location in a day, the location for working out the amount they are eligible for is one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">For a meal that is on the last day of their journey — the location they are at, at the beginning of the day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">For any other meal — the location they are at, at the end of the day.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.5.37 When there is no eligibility for incidentals

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is not eligible for incidentals for any part of a travel period when they meet any of these conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are doing a period of recruit training in the Reserves and are not entitled to field allowance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are on a journey related to discharge or dismissal for any of these reasons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Misconduct.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Disciplinary reasons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>Medical unfitness they caused.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">Despite paragraph 1.g, if the member is on a live-in training course that is longer than 21 consecutive days, the member is eligible for incidentals from the 21st day.</td>

|---|---|

<table>

###### 9.5.46 Recall from recreation leave or long service leave

| 1. | If a member on recreation or long service leave is recalled to duty, they are taken to be on duty from the time they start travel to return to duty. |
|---|---|
| 2. | If the member travels by private vehicle or private aircraft, their eligibility under this Division will be limited to the amount of travelling allowance that would be payable if they returned to duty by the most efficient and economical means of travel. |

###### 9.5.47 Additional travelling allowance

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member's maximum eligibility for travelling allowance may be less than they actually spend on accommodation, meals or incidentals during the travel period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>

<td></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Whether the extra cost is reasonable.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Any special needs due to the age or medical needs of the member's resident family or recognised other persons.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.5.48 Confirming actual travel costs

| 1. | A member must confirm whether any travel period for which they have received travelling allowance has been taken, using the Defence travel management system. They must do this within 28 days after they end their travel. |
|---|---|
| 2. | If the member has received more travelling allowance than they were eligible for (including any extra amount approved by CDF), they must repay the difference. |

##### Division 4: Travel allowance on removal

###### 9.5.49 Member this Division applies to

|  | This Division applies to a member who is eligible for the removal under Chapter 6 Part 5. |
|---|---|

###### 9.5.50 Definitions

|  | In this Division, the following apply. |
|---|---|
|  | **Person** means the member, their resident family or recognised other persons. |
|  | **Travel allowance** has the meaning given in section 9.5.51 |

###### 9.5.51 Travel allowance on removal

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Travel allowance means the sum of any of the following components that the member is eligible for.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Meals on removal.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Incidentals on removal.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Door-to-door costs on removal.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> The total travel allowance on removal may be reduced by section 6.5A.12.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.5.52 Measurement of distances

|  | For the purpose of this Division, a distance is the number of kilometres to be travelled by the most direct and practicable route. |
|---|---|

###### 9.5.53 Accommodation on removal

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>

</tr>

<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The person is travelling in connection with the member’s removal.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The person is travelling in a vehicle for which vehicle allowance is payable.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member were to drive a vehicle, the distance to be driven is equal to or greater than one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>If the vehicle is towing an item — 360 km.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>If the vehicle is not towing an item — 480 km.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The rate of travel allowance for accommodation is the sum of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">For the member and every third person thereafter, one of the following rates.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>If the member holds a rank of Brigadier or higher — the rate in column B of item 12 of the table in Part 1 of Annex 9.5.A.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>If the member holds a rank of Colonel or lower — the rate in column C of item 12 of the table in Part 1 of Annex 9.5.A.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">For every other person who is 6 years old or older — 20 % of the rate payable for the member under paragraph a.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">For every other person who is younger than 6 years old — 10 % of the rate payable for the member under paragraph a.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> A person is not generally expected to occupy a room with more than 2 other people.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.5.54 Meals on removal

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is eligible for the meals component of travel allowance if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The person is travelling in connection with the member’s removal.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">A person is travelling over a meal period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">One of the following applies.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The person does not drive or is not a passenger in a vehicle and the meal is being provided by a carrier at an additional cost.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The person drives a vehicle not towing an item and the distance to be driven is 480 km or greater.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>If the person drives a vehicle towing an item and, the distance to be driven is 360 km or greater.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is not eligible for the meals component of travel allowance for a meal which they have received another benefit for under this Determination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">The rate of travel allowance for meals is the sum of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">For every person who is 10 years old or older — the following rate specified in item 2 of the table in Part 4 of Annex 9.5.A.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>For breakfast the amount in column B.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>For lunch the amount in column C.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>For dinner the amount in column D.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">For every person who is less than 10 years old — 50% of the rate payable in paragraph a.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.5.55 Incidentals on removal

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for the incidentals component of travel allowance for each day of allowable travel time in connection with their removal under Chapter 6 Part 5 if the member were to drive a vehicle and the distance to be driven is equal to or greater than one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the vehicle is towing an item — 360 km.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the vehicle is not towing an item — 480 km.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The rate of the travel allowance for incidentals is the rate specified in column C of item 2 of the table in Part 4 of Annex 9.5.A.</td>
</tr>
</table>

#### Part 6: Vehicle allowance

##### Division 1: General

###### 9.6.4 Purpose

|  | Vehicle allowance assists a member with reasonable costs when they are authorised to use a private vehicle in Australia. |
|---|---|

###### 9.6.5 Member this Part applies to

|  | This Part applies to a member, including a member on Reserve service. |
|---|---|

###### 9.6.6 Member this Part does not apply to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Part does not apply to a member if they meet any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are eligible for travel on ceasing continuous full-time service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They hold a rank of Brigadier or higher, unless the CDF has approved private vehicle as the most economical means of travel for the member under section 9.1.3.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.6.7 Definitions

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">In this Part, the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Additional costs</b> means any of the following costs, excluding parking or traffic fines.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Registration or insurance fees levied as a result of eligibility for vehicle allowance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Bridge, road and ferry tolls.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Parking fees in a restricted parking area, if they are reasonable because of the distance from the place of duty to the nearest unrestricted parking area.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Authorised</b> means authorised for an allowance under this Part by the CDF.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Greater efficiency</b> means the use of a private vehicle results in greater efficiency if any of the following are met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Using the vehicle allows the member to perform duties more efficiently than the use of the normal means of travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Using the vehicle enables the most effective use of Defence personnel and vehicle resources.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The CDF is satisfied that the member’s personal interests would be harmed if they used the normal means of travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Private vehicle</b> means one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>For travel on removal by a member, their resident family or recognised other person — a motor vehicle owned by the member, their resident family or recognised other person that is to be removed.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>For other travel by a member — a motor vehicle they own, hire or borrow.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Saving to Defence</b> means that Defence would pay less for a member to use a private vehicle than the normal means of travel.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.6.8 Insurance

| 1. | The Commonwealth will not pay for any financial liability or loss if a private vehicle on an authorised journey is involved in an accident. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The member is responsible for checking how their insurance company classifies a vehicle used to travel on duty. If they classify it as a business vehicle and charge an additional premium, the member must arrange insurance as necessary. |
| 3. | The member may be reimbursed any additional premium if they are eligible for additional costs under Division 5 section 9.6.27, Additional vehicle allowance. |
| 4. | If the Commonwealth is found liable for damage from an accident involving the private vehicle, it may claim against the member to recover any damages awarded against it. |

###### 9.6.9 Journey varied or not made

|  | This table sets out what happens when a member's journey is varied or not made. |
|---|---|

| Item | If a member's authorised journey is… | then they… |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | shortened | must repay any vehicle allowance they received that covered the part of the journey they did not make. |
| 2. | extended | are eligible for an additional amount to cover the costs of the extended journey. |
| 3. | not made | must repay all the vehicle allowance they received. |

##### Division 5: Vehicle allowance amounts and limits

###### 9.6.24 Purpose

|  | This Division sets out how vehicle allowance is worked out. It also shows how it can be increased and the limits to the amount that will be paid. |
|---|---|

###### 9.6.25 Amount of allowance and calculation of distance

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">The amount of vehicle allowance is worked out using the following formula.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">[image: Start formula vehicle allowance equals start fraction A times B over 100 end fraction end formula]</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">Where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>A</b></td>
<td colspan="2">is one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td rowspan="2"></td>
<td rowspan="2"></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The number of whole kilometres for the shortest route it is reasonable to take.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The number of whole kilometres for a longer route set by the CDF.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>B</b></td>
<td colspan="2">is, for a vehicle with an engine type in column A that has a capacity in column B, the rate in column C of the same item.</td>
</tr>
</table>

| Item | Column A<br>Engine type | Column B<br>Engine capacity | Column C<br>Rate per km<br>(cents) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. | Non-rotary | 1600cc or less | 82 |
| 2. | Non-rotary | 1601cc – 2600cc | 105 |
| 3. | Non-rotary | More than 2600cc | 106 |
| 4. | Rotary | 800cc or less | 82 |
| 5. | Rotary | 801cc – 1300cc | 105 |
| 6. | Rotary | More than 1300cc | 106 |
| 7. | Electric | – | 82 |

| 2. | In setting a longer route for the purpose of subsection 1, the CDF must be satisfied that the shortest route was not reasonable for the travel. |
|---|---|

###### 9.6.26 Increased rate for passengers, equipment etc

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The rate of allowance under section 9.6.25 is increased by 1.12 cents per kilometre if the member meets any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They carry a passenger in the vehicle who would otherwise be eligible for travel expenses for the journey under this Determination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They carry Commonwealth‑owned or hired equipment, tools or materials that weigh at least 100 kg.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>They tow a Commonwealth‑owned or hired caravan or trailer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The amount paid under subsection 1 must not exceed what a member would have been paid had the travel been by the most economical means.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.6.27 Additional vehicle allowance

| 1. | The CDF may approve an additional amount of vehicle allowance. The CDF must be satisfied that a member pays reasonable costs above the amount they are eligible for. |
|---|---|
| 2. | Costs arising out of non-standard vehicle modifications will not be reimbursed under this section. |
| 3. | The member must provide the CDF with written relevant information to support a claim for an additional amount. The information must be about the running costs of the vehicle over 12 months or as close as reasonably practical to that period. This table sets out the kind of information that may be relevant to a claim. |

| Item | Information that may be relevant |
|---|---|
| 1. | Vehicle make, model, year, engine capacity, automatic or manual transmission. |
| 2. | The period over which the claim is made. |
| 3. | Estimated distance travelled on duty and private business. |
| 4. | The total amount of vehicle allowance received over the nominated period. |
| 5. | Vehicle usage – for example, is it used regularly or intermittently? is it used in city conditions or away from sealed roads? |
| 6. | Depreciation. This is worked out by:<br>a. establishing a vehicle's market value at the beginning of a nominated period, then<br>b. deducting from that amount the vehicle's market value at the end of that period. |
| 7. | Interest – the amount paid over the nominated period on a loan taken out to buy the vehicle. |
| 8. | Comprehensive insurance. This includes the amount of premium paid, stamp duty, no-claim bonuses and any payment for removal of excess. |
| 9. | Third party insurance, registration, driver's licence and motoring organisation subscription. Fees associated with each of these costs must be provided. |
| 10. | Petrol – grade used, total expenditure over nominated period, prices generally paid. |
| 11. | Repairs and maintenance. This includes both of the following.<br>a. Preventive or corrective maintenance, such as regular grease and oil changes, and replacement of oil filters, air cleaners, spark plugs and battery.<br>b. Repairs and maintenance arising out of normal wear and tear, for example, replacement of brake pads or shoes, or a muffler. |
| 12. | Relevant costs associated with damage caused by accident, adverse road conditions, etc. The member should give details of both of the following.<br>a. Circumstances leading to damage.<br>b. Details of any settlement arising out of a claim against a comprehensive insurance policy or other party. |
| 13. | Tyres – brand, type and size specifications. Wear and tear should be worked out using the formula below.<br>[image: Start formula start fraction Distance travelled on duty in nominated period over Actual or expected tyre life open bracket km close bracket end fraction times Original tyre price open bracket $ close bracket end formula] |

<td>a.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>On posting or on commencing an alternate work agreement.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>On recreation leave or recall from recreation leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>

</tr>
</table>

###### 9.7.2 Member this Part applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This Part applies to a member who undertakes authorised travel by flying a private aircraft. This includes a member on Reserve service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">To be eligible for aircraft allowance, a member must meet both of these criteria.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They must hold an appropriate pilot’s licence in force under the <i>Air Navigation Act 1920</i> and the <i>Air Navigation Regulations 1947</i>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They must comply with both of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The <i>Air Navigation Regulations 1947</i>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Any requirements of the Department of Transport and Regional Services and the Civil Aviation Safety Authority.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.7.3 When this Part does not apply

|  | A member is not eligible for payment under this Part in relation to a light aircraft hired by the ADF. |
|---|---|

###### 9.7.4 Definitions

|  | In this Part, the following apply. |
|---|---|
|  | **Authorised** means authorised for an allowance under this Part by the CDF. |
|  | **Private aircraft** means an aircraft that is registered in Australia and that the member is licensed to fly. |

###### 9.7.5 Authorised travel by private aircraft

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member’s travel by flying a private aircraft may be authorised in the same way as travel by a private vehicle is authorised under Part 6 of this Chapter. The same circumstances and conditions apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">For subsection 1 above, both of these conditions must apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A private aircraft is the same as a private vehicle in relation to 'greater efficiency' under section 9.6.7.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Aircraft allowance is the same as vehicle allowance in relation to 'a saving to the Commonwealth' under subsection 9.6.7.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> Decisions are made in the same way as they are for deciding vehicle allowance. They may rely on the CDF being satisfied that the member's personal interests would be harmed if they used the normal means of travel.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.7.6 Benefit

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member authorised to travel by flying a private aircraft instead of travelling by the most economical means of travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subject to section 9.7.8, the member has all of these benefits for the travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The allowance worked out under section 9.7.7.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Travel costs under Part 5 of this Chapter that they would otherwise be eligible for.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Any unavoidable costs or charges they pay for the use of the aircraft. To qualify, they must be eligible for the reimbursement of additional costs under Part 6 for use of a private vehicle in the same circumstances.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.7.7 Amount of allowance

|  | The amount of allowance is worked out using this formula. |
|---|---|
|  | [image: Start formula start fraction Distance times Hourly cost over Cruising speed end fraction end formula] |

<table>
<tr>
<td>Term</td>
<td colspan="2">Definition</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Distance</td>
<td colspan="2">The distance must take into account these factors.<br>a. It must be measured in nautical miles.<br>b. It must be based on the straight-line ground distance between the airfield where the travel begins and the airfield where the travel ends.<br>c. It may be adjusted, to take into account necessary fuel stops, and to be consistent with safe air navigation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Cruising speed</td>
<td colspan="2">The cruising speed of the aircraft in nautical miles an hour.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td rowspan="3">Hourly cost</td>
<td><b>If...</b></td>
<td><b>the hourly cost is...</b></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>the member owns the aircraft</td>
<td>the hourly cost of operating the aircraft.<br>This is based on budgeting figures for the aircraft, taking all these factors into account.<br>a. The aircraft type, model and engine capacity.<br>b. The yearly cost of operating the aircraft.<br>c. The average yearly flying time of the aircraft.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>the member hires the aircraft</td>
<td>the hourly hire charge for the aircraft.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.7.8 Limit to benefit

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s total benefit for the travel must not be more than the sum of these two amounts.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Fares and travel costs under Part 5 of this Chapter, worked out as if they were travelling by the normal means of travel. This includes the benefit for any passenger they are authorised to carry and who would otherwise travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Any other relevant charge. This includes the cost of transporting any goods owned or hired by the Commonwealth that they are authorised to carry.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 9.7.9 Insurance

| 1. | A member must provide the CDF with written evidence that the aircraft is insured before the CDF can authorise the travel. The aircraft must be covered by both comprehensive and third party insurance. |
|---|---|
| 2. | If a private aircraft is authorised for use on duty, the Commonwealth will not accept responsibility for any financial liability or loss arising from an accident it is involved in. |
| 3. | If the Commonwealth is found liable for damage from an accident involving the aircraft, it may claim against the member to recover any damages awarded against it. |

### Chapter 11: ADF-related compensation

#### Part 2: Additional military compensation

##### Division 1: General provisions

###### 11.2.1 Purpose

|  | This Part provides for additional compensation for members who suffer an injury that results in death or severe impairment and in respect of which compensation is payable under the *Safety, Rehabilitation and Compensation Act 1988* (SRC Act). |
|---|---|

###### 11.2.3 Limits to application of benefits under this Part

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This Part applies only to injuries that meet both these conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A member suffered them after 10 June 1997 and before 1 July 2004.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They resulted in the death or severe impairment of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">This Part does not apply to any injury that a member is entitled to compensation for under the <i>Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Act 2004</i>.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 11.2.4 Definitions

|  | In this Part the following apply. |
|---|---|
| 1. | **ADB** means additional death benefit |
|  | **Basic amount** means the amount calculated under subsection 11.2.11.1. |
|  | **Commonwealth authority** has the same meaning as in section 4 of the SRC Act. |
|  | **Compensation** means SRC compensation, State compensation and State workers’ compensation. |
|  | **Dependent child amount** means the amount payable under subsection 11.2.8.2 or 11.2.11.2. |
|  | **Impairment** has the same meaning as in section 4 of the SRC Act. |
|  | **Interim payment amount** means the amount calculated under subsection 11.2.13.3. |
|  | **Member** despite section 1.2.2, a reference to a member includes a member of the Reserves. |
|  | **Non-economic loss** has the same meaning as in section 4 of the SRC Act. |
|  | **Permanent** has the same meaning as in section 4 of the SRC Act. |
|  | **Severe injury** means an injury for the purpose of the SRC Act affecting the brain or spinal cord of a person and must result in quadriplegia, paraplegia, hemiplegia, an organic brain syndrome, chronic blindness or a condition of similar effect. |
|  | **SIA** means severe injury adjustment. |
|  | **Spouse** has the same meaning as in the SRC Act. |
|  | **Spouse amount** means the amount payable under subsection 11.2.8.1. |
|  | **SRC Act** means the *Safety, Rehabilitation and Compensation Act 1988.* |
|  | **SRC Compensation** means compensation payable under subsection 17(3) or 17(4), or section 24 or 27 of the SRC Act. |
|  | **State compensation** has the same meaning as in section 119 of the SRC Act. |
|  | **State workers’ compensation** has the same meaning as in section 118 of the SRC Act. |
|  | **The Secretary** means the Secretary of the Department of Veterans’ Affairs. |

###### 11.2.4A Dependent child

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A <b>dependent child</b> means a person who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They meet the definition of child under section 1.3.35.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are wholly or partly dependent on the member for economic support.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">They meet one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They are under 16 years old.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They are 16 or more years old, but less than 25 years old, and meet the education test.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">In this section, <b>education test</b> means meeting both of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The person is in full-time education at a school, college, university or other educational institution.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The person is not ordinarily in employment or working on their own account.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 11.2.5 Some aspects of dependency

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A child of a member is taken to have been wholly or partly dependent on a member at a time if the child would have been so dependent at that time but for an incapacity of the member as the result of an injury.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">A child of a member who, immediately before the occurrence of an event, lived with the member is taken to have been wholly dependent on the member at the time of the occurrence of that event.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">A child of a member who was born alive after the member’s death is taken to have been born immediately before the member’s death and to have been wholly dependent on the member at the time of the member’s death.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">A child of a member who was conceived before the time of an assessment of the member’s SRC compensation mentioned in subsection 11.2.11.2, and was born alive after that time, is taken to have been born immediately before that time and to have been wholly dependent on the member at that time.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">In deciding whether a child is or was dependent on a member at a time, none of these amounts payable for the child under the <i>Social Security Act 1991</i> are to be taken into account.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Family allowance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Family allowance supplement.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Child disability allowance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Double orphan pension.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 11.2.6 Damages or compensation recovered or received for the benefit of a member’s resident family

| 1. | A reference in this Division to SIA, ADB, compensation or damages paid or payable to a member’s resident family includes a reference to SIA, ADB, compensation or damages paid or payable to a person other than the member’s resident family for the benefit of the resident family. |
|---|---|
| 2. | A reference in this Division to compensation or damages received or recovered by a member’s resident family includes a reference to compensation or damages received or recovered by a person other than the resident family for the benefit of the resident family. |

##### Division 2: Additional death benefit

###### 11.2.7 Entitlement to additional death benefit

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">An additional death benefit is payable in relation to a member under this Division if all these conditions are met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member meets both of the following conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>On or after 10 June 1997, the member suffered an injury, being an injury or disease for the purpose of the SRC Act.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The injury results in the member's death, regardless of the date of the death.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is survived by any of these sets of people.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>A partner.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>One or more dependent children.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>Both a partner and one or more dependent children.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">SRC compensation in respect of the injury is payable to, or for the benefit of, the partner or one or more dependent children.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The ADB in relation to a member is the total of the amounts payable in relation to the member under this Division.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">The ADB is payable in addition to any SRC compensation that is payable in relation to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 11.2.8 Calculation of the ADB

| 1. | The partner of a deceased member is entitled to a payment of $47,395.78. |
|---|---|
| 2. | In addition to the partner amount (if any), an amount of $70,277.43 is payable for each person who was a dependent child of the member at the time of the member’s death.<br>**Note:** The dollar amounts in this section are indexed. |

###### 11.2.9 Who the ADB is payable to

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The ADB is payable to the partner.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subsection 3 or 4 applies if the deceased member is survived by a dependent child and one of the following conditions is met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The deceased member is not survived by a partner.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The partner does not have primary responsibility for the daily care of the child.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the child is under 18 years old, the dependent child amount is payable to a person who has primary responsibility for the daily care of the child.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the child is 18 or more years old, the dependent child amount is payable to the child.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 3: Severe injury adjustment

###### 11.2.10 Entitlement to a severe injury adjustment

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A severe injury adjustment is payable in relation to a member under this Division if the member meets all these conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member suffered a severe injury in relation to service in respect of which SRC Act compensation is payable.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The injury set out in paragraph a. of this subsection occurred on a date set out in the following table.</td>
</tr>
</table>

| Item | If the claim was... | the severe injury must be... |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | made in relation to an injury (other than a disease) for the purposes of the SRC Act | suffered on or after 10 June 1997 but before 1 July 2004. |
| 2. | made in relation to an injury that is a disease for the purposes of the SRC Act | suffered on or after 10 June 1997. |

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The degree of permanent impairment of the member as a result of the injury is finally determined, under section 24 of the SRC Act, to be not less than 80%.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The SIA in relation to the member is the total of the amounts payable in relation to the member under this Division.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The SIA is payable in addition to any SRC compensation that is payable in relation to the member in respect of the injury.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">The SIA is payable whether or not the member makes a request, under section 43 of the SRC Act, that the SRC compensation in respect of the injury not be paid to, or for the benefit of, the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">The SIA is payable whether or not the member chooses, under section 45 of the SRC Act, to begin proceedings in relation to damages.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 11.2.11 Calculation of the SIA

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The basic amount of SIA in relation to a member is this amount.<br><b>A - B</b><br>where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>A</b></td>
<td>is the total of the maximum amount of permanent impairment compensation payable under the SRC Act, plus $68,063.38.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>B</b></td>
<td>is the total amount of SRC Act compensation payable (or that would be payable but for a request under section 43 of the SRC Act or an election under section 45 of that Act) to the member in respect of the injury.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">An amount of $70,277.43 is payable, in addition to the basic amount, for each person who was a dependent child of the member at the time of the assessment of the member’s SRC compensation under section 24 of the SRC Act.<br><b>Note:</b> The dollar amounts in this section are indexed.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 11.2.12 Who the SIA is payable to

| 1. | The SIA in relation to a member is payable to the member. |
|---|---|
| 2. | If an amount is payable under subsection 11.2.11.2 and the member does not have primary responsibility for the daily care of the child, the payment is payable to the person who has primary responsibility for the daily care of the child. |

###### 11.2.13 Interim payment of SIA

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies if, under section 25 of the SRC Act, both these conditions are met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>An interim payment of SRC compensation is made to the member in respect of the injury.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The amount has been assessed on an interim determination that the degree of permanent impairment of the member is not less than 80%.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">An interim payment of SIA is payable to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The interim payment amount is this amount.<br><b>A – B</b><br>where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>A</b></td>
<td>is the total of the maximum amount of permanent impairment compensation payable under the SRC Act, plus $68,063.38.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>B</b></td>
<td>is the maximum total amount of SRC Act compensation payable (or that would be payable but for a request under section 43 of the SRC Act or an election under section 45 of that Act) to the member in respect of the injury.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">When, under section 24 of the SRC Act, the degree of permanent impairment of the member as a result of the injury is finally determined, there is payable to the member an amount of SIA equal to the difference (if any) between the basic amount and the interim payment amount.<br><b>Note:</b> The dollar amounts in this section are indexed.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 4: Avoidance of double benefits

###### 11.2.14 Notice of proceedings against a third party

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies if all these conditions are met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>SIA or ADB is payable (or would be payable but for this Division) in relation to a member in respect of an injury.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The injury happened in circumstances that appear to create a legal liability in a person (other than the Commonwealth, a Commonwealth authority or an employee of the Commonwealth) to pay damages in respect of the injury.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>After 9 February 1998, the member or their resident family begins proceedings to recover damages from the person.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member or their resident family, as the case requires, must notify the Secretary in writing of the proceedings not later than 7 days after the day the member or their resident family begins the proceedings.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 11.2.15 SIA or ADB not payable if damages are recovered

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies if both these conditions are met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>But for this section, SIA or ADB would be payable to a member or their resident family in respect of an injury suffered by the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member or their resident family recovered, or recovers, damages in respect of the injury.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member or their resident family recovers damages on or after 9 February 1998, the member or their resident family, as the case requires, must notify the Secretary in writing, within 28 days after the day the damages are recovered, of the recovery of the damages and the amount of damages.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">If SIA or ADB was paid to the member or their resident family before the damages are recovered, the member or their resident family, as the case requires, must repay an amount equal to the amount (if any) of SIA or ADB that, when added to the amount of SRC compensation (if any) paid to the member or their resident family, does not exceed the amount of the damages.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">SIA or ADB is not payable to the member or their resident family after the day the member or their resident family recovered, or recovers, the damages.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subsection 3 does not apply if the damages were recovered in proceedings instituted by the member under section 45 of the SRC Act, or by way of a settlement of the proceedings.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subsection 4 does not apply if the damages were recovered in any of these ways.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>As a result of proceedings begun by the member after making an election under section 45 of the SRC Act.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>As a result of proceedings begun or taken over by the Commonwealth against a person (other than the Commonwealth, a Commonwealth authority or an employee of the Commonwealth).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>In a settlement of those proceedings.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>7.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member or their resident family satisfies the Secretary that a part of the damages recovered by the member or their resident family was not in respect of death, permanent impairment or non-economic loss as a result of the injury, this section has effect in relation to that member or their resident family, as the case requires, as if the amount of the damages recovered by the member or their resident family were an amount equal to so much (if any) of the damages as was in respect of death, permanent impairment or non-economic loss as a result of the injury.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>8.</td>
<td colspan="2">In this section, damages does not include an amount of damages paid under section 76 of the <i>Veterans’ Entitlements Act 1986</i>.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 11.2.16 No double benefit if State workers' compensation is received

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies if both these conditions are met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>But for this section, SIA or ADB would be payable in relation to a member or their resident family in respect of an injury suffered by the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member or their resident family received, or receives, State workers’ compensation in respect of the injury.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">SIA or ADB is not payable in relation to the member or their resident family in respect of the injury.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">If SIA or ADB is paid to the member or their resident family before the State workers’ compensation is received, the member or their resident family, as the case requires, must pay back an amount equal to the amount of SIA or ADB so paid.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 11.2.17 No double benefit if State compensation is received

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies if both these conditions are met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>But for this section, SIA or ADB would be payable in relation to a member or their resident family in respect of an injury suffered by the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member or their resident family received, or receives, State compensation in respect of the injury.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The amount of SIA or ADB payable in relation to the member or their resident family in respect of the injury is so much (if any) of the amount that would be payable but for this section as, when added to the amount (if any) of SRC compensation determined in respect of the injury in relation to the member or their resident family, exceeds the amount of State compensation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">If SIA or ADB is paid to the member or their resident family before the State compensation is received, the member or their resident family, as the case requires, must repay an amount equal to the amount (if any) of the SIA or ADB that, when added to the amount of SRC compensation (if any) determined in respect of the injury in relation to the member or their resident family, does not exceed the amount of State compensation</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member or their resident family satisfies the Secretary that a part of the State compensation received by the member or their resident family was not in respect of death, permanent impairment or non-economic loss as a result of the injury, this section has effect in relation to that member or their resident family , as the case requires, as if the amount of the State compensation received by the member or their resident family were an amount equal to so much of the State compensation as was in respect of death, permanent impairment or non-economic loss as a result of the injury.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 11.2.18 Statutory declaration as to State workers' compensation etc.

|  | The Secretary may require a member or their resident family to give to the Secretary a statutory declaration stating whether any damages, State workers’ compensation or State compensation has been paid to, or for the benefit of, the member or their resident family for an injury for which, but for section 11.2.15, 11.2.16, or 11.2.17, SIA or ADB would be payable. |
|---|---|

###### 11.2.19 Reduction of SIA or ADB if similar compensation received before commencement

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Under this Division, a person is not required to repay an amount of compensation of the same kind as SIA or ADB that meets the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>It was paid before 9 February 1998.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>It was paid in respect of an injury for which SIA or ADB is payable under this Part.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The amount of SIA or ADB payable to a person under this Part is reduced by the amount of compensation a person has received under subsection 1.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 11.2.20 Recovery of SIA or ADB that is repayable

|  | The amount of SIA or ADB repayable under section 11.2.15, 11.2.16 or 11.2.17 is recoverable in a court of competent jurisdiction as a debt due to the Commonwealth. |
|---|---|

##### Division 5: Authorisation of payment and review of decisions

###### 11.2.21 Payment of SIA or ADB

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The Secretary may authorise the payment to a person of an amount of SIA or ADB payable under this Part in relation to a member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Without limiting the discretion of the Secretary under subsection 1, the Secretary may refuse to authorise a payment to a person if the person meets either of these conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They failed, without reasonable excuse, to notify the Secretary under Division 4 section 11.2.14 of proceedings mentioned in that section.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They refused, or failed without reasonable excuse, to give a statutory declaration under Division 4 section 11.2.18.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">If an amount is payable to a person who is under a legal disability, Chapter 1 Part 6 section 1.6.3 applies to the payment as if a reference to the CDF were a reference to the Secretary.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 11.2.22 Notice of decisions

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The Secretary must give notice of a decision to authorise, or not to authorise, a payment of an amount of SIA or ADB in relation to a member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The notice must be given to each person who is, to the Secretary’s knowledge, one of the member’s resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The notice must have with it a statement by the Secretary of the Secretary’s reasons for making the decision.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">The notice must include a statement to the effect that, if dissatisfied with the decision, the person may do these things.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>In the case of notice of a decision (other than a decision made by the Secretary under section 11.2.23 confirming or varying an earlier reviewable decision of the Secretary) – request reconsideration of the decision under section 11.2.23.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>In the case of notice of a decision made by the Secretary under section 11.2.23 confirming or varying an earlier reviewable decision of the Secretary – apply to the Administrative Review Tribunal for review of the decision so confirmed or varied.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">Failure to comply with subsection 4 in relation to a decision does not affect the validity of the decision.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 11.2.23 Reconsideration of decisions

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A person who is dissatisfied with a decision of the Secretary (other than a decision made under this section) may, by notice in writing to the Secretary, request the Secretary to reconsider the decision.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The notice must be given to the Secretary within either of these times.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>30 days after the day the person first receives notice of the decision.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Any further period that the Secretary allows.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The person must set out in the notice the reasons for the request.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">The Secretary must reconsider the decision. The Secretary may do either of these things.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Confirm the decision.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Vary or revoke the decision.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 11.2.24 Review by Tribunal of reconsidered decisions

|  | An application may be made to the Administrative Review Tribunal for review of a decision of the Secretary to confirm or vary a decision under subsection 11.2.23.4. |
|---|---|

#### Part 3: Payment of financial entitlements on death

###### 11.3.1 Purpose

|  | This Part sets out financial benefits that may be provided on the death of a member. They include payments for leave not taken, bereavement payments and reimbursement for financial or legal advice. |
|---|---|

###### 11.3.2 Entitlement for leave and other compensation

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies if a member, including a member of the Reserves, dies.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">A person is eligible for the sum of what would have been payable to the member for the following if they had ceased to be a member on the day they died.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Recreation leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Long service leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>War service leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Compensation for loss or damage to clothing or personal effects.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">In this section, <b>a person</b> means a person who is eligible to receive a payment under section 1.6.4.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 11.3.3 Bereavement payment – member on continuous full-time service

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">In this section the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Dependent person</b> means a person who was financially dependent on the deceased member during the relevant pay period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Gross fortnightly pay</b> means the greater of the following amounts.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The total amount of the fortnightly instalments of salary and allowances the member would have been entitled to for the relevant pay period, and includes amount payable for any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Income tax.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Superannuation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>A debt due to the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The average amount of gross fortnightly pay that the member was entitled to for each completed pay period in the last 3 months of service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Relevant pay period</b> means the fortnight that ends on the day immediately before the day the member died.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies if all of the following have occurred.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member has died.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">During all or part of the relevant pay period, the member met one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They were on continuous full-time service and salary was payable.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They were on a flexible service determination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section does not apply if there is no dependent person.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">A dependent person is eligible to receive four times the member's gross fortnightly pay as a bereavement payment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="3">Payment must be made in four equal fortnightly instalments, and begins on the first day of the pay period immediately after the member’s death.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6.</td>
<td colspan="3">A bereavement payment must not be made to more than one dependent person unless the CDF is satisfied that there are exceptional circumstances.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 11.3.3A Bereavement payment – Reserves

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">In this section, the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Dependent person</b> means a person who was financially dependent on the deceased member during the fortnight that ends on the day immediately before the day the member died.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A dependent person is eligible to receive a bereavement payment if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member was a member of the Reserves not on continuous full-time service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member died in any of the following circumstances.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member was on Reserve service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member was scheduled on Reserve service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The member was not scheduled on Reserve service and the decision maker is satisfied that exceptional and compelling circumstances exist.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">The bereavement payment is calculated in accordance with the following formula</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">[image: start formula bereavement payment equals A times 56 end formula]</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">Where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>A</b></td>
<td colspan="2">is the member’s Reserve daily rate of salary.<br><b>Note:</b> A member of the Reserves’ daily rate of salary is provided under section A.1.5 of DFRT Determination, 2017 No. 2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">A bereavement payment must not be made to more than one dependent person unless the CDF is satisfied that there are exceptional circumstances.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="3">The bereavement payment is paid in 4 fortnightly instalments from the first day of the pay period immediately after the member’s death.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 11.3.4 Payment for financial or legal advice

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This payment assists persons with legal or financial responsibility upon a member's death to carry out their duties. It is intended to assist the person to make sound and rational decisions associated with their role.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies to a person who meets both of the following conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They must be a member of the family as defined under section 58A of <i>Defence Act 1903.</i></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They hold any of the following roles.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>An executor of the deceased member's will.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>A beneficiary of the deceased member's estate.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>A legal personal representative of the beneficiary of the deceased member's estate.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">The person may be eligible for a payment under this section if all of the following have been met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF forms a belief that the person would have difficulty making decisions required of them, but that this is unlikely to result in the appointment of another person to make the decision on their behalf.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF believes the difficulty is caused by either of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>A lack of demonstrated adult cognitive maturity.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Another cognitive or functional impairment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF decides that based on his belief, the person needs the support to carry out their role in making sound and rational decisions on financial or legal matters.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">The person may be reimbursed up to $2,000 for each of the following costs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Financial advice obtained from a financial advisor who holds a current Australian financial services licence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Legal advice obtained from a legal practitioner, not including costs for obtaining legal advice relating to a dispute.<br><b>Note:</b> Legal advice does not include legal or court costs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
</tr>
</table>

#### Part 4: Funeral and transportation costs on death

##### Division 1A: General provisions

###### 11.4.1 Purpose

|  | The purpose of this Part is to provide assistance to a member, former member or their resident family when a death occurs. |
|---|---|

###### 11.4.2 Dual entitlement

|  | If a deceased member was also recognised as a member’s resident family, the conditions and benefits set out in Division 1 apply. |
|---|---|

###### 11.4.4 Administration

|  | To be eligible for reimbursement of approved costs under this Part, the claimant must submit all relevant invoices and receipts to Defence Member and Family Support. |
|---|---|

###### 11.4.4A Legal personal representative

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">In this Part, <b>legal personal representative</b> means one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The executor of the deceased member or former member’s will.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The administrator of the deceased member or former member’s estate.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 1: Funeral costs, floral and non-floral tributes for deceased members or former members

###### 11.4.5 Purpose

|  | The purpose of this Division is to provide financial assistance for funeral costs, floral and non-floral tributes to a member’s resident family when a member or a former member dies. |
|---|---|

###### 11.4.6 Member or former member this Division applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This Division applies in relation to a deceased member or former member who was in any of the following classes immediately before they died.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member of the Permanent Forces.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member of the Reserves in any of the following circumstances at the time of death.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>On continuous full-time service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Undergoing training.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>Attending a parade or bivouac.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>iv.</td>
<td>The death is due to injuries suffered, or illness contracted, while serving in the ADF.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>v.</td>
<td>The member had been on overseas operational deployment within the previous 12 months.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member of the Reserves or a retired member who met one of the following conditions before death.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member held the rank of two-Star or above.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The relevant Service Chief has requested that a benefit be provided for the member under this Part, having regard to the member's distinguished career.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>A member of the Air Force who held a one-star rank or above before 7 May 1999.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iv.</td>
<td>A Chaplain who was appointed as a Principal Air Chaplain before 7 May 1999.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">A recipient of the Victoria Cross or the Victoria Cross for Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The Director General Defence Member and Family Support may approve funeral expenses for a deceased member or former member not specified under subsection 1 if requested by the relevant Service Chief.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 11.4.7 Member this Division does not apply to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Division does not make any provision in relation to the following deceased members.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A member who was absent without leave at the time of death.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A member who died while on duty overseas and who has an overseas funeral under Chapter 12 Part 7.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 11.4.9 Funeral costs

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The Director General Defence Member and Family Support may approve an application for the payment for costs related to a deceased member or former member's funeral, up to $14,000.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">When considering whether to approve costs under subsection 1, the Director General Defence Member and Family Support must have regard to the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The person's wishes, as communicated through the deceased member or former member's legal personal representative.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Any requirements of the relevant religion, faith or culture of the deceased member or former member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The Director General Defence Member and Family Support may approve payment of additional costs related to the funeral amount specified in subsection 1, if satisfied that there are exceptional circumstances.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">The approved costs under this Division may be paid to any of the following people.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The deceased member or former member's resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The deceased member or former member's legal personal representative.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The service provider.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 11.4.10 Funeral overseas

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies if both of the following conditions are met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>An eligible member or former member dies in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The deceased member or former member's family choose to have a private funeral overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The Director General Defence Member and Family Support may approve costs up to the amount specified in subsection 11.4.9.1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">Overseas funeral arrangements are the responsibility of the deceased member or former member's next of kin or legal personal representative.<br><b>Note:</b> A mourner’s travel and accommodation costs will not be paid for.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 11.4.10A Memorial services after the COVID-19 pandemic

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">In this section:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Beneficiary</b>, in respect of a member, means one of the following persons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Resident family of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s legal personal representative.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>COVID-19 control measure</b> means a measure, however described, taken to limit the spread of COVID-19 issued by the Commonwealth government or a State or Territory government.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Member</b> means a deceased member or deceased former member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A beneficiary is eligible for financial assistance towards the costs of a memorial service of a member if all the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s funeral occurs while COVID-19 control measures relating to funerals are in place.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The memorial service is to be held in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">Director General Defence Member and Family Support is satisfied of all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The memorial service is consistent with the member’s wishes.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The memorial service is consistent with the requirements of the member’s faith, religion or culture.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">The memorial service must occur between the following days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The day COVID-19 control measures relating to funerals ends.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The day 12 months after COVID-19 control measures relating to funerals ends.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">The maximum financial assistance available is the greater of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The lesser of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td rowspan="2"></td>
<td rowspan="2"></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The cost of the memorial service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>$14,000 less the amount paid under section 11.4.9 or 15.9.3, if any.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If there are exceptional circumstances  the amount approved by the Director General Defence Member and Family Support.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="3">The financial assistance available under this section may be paid to a service provider.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 11.4.11 Travel and accommodation

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">In this section, <b>member</b> means a deceased member or deceased former member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1A.</td>
<td colspan="3">Subject to subsection 1B, any of the following persons are eligible for travel and 2 nights’ accommodation in Australia to attend the funeral or memorial service of a member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Resident family of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">A person accompanying the resident family if the resident family is very young, aged, have an illness or are severely distressed.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s parents.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1B.</td>
<td colspan="3">Section 1A does not apply if any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The funeral or memorial service is to be held in the location where the person eligible for travel and accommodation under subsection 2 lives.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The funeral or memorial service is to be held overseas under one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Section 11.4.10, Funeral overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Section 15.9.3, Assistance if member dies.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A person eligible for accommodation under subsection 1A is eligible for an additional night’s accommodation if all the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The person is attending a funeral to which section 11.4.9 applies.<br><b>Note:</b> This does not apply to memorial services.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The Director General Defence Member and Family Support is satisfied that it is required due to travel requirements and the time of the funeral service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">Travel and accommodation must be organised using Defence business travel arrangements up to the maximum amount that would have been paid if they were eligible for travel and accommodation costs under Chapter 9.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">The Director General Defence Member and Family Support may approve a higher maximum amount payable for accommodation under subsection 3 if either of the following occurs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">There is no accommodation under the Defence business travel arrangements at the rate specified under Annex 9.5.A.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">There is no accommodation under the Defence business travel arrangements at the funeral location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="3">People approved under subsection 1 will be reimbursed the cost of meals, up to the amount they would have been paid if they were eligible for meal costs under Annex 9.5.A.<br><b>Note:</b> The cost of incidentals will not be reimbursed.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 11.4.12 Floral and non-floral tributes

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may approve floral and non-floral tributes in respect of a member for any of the following events.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>An annual celebration of remembrance for a deceased member or deceased former member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A memorial occasion of national importance for the remembrance of a deceased member or deceased former member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The maximum amount payable for floral and non-floral tributes is $250.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 2: Assistance on death of resident family in Australia

###### 11.4.13 Purpose

|  | The purpose of this Division is to provide financial assistance to a member when a person recognised as resident family dies. |
|---|---|

###### 11.4.14 Member this Division applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Division applies to a member if all of the following conditions apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member has resident family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A person who is recognised as resident family of the member dies in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The person under paragraph b is not in the location where the funeral is to take place.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 11.4.15 Assistance provided when resident family dies

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">The Director General Defence Member and Family Support may approve assistance with the following costs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The reasonable cost of the preparation of the deceased person’s remains.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Reasonable transport costs of the deceased to either of the following locations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>To the location in Australia where the funeral will be held.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>To the nearest Australian departure point when the funeral will be held outside of Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">Despite subparagraph 1.b.ii, no transport costs are paid if the deceased person is at the Australian departure point.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member may elect that the assistance under this section be paid to any of the following people.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The deceased person's legal personal representative.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The service provider.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The person who paid for the preparation or transportation of the deceased person.</td>
</tr>
</table>
