**About this compilation**

**This compilation**

This is a compilation of *Defence Determination 2016/19, Conditions of service*, that shows the text of the law as amended and in force on 10/09/2026 (the ***compilation date***).

The notes at the end of this compilation (the endnotes) include information about amending laws and the amendment history of provisions of the compiled law.

**Uncommenced amendments**

The effect of uncommenced amendments is not shown in the text of the compiled law. The details of amendments made up to, but not commenced at, the compilation date are underlined in the endnotes. Any uncommenced amendments affecting the law are accessible on the Register (www.legislation.gov.au).

**Application, saving and transitional provisions**

If the operation of a provision or amendment of the compiled law is affected by an application, saving or transitional provision that is not included in this compilation, details are included in the endnotes.

**Modifications**

If the compiled law is modified by another law, the compiled law operates as modified but the modification does not amend the text of the law. Accordingly, this compilation does not show the text of the compiled law as modified. Any modifications affecting the law are accessible on the Register.

**Self repealing provisions**

If a provision of the compiled law has been repealed in accordance with a provision of the law, details are included in the endnotes.

### Chapter 12: Overseas conditions of service – overview

#### Part 1: General information on Chapters 12 to 16

###### 12.1.1 Member Chapters 12 to 16 apply to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">Chapters 12 to 16 apply to a member, including a member of the Reserves, performing duty overseas and includes any of the following periods.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">For the purpose of commencing duty overseas, the period immediately before commencing duty overseas for any of the following purposes.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>To allow the member and dependant to complete all things necessary to travel to the overseas location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>To allow the member and dependants to complete an isolation period required by a law of a foreign government.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">During the COVID-19 pandemic, the later of the following periods.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The period ending when the member returns to their posting location in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>If the member returns to their posting location and is required to isolate — the end of their isolation period.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 12.1.2 Member Chapters 12 to 16 do not apply to

|  | Chapters 12 to 16 do not apply to a member who is undertaking official travel if they are eligible for travel benefits under a determination made by the Remuneration Tribunal for that travel. |
|---|---|

<td colspan="3"><b>Post index</b> has the same meaning given by section 12.3.14A.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Posting location</b>, in relation to a long-term posting overseas, means one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The location to which the member is posted.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is posted to a position on Manhattan Island — New York State, excluding Manhattan.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is posted to a position on Manhattan Island and is directed to live on Manhattan Island — Manhattan.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Posting period overseas</b> has the same meaning given by section 12.3.16.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Regional leave centre</b> means one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">A location listed as a regional leave centre in Annex 16.B column C.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">A substituted leave centre.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">During the COVID-19 pandemic — unless the location in paragraph a is in the country to which the member is posted, a capital city in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Relief leave centre</b> means one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">A location listed as a relief leave centre in Annex 16.B column C.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">A substituted leave centre.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">During the COVID-19 pandemic — unless the location in paragraph a. is in the country to which the member is posted, a capital city in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Short-term duty overseas</b> has the same meaning given by section 12.3.18.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Specified area</b> means the area where the nature of service applies as declared by the Minister for Defence under section 5C of the <i>Veterans’ Entitlements Act 1986</i>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Substituted leave centre</b> means a location that the Director Overseas and Housing Policy specifies as a substituted leave centre if satisfied the determined leave centre is temporarily unsuitable because it is affected by any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">War.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Civil disorder.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">Natural disaster.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">A similar event.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Temporary accommodation</b> means a serviced apartment, or other similar accommodation in which meals can be prepared.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Time zone hour</b> means a change of one time zone during air travel, measured using Coordinated Universal Time (old Greenwich Mean Time).<br><b>Note:</b> Summer time and daylight saving time are disregarded for the purposes of this definition.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Travel time</b> means the period that meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">It begins on the latest allowed check-in time for the scheduled departure.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">It ends on the arrival time at the destination airport.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">It does not include any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Rest periods.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>A stopover where the member is not on duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Unaccompanied member</b> means a member who is not an accompanied member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Utilities</b> has the meaning given by section 12.3.19.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 12.3.2 Accompanied member

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">An accompanied member means a member who is on long‑term posting overseas and has a partner who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They live, or intend to live, with the member at the posting location for at least 12 months.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are not away from the posting location for more than 28 consecutive days, unless one of the following applies.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They are joining the member on recreation leave the member accrued at the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They are on temporary absence to give birth or for a medical evacuation within the accepted period.<br><b>Note:</b> Section 12.3.1 provides the definition of accepted period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is not accompanied for the purpose of benefits if their partner accompanies them at the posting location at private expense.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 12.3.3 Allowable travel cost

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subject to subsection 2, allowable travel cost means any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The minimum cost of air travel between 2 locations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Compulsory insurance costs the member paid to secure a discounted fare.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Rebooking or cancellation fees, because travel was not possible on the scheduled date, for Service reasons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">All of the following limitations apply to travel under paragraph 1.a.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The travel must be by an airline with seats available.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The airline must offer a standard of safety and security comparable to air travel within Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Stopovers are avoided if possible.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Concessions and discounts are used if possible, including discounts for advance purchase.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">Despite paragraph 1.a, allowable travel costs may exceed the minimum cost if the CDF is satisfied it is reasonable in the circumstances after considering all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The standards of safety, security, amenity and hygiene at both ground facilities and on board the aircraft.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The time of year when the travel is undertaken.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The duration of the travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The extent to which the person may, in the course of travel, be subjected to discrimination within the meaning of the <i>Human Rights and Equal Opportunity Commission Act 1986</i>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>Any other factor relevant to the person's travel.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 12.3.5 Dependant

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">For overseas conditions of service, a dependant means any of these persons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">A partner who normally lives with the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">A child of the member, or of the member’s partner, who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They are under the age of 18.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They are dependent on the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>They normally live with the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">A person who has a recognised special need under section 1.3.6 regardless of their age.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member may have another person approved as a member’s dependant if the CDF is satisfied that all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The person must be a relative of the member or of the member's partner.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF must specify the period the person is the dependant of the member and for what conditions of service benefits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF must consider all of the following criteria before giving approval.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The extent of the person’s dependency on the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Whether the person’s normal place of residence is the member’s normal place of residence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The length and timing of the member’s posting period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iv.</td>
<td>The period during which the person intends to live with the member at the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>v.</td>
<td>If the person intends to leave the posting location, their reason for that.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>vi.</td>
<td>The expected effect on the person, if the member could make alternative arrangements for the person’s care and maintenance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>vii.</td>
<td>Any other special circumstance bearing on the member’s relationship to the person.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">Benefits under Chapters 12, 14, 15 and 16 are provided for dependants. These conditions apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member must be on a long-term posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The dependant must meet one of these conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The dependant lives, or intends to live, with the member at the posting location for at least 12 months.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The dependant is eligible for education assistance under Chapter 15 Part 6.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">For subparagraph 3.b.i, the CDF may approve a period of longer than 6 months but less than 12 months. The CDF must consider all these criteria.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The nature of the posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The length of the posting period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The likely cost and benefit to the Commonwealth of providing benefits for the dependant.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">The family circumstances of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td colspan="2">Any other factor relevant to the posting.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 12.3.9 Long-term posting overseas

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A long-term posting overseas is one of these periods.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">A continuous period of duty in an overseas country for longer than 6 months other than a period of short-term duty overseas that has been extended under subsection 12.3.18.2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">A continuous period of duty in a series of overseas countries, for longer than 6 months in total. The CDF may approve these periods of duty as a long-term posting. The CDF must consider all these criteria.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The accommodation and living arrangements likely to be adopted by the member during the period of duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The period the member is to spend in each country.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>Any other factor relevant to the period of duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">A period of short-term duty that the CDF extends beyond 6 months, other than an extension under subsection 12.3.18.2. The long-term posting starts on the date of approval of the extension.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">This subsection applies to a member who has spent time at a location while assigned to a deployment, and then does further duty there after the end of their deployment. The further duty is a long-term posting if the total period is longer than 6 months. The long-term posting starts on the date of approval of the further duty.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 12.3.14A Post index

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subject to subsection 2, the post index for a post index location in an item in column A of the table in Annex 12.3.B is the standard figure provided to Defence by a data service provider for a location specified in column B of the same item.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">If any of the following circumstances apply, the post index for the posting location is 100.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the figure provided by the data service provider for the post index location is less than 100.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The post index location is not listed in Annex 12.3.B column A.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The post index location listed in Annex 12.3.B column A for a member's posting location is determined in accordance with the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the posting location is Manhattan — the post index location is Manhattan.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the posting location is a city listed in Annex 12.3.B column A — the post index location is the city.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>If the posting location is a city that is not listed in Annex 12.3.B column A or an establishment and the state where the city or establishment is located <b>is</b> listed — the post index location is the state.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>If the posting location is a city or establishment and the state where the city or establishment is located is not listed in Annex 12.3.B column A — the post index location is the country where it is located.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>If paragraphs a, b, c or d do not apply, the post index is determined by subsection 12.3.14A.2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">For the purpose of subsection 3 the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>City</b> means the city and any part of the city (unless otherwise specified).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>State</b> means a state, county, region, province or territory.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 12.3.16 Posting period overseas

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A posting period overseas means the period between the following days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The day the member starts duty at the posting location after any rest period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The day the member leaves their settling-out accommodation at the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Despite subsection 1, if the member arrives or departs on a day observed locally as a weekend or public holiday, all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the member arrives at the posting location on a day observed locally as a weekend or public holiday and starts duty on the next working day — the posting period begins on the day the member arrives at the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the member departs the posting location on a day observed locally as a weekend or public holiday and finishes duty on the preceding working day — the posting period ends on the day the member departs from the posting location.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 12.3.18 Short-term duty overseas

| 1. | Short-term duty overseas means a period of duty a member undertakes at an overseas location that is away from their normal place of duty for a period of 6 months or less. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The duration of the short-term duty may be extended if the CDF is satisfied that the extension is necessary. |
| 3. | The CDF must not give an extension under subsection 2 that will cause the duration of short-term duty overseas to exceed 7 months. |

###### 12.3.19 Utilities

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Utilities</b> means all of the following services.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Water.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Gas and electricity.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Other fuel for ordinary household purposes.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Garbage.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>Sewerage.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td>Drinking water if the CDF is satisfied that the water at the member’s residence is not fit for consumption.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">For the purpose of paragraph f, the CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The standards for Australian drinking water quality, established by the National Health and Medical Research Council.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The quality of the water ordinarily available at the member’s residence.</td>
</tr>
</table>

#### Part 4: Service with the United Nations

##### Division 1: Member remunerated by the UN

###### 12.4.4 Purpose

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">The purpose of this Division is to outline the conditions of service for members who meet all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are undertaking a period of service with the United Nations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are receiving remuneration from the United Nations.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 12.4.5 Member this Division applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Division applies to a member who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are released from duty to undertake a period of service with the United Nations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are receiving remuneration from the United Nations.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 12.4.6 Allowances and benefits not payable

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member and their dependants are not eligible for benefits under Chapters 1 to 17 for any of the following periods.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The period of service with the United Nations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Any period immediately before or after the period of service with the United Nations, in relation to any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Conditions of service for long-term posting overseas that would be payable in relation to the period of service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Travel costs or any other costs incurred by the member or a dependant in connection with the service with the United Nations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">Despite subsection 1, the CDF may approve any of the following benefits, as if the member were going on, or on a long-term posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Storage of the member's and dependant's possessions within Australia, while the member is on a period of service with the United Nations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Reimbursement for insurance of the possessions stored under paragraph a.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">Outlay advance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">Assistance with health services provided overseas for a member and their dependants.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td colspan="2">Temporary accommodation allowance while in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">For subsection 2, the CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Whether there is a similar benefit provided by the United Nations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The costs incurred by the member and dependants.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">Any other factor relevant to the member's circumstances during the approved period of service with the United Nations.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 2: Member remunerated by the ADF

###### 12.4.7 Purpose

|  | The purpose of this Division is to outline the conditions of service for members undertaking a period of service with the United Nations and receiving remuneration from the ADF. |
|---|---|

###### 12.4.8 Member this Division applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Division applies to a member who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member is released from duty to undertake a period of service with the United Nations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member is receiving remuneration from the ADF.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 12.4.9 Allowances and benefits payable

|  | Chapters 1 to 12 and Chapters 14 to 16 apply to a member under this Division as if the member were on a long-term posting overseas.<br>**Note:** The member is subject to any eligibility conditions set out in the allowance or benefit. |
|---|---|

###### 12.4.10 Leave arrangements during the period of service with the United Nations

|  | The member must use their ADF leave credits when taking any period of leave during their service with the United Nations.<br>**Note:** This includes periods of leave that the member has been directed to take by the United Nations. |
|---|---|

#### Part 5: International travel and isolation periods

###### 12.5.1 Purpose

|  | This Part provides benefits for members and their dependants who are required to isolate for the purpose of responding to public health and safety emergencies that is related to a member’s service overseas. |
|---|---|

###### 12.5.2 Persons this Part applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">This Part applies to any of the following persons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member on any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Short-term duty overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Long-term posting overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>Deployment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member travelling, or being required to isolate, for the purpose of commencing service under paragraph a.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">A dependant who accompanies a member travelling, or being required to isolate, for the purpose of commencing short-term duty or long-term posting overseas.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 12.5.3 Cost of isolation accommodation

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A person is eligible to receive the costs associated with a requirement to isolate if they satisfy all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are required to isolate in specified accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are required to pay a charge for the accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The requirement to isolate is in connection with travel provided under Chapters 12 to 17 of this Determination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> A benefit is not available under this section for travel undertaken for any other purpose.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is eligible for the amount of charge for the accommodation occupied during isolation period.<br><b>Note:</b> A person may receive this benefit more than once for a journey.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section does not apply in any of the following circumstances.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The charge is for board or rent that the person would pay had they not been required to isolate.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member has received a benefit for the same accommodation under this Determination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The charge has been paid by another organisation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">The benefit under this section may be provided as a reimbursement to the member or by direct payment to the organisation responsible for collecting the charge.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 12.5.4 Alternative accommodation

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member is not required to isolate.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member’s dependants are required to isolate.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The member’s dependants isolate in the member’s home at the posting location overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The member occupies temporary accommodation for the dependant’s isolation period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is eligible for temporary accommodation for themself in their posting location for the dependant’s isolation period.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 12.5.4A Accommodation at end of duty overseas – quarantine residence

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A person is eligible to occupy a quarantine residence for their isolation period if any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If they are a member and all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They have returned to Australia at the end of a period of duty overseas, other than on a deployment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They are required to isolate.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>They are not required to isolate in a State or Territory operated quarantine facility.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iv.</td>
<td>They are not able complete their isolation period in their home.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>v.</td>
<td>A quarantine residence is available to occupy.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If they are a dependant of a member all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They have returned to Australia in connection with the end of the member’s long-term posting overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They are required to isolate.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>They are not required to isolate in a State or Territory operated quarantine facility.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iv.</td>
<td>They are not able complete their isolation period in their home.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>v.</td>
<td>A quarantine residence is available to occupy.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">If a member and their dependant are eligible for a benefit under this section at the same time, the member and their dependant share the same quarantine residence.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 12.5.5 Meal supplement allowance – outside of Australia

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies to a person who is outside of Australia and is eligible for any of the following benefits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Cost of isolation accommodation under section 12.5.3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Alternative accommodation under section 12.5.4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">Subject to subsection 3, a person is eligible for meal supplement allowance for each day of the isolation period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">Meal supplement allowance is not payable for a day on which a person receives 3 or more meals without a fee being charged to the person.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">The rate of meal supplement assistance for a person required to isolate outside of Australia is one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the country where the person is required to isolate is listed in Annex 13.3.A Part 2, one of the following applies.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>If the person is 13 years old or older — the rate specified for the limit for each day: meals in the table in Annex 13.3.A Part 2 for the country.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>If the person is younger than 13 years old — two-thirds of the rate specified in subparagraph i.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the country where the person is required to isolate is not listed in the table in Annex 13.3.A Part 2 — one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>If the person is 13 years old or older — AUD 42.50 per day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>If the person is younger than 13 years old — AUD 21.25 per day.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 12.5.6 Incidentals – outside of Australia

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are eligible for meals supplement allowance under section 12.5.5.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are on short-term duty overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is eligible for incidentals.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The rate of incidentals is one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the country where the person is required to isolate is listed in Annex 13.3.A Part 2, the rate specified for the limit for each day: incidentals in the table in Annex 13.3.A Part 2 for the country.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the country where the person is required to isolate is not listed in Annex 13.3.A Part 2, the rate specified for the limit for each day: incidentals in item 92 of the table in Annex 13.3.A, Part 2.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 12.5.7 Meal supplement allowance – in Australia

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies to a person who is in Australia and is eligible for isolation accommodation under section 12.5.4A.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A person is eligible for meal supplement allowance for each day of their isolation period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">The daily rate of meal supplement allowance is the sum of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The meals component.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the person is a member and not in their own residence — the incidentals component.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">Subject to subsection 5, the meals component of meal supplement allowance is the sum of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The sum of the costs of the meals for which the member is eligible to receive meal supplement allowance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The sum of the amounts for the following meals that corresponds with the location of the member in column A of the table in Annex 9.5.A Part 4 that the member is eligible to receive meal supplement allowance for.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>For breakfast — the amount in column B.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>For lunch — the amount in column C.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>For dinner — the amount in column D.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="3">All of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">A person is not eligible for the meals component of the meal supplement allowance for a meal that has been provided to the person at no cost.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the person is 10 years old or less, the meal component is 50% of what the person would have otherwise been eligible for.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6.</td>
<td colspan="3">The incidentals component of meal supplement allowance is the amount payable for the location of the member in column A of the table in Annex 9.5.A Part 4 that is specified in column E.</td>
</tr>
</table>

#### Part 6: Imprisonment, detention and custody overseas

###### 12.6.1 Purpose

|  | This Part sets out what happens to a member’s benefits during a period of imprisonment, detention or custody while overseas. |
|---|---|

###### 12.6.2 Member this Part applies to

|  | This Part applies to all members, including a member of the Reserves on Reserve service, on short-term duty or long-term posting overseas. |
|---|---|

###### 12.6.3 Member this Part does not apply to

| 1. | The CDF or the Chief of Defence Intelligence may identify a member to whom this Part does not apply for a particular period or activity. |
|---|---|
| 2. | When making a decision under subsection 1, the CDF or the Chief of Defence Intelligence must have regard to the nature of the member’s duty. |

###### 12.6.4 Dependants remaining in overseas location

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member's dependants remain in the overseas location while the member is imprisoned, detained or in custody.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member must pay 30% of their salary which was payable immediately before their imprisonment, detainment or custody for the dependant's housing.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member is not eligible for a reimbursement of utilities costs under section 15.4.15.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is in financial hardship the CDF may reduce the amount payable under subsection 1.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 12.6.5 Return travel to Australia before duty period has ended

|  | If a member has been imprisoned, detained or held in custody, and the member is released before the end of the duty period, the member's return travel benefits to Australia apply. |
|---|---|

###### 12.6.6 Return travel to Australia after duty period has ended

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member was imprisoned or taken into custody overseas and is released after their duty period has ended, the member is eligible for return travel to Australia as soon as practicable after release.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is eligible for travel costs under one of the following from the date of their release until the member arrives in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>For a member on short-term duty — Chapter 13 Part 3 Division 1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>For a member on long-term posting — Chapter 14 Part 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">Travel on return to Australia must be by a route that meets the conditions under subsection 14.4.5.3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is not eligible for a rest period during the return travel to Australia. The member may be eligible for a rest period on their return to the member’s posting location in Australia.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 12.6.7 Member deported from country

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member is deported from the country where the member was imprisoned or in custody, any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the member is deported to Australia — the member is not eligible for travel benefits to return to Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the member is deported to a third country — the member is eligible for travel benefits from the third country to Australia as soon as practicable after the member's arrival in the third country to return to Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member voluntarily leaves the country before their deportation and within the specified deportation period, the member is eligible for travel benefits to return to Australia.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 12.6.8 Travel for a member’s dependants

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is accompanied overseas, all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member’s dependants are eligible for return travel to Australia under Chapter 14.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the dependants return to Australia while the member is still imprisoned or in custody, the dependants are not eligible for travel benefits to return to the location where the member is imprisoned.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>If the dependants remain in the overseas posting location the dependants are not eligible for assisted leave travel under Chapter 16 Part 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is unaccompanied, the member and dependants are not eligible for overseas reunion travel.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 12.6.9 Additional recreation leave and assisted leave travel

|  | A member who is imprisoned, detained or taken into custody overseas is not eligible for additional recreation leave or assisted leave travel during the period of the imprisonment, detention or custody. |
|---|---|

###### 12.6.10 Leave on release

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A member who has been released from imprisonment or custody is not eligible to take any form of leave until one of the following applies.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member returns to their overseas posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the member does not have an overseas posting location, the member returns to the location that was their posting location immediately before their departure from Australia.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 12.6.11 Storage

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member has furniture and effects stored under Chapter 6 Part 5 Division 7 and the CDF decides to end the benefit under subsection 1.7.4.3, the member is liable for the costs of storage from the day on which they are imprisoned or taken into custody until their release.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member may appoint an agent to take possession of the property. All of the following conditions apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The appointment must be in writing.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The agent must remove all of the property from storage.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The Commonwealth is not liable for any loss or damage to the property while the property is not being removed or stored by a benefit provided under this Determination.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 12.6.12 Funeral expenses

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">If a member dies while imprisoned or in custody overseas the member's dependant or their legal representative is eligible for all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The reasonable cost of preparing the remains.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The cost of returning the member’s remains to Australia, if requested by the member’s next of kin.</td>
</tr>
</table>

#### Part 7: Death of member or dependant overseas

###### 12.7.1 Purpose

|  | The purpose of this Part is to provide assistance to family members if a member or their dependant dies overseas. |
|---|---|

###### 12.7.3 Person this Part applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">This Part applies to any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member, including a member on Reserve service, who meets one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They are on a long-term posting overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They are on short-term duty overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">A beneficiary of a member in paragraph a, if the member has died.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">A close relative of a member in paragraph a.<br><b>Note:</b> Close relative is defined at 1.3.2.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 12.7.4 Assistance if member dies

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">If a member dies overseas, the member’s beneficiary is eligible for all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The reasonable cost of preparing the remains.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If requested by the member’s next of kin — the cost of returning the remains to Australia</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">If approved by the Director General Defence Member and Family Support — financial assistance for a funeral.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> The funeral may be held in an overseas location or in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The amount of financial assistance payable under paragraph 1.c. is the lesser of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The cost of the funeral.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">AUD 14,000.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">A beneficiary is eligible for financial assistance for a memorial service of a member if all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s funeral occurs while COVID-19 control measures relating to funerals are in place in the location where the funeral is to be held.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The memorial service occurs between the following days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The day the COVID-19 control measures relating to funerals end.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The day 12 months after the COVID-19 control measures relating to funerals end.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The assistance is approved by the Director General Defence Member and Family Support.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">The amount of financial assistance available under subsection 3 is the greater of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The lesser of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The cost of the memorial service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>AUD 14,000 less the amount paid under section 11.4.9 or this section, if any.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If there are exceptional circumstances — the amount approved by the Director General Defence Member and Family Support.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 12.7.5 Assistance if dependant dies

<table>
<tr>

<td colspan="3">This section applies to a member who meets all of the following.</td>

<td></td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The dependant in paragraph a. dies.</td>
</tr>

<td></td>

<td>i.</td>
<td>The preparation of the dependant’s remains.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The returning of the dependant’s remains to Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">A funeral in the overseas location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>

</tr>
<tr>

<tr>

</tr>

<td></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

<td colspan="2">The memorial service does not occur after 12 months from the day the COVID-19 control measures relating to funerals ends.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>

</tr>
<tr>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>

</tr>
</table>

###### 12.7.5A Travel for a close relative following a death overseas

<table>
<tr>

<td></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

<td>The actual fares paid for the travel.</td>

</table>

###### 12.7.6 Continuing benefits for dependants

<table>
<tr>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The situation of the dependants who continue to live at the posting location after the member’s death.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Any other factor relevant to the dependants.</td>
</tr>
<tr>

<td colspan="2">All of the following conditions apply to benefits provided under subsection 1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>

</tr>

<td></td>
<td>b.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>

</tr>

###### 12.7.7 Reimbursement for loss on sale of vehicle if member dies

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">If a member dies overseas, the member’s beneficiary is eligible for a reimbursement under subsection 2 if all of the following apply.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The beneficiary sold the vehicle or towable item at a financial loss.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF is satisfied that the beneficiary made reasonable efforts to sell the vehicle or towable item without making a loss having regard to all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>When and how widely the person advertised the vehicle or towable item for sale.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>How the person tried to sell the vehicle or towable item.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The nature and extent of offers made for the vehicle or towable item.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iv.</td>

<td></td>
<td>b.</td>

<tr>

</tr>
</table>

#### Part 8: Australians dangerously ill scheme – overseas

##### Division 1: General provisions

###### Subdivision 1: Interpretation

###### 12.8.1 Simplified outline of this Part

This Part provides support to a member who is in hospital with a very serious or serious illness by enabling family to visit the member to assist with their recovery and rehabilitation.

Assistance under this Part includes return travel, accommodation, meals and other costs associated with travelling to the location where the member is in hospital.

###### 12.8.2 Definitions

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">In this Part the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Additional approved visitor</b> has the meaning given in section 12.8.4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Approved period</b> means any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A period of up to 7 consecutive days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>An extended period under section 12.8.6.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Approved visitor</b> has the meaning given in section 12.8.3.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 12.8.3 Approved visitor

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">Subject to subsection 2, an <b>approved visitor</b> means one of the following people.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">A person identified by the member and recorded on PMKeyS as the primary emergency contact in the event of a casualty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s partner.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s dependant.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member has no dependants, one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>A biological parent.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>An adoptive parent.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>A former or current foster parent.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iv.</td>
<td>A step-parent.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s child.<br><b>Note:</b> The child is not required to be a 'dependent' of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the all of following apply, any other person the CDF identifies who is able to meet the needs of the member for an approved visitor.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>A person listed in paragraphs a. to e. is incapable or unable to travel and provide support to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The person is nominated by a person who would have been the approved visitor under this section.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The person is suitable to provide support to the member as an approved visitor.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The approved visitor must meet all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They meet one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They normally live in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They live with the member in the overseas posting location which is not the location where the member is in hospital.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are fit to travel to the member’s location.<br><b>Note:</b> An approved visitor who has a medical condition that may affect their ability to travel must obtain written certification from a qualified medical practitioner that they are fit to travel.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 12.8.4 Additional approved visitor

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subject to subsection 2, an <b>additional approved visitor</b> means one of the following people.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A second parent of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>One or more children of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>A chaperone for the member's child.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>A carer of the approved visitor.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">All of the following apply to an additional approved visitor.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The CDF must be satisfied that exceptional circumstances apply which require the additional approved visitor to travel with the approved visitor.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The additional approved visitor must be fit to travel.<br><b>Note:</b> An additional approved visitor who has a medical condition that may affect their ability to travel must obtain written certification from a qualified medical practitioner that they are fit to travel.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### Subdivision 2: Application

###### 12.8.5 Member this Part applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

<td>They are a member of the Reserves on Reserve service.</td>

<td></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Very seriously ill.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Seriously ill.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">The medical authority has recommended that a visit will benefit the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>

</tr>
<tr>

<td colspan="2">One of the following applies to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They are on leave during a long-term posting overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>

<td>They are on relief-out-of-country travel fare assistance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Paragraphs 1.c and 1.d apply to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF is satisfied that providing benefits under this Part is reasonable.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 2: Extension or cessation of approved period

###### 12.8.6 Extension of approved period

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">The approved period may be extended by a period under subsection 2 if the CDF is satisfied that all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The medical authority has recommended that a longer period will significantly benefit the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">One of the following applies.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member has had major surgery and the post-operative recovery is expected to last longer than 7 consecutive days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member is undergoing specialist treatment in hospital that is expected to last longer than 7 consecutive days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The medical authority has assessed the member as likely to remain very seriously ill or seriously ill for longer than 21 consecutive days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The extension under subsection 1 may be for one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If subparagraph 2.b.i or 2.b.ii applies — up to 21 consecutive days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If subparagraph 2.b.iii applies — a period that the CDF considers reasonable in the circumstances.</td>
</tr>
</table>

<table>
<tr>

<tr>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member has a long-term condition and they have been are provided a sustainable welfare management plan.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The period under subsection 1 may be extended if the CDF is satisfied all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The approved visitor has made reasonable efforts to arrange return travel within the 24 hours.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Return travel is unavailable.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 12.8.8 Cessation of approved period – death of member

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies if all of the following are met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>

<tr>

<tr>
<td></td>

<td>Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member’s long-term posting location overseas if the approved visitor accompanied the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The day the member’s remains are returned to Australia under section 12.7.4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>

</tr>
</table>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The airport, bus or train terminal.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The approved visitor's home.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 12.8.15 Accommodation

|  | Accommodation within a reasonable distance from the hospital where the member is located arranged by Defence for the approved period.<br>**Note:** Accommodation costs are not reimbursable if the accommodation was arranged by the approved visitor or additional approved visitor. |
|---|---|

###### 12.8.16 Meals

|  | The reimbursement of the cost for meals up to the daily limit for meals provided under Annex 13.3.A.<br>**Note:** The cost of alcoholic beverages are not reimbursable. |
|---|---|

### Chapter 13: Short-term duty and peacetime deployment overseas

#### Part 1: General provisions

###### 13.1.1 Purpose

|  | This Part sets out the rules for the benefits and allowances that apply to members who travel overseas on short-term duty. |
|---|---|
|  | **Note:** Members on short-term duty overseas may be eligible for hardship location conditions in Chapter 16 if they meet the eligibility conditions. |

###### 13.1.1A Definitions

</tr>
<tr>

<td>Overseas adventure training.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Work experience.</td>
</tr>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>

<td>A member who performs short-term duty overseas while on a long-term posting.</td>

##### Division 1A: General Provisions

###### 13.2.1 Member this Part does not apply to

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

</tr>

<tr>
<td></td>

<td>The nature of the duty overseas.</td>

<table>

<tr>
<td></td>

<td>Domestically within a foreign country.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Between foreign countries.</td>
</tr>

###### 13.2.8 CDF discretion for first class air travel

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may upgrade a member to first class for special reasons. This can happen if a member is <b>not</b> eligible for first class air travel under paragraph 13.2.6.1.b.</td>

<td></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>

<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The length of the journey.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>

<tr>
<td></td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td>h.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Any other factor relevant to the travel.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 2: Rest periods

###### 13.2.9 Purpose

|  | Rest periods provide a chance to recover from jet lag, during or after air travel undertaken for duty. |
|---|---|

###### 13.2.10 Member this Division does not apply to

|  | This Division does not apply to a member on peacetime deployment. |
|---|---|

###### 13.2.11 Rest period benefits

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A rest period is between 12 and 24 hours. The member is considered on duty for conditions of service purposes.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for 1 rest period if they travel by the direct route for at least four time zone hours, or with a travelling time of at least 12 hours.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2A.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for 2 rest periods if they travel by the direct route for at least six time zone hours.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The same eligibility applies to the journey, whether it is by a direct or indirect route.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member may choose whether to take a rest period during the journey or at the final destination, or both.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a rest period taken at the journey’s destination falls outside normal working hours, it will not entitle the member to time off duty instead.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member may have an unavoidable stopover on the journey. If the stopover is at least 12 hours, it will be regarded as a rest period. This will satisfy the rest period benefit under this section.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>7.</td>
<td colspan="2">No journey can have more than 2 rest periods.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>8.</td>
<td colspan="2">For an overnight rest period, the member is eligible to be paid all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The accommodation costs they would be eligible for under section 13.3.6.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The meal and incidental costs up to the daily limit as provided under Annex 13.3.A.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> A member who is approved recreation leave may take the leave during or at the end of a journey in conjunction with a rest period. Time spent on a rest period is not to be deducted from recreation leave credits.</td>
</tr>
</table>

#### Part 3: Travel costs for short-term duty overseas

##### Division 1A: General provisions

###### 13.3.1 Purpose

|  | This Part sets out how a member who travels on short-term duty or peacetime deployment overseas may use an official charge card (the Defence travel card) for travel costs. |
|---|---|

###### 13.3.2 Basis

|  | Use of the travel card is based on the principle that a member will neither gain nor lose financially when they travel on Defence business. |
|---|---|

###### 13.3.4 Use of the Defence travel card

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member must use the Defence travel card for all of the following benefits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Meals.<br><b>Note:</b> Meals are provided under Division 1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Accommodation charges.<br><b>Note:</b> Accommodation charges are provided under Division 1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">Incidentals.<br><b>Note:</b> Incidentals are provided under Division 1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">Equipment costs.<br><b>Note:</b> Equipment costs are provided under Division 2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member must not use the travel card for any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Periods the member is on any of the following types of leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Recreation leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Long service leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are on an officially approved activity and are eligible for a benefit under Part 4 Division 2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">Part-day travel allowance.<br><b>Note:</b> Part-day travel allowance is provided under section 13.3.15.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 1: Rates, limitations and specific situations

###### 13.3.6 Travel costs while living out

| 1. | A member holding the rank set out in column A of the following table who lives out while on short-term duty or peacetime deployment overseas is eligible for the travel cost set out in column B at the rate set out in column C of the same item. |
|---|---|

<table>
<tr>
<td>Item</td>
<td>Column A<br>Rank</td>
<td>Column B<br>Travel cost</td>
<td>Column C<br>Rate</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td rowspan="3">1.</td>
<td rowspan="3">Brigadier or higher</td>
<td>Accommodation for each night in the period</td>
<td>The cost of accommodation of a reasonable standard for all of the following.<br>a. The member’s rank.<br>b. The nature of the duties performed by the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Meals for each day of the period.</td>
<td>The rate set out in Part 1 of Annex 13.3.A for the location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>

<td>The rate set out in Part 1 of Annex 13.3.A for the location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td rowspan="3">2.</td>
<td rowspan="3">Colonel or lower</td>
<td>Accommodation for each night in the period</td>
<td>The cost of accommodation of a reasonable standard for all of the following.<br>a. The member’s rank.<br>b. The nature of the duties performed by the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Meals for each day of the period.</td>
<td>The rate set out in Part 2 of Annex 13.3.A for the location.</td>
</tr>

| 2. | A member who has been given an allowance for accommodation, meals or incidentals for a period and location by a non-Commonwealth organisation is not eligible for an allowance under this Part to pay costs for the same period and location.<br>**Note:** Subsection 13.3.12 provides for the topping-up of costs if another organisation pays some but not all of the travel costs that the member would be eligible for under this Part. |
|---|---|
| 4. | For this Part, a member attending the Royal College of Defence Studies in the UK is eligible for benefits at the rank of Brigadier. |

###### 13.3.7 Allowance to pay for travel costs

| 1. | A member is eligible for an allowance to pay for their travel cost if they are on short-term duty or peacetime deployment overseas. |
|---|---|
| 2. | For the purpose of subsection 1, the rate of allowance for accommodation, meals and incidentals is what they would otherwise have been eligible for under this Part. |

###### 13.3.8 Limits on benefits

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is not eligible for meal costs for a meal period if any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A meal is provided to the member at no cost.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A meal is included in a fare paid for travel during the period of duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is not eligible for accommodation costs on a night that any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member's travel continues overnight without a break for accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member occupies accommodation provided on a non-commercial basis.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member who travels within Australia as part of their journey to an overseas location for short-term duty or peacetime deployment is not eligible travel costs under this Part to pay the domestic travel costs.<br><b>Note:</b> Domestic travel costs are set out in Chapter 9 Part 5.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">The maximum meal amount for a member who meets all of the following is two-thirds the amount which they would otherwise be eligible for under section 13.3.6.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are living out at a location for 5 days or longer.<br><b>Note:</b> The member’s days of arrival and departure do not count towards the 5 days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Their accommodation provides cooking facilities and utensils that are of a standard that would allow them to prepare their own meals.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 13.3.9 Reduced rates for meals on day of arrival or departure

| 1. | The rate for meals on the day a member arrives or departs depends on what time they arrive or depart. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The rate for meals on the day of arrival with an arrival time in column A of the following table is the daily rate for meals multiplied by the percentage in column B of the same item. |

| Item | Column A<br>Time of arrival | Column B<br>Percentage of daily rate |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | Before 0700 | 100% |
| 2. | Between 0700 and 1300 | 75% |
| 3. | Between 1301 and 1900 | 50% |
| 4. | After 1900 | 0% |

|  | **Note:** Annex 13.3.A provides the daily rate for meals. |
|---|---|
| 3. | The rate for meals on the day of departure with a departure time in column A of the following table is the daily rate for meals multiplied by the percentage in column B of the same item. |

| Item | Column A<br>Time of departure | Column B<br>Percentage of daily rate |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | Before 0700 | 0% |
| 2. | Between 0700 and 1300 | 25% |
| 3. | Between 1301 and 1900 | 50% |
| 4. | After 1900 | 100% |

|  | **Note:** Annex 13.3.A provides the daily rate for meals. |
|---|---|

###### 13.3.10 Reduced eligibility for incidentals

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The rate for incidental costs on the day a member arrives or departs depends on what time they arrive or depart. They are only eligible for half the daily rate if any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They arrive after noon.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They depart before noon.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for half the normal rate for incidental costs if any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They stay on duty at a location after being on short-term duty or peacetime deployment there for a continuous period of 28 days. They get half the listed rate for the period beyond the 28 days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are on a long-term posting overseas, and they go on short-term duty within the country of posting. The lower benefit applies to the short-term duty only.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>They are in an overseas country on leave and the CDF recalls them to undertake short-term duty in that country. They get half the listed rate for the short-term duty only.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>They are accommodated on board a seagoing ship while it is visiting an overseas port. They get half the listed rate during the visit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">A break of less than 7 days from their short-term duty location may not break a member's continuity for the purposes of paragraph 2.a above. The break does not count if the member was advised that the period of absence was to be for less than 7 days.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 13.3.11 Additional travel costs

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member's maximum benefit may be less than they actually spend on accommodation, meals or incidentals on their short-term duty or peacetime deployment. In this case, the CDF may approve an additional amount.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF must consider any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The length of the member’s short-term duty period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The nature of the duties the member undertakes.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The nature and cost of meals, accommodation and relevant services at the location of the duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Any other factor relevant to the costs.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 13.3.12 Top-up of costs paid by another organisation

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member may apply for additional travel costs under section 13.3.11 if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A non-Commonwealth organisation has given the member an allowance for accommodation, meals or incidentals for a period and location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The amount given to the member under paragraph a. is less that the amount to which the member would be eligible under this Part.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section does not apply if the member is on exchange duty overseas.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 13.3.13 Travel costs when in hospital

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A member who is in hospital for a period during short-term duty or peacetime deployment overseas is eligible for all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Incidentals for the location at the rate that applies to a Colonel or lower in Part 1 of Annex 13.3.A.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The costs for accommodation and other charges that the member continues to be liable for outside hospital that the member cannot avoid up to what they would have been eligible for under this Part if they were not in hospital.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 13.3.15 Part-day travel

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member who meets all of the following conditions is eligible for part-day travelling allowance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member is required to perform duty away from the location where the member normally performs duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member holds the rank of Colonel or lower.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The member is absent from their normal duty location for more than 10 hours.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The member is not absent from their normal duty location overnight.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Part-day travelling allowance is an amount calculated at 60% of the meal amount listed for the location in Part 2 of Annex 13.3.A.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 13.3.16 Travelling allowance while occupying living-in accommodation

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member who occupies living‑in accommodation while on one of the following is eligible for traveling allowance benefits in column A of the following table up to a daily maximum amount in column B of the same item.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Short-term duty overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Peacetime deployment overseas.</td>
</tr>
</table>

| Item | Column A<br>Travel allowance benefit | Column B<br>Maximum amount |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | Compulsory mess and accommodation charges | Amount of the charges. |
| 2. | Meals | Amount that the CDF considers reasonable, but not more than the applicable limit in Annex 13.3.A for the location. |
| 3. | Incidentals | Applicable amount in Annex 13.3.A for the location. |

<table>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">For item 2 of the table, the CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The location where the member is accommodated.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The cost of meals at the location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The nature of the member's accommodation and living arrangements.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Any other factor relevant to the member's meals.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 2: Equipment costs

###### 13.3.17 Purpose

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">The payment of basic equipment costs helps a member in two ways when they travel from Australia to short-term duty overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>It helps them pay for travel equipment and other necessary items.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>It has an element to pay them for the extra wear and tear on their possessions.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 13.3.17A Member this Division does not apply to

|  | This Division does not apply to a member on peacetime deployment. |
|---|---|

###### 13.3.18 Benefit

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for up to one of the following for the cost of equipment in any 3-year period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the member only travels to New Zealand — AUD 115.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the member travels to any other location — AUD 225.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>If the member travels to new Zealand and any other location — AUD 225, but not more than a total of AUD 115 for travel to New Zealand.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section does not apply to a member purchasing equipment for use in any of the following situations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Participating in an officially approved activity.<br><b>Note:</b> Officially approved activity is defined under section 13.1.1A.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Serving in a seagoing ship or submarine and required to live ashore while the vessel is in an overseas port.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Travelling on short-term duty to Australia from an overseas location where they are on a long-term posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>For use at a long-term posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member purchases equipment using a benefit under this section and then does not go overseas, they must repay the total amount of the benefit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">Despite subsection 4, a member is not required to repay the amount if the CDF is satisfied that they are unable to recover the cost of any items they bought.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 13.3.19 Additional equipment costs

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member may use the travel card to buy special clothing for overseas climates that are different from the usual climate at their normal place of duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subject to subjection 3, a member is eligible for the cost of additional equipment if the CDF is satisfied that the maximum benefit under section 13.3.18 is not enough to meet the member’s needs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The climate at the member’s destination compared to the climate at their normal place of duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The length of the proposed travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The means of travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The climate likely to be met at locations during the travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>The duties the member will perform during the travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td>How much clothing the Commonwealth supplies the member for the travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>g.</td>
<td>How much more wear and tear the member’s clothing will face due to the travel, compared to ordinary wear and tear.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>h.</td>
<td>Any benefits the member was eligible for under this determination to buy clothes for previous duty travel within Australia or overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for AUD 205 to purchase additional equipment. The member may spend up to this amount once in any 3-year period for use in each of these three regions as they are identified in the CDF approval.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A tropical region.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A cold region.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Another climatic region.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">If subsection 4 applies, a member is eligible for an additional AUD 205 for additional equipment in any 3-year period. Approval may only be given if the CDF is satisfied that they meet all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are to travel on short-term duty to a location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are likely to be exposed to an extremely cold winter climate at that location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The additional equipment they are eligible to buy under section 13.3.18 and subsection 4 above will not meet their clothing needs for travel to the location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>7.</td>
<td colspan="2">Additional equipment allowance may be paid to members on long-term overseas postings who must travel to other overseas locations for short-term duty.</td>
</tr>
</table>
