#### Part 4: Special conditions and allowances

##### Division 1: Member on Defence co-operation program or project

###### 13.4.3 Member this Division applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This Division applies to a member serving for a period overseas on one of the following projects.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A Defence co-operation program or project.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A similar program or project approved by the CDF.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The duties performed by the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The circumstances in which the program or project is conducted.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The duration of the program or project.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Any other relevant factor.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 13.4.4 Member this Division does not apply to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Division does not apply to any of the following members.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A member who is eligible for maritime disability allowance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A member on peacetime deployment.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 13.4.5 Allowance if meals not provided

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to the member during part or all of their stay at a location overseas. All of the following must be met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member does not stay in a hotel or other commercial lodging, or living-in accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member is not provided with food.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is eligible for all of the following for the period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>An allowance for the costs that the CDF considers reasonable for food and drinks, excluding alcohol.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Half the normal rate for incidentals under Part 3, Travel costs for short-term duty overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">For paragraph 2.a, the CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The cost the member incurred for food and drinks.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member’s welfare and dietary needs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The cost and availability of supplies at the place where the member is on duty, and alternative sources of supply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The cost of transporting goods to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>Any other factor relevant to the member's situation.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 13.4.6 Allowance for supplementary dietary needs

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may decide that the food provided to a member does not satisfy ordinary dietary needs. If so, the member may be reimbursed food costs incurred in meeting those needs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">When making a decision, the CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The quantity and quality of the food provided.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The ordinary dietary requirements of someone serving in the member's circumstances.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Any other factor relevant to the food provided.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 2: Officially approved activities

###### 13.4.7 Member this Division applies to

|  | This Division applies to a member participating in officially approved activities overseas. |
|---|---|

###### 13.4.7A Member this Division does not apply to

|  | This Division does not apply to a member on peacetime deployment. |
|---|---|

###### 13.4.8 Help with travel costs

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF can decide an amount to help with travel costs associated with participation in officially approved activities. The CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The activity's nature, duration and location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The approved itinerary and transport arrangements.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c</td>
<td>The nature and extent of travel costs incurred by the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The benefit to the ADF of the member’s participation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>The nature and level of interest in the activity among ADF members.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td>The value of any other subsidy of the member’s participation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>g.</td>
<td>Any other factor relevant to the activity.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The amount must not be more than the lesser of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The total travel costs the member would be eligible for if the travel were for short‑term duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The costs the member incurs for participating in the activity.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is not eligible for any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Other travel costs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The cost of transportation.</td>
</tr>
</table>

### Chapter 14: Relocating to or from a long-term posting overseas

#### Part 1: General provisions

###### 14.1.1 Member this Chapter does not apply to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This chapter does not apply to a member if any of the following conditions apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are not entitled to salary.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are on a scholarship, bursary or endowment for studying overseas from an organisation other than the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>They are on short-term duty overseas.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 14.1.2 Definitions

|  | In this Chapter the following apply. |
|---|---|
|  | **Evacuation** means members and dependants are directed by the Commonwealth to withdraw from the location because of international relations, political, security or other special circumstances at the location. |

#### Part 2: Before leaving Australia

##### Division 1: Pre-departure certificate of fitness

###### 14.2.3 Person this Division applies to

|  | This Division applies to a member’s dependants who have been approved to live at the member’s posting location. |
|---|---|

###### 14.2.4 Pre-departure certificate of fitness

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Before a person departs Australia for the posting location, they must obtain certificates of both medical and dental fitness. Certificates must state that the person is fit to travel to and live at the posting location.<br><b>Note:</b> This section also applies to dependants embarking on reunion visits to the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Certificates must be provided by doctors and dentists authorised by Defence who meet all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They must be informed that the examinations are required for travelling to and living at the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They must provide a results report to the Joint Health Command (JHC) for approval.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note 1:</b> The provisions of the <i>Privacy Act 1988</i> apply to the certificates under this section as set out in section 1.2.6.<br><b>Note 2:</b> The certificates are to be provided to the JHC for review and to advise the Overseas Administration Team of approval or further action required.<br><b>Note 3:</b> The certificates are to be filed and kept by the JHC as Official: Sensitive, Personal privacy//Health Information.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">The examinations must allow sufficient time for any necessary medical or dental treatment to be undertaken before departure from Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the examinations reveal a medical, dental, physical, mental or intellectual condition, the JHC must consider if the posting location has suitable facilities for ongoing treatment of that condition.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a person has special needs recognised under section 1.3.6, the decision maker in the JHC must consider if the posting location has suitable facilities for ongoing treatment and care of the condition.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>7.</td>
<td colspan="2">This subsection applies if a medical examination shows that a person has a special need. The member may apply for recognition of the person’s special need under section 1.3.6, if the person is not already recognised under that section.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>8.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a person is not certified as fit, the CDF may approve that the person is eligible for health care costs outlined in this Part. The CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The state of health of the person.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The nature, availability and cost of health, therapeutic or special needs facilities at the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The interests of the Commonwealth that would be furthered by the person living at the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Any climatic or other environmental factor at the posting location that may be especially adverse to the health or the person.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>Any other factor relevant to the person's fitness to live at the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>9.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is eligible for the reimbursement for any costs to obtain the certificate of fitness.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>10.</td>
<td colspan="2">Eligible persons are also eligible to be provided with all necessary inoculations, vaccinations and anti-malarial drugs.<br><b>Note:</b> This includes dependants embarking on reunion visits.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 2: Financial advances

###### 14.2.5 Member this Division applies to

|  | This Division applies to a member who has received an official written notice of posting. |
|---|---|

###### 14.2.6 Outlay advance — purpose

|  | Outlay advance is a loan to help with the member’s establishment costs at their next posting location. |
|---|---|

###### 14.2.7 Outlay advance — payment

| 1. | A member may apply for an outlay advance for use at the start of a long-term posting. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The member may select an advance amount up to a maximum of AUD 15,000. |
| 3. | A member must enter into a deed using the approved form to apply for an outlay advance. |
| 4. | When a member and their partner (who is also a member) are posted to the same location overseas, only the member receiving overseas living allowances is eligible for an outlay advance. |
| 5. | A member may claim an outlay advance for each long-term posting. The maximum amount that a member can have outstanding at any time is AUD 15,000. |

###### 14.2.8 Outlay advance — statement

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">The member must provide a statement that meets all of the following requirements.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The statement must be provided within the 6 months after the member receives the outlay advance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The statement must be in writing.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The statement must list all costs paid from the outlay advance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The statement must be provided to the Overseas Administration Team.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> If these requirements are not met there are fringe benefits tax implications for the member.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 3: Expenses if overseas posting is cancelled

###### 14.2.11 Reimbursement of costs if long-term posting cancelled

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a long-term posting is cancelled before the member begins the posting, they may not be able to be refunded by the supplier for goods and services they bought for the posting. They are eligible for an amount for what they would have been reimbursed for the goods and services, if the posting had not been cancelled. All of the following must be met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member received written notification of posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The cancellation did not result from the member’s personal circumstances.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The member paid for goods or services as a direct result of the notification.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The member cannot make use of the goods or services.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>The member is not able to be refunded by the supplier of the goods or services.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">If no existing condition of service in subsection 3 covers unavoidable costs incurred in subsection 1, the member may be paid an amount the CDF considers reasonable in the circumstances. The CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The nature of the costs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The circumstances under which the costs were paid.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The residual benefit of the goods and services bought.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Any other factor relevant to the costs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">For subsection 2, <b>conditions of service</b> means any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Transfer allowance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Housing assistance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Reimbursement of education costs for a child.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 4: Delay in departure accommodation

###### 14.2.13 People this Division applies

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Division applies to any of the following people.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A member who is to depart Australia to commence a long-term posting overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A dependant of a member who is to depart Australia and is to accompany a member commencing a long-term posting overseas, regardless of whether they travel at the same time as the member.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 14.2.14 Eligibility for temporary accommodation

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">Subject to subsection 2, a person is eligible for temporary accommodation if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Travel to the posting location is delayed by one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>COVID-19 related travel restrictions that prevent the person from travelling.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>An inability to travel on scheduled flights because of the COVID-19 pandemic.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The cause of the delay in paragraph a. was not in place before the member had a removal under section 14.3.5.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">For the purpose of subparagraph 1.a.ii, reasons a person may be unable to travel on a scheduled flight because of the COVID-19 pandemic include, but are not limited to, the flight being cancelled or rescheduled, or the person contracting COVID-19 before their departure.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">If the person is travelling with another person who is in the same family group, the family group is required to occupy the same accommodation if a CDF is satisfied that it is reasonable to do so.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 14.2.15 Duration of eligibility

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The person is eligible to occupy temporary accommodation under section 14.2.13 from the day travel to the posting location is delayed.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The person ceases to be eligible to occupy temporary accommodation under section 14.2.13 or the earlier of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The day they depart Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The day that is 2 weeks after the day they became eligible to occupy the temporary accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">Despite paragraph 2.b, the CDF may extend the eligibility of a person to occupy the temporary accommodation by up to 2 weeks if they are satisfied it is reasonable in the circumstances.<br><b>Note:</b> A decision under this section may be made more than once in relation to the same person.</td>
</tr>
</table>

#### Part 3: Removals

##### Division 1A: General provisions

###### 14.3.1 Overview

|  | This Part outlines the removal benefits for a member, going to or from a long-term overseas posting. |
|---|---|

###### 14.3.2 Member this Part applies to

|  | This Part applies to a member who has received an official written notice of posting. It also applies to their eligible dependants. |
|---|---|

###### 14.3.3 Dual eligibility

|  | If a member and their partner are both eligible for removal benefits under this Part, only the member receiving overseas living allowances is eligible for a removal. |
|---|---|

##### Division 1: Removal, storage or sale of items

###### 14.3.5 Removal at beginning of posting

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for the cost of the removal of items to the posting location at the beginning of a posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">When the member has made an inventory of items to be removed, the CDF will approve what items may be removed, and how they are to be removed. The CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Criteria about the posting</b></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The location from which the member departs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The location to which the member is posted and the circumstances at the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The intended duration of the posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Any prospective postings and the member's expected career path.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Criteria about the dependants</b></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>The number, age and health of any dependants of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td>Any other factor relevant to the residential arrangements of the member and dependants at the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Criteria about the removal</b></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>g.</td>
<td>The quantity and nature of the goods to be removed.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>h.</td>
<td>The most efficient and effective means of transport available to remove the goods.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The cost of removal by available means of transport.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>j.</td>
<td>The need for the goods to arrive as close as possible to the date of the member’s arrival at the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>k.</td>
<td>Any other factor relevant to the removal.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">For a member privately arranging removals, the conditions in subsection 6.5.15.2 applies.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 14.3.6 Pet relocation

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member may be reimbursed up to AUD 652 for pet transportation, both to and from the overseas posting location.<br><b>Note:</b> Relocation of pets within Australia is provided under Chapter 6 Part 1 Division 3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The benefit includes reimbursement for any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Commercial transportation and associated boarding.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Any veterinary fees for the sedation of a pet during transport.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Any fees and charges in relation to quarantine, if imposed by the Commonwealth or not.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The benefit does not include reimbursement for any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Items bought for the transportation or boarding of pets.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The transportation and boarding of any animal that the member or dependant owns primarily for economic or business purposes.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">To be reimbursed, the member must apply in writing to the Overseas Administration Team, attaching receipts.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 14.3.7 Storage of items not removed

| 1. | Subject to subsection 2, a member who is eligible for a removal under this Part may choose to store in Australia some of their portable household items under Chapter 6 Part 5 Division 2 for the duration of the posting. |
|---|---|
| 2. | An unaccompanied member whose dependants remain in Australia is not eligible for a benefit under this section. |
| 3. | A member is eligible for the removal of stored items to their permanent accommodation in Australia at the end of their overseas posting. |

###### 14.3.7A Items placed in temporary storage

| 1. | A member is eligible for the storage of items removed under section 14.3.5 if the accommodation provided under Chapter 15 Part 4 Division 1 is not available when the member arrives in the posting location. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The member is eligible for the removal of items stored under subsection 1 to their accommodation when the accommodation becomes available. |

###### 14.3.8 Loss on sale or disposal of items

| 1. | If a member disposes of an item instead of removing it to the posting location or storing it in Australia, the member is eligible to be reimbursed an amount equal to any loss as a result of the disposal unless the item was obtained through a grant. |
|---|---|
| 2. | For subsection 1, the maximum amount payable is what the Commonwealth would have paid to remove and store the possessions. |
| 3. | To claim this benefit, the member must apply in writing to the Overseas Administration Team. |

###### 14.3.9 Storage of excess items

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">In certain situations, a member may discover removed items cannot be accommodated at the new overseas posting location. This excludes necessary items bought while overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">If subsection 1 applies, the member may do any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Have the item removed back to Australia and stored for the remainder of the overseas posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Sell the item and claim any loss on the disposal of the item as in section 14.3.8, Loss on sale or disposal of items.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Store the item overseas, before removal back to Australia.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 14.3.11 Removal at end of posting

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for a removal of items to the next posting location or to Australia in any of the following situations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>At the end of the posting period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>On termination of the posting by the CDF.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>On leaving the ADF.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is eligible for a removal from the USA or Canada to Australia, a volume-based removal applies. The CDF may approve a member to fill the available space without consideration of the factors in subsection 3. Additional space is not provided under subsection 4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">When the member has made an inventory of desired items to be removed, the CDF will approve what items may be removed and how they are to be removed. The CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Criteria about the return from overseas posting</b></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The location from which the member is returning.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The period since the member last lived in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The next location to which the member is posted and the circumstances at the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The intended duration of the next posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>Any prospective postings and the member's expected career path.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Criteria about the dependants</b></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td>The number, age and health of any dependants of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>g.</td>
<td>Any other factor relevant to the residential arrangements of the member and dependants at the next posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Criteria about the removal</b></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>h.</td>
<td>The quantity and nature of the goods to be removed.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The most efficient and effective means of transport available to remove the goods.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>j.</td>
<td>The cost of removal by available means of transport.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>k.</td>
<td>The need for the goods to arrive as close as possible to the date of the member’s next posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>l.</td>
<td>Any other factor relevant to the removal.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is also eligible for an additional 2.25 cubic metres of space to place certain items for removal from the posting location. This is for furniture and whitegoods only. The additional space is provided over and above the volume of goods removed to the post.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF will approve the most efficient and effective transport for the removal.</td>
</tr>

###### 14.3.12 Unacceptable items for removal

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">These items are not acceptable for any overseas removal at Commonwealth cost.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The Commonwealth will not knowingly remove any of the items covered by this subsection. The member must take personal responsibility for any charges or penalties arising from including any of the following items in a removal.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Dangerous goods.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Items that contravene Customs or quarantine regulations, in Australia or the host country.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The Commonwealth will not remove any of the following items, except under any special conditions that are stated.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Furniture, except in special circumstances subject to CDF approval under section 14.3.5 or 14.3.11.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Non-portable items that cannot be carried by one person.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Private vehicles or towable items of any kind.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Water recreational equipment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>Aircraft of any sort.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td>Household furnishings and appliances.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>g.</td>
<td>Air conditioners.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>h.</td>
<td>Large or heavy gardening equipment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Perishable foods of any kind, including packaged or frozen food.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">Despite paragraph 3.g, a personal air conditioner may be removed under section 14.3.11 if the member is moving to or from a location in Papua New Guinea, other than Port Moresby.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 14.3.13 Benefits if enlisted overseas

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member appointed or enlisted outside Australia for service in Australia is eligible for all of the following assistance with travel and removal to Australia for themselves and their dependants.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Air travel at Defence expense as provided under Part 4 Division 1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Rest periods as provided under Part 4 Division 3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Removal of a reasonable amount of personal effects and household items, including furniture, to the housing benefit location in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Travel costs, including accommodation costs for authorised rest periods, for the period of travel to Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>Accommodation costs if it is necessary to spend a night in temporary accommodation before departure and on arrival in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td>Temporary accommodation allowance and rent allowance at the initial housing benefit location in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>g.</td>
<td>Reimbursement of any medical or migration processing fees.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>h.</td>
<td>Baggage benefits as provided under Part 4 Division 2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member whose dependants make their first Australian home in a family benefit location, is eligible for all of the following benefits for their family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Temporary accommodation allowance for the dependants in the family benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Rent allowance or a Service residence for the dependants in the family benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Removal of a reasonable amount of the dependant’s personal effects to the family benefit location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">In this section, <b>dependant</b> may include a person who would be recognised as a <b>child</b> under section 1.3.35.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 2: Storage and removal of private vehicles

###### 14.3.15 Storage of vehicle

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member posted overseas may choose to store a vehicle. All of the following must be met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The vehicle is owned by the member, on the date the official written notice of the posting was issued.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The vehicle is stored in a commercial storage area.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member may be reimbursed for storage costs up to AUD 1,400. This amount includes maintenance costs included in the storage costs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member must meet the following costs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Transporting the vehicle from the housing benefit location in Australia to or from the commercial storage facility.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Preparing the vehicle for storage.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Insurance for the vehicle, if it becomes unregistered.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Any damage caused by or to the vehicle, if it becomes unregistered and is unsafe to drive.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">To be reimbursed under subsection 2, the member must apply in writing to the Overseas Administration Team, attaching receipts.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member may choose to transfer their storage benefit from a private vehicle to a towable item. This includes a caravan or trailer.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 14.3.16 Removal of vehicle on return to Australia

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member retains ownership of a vehicle in Australia during the period of posting overseas, they are eligible for a removal of the vehicle on return to Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The maximum amount that may be reimbursed is the cost of removal from the member’s last posting in Australia, to the new housing benefit location in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member must meet any costs in excess of subsection 2. This includes any of the following costs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Travel costs from any other storage location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Insurance for the vehicle if it becomes unregistered.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Any damage caused by or to the vehicle while it is being removed, if it becomes unregistered and is unsafe to drive.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Any damage the vehicle causes while it is being removed if it becomes unregistered and is unsafe to drive.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for a removal of up to 2 vehicles on return to Australia under Chapter 6 Part 5A Division 2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">For the purpose of subsection 4, if paragraphs 6.5A.7.b and 6.5A.7.c are not met, the vehicle may be transported if the member provides a written statement that the vehicle is safe to drive.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 3: Transfer allowance

###### 14.3.17 Purpose

|  | The purpose of transfer allowance is to pay towards miscellaneous costs associated with overseas removals. |
|---|---|

###### 14.3.18 Transfer allowance

| 1. | Subject to subsection 5, if a member is moving from Australia to an overseas location and they meet a condition under column A of the following table, they are eligible for the amount of transfer allowance under column B of the same item for each person moving with the member. |
|---|---|

| Item | Column A<br>Condition | Column B<br>Transfer allowance (AUD) |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | If the member occupied living-in accommodation before departure from Australia | 635 for the member<br>294 for each dependant |
| 2. | If the member has a partner | 749 each for the member and partner<br>294 for each dependant (excluding partner) |
| 3. | Any other situation | 775 for the member<br>294 for each dependant |

| 2. | Subject to subsection 5, if a member is moving from an overseas location to Australia and they meet a condition under column A of the following table, they are eligible for the amount of transfer allowance under column B of the same item for each person moving with the member. |
|---|---|

| Item | Column A<br>Condition | Column B<br>Transfer allowance (AUD) |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | If the member occupied living-in accommodation before departure from the overseas location | 79 for the member<br>133 for each dependant |
| 2. | If the member has a partner | 161 each for the member and partner<br>133 for each dependant (excluding partner) |
| 3. | Any other situation | 179 for the member<br>133 for each dependant |

| 3. | Subject to subsection 5, if a member is moving from an overseas location to another overseas location and they meet a condition under column A of the following table, they are eligible for the amount of transfer allowance under column B of the same item for each person moving with the member. |
|---|---|

| Item | Column A<br>Condition | Column B<br>Transfer allowance (AUD) |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | If the member occupied living-in accommodation before departure from the overseas location | 301 for the member<br>229 for each dependant |
| 2. | If the member has a partner | 365 each for the member and partner<br>229 for each dependant (excluding partner) |
| 3. | Any other situation | 407 for the member<br>229 for each dependant |

| 4. | Subject to subsection 5, if a member is moving from a residence in an overseas location to another residence in the same location and they meet a condition under column A of the following table, they are eligible for the amount of transfer allowance under column B of the same item for each person moving with the member. |
|---|---|

| Item | Column A<br>Condition | Column B<br>Transfer allowance (AUD) |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | If the member occupied living-in accommodation and moves to another residence | 301 for the member<br>229 for each dependant |
| 2. | Any other situation | 152 for the member<br>The costs incurred by the member for telephone disconnection and reconnection |

<table>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">The following apply to the payment of transfer allowance under this section.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the member meets both conditions of table items 1 and 2 of a table in subsection 1, 2 or 3, the member is eligible for the higher rate of transfer allowance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the member and any dependant move to the new location at different times, the amount of transfer allowance under this section remains payable to the member as if the member and their dependants moved at the same time.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 5: Dependant removals in special cases

###### 14.3.20 Purpose

|  | The purpose of this Division is to outline cases where removals may be granted to dependants in special circumstances. |
|---|---|

###### 14.3.21 Separate removal of member and dependant

| 1. | In certain situations, a member and dependant may have items removed from the posting location at different times. |
|---|---|
| 2. | If the total amount for these separate removals is greater than the amount for a single removal, the member must pay the extra amount. |
| 3. | The CDF may meet the total cost of all removals and storage charges for special circumstances. |

###### 14.3.22 Moving dependants within Australia

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member on long-term posting is eligible for a removal to move dependants remaining in Australia to another Australian location if all of the following are met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is unaccompanied.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF decides that any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The dependants must vacate a Service residence as a result of the member’s posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>There are no family members available to provide support for dependent children, in the member’s absence from the location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The location of the current home is too remote to provide social and educational facilities for dependant children.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>iv.</td>
<td>The dependant has a medical condition that requires them to move to another location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>v.</td>
<td>The safety or welfare of the dependants would be at high risk if they remained in the accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>vi.</td>
<td>A change in family circumstances requires urgent action.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2"></td>
<td>vii.</td>
<td>The removal is necessary to prevent an emergency.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The CDF may approve a removal to any suitable destination in Australia. The CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The location of the member’s next posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If it is expected that the member will complete their service within 12 months of returning to Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">If granted a removal under this section, the member is eligible for the normal conditions of service for a removal within Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">Despite subsection 2, a member is eligible to be reimbursed the cost of the removal if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The removal was privately arranged by the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The removal was approved by the CDF.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="3">For the purpose of subsection 4, the reimbursement must not exceed the cost of the removal benefit provided under this Determination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td></td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 6: Removals if dependant status changes

###### 14.3.23 Purpose

|  | This Division describes the removal benefits for a member whose domestic or marital status changes, while serving overseas on long-term posting. |
|---|---|

###### 14.3.24 Member marries or has partnership recognised at posting location

|  | When a member marries or has a partnership recognised at the posting location, there is no removal benefit to have the partner's possessions moved to the member’s permanent accommodation overseas. |
|---|---|

###### 14.3.25 Member marries or has partnership recognised away from posting location

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member marries elsewhere than the posting location, the CDF may grant a removal of personal effects to the posting location if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member must have at least 12 months’ service remaining at the posting location. This time is effective from the approved date the member's partner travels to accompany the member at the overseas location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Only the partner’s personal possessions and wedding presents are removed from the place of marriage, to the member’s permanent accommodation at the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member has a partnership recognised by the ADF elsewhere than the posting location, the CDF may grant a removal of personal effects to the posting location if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member must have at least 12 months’ service remaining at the posting location. This time is effective from the approved date the member's partner travels to accompany the member at the overseas location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Only the partner's personal possessions are removed from the place where the couple's common household was established, to the member’s permanent accommodation at the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the new partner has a child, the member is eligible for the removal of the child’s personal effects if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The child is eligible as a member’s dependant for removal purposes.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The child normally lives with the partner.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The child is to live with the member at the overseas posting location.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 14.3.26 Removal on next posting

| 1. | Division 1 section 14.3.11 applies to the member's and any dependants' removal on the next posting after the member's marriage or ADF recognition of partnership, whichever is applicable. |
|---|---|
| 2. | On the member’s and dependants’ arrival in Australia after the long-term posting, the removal provisions under Chapter 6 Part 5 apply. |

###### 14.3.27 Ceasing to be a member with dependants overseas

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A member on long-term posting overseas may cease to be a member with dependants. This means they no longer have a requirement to maintain a home for dependants at the overseas posting location. The member is eligible for any of the following removals for their dependants.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Removal of items to the intended location of residence in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Temporary removal of items to storage in Australia, until completion of the overseas posting. In addition, a subsequent removal from storage to the intended location of residence in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Removal of items to any other location. This is provided the cost is no more than the cost if all items been removed at the same time.</td>
</tr>
</table>

#### Part 4: Travel to and from the posting location

##### Division 1A: General provisions

###### 14.4.1 Overview

|  | This Part outlines travel benefits for journeys taken at the beginning and end of a posting period. This means the journey to the posting location before the settling-in period starts, and the journey from the posting location after the settling-out period ends. |
|---|---|

###### 14.4.2 Member this Part applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This Part applies to a member, when the member has an official written notice of a posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Dependants can receive the same benefits as the member under this Part. All of the following must be met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The dependants are being removed to the posting location with the member under section 14.4.5.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The dependants are able to spend the minimum period under section 12.3.5 as part of the member's household at the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The dependants are not travelling to a posting designated as unaccompanied.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">For this Part, the Commonwealth will not pay for any chaperones accompanying a dependant in any circumstances.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 1: Travel benefits

###### 14.4.4 International best fare

|  | In this Division, international best fare has the meaning given in the Department of Finance Resource Management Guide No. 405 as published in October 2016.<br>**Note:** International best fare takes into account matters such as cost, practicality and value for money. |
|---|---|

###### 14.4.5 Travel benefit

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is eligible for the cost of their and their dependant’s travel to and from the posting location if any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>To begin the posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>At the end of the posting period, to travel back to Australia, or to the next posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>On evacuation of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>On termination of the posting by the CDF.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>On termination of the posting by the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The Director Defence Print and Travel Services must approve the routes that may attract travel assistance. Before making the decision they must consider the whole-of-Australian-Government international best fare policy.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">Travel assistance may only be paid for a route that the CDF is satisfied meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>It is a route approved under subsection 2.<br><b>Note:</b> Package holidays are not approved under subsection 2, and are not available.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>It is the international best fare.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for the fare to Australia for each of the member’s dependants who join the member’s household during the posting period.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 14.4.6 Travel costs

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">For travel at the beginning and end of a posting period, a member and dependants may be paid travel costs for accommodation, meals and incidentals.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The travel cost limits payable for meals, accommodation and incidentals for the journey are as follows.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">For the portion of the journey that is overseas any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>For a dependant less than 12 years old — two-thirds of the cost limits for travel to or from the posting location under Chapter 13 Part 3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>For a member or a dependant 12 years or older — the same cost limits for travel to or from the posting location under Chapter 13 Part 3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">For the portion of the journey within Australia — the cost limits under Chapter 9 Part 5 for travelling within Australia on posting apply.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 14.4.7 Class of air travel for long-term posting

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is eligible for travel at business class, if available. This includes connecting flights for the journey to or from the overseas posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">If business class is not available, members with the rank of Colonel or lower must travel economy class.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for travel at first class, if business class is not available and the member meets any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They hold the rank of Brigadier or higher.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They have special travel requirements.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member with special travel requirements is a member travelling to or from the posting location for more than 5 hours on the aircraft. They must also satisfy any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member is certified by a doctor as being pregnant at the time or travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member is accompanying a dependent who is certified by a doctor as being pregnant at the time of travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The member is accompanying a child under 7 years of age at the time of travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member is unable to accompany their pregnant dependent, the dependent may travel first class, if business class is not available.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member is unable to accompany a child under 7 years of age, but the child is travelling with the member's partner, the partner and the child may travel first class if business class is not available.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>7.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may approve a member to travel first class in other special circumstances. The CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Standards of amenities and hygiene if not travelling first class, both on the ground and on board the aircraft.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member's health.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The time of year when travelling.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The duration of travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>The nature of duties (if any) being undertaken while travelling.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td>The extent to which the member may be subject to discrimination, within the meaning of the <i>Human Rights and Equal Opportunity Commission Act 1986</i>, while travelling.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>g.</td>
<td>Any other factor relevant to the member's travel.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 14.4.8 Alternative travel modes and routes

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for travel costs under section 14.4.5 by a route that is approved by Director Defence Print and Travel Services if all of the following have been met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The approval is given before the member or dependant books the travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The travel is not a holiday package.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Any of the following costs can be paid for travel approved under subsection 1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Airfares at the class provided for under section 14.4.7.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Vehicle allowance payable under Chapter 9 Part 6 for any surface travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Costs payable under Division 3 for any rest period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The value of airfares and surface travel costs paid under subsection 2 must not be more than the airfare component of the travel that would otherwise be provided under section 14.4.5 and section 14.4.6.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the route approved under this section is cheaper than the route approved under section 14.4.5 the member is not entitled to the difference.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 14.4.9 Travel by private vehicle

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member has travel approved by private vehicle under section 14.4.8 they are eligible for all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Vehicle allowance payable under Chapter 9 Part 6.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>An amount for meals up to the rate payable under Annex 13.3.A.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Costs for incidentals, which is payable at half the normal rate applicable under Annex 13.3.A.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The benefit payable under subsection 1 must not be more than what would have been paid for the member's transport if the member had not used the vehicle.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 2: Baggage benefits

###### 14.4.10 Baggage benefits

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member and each dependant authorised to travel to or from the overseas posting location can transport any of the following baggage at no cost to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>30 kg of baggage.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Two suitcases if the carrier charges for each bag rather than by weight.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">This benefit includes the amount of baggage the carrier allows the passenger to carry for no extra charge.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 14.4.11 Excess baggage

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is eligible for the cost of excess baggage that exceeds the baggage allowance under subsection 14.4.10.1 if the CDF is satisfied it is reasonable having regard to all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The nature and content of the baggage, including any special equipment being carried.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Removal arrangements under this Determination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The duration and timing of the posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">For the purpose of subsection 1, all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The excess baggage must not exceed any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>If the carrier charges for the combined weight of baggage — 45 kg of total baggage weight.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>If the carrier charges per suitcase — 3 suitcases.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The cost must not exceed the cost for excess baggage that would be payable for travel by the most direct route.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">Despite subsection 2.a, if the CDF is satisfied global shipping and supply chain disruptions are expected to significantly impact the movement of the member’s personal effects, the excess baggage must not exceed any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the carrier charges for the combined weight of baggage — 60 kg of total baggage weight.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the carrier charges per suitcase — 4 suitcases.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td colspan="2">Assistant Director-General Customer and International Engagement Australian Signals Directorate.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 14.4.12 Unaccompanied baggage or air freight

| 1. | The benefit in section 14.4.11 may be converted to unaccompanied baggage or air freight. |
|---|---|
| 2. | If the member sends their baggage unaccompanied, the maximum benefit is the same that applies to moving the baggage by air at the accompanied rate under section 14.4.11. |
| 4. | If there is no unaccompanied baggage rate available, air freight may be used on the same principle. |

##### Division 3: Rest periods

###### 14.4.13 Purpose

|  | Rest periods provide a chance to recover from jet lag, during or after air travel undertaken for duty. |
|---|---|

###### 14.4.15 Rest period benefits

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A rest period is between 12 and 24 hours. The member is considered on duty for conditions of service purposes.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for 1 rest period if they travel by the direct route for at least four time zone hours, or with a travelling time of at least 12 hours.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2A.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for 2 rest periods if they travel by the direct route for at least six time zone hours.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is taken to be on duty during a rest period. If a rest period taken at the journey’s destination falls outside normal working hours, it will not entitle the member to time off duty instead.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">The same benefit applies to a given journey, whether it is by a direct or indirect route.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member may choose whether to take a rest period during the journey or at the final destination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member may have an unavoidable stopover on the journey. If the stopover is at least 12 hours, it will be regarded as a rest period. This will satisfy the rest period benefit under this section.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>7.</td>
<td colspan="2">No journey can have more than 2 rest periods.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>8.</td>
<td colspan="2">For an overnight rest period, the member is eligible for all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The accommodation costs they would be eligible for under section 13.3.6.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Meals and incidental costs under Chapter 13 Part 3, Travel costs for short-term duty overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> A member who is approved recreation leave may take the leave during or at the end of a journey in conjunction with a rest period. Time spent on a rest period is not to be deducted from recreation leave credits.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 4: Dependants not travelling with the member

###### 14.4.17 Dependants not travelling with member

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>

</tr>
<tr>

<td>a.</td>

</tr>

<td></td>

<td>A relative of the member suffers ill health and the dependant needs to remain to help the relative.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The short posting notice does not provide adequate time to make domestic arrangements before departure.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>Any other circumstances that the CDF is satisfied requires the dependant to delay their departure.</td>
</tr>
<tr>

</tr>
<tr>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

<td>The dependant is not travelling to or from the posting location on any other type of assisted airfare, based on the allowable travel cost.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>If the dependant returned unaccompanied to Australia under this Determination — the member served at least 12 months at the overseas posting location.</td>

<tr>
<td>2A.</td>
<td colspan="2">The period in paragraph 2.d may be reduced to less than 12 months if the CDF is satisfied there are special circumstances.</td>
</tr>

| Item | For... | The maximum amount payable is the... |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | a child who travels to or from the posting location, unaccompanied by the member or member's partner | allowable travel cost to the location. |
| 2. | any other dependant not travelling with the member | amount that would have been paid, if the dependant had accompanied the member for travel. |

<table>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">For this section, the dependant must not travel:</td>
</tr>

<td>before the date of effect of the posting order, or</td>

<td></td>

<td>more than 12 months after the member's travel from the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>

###### 14.4.17A Dependant joining member

<table>
<tr>

<td colspan="3">This section applies to a member who meets any of the following.</td>
</tr>
