#### Part 5: Settling in and out

###### 14.5.1 Purpose

|  | The purpose of this Part is to cover the additional costs of meals when a member and dependants are obliged to live in temporary accommodation, including motels and serviced apartments. |
|---|---|

###### 14.5.2 Member this Part applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This Part applies to a member and their dependants who are authorised to live in temporary accommodation overseas for any of the following reasons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member is arriving at the posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member is leaving the posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The member's housing has become unfit for occupation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">During a period of settling in and settling out, a member is eligible for the overseas living allowances. They must also pay a rent and utilities contribution.<br><b>Note:</b> Benefits under this Part apply to a deceased member's dependants under section 12.7.6. However, additional limits may apply under subsection 12.7.6.3.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 14.5.3 Settling in at the posting location

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for settling in allowance for themselves and each dependant if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member and their dependant occupies temporary accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are receiving overseas living allowances.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> If the member’s partner is also a member, only the member receiving overseas living allowances receives settling in allowance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The settling in period <b>begins</b> on the first day of the member’s posting period. It <b>ends</b> on the earlier of the following days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The day when permanent accommodation becomes available at the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Six weeks after the day when the member’s posting period begins.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member has not obtained permanent accommodation within the period in subsection 2, the CDF may approve a longer period for the allowance. The CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The availability of suitable accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The action taken by the member to obtain suitable accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The efficient operation of the ADF.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Costs associated with extending the period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>Any special circumstances relating to the member or their dependants.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td>The reasonable accommodation needs of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>g.</td>
<td>Any other factor relevant to the provision of suitable accommodation to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member refuses or rejects suitable accommodation at the posting location, the eligibility to settling in allowance ceases.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 14.5.4 Settling out of posting location

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is eligible for settling out allowance for themselves and their dependants if they live in temporary accommodation before leaving the member’s posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">For the purpose of subsection 1, the period of eligibility is between the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The day permanent accommodation becomes unavailable because of the completion of the member’s posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The later of the following days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The day the member’s period of posting ends.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The day 2 weeks after the beginning of the settling out period in paragraph a.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The day specified by the CDF.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 14.5.5 Settling in/settling out allowance

| 1. | If arriving at or leaving the posting location within the periods outlined in this Division, these benefits apply. |
|---|---|

| Item | For... | the allowance for each complete day is... |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | the member and each dependant 12 years or older | two-thirds of the amount listed for meals at the member's location in Annex 13.3.A. |
| 2. | each dependant less than 12 years old | two-thirds of the amount in item 1. |

| 2. | If the accommodation tariff includes the cost of a meal, the amount of meals supplement under subsection 1 is to be reduced by the amounts in this table. |
|---|---|

| Item | For... | the allowance is to be reduced by... |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | breakfast | 25%. |
| 2. | lunch | 25%. |
| 3. | dinner | 50%. |

| 3. | On the first and last days of a period, the benefit is worked out by multiplying the amounts in subsection 1 by the applicable percentages in this table. |
|---|---|

| Item | Local time of arrival or departure | % rate for day of arrival | % rate for day of departure |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. | Before 0700 | 100 | 0 |
| 2. | 0700 – 1300 | 75 | 25 |
| 3. | 1301 – 1900 | 50 | 50 |
| 4. | After 1900 | 0 | 100 |

<table>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is not eligible for meals supplement if any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the member or dependant has meals provided or paid for.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>During the member's recreation leave, including weekends and public holidays during the leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>While the member occupies accommodation with facilities to allow the member to prepare a cooked meal.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">Paragraph 4.c does not apply to a member if the member is required to isolate themselves in response to control measures, however described, to limit the spread of COVID-19 issued by a government, or government authority in the posting location overseas.</td>
</tr>
</table>

#### Part 6: Evacuations and withdrawals from posting

##### Division 1: Evacuations

###### Subdivision 1: Evacuation benefits

###### 14.6.4 Member this subdivision applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This subdivision applies to members and their dependants, authorised by the CDF if any of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A member and dependants are directed to evacuate a posting location, because of an emergency.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A member’s dependants are given the option to voluntarily depart from the location.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 14.6.4A Member this subdivision does not apply to

|  | This subdivision does not apply to a person who is eligible to receive benefits under Chapter 14A Part 1. |
|---|---|

###### 14.6.5 Period of evacuation

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">An evacuation period begins on the day the member or their dependant is evacuated from the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">An evacuation period ends on one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">For the member — on the earlier of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The day the member returns to their posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The day the member's posting is terminated.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The day the member begins living permanently in Australia or their next posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">For their dependants — on the earlier of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The day the dependant returns to the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The day the member leaves the posting location because of termination of the member’s posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The day the dependant begins living permanently in Australia or at a location other than the posting location.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 14.6.6 Transport for evacuation

| 1. | Transport for evacuation is by the means and class of travel available at short notice. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The member is eligible for any excess baggage charges. |

###### 14.6.7 Accommodation and meals during evacuation

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">If a member or dependant is evacuated from the posting location, the member is eligible for the reimbursement of any of the following costs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s or dependant’s accommodation at the evacuation location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Settling in allowance as if the member or dependant met all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They were arriving at the evacuation location as if it were a posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii</td>
<td>They were staying in accommodation without facilities for them to prepare a cooked meal.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">If a member or dependant is evacuated to Australia, they are eligible for two-thirds of the amount as if settling in or out. This is worked out as if the member were temporarily performing duty in Canberra for less than 21 days.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 14.6.8 Conditions of service during evacuation

| 1. | During an evacuation the normal long-term posting provisions under Chapter 15 apply. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The member must continue to pay rent and utilities contributions during the evacuation period. |
| 3. | A member continues to be eligible for utilities costs during an evacuation. |

###### 14.6.9 Overseas living allowances

|  | The member is eligible for the overseas living allowances, that would have applied had they not been evacuated, during the period of evacuation. |
|---|---|

###### 14.6.10 Purchase of clothes during evacuation

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member or dependant is evacuated from the overseas posting location, the member may be reimbursed the cost of clothes and other personal items.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF must decide it is essential for the member or dependant to buy clothes or other personal items to live at the evacuation location. The CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The circumstances of the evacuation of the member or dependant.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The locations involved in the evacuation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The expected duration of the evacuation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Any other factor relevant to the evacuation.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 14.6.11 Storage during evacuation

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A member who is evacuated from their posting location is eligible for the storage of all of the following items for the period of the evacuation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The amount a member is eligible for when moving items from one residence to another at the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A private vehicle owned by the member or dependant.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 14.6.12 Health assistance

|  | A member is eligible for assistance with medical, dental and hospital costs incurred at the overseas evacuation centre payable under Chapter 15 Part 5 as if the member and dependants were still at the posting location. |
|---|---|

###### 14.6.13 Education assistance during evacuation

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member's child may be evacuated from the posting location to another overseas location. This section applies as if the member was on long-term posting to the other location, for the period of the evacuation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member’s child is evacuated to a location in Australia and the child continues to study the overseas school’s curriculum, the member continues to be eligible for any of the following benefits the member was eligible for before the evacuation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Compulsory examination fees under section 15.6.9.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Compulsory tuition fees under section 15.6.10.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Excess school transport costs under section 15.6.12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Language and communication tuition under section 15.6.13.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>Remedial tuition under section 15.6.14.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF can pay an amount considered reasonable for additional costs incurred as a result of distance education mode.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 14.6.14 Reunion visits during evacuation

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">During a period of evacuation, a member may travel from the posting location to another location for a reunion visit with dependants. In this case, the member is eligible for the reimbursement of any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Return travel by the member and dependants to the location during the period of evacuation. This is as if the travel were reunion travel under Chapter 15 Part 3 Division 3, Overseas reunion Travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Accommodation that the CDF considers suitable at the location for the period of the reunion visit. The CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The cooking and dining facilities in the accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>If the facilities are similar to those generally available in an apartment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The services provided in the accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">Under this section, the total period of reunion visits in a year must be no longer than the period of recreation leave accrued for a year’s service at the member’s posting location.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 14.6.15 Assisted leave travel during evacuation

| 1. | Chapter 16 Part 4 applies during a period of evacuation if the person remains in a hardship location. |
|---|---|
| 2. | Despite section 16.4.5 and section 16.4.6, if a member is evacuated to another hardship location, assisted leave travel is from that hardship location. |

###### Subdivision 2: Members remaining at post during an evacuation

###### 14.6.16 Definitions

|  | In this subdivision, the following apply. |
|---|---|
|  | **Evacuation order**, in relation to a posting location, has the meaning given in section 14.6.16A. |

###### 14.6.16A Evacuation order

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Evacuation order</b>, in relation to a posting location, means any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">A direction to evacuate a member’s dependants.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">An option to voluntarily evacuate a member’s dependants.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">Any of the following that would have been made in relation to the location, if there were dependants in the location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>A direction to evacuate a member’s dependants.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>An option to voluntarily evacuate a member’s dependants.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> An evacuation order is authorised under section 14.6.4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">For the purpose of paragraph 1.c, the day the order is taken to be made is the day the order would have been made if the evacuation order were to have been issued.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 14.6.16B Member this subdivision applies to

|  | This subdivision applies to a member who is posted to a posting location to which an evacuation order was issued, or would have been issued, on or after 25 February 2026 applies. |
|---|---|

###### 14.6.16C Additional (evacuations) recreation leave

| 1. | The member is eligible for additional (evacuations) recreation leave credits if they have continued to live in the posting location for 6 months from the day the evacuation order was made, or would have been made. |
|---|---|
| 2. | A member ceases to be eligible for additional (evacuations) recreation leave credits if the member’s dependants were permitted, or would have been permitted, to return to the posting location less than 6 months after the evacuation or was made. |
| 3. | If more than one evacuation order was made, or would have been made, in relation to the same incident, the day the first evacuation order is to apply. |

###### 14.6.16D Calculation of additional recreation leave

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Additional (evacuations) recreation leave credits under section 14.6.16C are calculated using the following formula.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">[image: Start formula additional open bracket evacuations close bracket recreation leave credits equals 7 minus open bracket A plus B close bracket end formula]</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>A</b></td>
<td>is the number of days of additional recreation leave credits the member accrued in connection with a non-warlike deployment in 6 months from the day this subdivision applied to the member.<br><b>Note:</b> Additional recreation leave in connection with non-warlike deployment is provided under Chapter 17 Part 7 Division 3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>B</b></td>
<td>is the number of days of war service leave credits the member accrued in 6 months from the day this subdivision applied to the member.<br><b>Note:</b> War service leave is provided under Chapter 5 Part 8.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note 1:</b> The recreation leave credits are credited to the member on the day this section applies to the member.<br><b>Note 2:</b> Recreation leave credits are managed under Chapter 5 Part 4 Division 7.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 2: Withdrawal from posting

###### 14.6.17 Losses if Defence withdraws from posting

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member and their dependants who have been directed to withdraw at short notice from a posting location overseas to return to Australia on a permanent basis.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">A withdrawal under this section does not include any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A withdrawal in connection with an evacuation under Division 1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>An early withdrawal of a member from a long‑term posting that is not a withdrawal at short notice.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is eligible for payment of an amount for their financial losses resulting from the withdrawal that the CDF is satisfied is reasonable taking all of the following into consideration.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The circumstances in which the member leaves the long-term posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The length of time given to the member to leave the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The remaining period of the expected duration of the posting at the time of leaving the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The extent to which the member entered into unavoidable financial commitments in the reasonable expectation that the posting would run its full term.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>Any other costs reasonably incurred by the member in the reasonable expectation that the posting would run its full term.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td>Any other factor relevant to the posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> Chapters 14, 15 and 16 continue to apply to a withdrawal under this section.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">For the purpose of this section, a <b>withdrawal at short notice</b> means a withdrawal from a posting location overseas that does not allow a member enough time for personal arrangements to be completed before departure in accordance with normal practice.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 3: Loss or damage to possessions overseas

###### 14.6.18 Purpose

|  | The purpose of this Division is to provide an amount for any lost or damaged possessions during an overseas posting. This is only if the loss or damage is directly caused by a specified event. |
|---|---|

###### 14.6.19 Member this Division applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Division applies to all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A member (including a member on Reserve service) on a long-term posting overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Dependants living with the member overseas.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 14.6.20 Definition – possessions

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">For this Division, possessions means any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Items approved for removal to an overseas posting location under this Determination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Items approved for removal to another residence at the overseas posting, or back to Australia, under this Determination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Food, beverages and other household consumable goods.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Private vehicles.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> Loss or damage to a member's clothing or effects used for service is provided under Chapter 10 Part 4.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 14.6.21 General conditions

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">Members are eligible for help if their possessions are lost or damaged as a result of any of the following specified events.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">War.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Civil disorder.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">Natural disaster.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">Another similar event.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">All of the following must apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member meets any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member fully insured the possessions, but was unsuccessful claiming from the insurer despite reasonable attempts.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member was unable to obtain appropriate insurance at a reasonable cost to cover the possessions in the circumstances in which they were lost or damaged.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member took reasonable steps to avoid the loss or damage.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member assigns to the Commonwealth the right to recover the loss or damage from an insurer or another person. The member also takes all necessary steps to help the Commonwealth with its claim.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member is eligible for an amount the CDF considers reasonable in the circumstances. In assessing the amount, the CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The nature and extent of the possessions lost or damaged.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The amount that an insurer would pay to the member for loss or damage.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">Any professional valuation of the loss or damage.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">The estimated residual value of the possessions. This must take into account the:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>initial cost, and</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>estimated amount of depreciation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td colspan="2">Any other factor relevant to the loss or damage.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="3">The payment must be reduced if all of the following are met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member has not insured the possessions, or has underinsured them.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF considers that it would have been reasonable to fully insure them against the event that caused the loss or damage.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6.</td>
<td colspan="3">The amount must be reduced by the amount the member could reasonably expect to have been paid by an insurer, if the goods had been adequately covered.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 14.6.22 Loss or damage – private vehicles

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for one of the following amounts if their private vehicle is lost or damaged as a result of an event specified in subsection 14.6.21.1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If their private vehicle is lost — the estimated residual value of the vehicle immediately before the loss occurred.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If their private vehicle is damaged — the difference between estimated residual values, both before and after the damage.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">This is how to work out the estimated residual value of the member’s vehicle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Find out how much the member paid to buy the vehicle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Subtract an amount of depreciation the CDF assesses as reasonable in the circumstances.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">When assessing the amount of depreciation, the CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The criteria set out in subsection 14.6.21.4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The type and cost of the vehicle bought by the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The age of the vehicle when bought, and the period the member owned the vehicle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The rate of depreciation that would usually occur on a similar vehicle at the member's posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>The estimated cost of repairing any defects to the vehicle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td>The insured value of the vehicle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>g.</td>
<td>Any other factor relevant to the member's ownership of the vehicle.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 14.6.23 CDF decision on loss

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF can direct that a member's possessions are presumed lost on a specific date.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The circumstances in which the member ended or interrupted a long-term posting and left the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The nature of the possessions abandoned by the member at the location, and their condition and value at that time.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The likelihood that the member may be able to recover the possessions in a reasonable condition for use.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The likelihood of the member resuming the posting or returning to the location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>Any other factor relevant to the member's loss of possessions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF is not to give the direction in subsection 1 unless the member assigns the possessions to the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
</table>

### Chapter 14A: COVID-19 response

#### Part 1: COVID 19 evacuations

##### Division 1A: General provisions

###### 14A.1.1 Purpose

|  | This Part provides benefits to a member and their dependant who are in an overseas location for work and are evacuated, or have a dependant evacuated, from that location on a voluntary or involuntary basis because of COVID-19. |
|---|---|

###### 14A.1.2 Definitions

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">In this Part the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Evacuation period</b> means the period commencing on the day a person arrives in Australia on a flight provided under section 14A.1.4 and ending on the earlier of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The day the person leaves Australia on a flight provided under section 14A.1.5.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the person is a member, the day a member’s long-term posting overseas or short-term duty overseas ends.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the person is a dependant, the earlier of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The day the long-term posting overseas or short-term duty overseas of the member in relation to whom they have been recognised as a dependant ends.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The day the dependant advises they are not going to return to the posting location or place of duty of the member in relation to whom they have been recognised as a dependant.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the person is a dependant who is a minor, the day the member advises the person is not going to return to the posting location or place of duty of the member in relation to whom they have been recognised as a dependant.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td colspan="2">A day set by the Director of Attaché and Overseas Management.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Permitted to evacuate</b> means evacuation on a voluntary basis.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Required to evacuate</b> means evacuation on an involuntary basis.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Senior ADF representative</b> means the most senior Defence Force member at a posting location.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 1: Evacuation flights

###### 14A.1.3 Person this Division applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Division applies to any of the following persons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A member on short-term duty overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A member on a long-term posting overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>A dependant who accompanied a member specified in paragraph a or b.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 14A.1.4 Evacuation flights

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subject to subsection 3, a person is eligible for an economy class flight from their location to one of the following if the CDF requires or permits them to evacuate.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the member is evacuated – the airport nearest the location where the member will work.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the member is evacuated at the same time as their dependants – the airport nearest the location where the member will work.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>In all other cases, the capital city nearest to the location where they will live.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note 1:</b> If more than one dependant from the same family group are evacuated at the same time, the location under paragraph b must be the same location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note 2:</b> Flights include domestic flights that may not be connected with an international flight.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1A.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subsection 1 also applies to a person who was evacuated on or after 27 March 2020 as though it were in force at that time.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">If more than one person in the same family group are evacuated at the same time and all of the following conditions apply, flights to the final destination may be broken once they have returned to Australia and completed an isolation period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>All persons in the family group are required to isolate themselves.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The final destination of the member and the dependants are different.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a person is required to evacuate and no reasonable economy class flights are available before the end of the period in which the person must have evacuated the location, the person is eligible for flights in the next higher class available.<br><b>Note:</b> Only economy class flights are available to people who evacuate to a location on a voluntary basis.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 14A.1.5 End of evacuation flights

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">Subject to subsection 3, any of the following persons is eligible for an economy class flight from their nearest capital city in Australia to their posting location overseas or location of short-term duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">A person who received an evacuation flight under section 14A.1.4.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>

#### Part 2A: Overseas living allowances

##### Division 1: General provisions

###### 15.2A.1 Simplified outline of Part 2A

Overseas living allowances offset the likely effects of a long‑term posting overseas on members and their dependants living with them at the posting location. These allowances assist the member in meeting unexpected living costs associated with the posting and the added costs at the posting location. Meal allowance and clothing allowance may be provided in limited circumstances.

Overseas living allowances consist of the following:

 Cost of living adjustment, which helps maintain the purchasing power of the member’s income and provide an equivalent standard of living at the posting location overseas. The allowance has the effect of adjusting the member’s salary by the post index rate that applies to their posting location (see Division 2).

 Cost of posting allowance, which compensates a member for financial and non-financial disadvantage due to the overseas posting. The allowance is based on a percentage of the member’s salary and is subject to lower and upper limits (see Division 3).

 Child supplement allowance, which assists a member with the additional costs inherent in maintaining a child by providing the member an allowance for each child living with a member in the posting location overseas. The base rate of allowance is a fixed amount relevant to the child’s age, which is modified by the post index rate of the posting location (see Division 4).

The overseas living allowances may be affected by the location and period of the member’s posting overseas, and the member’s categorisation. The absence of the member or their family from the posting location also affects the payment of overseas living allowances (see Division 5).

Meal allowances may be provided to a member who performs additional duty on a day (see section 15.2A.27) or for the costs of meals when they are in living-in accommodation (see section 15.2A.28).

An allowance for the cost of special garments is also available if the member is required to purchase additional garments due to dress codes imposed by religious custom or law at the posting location (see section 15.2A.29).

###### 15.2A.8 Effect of non-Commonwealth allowances on the overseas living allowances

| 1. | This section applies if a member receives a benefit from another entity for a similar or comparable purpose to that of a benefit provided by this Part. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The comparable benefit paid under this Part is reduced by the amount of the benefit received. |

###### 15.2A.9 The dual Commonwealth benefit rule

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member if all of the following apply to their partner.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member’s partner is posted to or resides in the same location as the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member’s partner is eligible for a benefit from the Commonwealth that is for the same or a comparable purpose to the benefits provided under this Part.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2</td>
<td colspan="2">The member ceases to be eligible for a benefit under this Part if the member’s partner has a higher salary than the member and has been nominated to receive the comparable benefit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3</td>
<td colspan="2">If subsection 2 applies, and the member receives a benefit under this Part, the member must repay the amount received.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 2: Cost of living adjustment

###### 15.2A.11 Eligibility – cost of living adjustment

| 1. | A member is eligible for a cost of living adjustment for the period of their overseas posting if their post index is more than 100. |
|---|---|
| 2. | A member is not eligible for cost of living adjustment if they are on leave without pay. |
|  | **Note 1:** Section 15.2A.8 may affect the payment of cost of living adjustment.<br>**Note 2:** Section 15.2A.25 may extend the period of eligibility if the member’s dependants remain at the posting location after the member permanently leaves at the end of the posting period. |

###### 15.2A.12 Rate of cost of living adjustment

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">The cost of living adjustment is calculated using the following formula.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">[image: cost of living adjustment equals start formula open bracet open bracket A minus B close bracket times C close bracket times open bracket start fraction D minus 100 over 100 end fraction close bracket end formula.]</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">Where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>A</b></td>
<td colspan="2">is the member's fortnightly salary plus any of the following payable to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Higher duties allowance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A salary non-reduction supplement provided under section 3.2.56.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> No other allowances are to be included.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>B</b></td>
<td colspan="2">is the Pay As You Go tax and any levies withheld from the fortnightly salary calculated under A.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>C</b></td>
<td colspan="2">is the spendable salary factor determined by a data service provider.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

<td colspan="2">is the post index for the member's posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> The dual Commonwealth benefit rule under section 15.2A.9 does not apply to the cost of living adjustment. A member will receive this adjustment even if their partner also receives the adjustment or comparable benefit.</td>

#### Part 3: Travel during a long-term posting

##### Division 1A: General provisions

###### 15.3.1 Purpose

|  | The purpose of this Part is to authorise travel benefits during a long-term posting. |
|---|---|

###### 15.3.2 Member this Part applies to

|  | This Part applies to a member who is on a long-term posting overseas and is required to travel while on the posting. It also applies to the member's dependants, who need to travel in special circumstances. |
|---|---|

##### Division 1: Travel for short-term duty while on long-term posting

###### 15.3.4 Travel for short-term duty while on long-term posting

|  | This Division applies to a member who is on a long-term posting overseas and is required to undertake short-term duty to travel between or within overseas countries. |
|---|---|

###### 15.3.4A Member this Division does not apply to

|  | This Division does not apply to a member who is undertaking service with the United Nations under Chapter 12 Part 4. |
|---|---|

###### 15.3.4B Benefits while on short-term duty

|  | A member on short-term duty while on a long-term posting overseas is eligible for benefits provided under Chapter 13. |
|---|---|

###### 15.3.5 Travel by private vehicle

| 1. | A member may choose to travel for duty by private vehicle. In this case, the member is eligible for vehicle allowance and payment of travel costs. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The benefit must not be more than if the member had travelled by the normal means. |
| 3. | The member is not eligible for the costs of transporting a private vehicle. |

##### Division 2: Excess commuting costs

###### 15.3.6 Purpose

|  | The purpose of this Division is to help with extra commuting costs. This is when the member is travelling to and from their home at the overseas posting location, to their place of duty.<br>**Note:** The member’s home should be located within a reasonable distance of the work location. The member is eligible for payment only for travel by the most direct practical route. |
|---|---|

###### 15.3.7 Public transport

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible to be reimbursed the excess costs of public transport if they meet all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They use public transport to travel between their home and their normal place of duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Their public transport costs exceed AUD 1,452.66 within a benefit period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Excess costs of public transport are calculated using the following formula.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">[image: Start formula excess costs of public transport equals open bracket A times B close bracket minus open bracket start fraction C over 213 end fraction times 1,452.66 close bracket end formula]</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>A</b></td>
<td>is the member's public transport costs at the location in local currency.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>B</b></td>
<td>is the exchange rate provided by the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade for the payday before the benefit period.<br><b>Note:</b> This is used to convert the local currency in which the member incurred the public transport costs into Australian dollars.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>C</b></td>
<td>is the number of days the member worked in the overseas location during the benefit period, not exceeding 213 days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> If the outcome is zero or less, the amount payable for excess costs of public transport is AUD 0.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">In this section, the following definition applies.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Benefit period</b> means a 12-month period commencing on 1 March of the relevant year.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.3.8 Private vehicle

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible to be reimbursed excess commuting costs if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member uses a private vehicle for the purpose of travel between their home and their primary place of duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member has been directed to live 30km or more away from their primary place of duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The purpose of travel under paragraph 1.a includes any routine stops that the member could be expected to make on their way to or from their primary place of duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is not eligible to be reimbursed for travel that meets any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>It is not between the member’s home and their primary place of duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>It is more than one trip between the member’s home and their primary place of duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">Excess commuting costs are calculated using the following formula.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">[image: Start formula excess commuting costs equals A times open bracket B minus 60 close bracket end formula]</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>A</b></td>
<td>is the applicable rate of vehicle allowance payable under subsection 15.3.21.4 on 1 March in that year.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>B</b></td>
<td>is the daily return distance by the most direct route between the member’s home and their primary place of duty, in kilometres.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.3.9 Use of public transport and private vehicle combined

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible to be reimbursed excess commuting costs if they travel to their normal place of duty using both public transport and their private vehicle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The amount the member is eligible to be reimbursed each month under subsection 1 is calculated using the following formula.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">[image: start formula excess costs equals open bracket A time B close bracket time 20 plus C minus open bracket D over 12 close bracket end formula]</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>A</b></td>

</tr>

</tr>
<tr>

##### Division 3: Overseas reunion travel

###### Subdivision 1: General provisions

###### 15.3.10 Simplified outline of this Division

When a member is posted to an overseas location all or some of their family may not travel with them to the location. The benefits provided in this Division help a member on a long-term posting overseas to maintain contact with their family by providing help with the cost of travel between the overseas location and where the family lives.

The benefits a member may receive for a reunion travel benefit are provided in Subdivision 2 and can include return flights and public transport for the people who are travelling. If there is an unavoidable stop during the reunion travel, the person travelling may also receive accommodation and costs for meals.

If a member does not have a partner or children they may be eligible to reunion travel under Subdivision 3 to help them maintain relationships with their family, friends and support networks in Australia.

If a member has a partner and children, the member and their family may be eligible to reunion travel under Subdivision 4 to help them maintain their relationships. The number of reunion travel benefits a member may be eligible for is based on their family makeup and where they live.

A member’s partner or child who lives with the member at the overseas location, or a child who attends boarding school in Australia, may use a reunion travel benefit to visit another person in Australia under Subdivision 5.

If a member’s child is travelling by themselves to visit the member, they may need to be accompanied by an adult. Travel costs for the chaperone are set out in Subdivision 6.

###### 15.3.11 Definitions

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">In this Division, the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Allowable travel costs for a chaperone</b> means one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the dependent child is travelling to the member's posting location — all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Allowable travel costs from the posting location to meet the dependent child at the international airport where the child can no longer travel unaccompanied.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Allowable travel costs from the international airport to chaperone the dependent child to the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the dependent child is travelling to return home — all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Allowable travel costs from the posting location to chaperone the dependent child to the international airport from where the child will travel home unaccompanied.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Allowable travel costs from the international airport back to the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Chaperone</b>, for the purpose of accompanying a dependent child, means a person over 18 years old who is one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">A person chosen by the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Dependent child</b> means a child who meets one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the child is living in Australia — they meet all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They are a child, as defined in section 1.3.35.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They are under 18 years of age.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the child is living at the member’s overseas location — they are a dependant under subsection 12.3.5.1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the child is living at another overseas location — they are a dependant of a person who is a recognised partner subsection 15.3.13.2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Dependent tertiary student</b> has the same meaning given by section 15.3.12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Eligible person</b> means any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">A dependent child.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">A dependent tertiary student.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">A recognised partner.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Recognised partner</b> has the same meaning given by section 15.3.13.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Reunion year</b> means the 12-month period commencing on the first day of the member’s long-term posting at the overseas location.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.3.12 Dependent tertiary student

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Dependent tertiary student</b> means a person who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are less than 25 years of age.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">They meet one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>For a tertiary student studying in another overseas location — a person who meets the criteria under subsection 2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>For a tertiary student studying in Australia — they are an adult child or they are recognised family under section 1.3.1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are undertaking full-time studies at a tertiary institution.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are living away from the member because of the member’s long-term posting overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">For the purpose of subparagraph 1.b.i, a person may be recognised as a dependent tertiary student if the CDF is satisfied that the person meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The person would live with the member at the member’s posting location but is unable to because a dependant is not permitted at the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The person is studying in another overseas location to be located closer to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">Immediately before the long-term posting overseas, the person was living with the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">The person has a level of dependency on the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> If a member has a person recognised as a dependent tertiary student under this subsection, the member is only eligible for reunion travel benefits for that person. No other overseas benefits will apply for that person.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.3.13 Recognised partner

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Recognised partner</b> means a person who is a recognised partner under one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the person is living in Australia — section 1.3.36.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the person is living at the member’s overseas posting location — subsection 12.3.5.1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>If the person is living in another overseas location — subsection 2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> Section 15.3.15 applies to a dual serving couple and identifies which member is eligible for the reunion travel benefits. The member who is not eligible for the benefits may be a recognised partner under paragraph 1.b or 1.c.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">For the purpose of paragraph 1.c, a person may be a recognised partner if they meet all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are the partner of a member who is eligible for the reunion travel benefits under this Division.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The person would be a dependant under subsection 12.3.5.1 if they lived with the member in the member’s posting location.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.3.14 Taking a reunion travel benefit

| 1. | A member must apply to use a reunion travel benefit for themself or an eligible person using the approved form. |
|---|---|
| 2. | If more than one eligible person travel at the same time, one reunion travel benefit under section 15.3.17G is used. |
| 3. | If the member is travelling on a reunion travel benefit they must be on a type of leave or absence for the period of the reunion travel. |
| 4. | A reunion travel benefit can be taken by the member or an eligible person. |
| 5. | A member must not take a reunion travel benefit within 3 months of the start or end of their posting period overseas unless the CDF is satisfied it is reasonable. |

###### 15.3.15 Dual serving couple

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">If a member is a part of a dual serving couple and both members are on a long-term posting overseas, only the following member is eligible for the number of reunion travel benefits under section 15.3.17G.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member who has been nominated by both members to receive the benefit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If a member has not been nominated, the member with the higher salary.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note 1:</b> Although only one member is eligible for the reunion travel benefits, both members can use the reunion travel benefits.<br><b>Note 2:</b> The members can be at the same posting location overseas or at another posting location overseas.<br><b>Note 3:</b> The member who is not eligible for the reunion travel benefits under this section is a recognised partner under section 15.3.13.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### Subdivision 2: Reunion travel benefit

###### 15.3.16 Reunion travel benefit

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">A reunion travel benefit includes any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Return air travel that meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>It is at economy class.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>It meets the allowable travel cost as provided under section 12.3.3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Return rail travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">Return coach travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> The member is not eligible for accommodation, meal or incidental costs during reunion travel.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.3.17 Reunion travel benefit to another overseas location

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies to a member who has an eligible person who meets any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The eligible person lives in another overseas location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The eligible person lives in Australia and is unable to travel to the posting location because the eligible person is not permitted at the posting location by Defence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member is eligible for any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the eligible person is travelling — one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>A reunion travel benefit between the location under paragraph 1.a and the member’s posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>A reunion travel benefit between Australia and a location in another overseas country where they will reunite with the member.<br><b>Note:</b> Only the allowable travel costs for the eligible person to the other overseas country will be covered.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> Travel under this paragraph cannot be to an overseas posting location where eligible persons are not permitted by Defence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is traveling — a reunion travel benefit between their overseas posting location and a location in another country to reunite with the eligible person.<br><b>Note:</b> Only the allowable travel costs for the member to travel to the other country location will be covered.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">If both the member and the eligible person are travelling — a reunion travel benefit for the eligible person between their location and a location in another country where they will reunite with the member.<br><b>Note:</b> Only the allowable travel costs for the eligible person to the other overseas country will be covered. The travel undertaken by the member will be at their own cost.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> To avoid doubt, a reunion travel benefit taken under this section reduces the number of reunion travel benefits a member is eligible for under section 15.3.17G.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">The cost of a return reunion travel benefit provided under this section is the lesser of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The allowable travel cost if the travel was between the member’s posting location and Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The actual cost of the travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">If the actual cost of travel is higher than cost under subsection 3, the member must pay any additional costs.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.3.17A Reimbursement

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">If travel under this Division is booked by the member, the benefit is provided by reimbursement up the lesser of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The allowable travel cost of return travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The cost of the return travel expenses incurred by the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> If the actual cost of return travel is higher than the allowable cost of return travel, the member is not eligible to be reimbursed any amount above the allowable travel cost.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.3.17B Public transport costs

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">The member is eligible for the reimbursement of public transport costs for themself or an eligible person, including costs for taxis and like services, between any of the following locations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member’s home in their posting location overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The airport, bus or train terminal.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>If the member has an eligible person, the eligible person’s home.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>If the member does not have any eligible persons, the accommodation where the member is staying in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> This does not include vehicle allowance for driving, the cost of a hire car, the cost of parking a vehicle or chauffeur services.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.3.17C Unavoidable stopover

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies if the travel under section 15.3.16 is broken into 2 or more consecutive segments and all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The break between 2 segments requires an overnight stay in the stopover location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF is satisfied that the stopover is unavoidable.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member is eligible for the following for each unavoidable stopover.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">One nights accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subject to subsection 3, both of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The cost of meals for each person travelling up to the amount specified for the member’s rank and the location of the stopover under Annex 13.3.A, as adjusted by section 13.3.9.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The amount for incidentals for each person travelling up to the amount for the member’s rank and the location of the stopover under Annex 13.3.A, as adjusted by section 13.3.10.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">If a dependent child is travelling and they are less than 12 years old, the amount for meals and incidentals is two-thirds of the amount payable under paragraph 2.b.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### Subdivision 3: Reunion travel for a member with no eligible persons

###### 15.3.17D Member this Subdivision applies to

|  | This Subdivision applies to a member on a long-term posting overseas who has no eligible persons. |
|---|---|

###### 15.3.17E Eligibility for reunion travel benefits

|  | A member is eligible for one reunion travel benefit to Australia during their posting period overseas. |
|---|---|

###### Subdivision 4: Reunion travel for a member with eligible persons

###### 15.3.17F Member this Subdivision applies to

|  | This Subdivision applies to a member on a long-term posting overseas who has eligible persons. |
|---|---|

###### 15.3.17G Eligibility for reunion travel benefits

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is eligible for any of the following number of reunion travel benefits in a reunion year.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If all of the following apply — 4 reunion travel benefits.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member and their recognised partner are at the posting location overseas.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member has a dependent child living in Australia or another overseas location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The member receives education assistance under Part 6 Division 3 or Division 4 for the dependent child.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If all of the following apply — 4 reunion travel benefits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member does not have a recognised partner.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member has a dependent child living in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The member receives education assistance under Part 6 Division 4 for their dependent child.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">If one of the following applies — 2 reunion travel benefits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member has a recognised partner living in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member has a recognised partner who lives in another location overseas.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>

<td>The member has a recognised partner and a dependent child living in Australia.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>

<td></td>

<td></td>

<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member who has used all of their reunion travel benefits in a reunion year under paragraph 1.c or 1.d, the member is eligible for one of the following if the CDF is satisfied it is reasonable.</td>

<td></td>

<td></td>

<td colspan="2">Any other opportunity to reunite with the eligible person.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>

###### Subdivision 5: Reunion visit for an eligible person with other persons

###### 15.3.17H Reunion visit with a person who is not an eligible person

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>

<td>a.</td>
<td>The recognised partner or dependent child lives at the member’s posting location overseas.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The person who is not an eligible person lives in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The CDF is satisfied that it is reasonable for the reunion travel benefit to be used by the recognised partner or a dependent child to visit the person who is not an eligible person.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">When making a decision made under paragraph 1.c, the CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>

<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The relationship of the people.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The degree to which the relationship has been maintained before and during the member's long‑term posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The extent of financial or other dependency of the people.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

<td>The circumstances relating to the recognised partner’s or dependent child’s removal to the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>Any other opportunities that the people may have to be reunited.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td>The age and welfare of the people.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>g.</td>
<td>The circumstances relating to the travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>h.</td>
<td>The duration of the travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Any other factor relevant the travel by the recognised partner or dependent child.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> A reunion travel benefit taken under this section is counted as one of the benefits a member is eligible for under section 15.3.17G.</td>
</tr>

###### 15.3.17J Reunion visit for a dependent child in boarding school in Australia

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies to a member who is eligible for a reunion travel benefit under section 15.3.17G for a dependent child if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The dependent child is attending a boarding school in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The dependant does not travel to the member’s posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The person the dependent child is visiting meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They have been approved by the member for the dependent child to visit them.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They live in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member is eligible for the reasonable costs of one the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Return door-to-door travel for the dependent child from the boarding school they are attending to a home in Australia of a person approved by the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Return door-to-door travel for the person approved by the member to accompany the dependent child in the following circumstances.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>To meet the dependent child at the boarding school and to accompany then to the person’s home in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>To accompany the dependent child to the boarding school and to return to the person’s home in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">If travel provided under this section is by air, the travel is to be economy class travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> A reunion travel benefit taken under this section is counted as one of benefits a member is eligible for under section 15.3.17G.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### Subdivision 6: Chaperone to accompany a dependent child

###### 15.3.17K Member this Subdivision applies to

|  | This Subdivision applies to a member on long-term posting overseas who has a dependent child who requires a chaperone to accompany them when travelling for a reunion visit. |
|---|---|

###### 15.3.17L Cost of a chaperone to accompany a dependent child – USA or Canada

<table>
<tr>

<td colspan="2">The member is on a long-term overseas posting in the USA or Canada.</td>

<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is eligible for a reunion visit for a dependent child who is less than 15 years old.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The dependent child is not being accompanied by an adult.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">The airlines will not ensure the dependent child's safe transfer between the international flight to or from Australia and one of the following unavoidable flights.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>A domestic flight within the USA or Canada.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>An international flight between the USA and Canada.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> The chaperone may accompany more than one child at a time.</td>
</tr>

<table>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is on a long-term overseas posting to the Marshall Islands.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is eligible for a reunion visit for a dependent child who is less than 18 years old.</td>

##### Division 4: Vehicle allowances

###### 15.3.18 Purpose

|  | The purpose of vehicle allowance is to help the member pay for vehicle costs in certain cases. |
|---|---|

###### 15.3.19 Member this Division applies to

|  | This Division applies to a member who is authorised to travel by private vehicle. |
|---|---|

###### 15.3.20 Member this Division does not apply to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Division does not apply to any of these members.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A member on short-term duty, authorised to travel by motor vehicle instead of the eligible type of transport.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A member wanting to transport their private vehicle to or from a posting location.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.3.21 Vehicle allowance

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is eligible for vehicle allowance, if the CDF approves their use of a private vehicle for official purposes. The vehicle may be owned, hired or borrowed by the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Travel between the member's home and normal place of duty is not to be included in any journey authorised under this section.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">When considering whether to authorise use of a private vehicle, the CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The purpose of the travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the use of the vehicle will result in greater efficiency than use of public transport.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>If Commonwealth transport is available for the journey.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>If there is any requirement for a Commonwealth driver to remain on duty outside normal hours.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>If the member has provided evidence of adequate insurance cover.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td>Any cost saving to the Commonwealth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>g.</td>
<td>The personal interests of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is eligible for an amount for each kilometre of the journey. This amount is calculated using the following formula with the rates that apply to the posting location:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">[image: Start formula vehicle allowance per km open bracket in local currency close bracket equals A times B times open bracket start fraction C over 100 end fraction close bracket end formula]</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>A</b></td>
<td>is the relevant rate of vehicle allowance under section 9.6.25, effective at the time of travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>B</b></td>
<td>is the exchange rate used to pay salary to members for the pay period in which the travel is approved.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>C</b></td>
<td>is the post index under section 12.3.14A used to calculate overseas allowances for the pay period in which the travel is approved.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">The kilometres travelled are taken to be the distance of the journey, using the shortest direct route on suitable roads.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6.</td>
<td colspan="2">The combined upper limit of the vehicle allowance and travel costs for the road trip is the total of the following amounts.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The cost of the member's fares by the means of transport normally authorised by the CDF for the journey.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The amount of travel costs payable if the journey was by that means of transport.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>7.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member eligible for vehicle allowance may also be reimbursed any of the following costs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Ferries.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Tolls.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Garage accommodation.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.3.22 Personal property tax on vehicle – USA

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

##### Division 5: Vehicle contribution

###### 15.3.23 Purpose

|  | The purpose of this Division is to authorise member contributions for the use of an official vehicle at a posting location. |

###### 15.3.25 Hire of official vehicle for casual short-term private use

<table>
<tr>

<td colspan="2">If the CDF allows a member to hire an official vehicle, the member must pay an amount worked out under Division 4 section 15.3.21. The member must pay for each kilometre the vehicle travelled, during the hire period.</td>

<td>2.</td>

<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subsection 2 does not apply to the member if the CDF believes it is essential for the member or dependant to be given a car with a driver. Approval may only be given if one of the following applies.</td>

<td>a.</td>

<td></td>
<td>b.</td>

<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member must pay the amount worked out using this formula.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">[image: Start formula A times 8000 times start fraction B over 365 end fraction end formula]</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td rowspan="2"></td>
