##### Division 6: Travel for compassionate reasons

###### 15.3.30 Purpose

|  | Travel for compassionate reasons helps a member, their partner or close relative with the costs of travel in the event of serious or very serious illness, or death. |
|---|---|

###### 15.3.32 Payment of benefits under this Division

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A benefit provided under this division may be paid to any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Directly to the service provider or their agent.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>By way of reimbursement to the person who incurred the cost.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.3.33 Close relative to visit a person overseas with a serious or very serious illness

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies if all of the following are met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member’s partner is accompanying the member on a long-term posting overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A doctor has certified that a member's partner has a serious illness or very serious illness.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The member’s partner continues to have the serious illness or very serious illness.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">A close relative is eligible for the cost of travel from their home to the location of the person who has a serious illness or very serious illness if the CDF is satisfied it is reasonable having considered all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Any views of the member’s partner or the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Any views of the member’s partner's personal legal representative, if relevant.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Any other factor relevant to the visit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2A.</td>
<td colspan="2">To avoid doubt, only one close relative is eligible for travel benefits under this section.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The cost of travel in subsection 2 is the lesser of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The allowable travel cost for the travel to the member’s posting location and return.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The cost of the fares paid for the travel.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.3.35 Member or partner to visit a close relative

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies to a member and the member's partner if any of the following apply to a close relative.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">All of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>A doctor has certified that the close relative has a serious illness or very serious illness.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The close relative continues to have a serious illness or very serious illness.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The close relative dies.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">All of the following people are eligible for the cost of travel from the posting location to the location of the close relative, or if they have deceased, the location of the funeral of the close relative, if the CDF is satisfied it is reasonable in the circumstances.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member who is on a long-term posting overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member's partner who is accompanying the member on a long-term posting overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">For the purpose of subsection 2, if more than one trip is to be approved to visit a close relative for the same serious or very serious illness, the CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The number of trips that have been provided under this section.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The relationship of the member or the member's partner to the close relative.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The reasons for the request.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">The cost of travel in subsection 2 is one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the travel is to a location within Australia, the lesser of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The allowable travel cost for the travel from the posting location to the close relative's home, or the location of the funeral and return.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The cost of the fares paid for the travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the travel is to a location outside of Australia, the lesser of the following amounts, but not less than $0.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The cost of the fares paid for the travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The cost of the travel calculated using the following formula.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">[image: Start formula cost of travel equals A minus B end formula]</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td><b>A</b></td>
<td>is the allowable travel cost from the overseas posting location to the overseas location of the close relative and return.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td><b>B</b></td>
<td>is the allowable travel cost from Sydney, Australia to the overseas location of the close relative and return.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.3.36 Fares for children

<table>

##### Division 7: Additional travel for extended or consecutive overseas postings

###### Subdivision 1: General provisions

###### 15.3.37 Purpose

|  | This Division provides a member and their dependant an additional travel benefit to provide respite from the overseas location and to reconnect with family and friends in Australia when a member's long-term posting overseas is extended or the member is posted for a consecutive long‑term posting overseas. |
|---|---|

###### 15.3.39 When travel under this Division must be taken

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">Travel under this Division must be taken within the following periods.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If Subdivision 2 applies — between the following days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The day that is 3 months before the day that the member’s current long-term posting overseas is expected to end.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The day that is 3 months after the day that the member’s extended posting period overseas or consecutive posting period overseas starts.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If Subdivision 3 applies — between the following days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The day the member’s posting period overseas ends at their current posting location.<br><b>Note:</b> To avoid doubt, only for the purposes of the additional travel benefit, the member or their dependant must not remain at the current posting location after the day the member’s posting period overseas ends. If section 14.4.17 applies to the dependant, they may remain at the overseas posting location, but would not be eligible for any other benefit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The day before the member’s posting period overseas starts at their next posting location.<br><b>Note:</b> To avoid doubt, the member or their dependant must not arrive at the next posting location before the member’s posting period overseas starts.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note 1:</b> Section 12.3.16 provides the definition of posting period overseas.<br><b>Note 2:</b> The member must be on leave for any period of absence from duty.<br><b>Note 3:</b> A member’s dependant may travel separately to the member on any leg of a journey.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">Any of the following persons may travel outside of the period specified in subsection 1 if the CDF is satisfied that it is reasonable.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If Subdivision 2 applies — the member and their dependant, travelling either together or separately.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If Subdivision 3 applies — the member and their dependant, if the travel meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The travel occurs on or before the day set by subparagraph 1.b.i.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The travel occurs on or after the day set by subparagraph 1.b.ii.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> This subsection does not apply to a dependant who is travelling separately to the member under section 14.4.17.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">For the purpose of subsection 2, the CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The reason the travel could not occur during the specified period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The welfare of the member and the dependant.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s work commitments over the next 6 months.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">The travel’s potential costs or savings to Defence.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.3.40 Reimbursement

|  | If travel under this Division is booked by the member, the benefit is provided by reimbursement. |
|---|---|

###### Subdivision 2: Additional travel if posted to same overseas location

###### 15.3.41 Member this subdivision applies to

|  | This Subdivision applies to a member on a long-term posting overseas who is required to remain in the same posting location for an additional 12 months or more.<br>**Note:** This may be due to an extension of their current posting, or a consecutive posting to the same location. |
|---|---|

###### 15.3.42 Travel benefits

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member is eligible for the allowable travel costs for all of the following for themself and their dependant.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Economy class travel from one of the following locations to a location in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member’s posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>If the CDF is satisfied that the travel is within the whole‑of‑Australian‑Government international best fare policy — any other overseas location.<br><b>Note 1:</b> Approval must be obtained before booking travel under this subparagraph.<br><b>Note 2:</b> The member is only eligible for the cost of travel up to the amount which would have been paid had the travel been from the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Economy class travel from a location in Australia to the member’s posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> The member is only eligible for the cost of travel up to the amount which would have been paid had the travel been from the posting location to the initial destination in Australia and return.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">If the member’s posting location is a hardship location, they are eligible for the excess baggage benefit under section 16.4.7.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### Subdivision 3: Additional travel if posted to different overseas location

###### 15.3.43 Member this subdivision applies to

|  | This Subdivision applies to a member on long‑term posting overseas who is posted for a consecutive posting for 12 months or more to a different overseas posting location. |
|---|---|

###### 15.3.44 Travel benefits

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member is eligible for the travel costs for all of the following for themself and their dependant.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Business class travel from one of the following locations to a location in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member’s posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>If the CDF is satisfied that the travel is within the whole‑of‑Australian‑Government international best fare policy — any other overseas location.<br><b>Note 1:</b> Approval must be obtained before booking travel under this subparagraph.<br><b>Note 2:</b> The member is only eligible for the cost of travel up to the amount which would have been paid had the travel been from the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Business class travel from a location in Australia to the member’s next posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> The member is only eligible for the cost of travel up to the amount which would have been paid had the travel been from the location they travelled to under paragraph a.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member who is travelling under this Subdivision is eligible for all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Excess baggage under section 14.4.11.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">For travel under paragraph 1.b — rest periods under Chapter 14 Part 4 Division 3.</td>
</tr>
</table>

#### Part 4: Housing

##### Division 1A: General provisions

###### 15.4.1 Purpose

|  | This Part sets out housing and utilities benefits for a member on a long-term overseas posting. |
|---|---|

###### 15.4.2 Member this Part applies to

|  | This Part applies to a member who is eligible for the overseas living allowances and who lives out. |
|---|---|

###### 15.4.3 Member this Part does not apply to

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This Part does not apply to a member while they meet any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">All of the following circumstances apply to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member is able to live in their own or their dependant’s home at the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The CDF is satisfied that the home is of a suitable standard for the member's rank and duties at the location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member's accommodation is paid for by a body other than the Commonwealth, as represented by the Department of Defence.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 1: Housing

###### 15.4.5 Purpose

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Division sets out the aim of housing assistance and general housing benefits for a member on a long-term posting overseas. The aim is to ensure the member and their dependants are provided with housing that meets all these conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Adequately furnished, based on the needs of the member's dependants.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Located within a reasonable distance of the place of duty.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Appropriate for the status and duties of the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Suitable in size based on the composition of the member's family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>Suitable for the conditions at the member's posting location.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.4.6 Housing benefits

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section does not apply to a member who meets any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are a senior member who is provided a house in connection with their posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are posted to a hardship location.<br><b>Note:</b> A hardship location is a location listed in Annex 16.B column A or a provisional hardship location as defined in section 16.1.3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>They are on an exchange posting and required to occupy housing provided by the host Service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is eligible for the cost of rent of privately arranged housing if the CDF considers it suitable having regard to all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member's posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The standard of housing at the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The location of the housing.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The standard and the location of the housing having regard to the member's rank and family needs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> The cost of rent is payable through one of the following.<br>a. Reimbursement to the member.<br>b. Direct payment to the landlord or their agent.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.4.7 Rental bond advance – USA, Canada and UK

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to members posted to the USA, Canada or the UK, to assist with the cost of privately leased housing.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may approve the payment of a rental bond advance to a member for privately leased housing.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member must repay the rental bond advance as a lump sum payment when all of the following events occur.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member's overseas posting ends.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member receives their rental bond back from the landlord.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member does not receive the full rental bond back from the landlord, the member must still repay the full amount of the advance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6.</td>
<td colspan="2">After the member has made a repayment under subsection 5, if the member disputes alleged damage to the property, section 15.4.9 may apply.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.4.8 Costs incurred under terms of occupancy

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A member who is required to pay any of the following under the terms and conditions of their lease is eligible for an amount that is equal to the amount of those payments.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Property taxes.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Other council payments.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.4.9 Dispute about damage to property

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Property leased by a member to live in at the post may be alleged to have been damaged. If this happens, a dispute may arise between the member and their landlord over the terms of the lease or return of the rental bond.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may pay the member an amount equal to the amount the member can show they had to pay for damage alleged to have been done to the property by them. The member must meet all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member did not breach the terms of the lease.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member did not cause damage to the property by their wrongful or negligent act.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The member cannot get their bond or rent returned, or has been forced to pay an extra amount to fix the alleged damage.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.4.10 Changing housing during posting

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A member is eligible for the cost of removing items if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member is moving from one residence in the posting location to another.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The move is due to organisational requirements.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.4.11 Housing becomes unavailable or unfit

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">If a member’s accommodation becomes unavailable or unfit for occupation, the member is eligible for all of the following from the day the accommodation becomes unavailable or unfit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Temporary accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Settling-in allowances listed in Chapter 14 Part 5.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 2: Utilities

###### 15.4.12 Purpose

|  | The purpose of this Division is to help a member on a long-term posting with the cost of utilities. |
|---|---|

###### 15.4.13 Member this Division does not apply to

|  | This Division does not apply to a member who is not required to pay a rent and utilities contribution. |
|---|---|

###### 15.4.15 Benefit

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member on long-term posting is eligible to be reimbursed the cost of utilities.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member fails to exercise care and economy, the member must pay an amount that the CDF considers reasonable for additional utilities costs having regard to all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The make-up of the member's family.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The condition and nature of the residence occupied by the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The climatic conditions at the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The level of use of utilities by the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>Any special circumstance affecting the member that may cause a high level of use of utilities.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member will not be reimbursed for swimming pool heating.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 4: Rent and utilities contribution

###### 15.4.17 Purpose

|  | The purpose of this Division is to provide for the contributions that a member is required to pay when occupying a house at an overseas posting. |
|---|---|

###### 15.4.18 Rent contribution

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member who receives a payment for rent under subsection 15.4.6.2 must pay a rent contribution.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Unless Division 5 applies, a member’s rent contribution for a member with a rent group in an item in column A of the table in Annex 15.4.B Part 1 is one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the member is an unaccompanied member, the amount in column B of the same item.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the member is an accompanied member, the amount in column C of the same item.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> Contributions are deducted from the member’s fortnightly salary.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.4.18A Utilities contribution

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member who is reimbursed the cost of utilities under section 15.4.15 must pay a utilities contribution.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Unless Division 5 applies, a member’s weekly utilities contribution for their rent group in an item in column A of Annex 15.4.B Part 2 is one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the member is an unaccompanied member, the amount in column B of the same item.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the member is an accompanied member, the amount in column C of the same item.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> Contributions are deducted from the member’s fortnightly salary.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.4.19 Dual liability

| 1. | Dual liability means both a member and their partner would be required to pay a rent and utilities contribution under this Part. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The member who receives overseas living allowances when dual liability occurs is the only one required to pay the rent and utilities contribution. |

###### 15.4.20 Rent and utilities contribution – member occupying living-in accommodation overseas

| 1. | A member who occupies living-in accommodation is eligible to be reimbursed any costs they incur for living-in accommodation. |
|---|---|
| 2. | If subsection 1 applies, a member who holds a rank listed in an item in column A of the following table must pay the rent and utilities contribution in column B of the same item. |

| Item | Column A<br>Member rank | Column B<br>Contribution AUD a week |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | Corporal or lower | 10.00 |
| 2. | Sergeant or higher non-commissioned rank | 20.00 |
| 3. | Warrant Officer | 20.00 |
| 4. | Officer | 30.00 |

###### 15.4.21 Exemptions from rent and utilities contribution

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is not required to pay a rent and utilities contribution if all of the following are met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member's partner normally lives with the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member is required to be unaccompanied at the post.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The requirement is due to hardship, safety or the length of the long-term posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Sometimes, a member's partner may be absent from the member's posting location. When this happens, the CDF may waive the rent and utilities contribution for a period. Approval may only be given if the CDF is satisfied that the absence is for a maximum period of time and reason shown in this table.</td>
</tr>
</table>

| Item | Period of absence | Reason for absence |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | 13 weeks | The member's partner has delayed their departure to allow the member's child to finish a school term or year at the school that the child attended immediately before the posting. |
| 2. | 9 weeks | Any of these reasons.<br>a. The member's partner has made an early departure to allow the member's child to begin school at a new location at the beginning of a school year or term.<br>b. The member's partner is eligible to be reimbursed the fares for the travel for any of these purposes.<br>i. Visiting another location for compassionate reasons.<br>ii. Obtaining medical treatment at another location.<br>iii. Chaperoning the member or dependant requiring medical treatment at another location.<br>iv. Supervising the enrolment of the member's child at a boarding school in Australia. |

| 3. | A rent and utilities contribution is not payable following the death of a member. |
|---|---|

##### Division 5: Reductions to rent and utilities contributions

###### 15.4.22 Purpose

|  | The purpose of this Division is to provide a member with a reduction in their rent and utilities contributions in some situations. |
|---|---|

###### 15.4.22A Posting to hardship locations

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">If the member's posting location has a hardship location grade, the sum of the following contributions that would be payable by the member is reduced by AUD 10 a week.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Rent contribution under section 15.4.18.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Utilities contribution under section 15.4.18A.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.4.23 Maintaining a household in Australia

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member establishes or maintains a home in Australia to accommodate a dependant, all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Subject to subsection 3, the member’s rate of rent contribution payable under section 15.4.18 may be reduced by the CDF.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member does not have to pay a utilities contribution.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">In setting the reduced rate of rent contribution, the CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The costs incurred by the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The reason the member established the household.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The location where the dependant lives before and after the beginning of the member's posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The age and welfare of the dependant.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>The financial circumstances of the member and the dependant.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td>Any other factor relevant to the establishment and maintenance of a household.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is not eligible for a reduction of rent contribution for a child if they are eligible for assistance with boarding school costs for the child.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.4.24 Substandard housing

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member who lives in substandard housing. This section does not apply to housing rented privately.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is required to make a payment for living in this type of housing, then this payment is taken to be a rent and utilities contribution.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may reduce in whole or in part the rent and utilities contribution that the member is liable to pay for a residence at a particular location. The CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The size, configuration, condition and surroundings of the residence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The nature and quality of the utilities supplied to the residence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>If the hardship location grade for the long-term posting location takes into account the deficiencies in the housing.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">Reductions of this nature are a short-term solution. If possible, the member should find more suitable accommodation on the local rental market.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.4.25 Reductions of rent and utilities contribution during short-term hardship

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A short-term hardship may be any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>War.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Natural disaster.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Civil disorder.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Another similar event.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">At times of short-term hardships, the Commonwealth may be unable to provide a member with housing and utilities of the quality normally available. The CDF may reduce the rent and utilities contribution. This may be up to the full rent and utilities contribution payable by the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The amount of the reduction must be equal to the reduction in the quality of the housing and utilities caused by the short-term hardship. When making a decision, the CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The quality of accommodation and utilities normally available to the members at the location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The nature and extent of any deficiency in the housing and utilities made available to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The extent to which the deficiencies arise from the event and the expected timing of repairs to remedy the deficiencies.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 6: Household help and support

###### 15.4.26 Purpose

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">The purpose of this Division is to assist a member with the costs of hiring staff for any of the following reasons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">To maintain a household at the overseas posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">To undertake daily activities in locations where the safety and security of any of the following may otherwise be at risk.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The member's dependants.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.4.27 Payment of benefits

|  | Benefits provided under this Division are paid by reimbursement.<br>**Note:** The member must provide proof of their expenditure. |
|---|---|

###### 15.4.28 Benefits not payable

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A member is not eligible for a benefit under this Division for any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The cost of hiring staff to assist with the member's representational duties.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The cost of a service the member has already received a benefit for.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The engagement of services that do not comply with local laws.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.4.30 Snow clearing

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A member occupying free-standing accommodation is eligible for the costs of using commercial snow clearing services if the CDF is satisfied that it is reasonable having regard to all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The amount of snowfall at the member’s posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The period of the year that snow persists on the ground at the location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

</tr>
</table>

#### Part 5: Overseas health costs

##### Division 1: General Provisions

###### 15.5.1 Simplified outline of this Part

This Part provides the health costs that may be covered by Defence for a person approved to live with a member on a long-term posting overseas. This Part sets out who can receive health costs during an overseas posting (see section 15.5.3). A person who is in the posting location on using a reunion travel benefit may be eligible for specific health costs in limited circumstances (see section 15.5.3 and 15.5.5). The Part also provides how costs can be claimed (see Division 2).

Health costs include costs for medical goods and services (see Division 4), hospital costs (see Division 5), dental treatment (see Division 7), pharmaceutical products (see Division 8), vaccinations and anti-malaria drugs (see section 15.5.23), mental health services (see section 15.5.24) and ambulance and other medical transport (see section 15.5.25). If the person is not eligible for a health cost under Part 5 of Chapter 15, they may be able to claim the cost as an ancillary service (see Division 10).

If a person is pregnant they must seek approval to be eligible for childbirth costs in the posting location (see Division 6). There are various factors that the CDF will consider when deciding whether childbirth costs will be covered in the posting location (see section 15.5.17).

If costs associated with childbirth are not approved in the posting location the pregnant person is eligible for travel benefits to and from Australia (see section 15.5.38). The member and their children may also be eligible for travel benefits to return to Australia to support the birth (see sections 15.5.39 and 15.5.40). The pregnant person will not receive reimbursement under Part 5 of Chapter 15 for any childbirth costs incurred in Australia or a third county.

A person may be eligible for travel costs to another location to receive emergency or non-emergency health care (see Division 11). Travel costs may also be available for a chaperone to accompany the person (see section 15.5.31), or for a child to accompany the person (see section 15.5.30). Travel costs may be approved for a location within the posting country, or another overseas location, including Australia.

<tr>
<td></td>

<td colspan="2">The specialised medical good or service cannot be delayed until any of the following occurs.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>

</tr>
</table>

##### Division 6: Childbirth

###### 15.5.16 Person this Division applies to

|  | This Division applies to a person who gives birth during a posting period overseas and their infant post birth. |
|---|---|

###### 15.5.17 Childbirth costs

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Childbirth costs</b> include any of the following associated with the birth of a child.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Hospital accommodation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>In-patient meals.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>In-patient post-partum care, including for the infant.<br><b>Note:</b> Only immediate in-patient care for the infant is provided under this section.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> Pre-natal care and out-patient post-natal care are provided by other health costs under this Part.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Childbirth costs do not include any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Costs associated with a home birth.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.5.18 Childbirth costs at the posting location

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A person is eligible for childbirth costs at the posting location if the CDF is satisfied of all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>There is suitable maternity treatment available at the location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>There is a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit at the location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Any treatment will be provided by a registered health professional similar to an Australian registered health professional who provides childbirth services.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Any other factors relevant to the pregnancy and birth.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note 1:</b> Childbirth costs under this Division will only be approved at the posting location and not at a third country location.<br><b>Note 2:</b> If the person does not receive approval for childbirth costs at the posting location under this Division they will not be reimbursed childbirth costs incurred in the posting location.<br><b>Note 3:</b> Travel costs associated with return to Australia for childbirth are under subdivision 3 of Division 11.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.5.19 Health costs for the infant

|  | The infant is not eligible for health costs or ancillary services under this Part unless the infant is recognised as a dependant of the member under subsection 12.3.5.<br>**Note:** In-patient treatment of the infant after they are born is provided under section 15.5.17. |
|---|---|

###### 15.5.28 Person this Division applies to

<table>

<td>a.</td>

<td></td>
<td>b.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>

<table>
<tr>

<td></td>

<td>Business class.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>If business class is not available — first class.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

#### Part 6: Education assistance for children

##### Division 1: General provisions

###### 15.6.1 Purpose

|  | Education assistance provides benefits to a member to assist with any increased costs for their child's education as a result of the member's posting overseas, and maintain a standard of education close to that received in Australian public schools. |
|---|---|

###### 15.6.1A Definitions

|  | In this Part, the following apply. |
|---|---|
|  | An **academic year** commences on the first day of the first teaching period in a school year and ends on the day before the first day of the teaching period of the next school year. |

###### 15.6.2 Member this Part applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">This Part applies to a member who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is on a long-term posting overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member has a dependant who is a child.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The child is enrolled in one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>A centre-based early childhood education facility.<br><b>Note 1:</b> This does not include hiring of a nanny or au pair, in-home care or family day care.<br><b>Note 2:</b> The child enrolled in an early childhood education facility does not have to be enrolled full-time.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Preschool.<br><b>Note:</b> The child enrolled in preschool does not have to be enrolled full-time.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>Full-time primary school.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iv.</td>
<td>Full-time secondary school.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>v.</td>
<td>Full-time tertiary education.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>vi.</td>
<td>Full-time junior college or similar institution in the USA.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.6.3 Dual benefit exclusion

|  | A member is not eligible for education assistance under this Part in respect of a child for whom they are receiving benefits under Chapter 8 Part 4. |
|---|---|

###### 15.6.5 How benefits are paid

| 1. | Unless otherwise specified, benefits under this Part may be paid by a reimbursement to the member or provided through the service provider.<br>**Note:** If a benefit is a reimbursement, it cannot be provided through a service provider. |
|---|---|
| 2. | If a fee or charge for which a benefit is provided under this Part is paid by the member in instalments, the member may be reimbursed the amount paid for each instalment.<br>**Note:** The total amount reimbursed for the fee or charge must not exceed the limit of the benefit. |

###### 15.6.6 Amount repayable if member receives refund

|  | If a member is refunded an amount from a provider for a benefit that has been paid to the provider or reimbursed to the member, the member must repay the part of the benefit that is refunded. |
|---|---|

##### Division 1A: Early childhood education assistance for children at the posting location

###### 15.6.6A Purpose

|  | The purpose of early childhood education assistance is to assist members who are on long-term posting overseas and have a child attending a centre-based early childhood education facility in the posting location with the associated fees. |
|---|---|

###### 15.6.6B Member this Division applies to

<td>a.</td>

</tr>

<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They live with the member at the overseas posting location.</td>

</tr>

<td></td>
<td>b.</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> Education assistance from a member’s accompanying child who is attending preschool is provided under Division 1.</td>
</tr>

<table>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Compulsory fees</b> means the mandatory costs incurred for application fees, enrolment fees and compulsory tuition fees.<br><b>Note:</b> Compulsory fees do not include uniforms or equivalent, incidentals, such as nappies and wipes, meals and snacks, excursions or any other charges above the benchmark.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Early childhood education facility</b> means a centre-based facility providing early childhood education.<br><b>Note:</b> It does not include alternative care types, such as an au pair or nanny, in-home care, family day care or playgroups.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Yearly benefit</b> means the amount calculated using the following formula.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">[image: Start formula yearly benefit (AUD) equals A minus B end formula.]</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">Where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>A</b></td>
<td colspan="2">is the compulsory fees charged by benchmark school in the member’s posting location in Australian Dollars.<br><b>Note:</b> The benchmark amount is converted from local currency to Australian Dollars using the exchange rate used to pay the member’s salary as at 1 July within the year prior to the date of processing the benefit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>B</b></td>
<td colspan="2">is one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>If the member is an unaccompanied member — AUD 14,861.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>If the member is an accompanied member — AUD 20,665.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.6.6F Eligibility

<table>
<tr>

<td colspan="3">A member is eligible for early childhood education assistance on a day the child attends an early childhood education facility and one of the following applies.</td>

<tr>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>

<td>The member is undertaking activity hours and their partner is unable to care for the child without assistance because of a medical condition.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> The member must provide evidence that their partner is undertaking activity hours or unable to care for their dependent child without assistance because of a medical condition. This may include a letter from the partner’s employer, a course enrolment letter with expected contact hours, or medical evidence.</td>
</tr>
<tr>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">5 days in a week.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>

###### 15.6.6G Rate of early childhood education assistance

| 1. | The hourly rate of early childhood education assistance is calculated using the following formula, rounded up to the nearest whole dollar. |
|---|---|
|  | [image: Start forumla education assistance (AUD) equals open bracket start fraction yearly benefit over 52 end fraction close bracket divided by 50 end formula.] |
| 2. | The total number of hours of early childhood education assistance on a day is rounded up to the full hour. |
| 3. | If the yearly rate changes, the rate of early childhood education assistance is the rate that applied on the day the costs were incurred. |

###### 15.6.6H Cessation of eligibility for early childhood education assistance

|  | A member ceases to be eligible for early childhood education assistance for a day 3 months after the invoice for that day has being issued. |
|---|---|

###### 15.6.10 Compulsory tuition fees

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member with a child attending a school in the overseas posting location is eligible for one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the child attends a school at the member’s posting location where there is a benchmark school, the lesser of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The compulsory tuition fees charged by the child’s school for the child’s attendance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The compulsory tuition fees charged by the benchmark school for a child in similar circumstances to the member’s child.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the child meets all of the following, the rate charged by the benchmark school for the child.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>They attend a preschool in the USA that is a benchmark school.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They will not be 5 years old on 31 December in the current USA school year.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">If any of the following apply, the amount under subsection 2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The child attends a preschool or kindergarten in the USA and the CDF is satisfied that the government pre-school where the member lives is not a suitable benchmark school.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The child attends a primary or secondary school in the District of Columbia, USA, and the member has been directed to live there.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The child attends a primary or secondary school in the USA and the CDF is satisfied that the benchmark school where the member lives is not suitable.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iv.</td>
<td>The child has completed secondary school in the USA and is attending a junior college, or similar institution in the USA, for admission to a tertiary institution in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">For the purpose of paragraph 1.c the amount is the lesser of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The compulsory tuition fees charged by the child's school for the child’s attendance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The amount calculated using the following formula.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">[image: Start formula compulsory tuition fee benefit equals AUD41,077 times open bracket start fraction A over 100 end fraction close bracket times B end formula]</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">Where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>A</b></td>
<td colspan="2">is the post index under section 12.3.14A used to calculate overseas allowances as at 1 July within the year prior to the date of processing the benefit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>B</b></td>
<td colspan="2">is the exchange rate used to pay the member’s salary as at 1 July within the year prior to the date of processing the benefit.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.6.11 Member contribution

<table>
<tr>

</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>

<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The rate in column B of the same item of the table.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>

</table>

| Item | Column A<br>School level | Column B<br>Annual contribution in AUD |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | Preschool or kindergarten | 662 |
| 2. | Primary school | 226 |
| 3. | Secondary school | 527 |
| 4. | Junior college (or similar institution in the USA) | 527 |

<table>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member's child will not complete a full academic year due to service reasons, the member’s annual contribution under subsection 2 is calculated using the following formula.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">[image: Start formula annual contribution equals A times start fraction B over C end fraction end formula]</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>

<tr>
<td></td>

###### 15.6.12 Excess school transport costs

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is eligible to be reimbursed the excess costs of school transport if their child meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">Their child uses one of the following to travel between their home and their school.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Public transport.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Transport provided by the school that is not included in the compulsory tuition fees.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Their child’s school transport costs exceed AUD 405.06 within an academic year.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">Excess costs of school transport are calculated using the following formula.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">[image: Start formula excess costs of school transport equals open bracket A times B close bracket minus open bracket start fraction C over 157 end fraction times 405.06 close bracket end formula]</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">Where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>A</b></td>
<td colspan="2">is the lesser of the following school transport costs at the location in local currency.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The costs that would be payable had the child attended a benchmark school.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The costs paid by the member for the child.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>B</b></td>
<td colspan="2">is the exchange rate provided by the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade for the payday before the academic year.<br><b>Note:</b> This is used to convert the local currency in which the member incurred the school transport costs into Australian dollars.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>C</b></td>
<td colspan="2">is the number of days the member’s child attended school in the overseas location during the academic year, not exceeding 157 days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> If the outcome is zero or less, the amount payable for excess costs of school transport is AUD 0.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 2A: Education assistance for children at the posting location – School holiday programs

###### 15.6.17B Definitions

|  | In this Division, the following apply. |
|---|---|
|  | **Reimbursement period** means the total number of weekdays of school holidays in the academic year for the school the child attends less 60 days.<br>**Note:** A public holiday that falls on a weekday within the school holidays is included when determining the number of days of school holidays. |

###### 15.6.17C Member this Division applies to

|  | This Division applies to a member whose child attends a preschool, kindergarten, primary or secondary school at the overseas posting location where, when combined, the school holiday period is greater than 60 weekdays in an academic year. |
|---|---|

###### 15.6.17D School holiday program costs

<table>
<tr>
<td>1A.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section does not apply to a member who is not eligible for a compulsory tuition fee benefit under section 15.6.10 for the child.<br><b>Note:</b> The benefit under section 15.6.10 applies to the child’s usual school, not the school holiday program.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">Subject to subsection 2, a member is eligible for reimbursement of costs for each weekday, that their child attends a school holiday program that meets all of the following.</td>

<td colspan="2">It meets any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>It is associated with an educational institution.<br><b>Note:</b> The educational institution the school holiday program is associated with does not need to be the school the child attends.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>It is an educational, vocational or developmental program, provided by a person qualified to deliver the program.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">It is held in a school type setting and is not a camp or an overnight program.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">It does not include any dangerous recreational activities.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The number of days the member can receive reimbursement must not exceed the reimbursement period.</td>
</tr>
</table>

<table>
<tr>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The amount calculated using the following formula.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">[image: Start formula maximum rate of reimbusement (AUD) equals start fraction AUD150 times A over 100 end fraction end formula]</td>

<td></td>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Where:</td>

##### Division 3: Education assistance for children overseas – special circumstances

###### 15.6.18 Education assistance – inadequate education facilities

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is eligible for education assistance for their child studying by one of the following means if the CDF is satisfied the benchmark school at the posting location overseas is inadequate for the child.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">By way of correspondence at the member's posting location overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">At an overseas location other than the member's posting location overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">Before making the decision under subsection 1, the CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The availability and nature of the education facilities at the member’s posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The alternative education arrangements made for the child and their cost.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The nature and cost of other arrangements that the member could be expected to make at the posting location or in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">Any other circumstance at the posting location affecting the educational welfare of the child.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">The amount of education assistance is one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If paragraph 1.a applies, one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The amount the member would be eligible for under Division 2 if their child was studying at the benchmark school at the posting location overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>An amount the CDF considers reasonable.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">If paragraph 1.b applies, the benefits the member would be eligible for under Division 4 if the child lived in Australia and attended a non‑Government school that provided for the child’s alternative education arrangements.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member eligible for education assistance for a child under this section is not eligible for education assistance under section 15.6.10 for that child.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.6.19 Travel benefit for child leaving posting location overseas

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member’s child leaves the member’s posting location overseas to begin school at another location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member will receive education assistance for the child in the other location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the child is to attend a school in Australia, the travel benefit is the lesser of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The allowable travel cost for the child to travel from the posting location overseas to the school.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The actual cost of the travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the child is to attend a school outside of Australia, the travel benefit is the lesser of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The allowable travel cost for the child to travel from the posting location overseas to the school.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The allowable travel cost for the child to travel from the posting location overseas to the last posting location in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The actual cost of the travel.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.6.20 Accompanying a child to begin boarding school

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies to a member who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s child has lived at the member’s posting location overseas for at least a year or a school year.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s child is leaving the posting location to attend boarding school in another location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s child has not previously attended a school as a boarder.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is eligible for education assistance for their child to attend primary or secondary school at their next location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member is eligible for the travel costs between the member’s posting location and the child’s school for the member or member's partner to accompany their child to begin boarding school outside the member's posting location overseas if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The travel arrangements with the child cannot be made in conjunction with other travel benefits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">One of the following applies.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The child is not permitted to travel alone.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>It would be severely detrimental to the child's welfare if the member or their partner did not accompany the child.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF approves the travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">For the purpose of paragraph 2.c, the CDF must not approve the travel unless all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">There are special circumstances that require the child to be accompanied to begin boarding school.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">It is reasonable having regards to all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The time the member has been overseas on posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>When the member or partner last travelled to the location where the child will be attending boarding school.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>Any other factor relevant to the child beginning boarding school.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">Travel costs under subsection 1 means the lesser of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">One of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>If the child is to attend a school in Australia — the allowable travel costs for one person to travel from the posting location overseas to the school’s location and return to the posting location overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>If the child is to attend a school outside of Australia — the allowable travel costs for one person to travel from the posting location to the member's last posting location in Australia and return to the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The actual cost of the travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is only eligible for a benefit under this section once for each child on a long‑term posting overseas.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 4: Education assistance for children in Australia

###### 15.6.23 Member this Division applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">This Division applies to a member on a long-term posting overseas who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s child is enrolled in one of the following in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>Primary school.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>Secondary school.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>A tertiary institution.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">During the child’s study, their primary accommodation is not the family home in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> This Division will continue to apply to a member after the member has been posted back to Australia until the member ceases to be eligible for education assistance under section 15.6.29.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.6.24 Member this Division does not apply to

|  | This Division does not apply to a member in relation to a child in Australia if the member’s partner also resides in Australia unless the CDF is satisfied that it is reasonable in the circumstances to provide education assistance in relation to the child.<br>**Note:** If the member has more than one child, the CDF may make a different decision in relation to each child. |
|---|---|

###### 15.6.25 Initial enrolment fees

| 1. | A member is eligible for an amount charged by the school in which their child is enrolled for the child's initial enrolment. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The benefit under this section may be reimbursed to the member or paid upfront to the provider. |

###### 15.6.26 Compulsory tuition fees

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Subject to subsection 3, a member who has a child attending preschool, primary or secondary school in Australia is eligible for the costs of compulsory tuition fees for the child.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The maximum benefit under subsection 1 is the lesser of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The amount of the compulsory tuition fees.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>AUD 41,077.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member who receives a benefit under subsection 1 must pay one of the following contributions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the child is in preschool or primary school — AUD 226.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the child is in secondary school — AUD 527.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">If a member's child will not complete a full academic year due to service reasons, the member’s annual contribution under subsection 3 is calculated using the following formula.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">[image: Start formula annual contribution equals A times start fraction B over C end fraction end formula]</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>A</b></td>
<td>is the number of days the child will attend the school for the academic year.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>B</b></td>
<td>is the annual contribution the member must pay for the child under subsection 3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>C</b></td>
<td>is the number of school days in the academic year.</td>
</tr>
</table>

<table>

<td>AUD 36,302.</td>

<td></td>

<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The actual cost.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>AUD 19,909.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>

<td></td>

</tr>
</table>

###### 15.6.28 Remedial tuition

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member is eligible to be reimbursed the cost of up to 50 hours of remedial tuition if the CDF is satisfied of all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">There has been a decline in the child’s academic performance as a result of the member’s overseas posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">A written evaluation has been provided by the child’s school which includes all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The child’s rate of academic progress at the school.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The reason remedial tuition is recommended.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>The recommended number of remedial tuition hours.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">Whether the child’s academic performance will reasonably improve if remedial tuition is provided.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">Any other factors relevant to the child's academic performance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member is eligible to be reimbursed the cost of up to a further 150 hours of remedial tuition for the same child in addition to the initial remedial tuition hours provided under subsection 1 if the CDF is satisfied it is reasonable.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">Remedial tuition approved by the CDF under this section must be taken within the later of the following dates.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">12 months from the date the member’s child commences at the new school in Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">12 months from the date the member commences their overseas posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="3">The maximum amount a member can be reimbursed for each hour of remedial tuition is the lesser of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The hourly rate the member paid.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The amount under paragraph 8.4.10.3.b.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.6.29 Child leaves the posting location overseas to attend school in Australia

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies to a member if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member has received compulsory tuition fees for study at the posting location overseas under Division 2 or Division 3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member’s child has relocated to Australia to study before the end of the member's posting.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member is ineligible for benefits under this Division unless all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">One of the following applies.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member has repaid any benefit for compulsory tuition fees for the child’s study overseas under section 15.6.10 for the period the child is not in the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The period for which the compulsory tuition fees for study at the posting location overseas has ended.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF is satisfied that the cost to Defence to provide the benefit is reasonable in the circumstances.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">If the member has paid a contribution under section 15.6.10 and the period for which the contribution has not ended, the member is eligible for a reimbursement calculated using the following formula.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">[image: Start formula reimbursable amount equals start fraction A over B end fraction times C end formula]</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3">Where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>A</b></td>
<td colspan="2">is the number of days left of the period the contribution covered from the day the Commonwealth was repaid the compulsory tuition fees it paid.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>B</b></td>
<td colspan="2">is the number of days the contribution covered.<br><b>Note:</b> The period could be a school term, number of school terms or the full school year. The dates for school terms and school years are determined by the school.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>C</b></td>
<td colspan="2">is the contribution the member paid.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.6.30 End of education assistance

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member ceases to be eligible for education assistance under this Division on the earlier of the following days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The day a parent of the child lives in Australia on a permanent basis unless the CDF is satisfied it is not reasonable for the child to live with the parent.<br><b>Note:</b> If the member has more than one child, the CDF may make a different decision in relation to each child.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The day the child changes schools after the member is posted back to Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the child is in primary school — the end of the school year after the member is posted back to Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the child is in secondary school and subsection 3 applies, one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>If the child is enrolled in a school year that is not one of the last 2 years of secondary school — the end of the school year after the member is posted back to Australia.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>If the child is enrolled in a school year that is one of the last 2 years of high school — the end of the last year of secondary school.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the child is enrolled in tertiary education — the child turns 18 years old.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">For the purpose of paragraph 1.d, the child must have been enrolled in a secondary school in the year in an item in column A of the following table for the period prescribed in column B of the same item.</td>
</tr>
</table>

| Item | Column A<br>Year at School | Column B<br>Prescribed period |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | The first year of secondary school | From the beginning of the school year. |
| 2. | Any other year of secondary school | For at least four school terms before the day on which the posting ends. |

#### Part 7: Foreign language training for partner

###### 15.7.1 Purpose

|  | The purpose of this Part is to provide foreign language training to a member's partner when they accompany the member on long-term posting. |
|---|---|

###### 15.7.1A Person this Part applies to

|  | This part applies to a member’s partner who accompanies a member on a long-term posting overseas. |
|---|---|

###### 15.7.2 Foreign language training

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member’s partner is eligible for up to 40 hours of training to learn a language other than English if the Director Attaché and Overseas Management is satisfied that it is reasonable having regard to any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Whether English is a common language in the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Whether the language is required for everyday or professional reasons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>Whether knowledge of the language will assist in the personal security of the member's partner.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member’s partner is eligible for up to an extra 40 hours training to learn a language other than English if the Director Attaché and Overseas Management is satisfied that it is reasonable having regard to any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The requirement of the partner to engage in representational activities.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The difficulty of the language.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The progress the partner has already made.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> A member’s partner is not eligible for a benefit under subsection 2 if no benefit is provided under subsection 1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">For the purpose of this section, training must be to learn a language commonly used in the posting location.</td>
</tr>
</table>

#### Part 8: Club membership

###### 15.8.1 Purpose

|  | The purpose of this Part is to provide for a member on a long-term posting and their dependants to pursue sporting, recreational and fitness activities. |
|---|---|

###### 15.8.2 Member’s location and approved club

<td colspan="2">For the purpose of this Part, a member’s location is one of the following.</td>

<td>If the member’s posting location is to a country listed in the table in subsection 2, member’s location is that country.</td>

<td>If the member is posted to a city or an establishment within a city that is listed in the table under subsection 2, member’s location is that city.</td>
