###### 15.8.4 Benefits in the member’s location

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is eligible for the cost of membership to an approved club or a similar club for any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member's dependants who reside in the member’s location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The maximum benefit is the cost of a membership at the approved club.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The cost of membership includes the joining fee and any ongoing annual membership fees.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.8.5 Additional club membership costs

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may decide to pay reasonable additional club membership costs having regards to all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Other recreational or social facilities available at the member’s location for a fee, including the arrangements for access to them and their cost.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The nature of the member's duties at the member’s location, including any representational duties.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The nature of the facilities at the approved club and at the club that the member joins.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>Any other factor relevant to the club membership at the member’s location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member may be eligible for the additional costs of club membership if all of the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The costs are associated with a dependant on a reunion visit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The reunion visit is to the location for which the member has received a benefit under this Part.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The CDF considers it is reasonable to do so in the circumstances.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 15.8.6 Payment of benefit

|  | A benefit under this Part may be paid by way of reimbursement to the member or directly to the service provider.<br>**Note:** If the benefit is paid directly to the service provider, the member must pay the Commonwealth the club membership costs that exceed the benefit provided in this Part. |
|---|---|

### Chapter 16: Overseas hardship locations

#### Part 1: General conditions and definitions

###### 16.1.1 Purpose

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">The purpose of the overseas hardship package is to provide assistance for members and their dependants for difficulties or hardships experienced on any of the following types of overseas service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Long-term posting at certain posting locations overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Short-term duty at certain overseas locations</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 16.1.2 Definitions

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">In this Chapter the following apply.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Capital city</b> means the capital city in Australia with the lowest allowable travel cost where the locations for the allowable travel costs are the member's posting location and a capital city in Australia other than Hobart or Darwin.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Provisional hardship location</b> has the meaning given by section 16.1.3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Qualifying location</b> means any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A hardship location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A location for which the member received deployment allowance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Qualifying period</b> has the meaning given by section 16.1.4</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 16.1.3 Provisional hardship location

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Provisional hardship location means a location determined by the CDF, taking all of the following into consideration.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Whether the ADF is required to provide humanitarian aid, disaster relief or reconstruction assistance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The level of assistance required of the ADF.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The level of hardship expected.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The nature of duties expected.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>The expected duration of duty at the location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td>Any other factors relevant to the location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">When determining a location under subsection 1, the CDF must also determine all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The hardship location grade for the location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The period the hardship location grade applies, but not longer than 3 months.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 16.1.4 Qualifying period

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Qualifying period means the lesser of the following periods of duty performed by a member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A period of 28 continuous days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A period determined by the CDF.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">For the purpose of paragraph 1.b, the CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Whether the ADF is required to provide humanitarian aid, disaster relief or reconstruction assistance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The level of assistance required of the ADF.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The level of hardship expected.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The nature of duties expected.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>The expected duration of duty at the location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td>Any other factors relevant to the location.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 16.1.5 Member this Chapter applies to

|  | This Chapter applies to a member performing duty in a hardship location. |
|---|---|

###### 16.1.6 Member this Chapter does not apply to

|  | This Chapter does not apply to a member on warlike or non-warlike deployments. |
|---|---|

#### Part 2A: Location allowance

###### 16.2A.1 Purpose

|  | Location allowance assists members and their dependants with the difficult conditions that may be encountered at a hardship location. |
|---|---|

###### 16.2A.2 Member this Part applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Part applies to a member who meets one of the following conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are posted to a hardship location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are performing a period of short-term duty at a hardship location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The member is performing duty at a provisional hardship location.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 16.2A.3 Member this Part does not apply to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This part does not apply to a member for a period when any of the following conditions apply to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are not entitled to salary.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are absent from a hardship location, except as provided in section 16.2A.6.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 16.2A.3A Dual Commonwealth benefit rule

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member if all of the following apply to their partner.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member’s partner is posted to or resides in the same location as the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member’s partner is eligible for a benefit from the Commonwealth that is for the same or comparable purpose to the benefits provided under this Part.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member ceases to be eligible for a benefit under this Part if the member’s partner has a higher salary than the member and has been nominated to receive the comparable benefit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">If subsection 2 applies, and the member receives a benefit under this Part, the member must repay the amount received.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 16.2A.3B Eligibility for location allowance

| 1. | A member is eligible for location allowance if they meet the qualifying period in one or more qualifying locations. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The dual Commonwealth benefit rule applies to this allowance. |

<table>
<tr>

<td></td>

<td>They are an unaccompanied member.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They are receiving deployment allowance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> This includes a day on deployment that contributed to the member’s qualifying period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

<td colspan="2">All of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>

<td></td>

<td>They are on short-term duty overseas.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>They are absent from the hardship location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

<td colspan="2"><b>Note 1:</b> Section 12.3.1 provides the definition of accepted period.<br><b>Note 2:</b> Section 16.2A.4A may modify the date a person returns to the posting location for the purpose of the accepted period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">They are on leave without pay.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 16.2A.4A Disrupted return to the posting location

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member who would not have been absent from their posting location for longer than the accepted period had their return to the posting location not been disrupted by any of the following in response to an infectious disease.</td>

<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Requirement to isolate.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Travel restriction or limited travel opportunity.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">For the purpose of paragraph 16.2A.4, the day the member is taken to have returned to the posting location is the earlier of the following days.</td>
</tr>

<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The day they commence the isolation period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The day they would have returned to the hardship location had it not been for the travel restriction or limited travel opportunity.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 16.2A.7 Duty in another hardship location

| 1. | This section applies to a member who receives location allowance immediately prior to beginning short-term duty (‘the member’s previous location’) in another hardship location. |
|---|---|
| 2. | If the short-term duty location has a higher hardship location grade than the member’s previous hardship location — the location allowance is payable at the rate for the grade of the location of the short-term duty. |
| 3. | If the short-term duty location has a lower hardship location grade than the member’s previous hardship location — the location allowance is payable at the rate for the grade of the member’s previous hardship location. |

#### Part 3A: Additional recreation leave

###### 16.3A.1 Purpose

<table>
<tr>

</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Obtain relief from the environment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>

</tr>

###### 16.3A.2 Member this Part applies to

|  | This Part applies to a member posted to a hardship location. |
|---|---|

</tr>

#### Part 4: Assisted leave travel

##### Division 1: Assisted leave travel benefit

###### 16.4.1 Purpose

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Assisted leave travel is provided to a member and each of their dependants living at a hardship location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Travel to a leave centre is to enable any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Access health and shopping facilities not normally available at the hardship location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Obtain relief from the environment at the hardship location.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 16.4.2 Definitions

|  | In this Part, the following apply. |
|---|---|
|  | **Ordinary posting period** means, for a location in an item in column A of the table in Annex 16.B, the period in months set out in column B of the same item. |

###### 16.4.3 Eligibility for assisted leave travel

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">A member who is posted to a hardship location is eligible for the number of assisted leave travel trips calculated under Division 2 for each of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Each of their dependants.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 16.4.4 Using assisted leave travel

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">The number of assisted leave travel trips allocated to a person is reduced by 1 each time any of the following occurs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They use an assisted leave travel benefit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They offset an assisted leave travel benefit under Division 3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>They use an additional travel benefit under Chapter 15 Division 7 Subdivision 2.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 16.4.5 Assisted leave travel benefit

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">An assisted leave travel trip is the lesser of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">One of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>If the travel is by a means other than private vehicle — the cost of return travel to a regional leave centre or relief leave centre.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>If the travel is by private vehicle — the amount calculated under section 16.4.6.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The allowable cost of return air travel subject to any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>For travel between Islamabad, Pakistan and Karachi, Pakistan — the next highest class above economy.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>For any other travel — economy class.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">All of the following apply to assisted leave travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is travelling, they must have been granted a period of recreation leave for the period they are absent from duty in connection with assisted leave travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">Assisted leave travel may be used by a member or the member’s dependants separately or together.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">A person cannot use more than 1 assisted leave travel benefit at a time.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td colspan="2">Assisted leave travel must commence at the hardship location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">For the purpose of paragraph 1, if a flight is being taken as part of the assisted leave travel benefit, costs include excess baggage costs provided under section 16.4.7.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 16.4.6 Travel by private vehicle

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The purpose of this section is to provide how to calculate the cost of return travel for the purpose of subparagraph 16.4.5.1.a.ii if the member or their dependant travels by private vehicle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The cost of return travel by private vehicle is the total of all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The amount of vehicle allowance that would be payable under section 15.3.21 if the vehicle was being used on official business.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Any cost incurred in transporting the vehicle and occupants for part of the travel, excluding accommodation or meal costs.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">If more than one person who is eligible for an assisted leave travel benefit travels in the same vehicle, vehicle allowance is only payable to one person.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 16.4.7 Excess baggage

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member posted to a location listed in Annex 16.B column A is eligible to be reimbursed the cost of excess baggage if it is indicated in column C of the same item.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member may be reimbursed the cost of up to 12 kg of excess baggage charged by the airline for the excess baggage for any of the following people travelling.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>A dependant of the member.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 2: Calculating number of trips

###### 16.4.9 Posting for the ordinary posting period

| 1. | This section applies to a member who is posted to a hardship location for the ordinary posting period. |
|---|---|
| 2. | A member posted to a location in an item in column 1 of the table in Annex 16.B is eligible for the number of assisted leave travel trips to a leave centre in column C of the same item. |
| 3. | The member may choose in writing the sequence in which assisted leave fares are taken for the leave centres during the ordinary posting period. |

###### 16.4.10 Posting longer than ordinary posting period

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member when their posting to a hardship location is longer than the ordinary posting period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The number of assisted leave travel trips the member is eligible for is calculated using the following formula.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">[image: Start formula number of trips equals start fraction open bracket A plus 1 close bracket times B over C end fraction plus A end formula]</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>A</b></td>
<td>is the total number of trips under Annex 16.B column C.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>B</b></td>
<td>is the extra posting period in months.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td><b>C</b></td>
<td>is the ordinary posting period in months under Annex 16.B column B.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The outcome of the formula in subsection 2 is rounded up to the nearest whole number.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the number of trips calculated under subsection 2 is more than what is provided under Annex 16.B column C, at least one of the additional trips must be to a regional leave centre.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 16.4.11 Posting shorter than ordinary posting period

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member when their posting to a hardship location is shorter than the ordinary posting period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section does not apply to a member who has had their posting period reduced, other than at the member’s request.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The number of assisted leave travel trips the member is eligible for is calculated using the following formula.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">[image: Start formula number of trips equals start fraction A times B over C end fraction end formula]</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Where:</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>

<td>is the total number of trips under Annex 16.B column C.</td>

<td></td>

<tr>
<td></td>

<tr>
<td></td>

#### Part 5: Accommodation on unavoidable stopovers

###### 16.5.1 Purpose

|  | In using assisted leave travel, members may incur accommodation costs on an unavoidable stopover. This can result from the limited choice of direct flights at the hardship location. This Part allows members to be reimbursed the accommodation costs. |
|---|---|

###### 16.5.3 Member this Part applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Part applies to a member who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are on a long-term posting to a hardship location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They are granted a reasonable period of leave.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 16.5.4 Member this Part does not apply to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Part does not apply to a member who meets any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>They are on short-term duty at a location for less than 28 days.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>They travel under Part 4 section 16.4.12 to a location other than a leave centre ('offset travel').</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 16.5.5 Accommodation

|  | Members are responsible for the costs involved with accommodation during assisted leave travel, unless they have an unavoidable stopover. |
|---|---|

###### 16.5.6 Accommodation – conditions for payment of costs

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the CDF is satisfied that a stopover is unavoidable during assisted leave travel, the member and dependants are to be reimbursed for one night's accommodation, meals and incidentals at the stopover location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">When making the decision under subsection 1, the CDF must consider any advice from the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>For travel from Australia – Defence Travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>For travel to Australia – the travel agent contracted by the post, or Defence Travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The limit of reimbursement is what would have been paid, if the member and dependants had been eligible for travel costs during the stopover under Chapter 13, Short-term duty overseas.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 16.5.7 Accommodation – Papua New Guinea stopover in Port Moresby

|  | Members who are on a long-term posting to the hardship location of Papua New Guinea, at a location other than Port Moresby, are eligible for one night's accommodation in Port Moresby, when returning from a leave centre. |
|---|---|

#### Part 7: Extraordinary costs

###### 16.7.1 Purpose

| 1. | A member might be at a posting location when war breaks out, there is civil disorder or a natural disaster or similar event. As a result, normal supplies of goods and services might be disrupted. They may need to pay more for goods and services essential to allow them to stay. |
|---|---|
| 2. | This Part is designed to reimburse members for these extra costs. The costs may only be reimbursed to members on long-term posting in some approved situations. |

###### 16.7.2 Member this Part applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">This Part applies to a member on a long-term posting overseas where normal supplies have been disrupted who meets one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member is unable to leave the posting location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member is required to stay at the posting location.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 16.7.3 Extraordinary costs incurred at posting location

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member may be reimbursed extraordinary costs incurred by the member in buying goods and services. Approval may only be given if the CDF is satisfied that the goods and services are essential for the member to remain at the location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The nature, duration and impact of the disruption to the normal supply of goods and services to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The nature and amount of the extraordinary costs incurred by the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The availability and cost of buying the goods and services from another supplier.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The allowances that are already being paid to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>The extent to which the Commonwealth is already providing the goods and services to the member.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>f.</td>
<td>The nature and extent of any other help provided to the member to buy goods and services.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>g.</td>
<td>Any other factor relevant to the extraordinary costs incurred by the member.</td>
</tr>
</table>

#### Part 8: Special location allowances

###### 16.8.1 Purpose

|  | A location allowance recognises the hazards of service in a location. |
|---|---|

###### 16.8.3 Special location allowance

| 1. | This section provides a special allowance as a consequence of additional hazards of service arising out of military conflict in a specific location. |
|---|---|
| 1A. | A member on long-term posting overseas to a location in column A of the following table is eligible for the daily rate of special location allowance listed in column B of the same item. |

| Item | Column A<br>Location | Column B<br>Special location allowance<br>AUD |
|---|---|---|
| 7. | Ukraine | 52.10 |

<table>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member is temporarily absent from the posting location for longer than 28 days, they cease to be eligible for the special location allowance from the 29th day of the absence until the day they return to the posting location.<br><b>Note:</b> To avoid doubt, the member continues to be eligible for the special location allowance until the end of the 28th day.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may do any of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Suspend eligibility for special location allowance for a location if they are satisfied that the hazards for which the location was specified has reduced.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Add a location if they are satisfied that the hazards in the location have increased.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">All of the following apply to a decision made under subsection 3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The decision must be made by notifiable instrument.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the decision is to add a location under paragraph 3.b, special location allowance is paid at the lowest rate payable under column B of the table in subsection 1A.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The decision may be revoked by notifiable instrument.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The decision ceases to have effect after 60 days.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 16.8.5 Attraction allowance for Papua New Guinea

| 1. | A member on long-term posting to Papua New Guinea receives an attraction allowance at the rate of AUD 10,000 a year. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The allowance is payable to the member on a pro rata fortnightly basis.<br>**Note:** This amount is subject to income tax. |

### Chapter 17: Warlike and non-warlike deployments

#### Part 1: General provisions

###### 17.1.1 Purpose

|  | This Chapter provides conditions of service for members on a warlike or non-warlike deployment to compensate them for additional disabilities or hardships that they are likely to experience. |
|---|---|

###### 17.1.3 Member this Chapter applies to

|  | This Chapter applies to members on warlike and non-warlike deployments. |
|---|---|

###### 17.1.4 Limited application of this Chapter

| 1. | A member on a peacetime deployment is eligible for relief out-of-country travel fare assistance under Division 4 of Part 7. |
|---|---|
| 2. | The remaining provisions of Chapter 17 do not apply to a member listed under subsection 1. |

#### Part 2: Eligibility to receive conditions of service

###### 17.2.1 Purpose

|  | The purpose of this Part is to describe who is eligible to receive conditions of service for deployment. |
|---|---|

###### 17.2.1A Period of eligibility

|  | A member, including a member of the Reserves, is eligible to receive benefits under this Chapter for the period they are force assigned. |
|---|---|

#### Part 3: Conditions of service – overview

###### 17.3.1 Introduction

|  | The ADF pay structure comprises a basic salary supplemented by work-related allowances. The basic salary, determined by the Defence Force Remuneration Tribunal, compensates a member for peacetime work. For United Nations or other multi-national force deployments, a special conditions of service package compensates members for additional hardships that they are likely to experience. |
|---|---|

###### 17.3.2 Class of air travel – warlike and non-warlike deployments

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to members travelling to, on or from warlike or non-warlike deployments.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">Other provisions about class of air travel do not apply to members who travel in an aircraft owned or chartered by the Commonwealth. The travel arrangements are as provided on board the aircraft.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">If members travel by commercial air service, they are eligible for travel in the class that corresponds to their rank, as follows.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>For a member who holds the rank of Brigadier or higher –– business class.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>For a member who holds the rank of Colonel or lower — economy class.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">Despite paragraph 17.3.2.3.b, the member is eligible to travel business class if the CDF is satisfied it is reasonable having regard to all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Any special circumstances prevent the person from travelling economy class.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member is part of a group, unit or headquarters travelling at the same time and for the same or a similar purpose.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The nature of the duties being undertaken in the course of the travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>The member’s health.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>e.</td>
<td>The status and class of air travel benefit of a person the member is required to accompany during the air travel in the course of duty.</td>
</tr>
</table>

#### Part 7: Allowances and leave

##### Division 1: Deployment allowance

###### 17.7.3 Purpose

|  | The purpose of deployment allowance is to compensate members for the hazard, stress and environmental factors that they are likely to experience over the term of a warlike or non-warlike deployment. |
|---|---|

###### 17.7.5 Member this Division applies to

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Deployment allowance is payable to a member who meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member is force assigned on a warlike or non-warlike deployment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member enters the specified area for the warlike or non-warlike deployment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">If no specified area is prescribed, deployment allowance is payable to a member who performs duty while assigned to an operation that is prescribed under section 5C of the <i>Veterans' Entitlements Act 1986</i>.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 17.7.7 Payment of allowance

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">Deployment allowance is payable at the relevant rate in section 17.7.6, for each day the member is in the specified area during the following period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Starting on the day the member first enters the specified area for the deployment to which they are assigned.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Ceasing on the day after the member leaves the specified area of the deployment they are assigned to for the last time on that deployment.<br><b>Note:</b> Subsection 17.7.8.3 applies if a member leaves the specified area for a reason which is not related to the deployment.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 17.7.8 Breaks in service

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member temporarily leaves the specified area during their deployment for any of the following reasons, the member continues to receive deployment allowance at the rate for the operation they are assigned to.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Operational reasons related to the deployment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Recreation or war service leave.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">After the period of temporary absence under subsection 1, the rate of deployment allowance payable is the rate for the specified area the member is deployed to on return.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member leaves the specified area for a reason which is not related to the deployment, the payment of deployment allowance ceases on the day after the member leaves the specified area and recommences if the member returns to the specified area.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 17.7.9 Eligibility for multiple rates

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">This section applies to a member who is in any of the following situations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member is assigned to an operation with more than one rate of deployment allowance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member is assigned to more than one operation, for which there are different rates of deployment allowance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the member temporarily leaves the specified area for a reason in subsection 17.7.8.1, then the rate of deployment allowance payable during their period of absence is the highest rate that has been payable to the member during their deployment.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 17.7.10 Member on transit through a specified area

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">If a member is required to transit through a specified area that is not the specified area for their deployment (the "other area"), the relevant of the following conditions applies.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>If the member has already been in their specified area and has left it temporarily for one of the reasons under subsection 17.7.8.1, the rate of deployment allowance payable to the member continues to be payable to them while they are in the other area.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the member has not yet arrived in their specified area, deployment allowance is not payable for time spent in the other area.<br><b>Note:</b> The member only receives deployment allowance when they meet the criteria under paragraph 17.7.5.1.a.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>If the member has left their specified area for the last time, deployment allowance is not payable in the other area as they have met the conditions under paragraph 17.7.7.b.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 17.7.11 Review of rates

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Deployment allowance rates may be reviewed on any of these occasions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>Every 6 months.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If forces are rotated.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>If there is a change in the assessed threat level.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>d.</td>
<td>If the Defence Force Remuneration Tribunal determines a general salary increase for the ADF.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">A member receiving deployment allowance must be made aware by their Commanding Officer that the rate initially determined may be amended and so could increase or decrease during their deployment, as a result of review.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">In the section, <b>threat level</b> means the level of operational threat and environmental hazard.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 17.7.12 Allowances that may be payable

|  | A member getting deployment allowance may be eligible for additional allowances in any of the following situations. |
|---|---|

| Item | Allowance | Additional information |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | Separation allowance | If applicable, separation allowance may be payable. |
| 2. | Travel costs | Travel costs are only payable to a member on any day the member has to pay for their own accommodation or meals while on deployment. |

##### Division 2: Civil practice support allowance

###### 17.7.13 Purpose

|  | The purpose of civil practice support allowance is to help medical officers in the Reserves with the costs of maintaining their civil medical practices. It applies while medical officers are on short periods of continuous full-time service with a deployment. |
|---|---|

###### 17.7.14 Member this Division applies to

|  | This Division applies to a medical officer in the Reserves who volunteers and is force assigned on a deployment. |
|---|---|

###### 17.7.15 Rate of allowance

<table>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2">The rate of civil practice support allowance for the period of service is AUD 1,600 a week. All of the following must be met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The CDF certifies that the member is on a specialist medical roster in support of a deployment or peacetime operation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member has a functioning civil medical practice.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 17.7.16 Period of service

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">A period of service is a period of continuous full-time service. The period is for not less than 2 weeks in an operational area on a deployment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The allowance is <b>not</b> payable for less than 2 weeks in any period of service unless the CDF approves payment for a lesser period. The CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The nature and period of the service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member's experience, qualifications and skills.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The likely benefit to the ADF.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">The allowance may be paid for more than one period of service during a deployment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">This subsection applies to a member whose deployment ceases before the end of 2 weeks or the lesser period of service approved by the CDF under subsection 2. The member is eligible for a portion of the allowance for the period of service completed. However, this only occurs in any of the following situations.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The member dies.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The member becomes medically unfit and cannot complete the period of service because of physical or mental incapacity not within the member's control.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td>The member cannot complete the period of service for reasons not in the member's control, and the CDF has agreed to that.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">While a member is eligible for civil practice support allowance, they are not eligible for any other allowance or reimbursement under Chapters 1 to 17 for any costs they incur in connection with their absence from their civil practice.</td>
</tr>
</table>

##### Division 3: Non-warlike deployments – additional recreation leave

###### 17.7.17 Purpose

|  | The purpose of additional recreation leave for non-warlike deployments is to enable a member to obtain relief from military and environmental hazards in an operational area. |
|---|---|

###### 17.7.18 Member this Division applies to

|  | This Division applies to a member for any period in which they are deployed to a non-warlike operation. |
|---|---|

###### 17.7.19 Rate of accrual

|  | The member accrues additional recreation leave up to a maximum of 10 days a year on a pro-rata basis for the period of their non-warlike deployment. |
|---|---|

##### Division 4: Relief out-of-country travel fare assistance

###### 17.7.21 Purpose

|  | The purpose of relief out-of-country travel fare assistance is to help the member have time away from the difficulties of a deployment. |
|---|---|

###### 17.7.22 Destination

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">Relief out-of-country travel fare assistance provides the member with return travel to an approved destination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF may approve the destination for relief out-of-country travel fare assistance. The CDF must choose a location that meets all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>A safe environment for rest and recreation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>Adequate rest and recreation facilities.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 17.7.23 Conditions

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="3">This section applies to a member who meets one of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is deployed for 6 months or more.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF is satisfied of all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>The member is on a deployment of less than 6 months.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>The duties the member performs are exceptionally demanding.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF is satisfied the member is likely to serve multiple deployments in a 12‑month period.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1A.</td>
<td colspan="3">Subject to operational constraints, a member is eligible for relief out-of-country travel fare assistance for return travel to an approved destination if all of the following conditions are met.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member travels to a destination approved under subsection 17.7.22.2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is outside the operational area on recreation or war service leave for 7 consecutive days or longer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>c.</td>
<td colspan="2">If practicable, the travel is planned to occur during regular intervals during the deployment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="3">A member whose deployment period is set out in an item in column A of the following table is eligible for relief out-of-country travel fare assistance for the number of trips in column B of the same item.</td>
</tr>
</table>

| Item | Column A<br>Deployment time | Column B<br>Number of trips |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | One of the following.<br>a. It is intended that the member be deployed for 6 months or more, but less than 9 months.<br>b. The member is approved for out-of-country travel fare assistance under paragraph 1.a. | 1 |
| 2. | It is intended that the member be deployed for 9 months or more, but less than 12 months. | 2 |
| 3. | It is intended that the member be deployed for 12 months or more, but less than 15 months. | 3 |
| 4. | It is intended that the member be deployed for 15 months or more, but less than 18 months. | 4 |
| 5. | It is intended that the member be deployed for 18 months or more. | 5 |

<table>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="3">The member is eligible for relief out-of-country travel fare assistance up to the following limits.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td colspan="2">The cost of return travel to the approved destination under these conditions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>i.</td>
<td>It is economy class.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>ii.</td>
<td>It is on the cheapest available airline that offers a reasonable standard of safety and security.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td></td>
<td>iii.</td>
<td>It does not include any avoidable stopovers.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td colspan="2">The member is not eligible for travel costs while on relief out of country travel fare assistance.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="3"><b>Note:</b> Short absence for travel provided under this Division may be available under Chapter 5 Part 11 Division 6.</td>
</tr>
</table>

###### 17.7.24 Offsetting fare assistance

<table>
<tr>
<td>1.</td>
<td colspan="2">If the CDF is satisfied that travel to another country meets the purpose of relief out-of-country travel fare assistance, the member may travel to a destination in another country that meets the purpose of assistance with relief travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2.</td>
<td colspan="2">The CDF must consider all of the following.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>The purpose of the relief travel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>The facilities and environment at the destination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3.</td>
<td colspan="2">For the purpose of subsection 1, the maximum relief out-of-country travel fare assistance is the amount they would have been eligible for under this Division.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4.</td>
<td colspan="2">Allowable offset arrangements are advised at the start of each deployment.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5.</td>
<td colspan="2">If it is intended that a member stay on deployment for 12 months or more, the member may apply to combine two trips that they are eligible for under the table in subsection 17.7.23.2, for any of the following reasons.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>a.</td>
<td>To assist the member and their dependants to use relief out-of-country travel fare assistance to reunite, in Australia or in an approved destination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td>b.</td>
<td>If the member has no dependants (or does not wish to reunite with them), to travel on relief out-of-country travel fare assistance to Australia or another country that is more expensive to travel to than the standard approved destination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td></td>
<td colspan="2"><b>Note:</b> The offset can only be used to purchase fares. The alternative location must still be approved under section 17.7.22.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>6.</td>
<td colspan="2">Proof of travel is required under section 16.4.16.</td>
</tr>
</table>

Defence Determination 2016/19, Conditions of service

made under section 58B of the Defence Act 1903

**Compilation No. 159**

**Compilation date:** 10 September 2026

**Includes amendments:** Defence Determination 2026/15

This compilation is in 4 volumes

Volume 1 Chapter 1 – Chapter 5

Volume 2 Chapter 6 – Chapter 11

Volume 3 Chapter 12 – Chapter 17

**Volume 4 Endnotes**

Each volume has its own contents

**About this compilation**

**This compilation**

This is a compilation of *Defence Determination 2016/19, Conditions of service*, that shows the text of the law as amended and in force on 10/09/2026 (the ***compilation date***).

The notes at the end of this compilation (the endnotes) include information about amending laws and the amendment history of provisions of the compiled law.

**Uncommenced amendments**

The effect of uncommenced amendments is not shown in the text of the compiled law. The details of amendments made up to, but not commenced at, the compilation date are underlined in the endnotes. Any uncommenced amendments affecting the law are accessible on the Register (www.legislation.gov.au).

**Application, saving and transitional provisions**

If the operation of a provision or amendment of the compiled law is affected by an application, saving or transitional provision that is not included in this compilation, details are included in the endnotes.

**Modifications**

If the compiled law is modified by another law, the compiled law operates as modified but the modification does not amend the text of the law. Accordingly, this compilation does not show the text of the compiled law as modified. Any modifications affecting the law are accessible on the Register.

**Self repealing provisions**

If a provision of the compiled law has been repealed in accordance with a provision of the law, details are included in the endnotes.

## Endnotes

### Endnote 1—About the endnotes

The endnotes provide information about this compilation and the compiled law.

The following endnotes are included in every compilation:

Endnote 1—About the endnotes

Endnote 2—Abbreviation key

Endnote 3—Legislation history

Endnote 4—Amendment history

**Abbreviation key—Endnote 2**

The abbreviation key sets out abbreviations that may be used in the endnotes.

**Legislation history and amendment history—Endnotes 3 and 4**

Amending laws are annotated in the legislation history and amendment history.

The legislation history in endnote 3 provides information about each law that has amended (or will amend) the compiled law. The information includes commencement details for amending laws and details of any application, saving or transitional provisions that are not included in this compilation.

The amendment history in endnote 4 provides information about amendments at the provision (generally section or equivalent) level. It also includes information about any provision of the compiled law that has been repealed in accordance with a provision of the law.

**Misdescribed amendments**

A misdescribed amendment is an amendment that does not accurately describe how an amendment is to be made. If, despite the misdescription, the amendment can be given effect as intended, then the misdescribed amendment can be incorporated through an editorial change made under section 15V of the *Legislation Act 2003*.

If a misdescribed amendment cannot be given effect as intended, the amendment is not incorporated and “(md not incorp)” is added to the amendment history.
